title: Madrid — months-long verification of declaraciones responsables and licences, with a paid ECU fast lane
who: any sector opening or changing premises (retail, hospitality, personal services, clinics, offices); autónomo, micro, small; chains and franchisees.
where: city of Madrid.
reality: Owners open on a declaración responsable, but the council's material check comes months later (target average 109 days). They operate exposed to requirements, closure orders or sanctions after spending on works. Activities that still need a prior licence wait a target average of 137 days, with only 40% resolved within 60 days. For certainty, owners pay a private ECU and municipal fees, plus 4% ICIO on works.
evidence:
- 109-day DR check standard (40% within 90 days); 137-day licence standard (40% within 60 days, 60% within 90 days); appointments needed for in-person help; ICIO 4% — [Carta de Servicios ADA 2026, evaluated 24 Feb 2026](https://www.madrid.es/UnidadesDescentralizadas/Calidad/CARTAS%20SERVICIOS/SistemaCartasServicio/41%20CS_de%20la%20Agencia%20de%20Actividades/DEFINITIVA/CS_ADA_2026.pdf)
- ECU maximum prices for 2026: DR €600 (≤50 m²) up to €1,250 (≤300 m²) plus €1.75/m² above that; first-occupation visit €1,080 (≤200 m²); second visits €325 — [ECU prices 2026, Junta de Gobierno 16 Oct 2025](https://www.madrid.es/UnidadesDescentralizadas/AgenciaActividades/ECUs/ficheros/AnexosI_II_III_IV_PreciosECU2026.pdf)
- 19 ECUs with 5–15% discounts — [Cuadro comparativo 2026](https://www.madrid.es/UnidadesDescentralizadas/AgenciaActividades/ECUs/ficheros/CuadroComparativoPreciosEcu_2026.pdf)
- Second independent source on actual delays: none found (single-source, official targets).
scale: 13,301 DRs and licences handled in 2025; 3,805 inspections (same charter).
cost_impact: €600–€1,250+ per ECU file, plus visits (€190–€1,080), *tasas* (amounts not retrieved) and 4% ICIO. The standard timelines imply about 3–5 months of regulatory uncertainty per opening.
driver_status: Ordenanza 6/2022 de Licencias y Declaraciones Responsables Urbanísticas (in force; listed in the 2026 charter). ECU 2026 prices are in force; prices for 2027 were approved on 15 Oct 2026.
solved_today: ECUs (voluntary, regulated prices); architects and engineers for technical projects (fees not found); gestorías. No documented complaints about ECUs were found.
software_solvable: partly. Pre-checks (use compatibility, document completeness), file tracking and ECU comparison are software; the statutory verification is public.
confidence: medium-high (official targets; actual 2025 results not retrieved).

title: València — chronic backlog in activity and environmental licences
who: activity openings, especially larger or environmental-impact ones (hospitality and nightlife, coworkings, hotels, factories); small to medium firms and investors.
where: city of València (Comunitat Valenciana).
reality: Files sat for months or years. Some applicants gave up (*"Muchos de ellos desisten de abrir actividades"*), and investors moved projects to Málaga or Granada.
evidence:
- 3,443 activity titles pending in August 2022 — [Valencia Plaza, 4 Sep 2022](https://valenciaplaza.com/valenciaplaza/pp-denuncia-un-atasco-de-mas-de-3400-licencias-de-actividad-en-el-ayuntamiento)
- Average 370 days for activity titles (2022 municipal study); 3,538 files in process; 1,470 environmental files stalled 1–7 years — [Valencia Plaza, 6 Feb 2023](https://valenciaplaza.com/valenciaplaza/el-pp-denuncia-que-urbanismo-de-valencia-tarda-725-dias-de-media-para-cerrar-un-informe-licencias-135-y-actividades-370)
- COGITI: delays of more than a year and "fuga de empresas" — [Valencia Plaza, 24 May 2023](https://valenciaplaza.com/ingenieros-tecnicos-industriales-critican-embudo-valencialicencias-municipales)
- Developers: about 2 years; PP estimate of more than 10,000 licences blocked — [Valencia Plaza, 19 Jun 2023](https://valenciaplaza.com/valenciaplaza/catala-unifica-las-concejalias-de-urbanismo-y-actividades-para-agilizar-las-licencias)
- Caveat: the figures come mostly from the PP opposition and were disputed by the then government.
scale: about 3,400–3,500 pending activity files (2022–2023).
cost_impact: delays of 1–2 years; flagship projects waited about 5 years; investment diverted (not quantified).
driver_status: Ley 6/2014 de la Comunitat Valenciana (environmental control of activities; in force, later amendments not verified). Ley 6/2024 de Simplificación Administrativa. The new municipal ordinance is a draft: drafting started 7 May 2025 ([valencia.es](https://www.valencia.es/cas/actualidad/-/content/nueva-ordenanza-de-obras)), and approval is not verified.
solved_today: private collaborating entities (ECUV), professional colleges offering help (COGITI), patience. No prices found.
software_solvable: partly. The bottleneck is municipal capacity; software helps with complete first-time files and tracking, and a business-to-government workflow could help the council.
confidence: medium (2022–2023 data, partisan sources; 2024–2026 status unknown).

title: Uncertainty over urban-use compatibility before signing a lease or investing
who: entrepreneurs and startups opening a first venue, franchisees, SMEs relocating (micro to medium).
where: a national pattern; evidence from València (CCU) and Madrid (consultation and certificates).
reality: A business commits to premises before knowing whether the use is allowed. In València, the compatibility certificate went from 15–45 days to more than a year for large projects, and late answers can force changes after the works. In Madrid, the urban-planning consultation carries a fee and an ECU compatibility certificate costs €500–€1,000.
evidence:
- COGITI on the CCU — [Valencia Plaza, 24 May 2023](https://valenciaplaza.com/ingenieros-tecnicos-industriales-critican-embudo-valencialicencias-municipales)
- Fees for urban-planning consultations — [ADA charter 2026](https://www.madrid.es/UnidadesDescentralizadas/Calidad/CARTAS%20SERVICIOS/SistemaCartasServicio/41%20CS_de%20la%20Agencia%20de%20Actividades/DEFINITIVA/CS_ADA_2026.pdf)
- ECU compatibility certificate €500 (≤100 m²), €700 (≤200 m²), €1,000 (≤300 m²) — [ECU prices 2026](https://www.madrid.es/UnidadesDescentralizadas/AgenciaActividades/ECUs/ficheros/AnexosI_II_III_IV_PreciosECU2026.pdf)
scale: not quantified (gap).
cost_impact: €500–€1,000 per certificate in Madrid, plus months of rent; projects can become unviable (COGITI).
driver_status: Ley 6/2014 de la Comunitat Valenciana (CCU; in force, amendments not verified); Madrid Ordenanza 6/2022 (in force).
solved_today: ECU certificates; consultations with architects or engineers; public assistants such as Málaga's ALU ([GMU Málaga](https://urbanismo.malaga.eu/)).
software_solvable: partly/yes. A preliminary "can I open X here?" answer from open planning data (general urban plans, PGOU) and rule engines; binding certificates stay official.

title: Diverging local and regional requirements that block or fragment activities (market-unity cases)
who: engineering and technical services (who may sign projects), telecom and fibre deployers, EV charging and battery storage, tourist-rental operators, training providers, passenger transport, fuel stations, funeral services. Mostly small and medium firms working across municipalities.
where: Andalucía, Canarias, Comunitat Valenciana, Navarra, Illes Balears (Palma, Calvià, Formentera), Euskadi; cities including Málaga, Sevilla, Zaragoza, Granada, Alicante, Badajoz, Murcia and Cornellà.
reality: The same activity needs different procedures, extra steps or particular professional signatures in each municipality or region. Firms escalate to the CNMC or SECUM, which takes months and ends in a report or a lawsuit.
evidence:
- 50 CNMC reports and rulings dated Sept 2025–Sept 2026 on page 1 of 14; the top sector is engineering and technical services (10) — [CNMC informes UM](https://www.cnmc.es/informes-unidad-de-mercado-2)
- CNMC appeals and objections in Badajoz (1 Oct 2026), Canarias (31 Jul 2026) and Valencian training grants (17 Jun 2026) — [CNMC](https://www.cnmc.es/ambitos-de-actuacion/unidad-de-mercado)
- CEOE (2026) on "asimetría de criterios entre administraciones" — [CEOE PRTR report](https://www.ceoe.es/sites/ceoe-corporativo/files/content/file/2026/06/26/104/informe-ejecucion-fondos-europeos-junio-2026.pdf)
- Regions produce 80.8% of bulletin pages — [INAP on CEOE 2022](https://laadministracionaldia.inap.es/noticia.asp?id=1232548)
scale: about 50 CNMC actions a year (my inference from the listing). This understates the problem, since most firms never complain.
cost_impact: blocked or delayed projects (for example the Badajoz petrol station, fibre deployments) and duplicate paperwork; no euro figures found.
driver_status: Ley 20/2013 de garantía de la unidad de mercado (in force and actively used by the CNMC in 2026).
solved_today: lawyers, trade associations, free CNMC or SECUM complaints.
software_solvable: partly. A municipality-by-municipality requirements map (who may sign, which procedure) helps; the root cause is legal.

title: Regulatory inflation and the cost of keeping up
who: all businesses, especially autónomos and micro firms without legal staff, and the gestorías and asesorías that serve them.
where: national, plus 17 regions and over 8,000 municipalities. The municipality count is general knowledge, not verified here.
reality: Official bulletins publish over a million pages a year, mostly regional. State-level urgent decree-laws keep changing obligations, and businesses cannot tell which changes apply to them.
evidence:
- 1.32M pages in 2022 (+22%), 80.8% regional; 849 state norms; 698 pages a day to keep up — [INAP on CEOE "Producción normativa en 2022"](https://laadministracionaldia.inap.es/noticia.asp?id=1232548)
- 2025: 6 laws, 267 normative royal decrees and RDLs 1 to 17/2025 — [IAEN 2025 (2026)](https://transparencia.gob.es/content/dam/transparencia_home/publicidadactiva/normativa/pan2025/IAEN%202025.pdf)
scale: universal (3,310,824 active companies — [INE DIRCE, 11 Dec 2025](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/Prensa/DIRCE2025.htm)).
cost_impact: no euro estimate found. The time burden is implied (698 pages a day).
driver_status: structural. Of the 2025 annual regulatory plan, 36.18% was approved and 46.23% was still in progress.
solved_today: gestorías and asesorías, trade associations, legal publishers (products and prices not verified).
software_solvable: yes. Monitoring filtered by sector code (CNAE) and municipality, with plain-language impact summaries.
confidence: medium (volume data from 2022; newer CEOE editions not retrieved).

title: SL formation — a "24-hour" legal promise versus 1–2 weeks of coordination
who: startups, new SMEs, autónomos incorporating, foreign founders.
where: national (Registro Mercantil; the Barcelona example).
reality: Founders chain together the name certificate, bank account and deposit certificate, notary, registry and post-registration tax steps, often with a gestor. Foreign founders also need an NIE and a digital certificate, and online guides even get the capital rule wrong.
evidence:
- Legal limits of 6 and 12 business hours and €1 capital — [BOE, Ley 18/2022](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2022-15818)
- 7–10 business days and €250–450 doing it yourself; FAQ wrongly says "€3,000 minimum" — [Strong Abogados, 17 Nov 2025](https://www.strongabogados.com/articles/sl-self-registration)
- Registro Mercantil de Barcelona 5–10 working days, "no hay un plazo garantizable" — [Billeo, 3 Aug 2026](https://www.billeo.es/blog/gestorias-especializadas-constitucion-sociedades-barcelona)
scale: new SLs per year not retrieved. About 1.45M non-natural-person businesses exist (DIRCE inference).
cost_impact: official fees about €100–€250 (search snippet, [Legálitas](https://www.legalitas.com/actualidad/crear-sl-con-un-euro)); €600–€1,500 with a gestor (search snippet, [Getrenn](https://getrenn.com/blog/how-to-register-a-company-in-spain)); 1–2 weeks.
driver_status: Ley 18/2022 (in force since 19 Oct 2022).
solved_today: CIRCE/PAE (low fees), notaries, gestorías, law firms bundling free formation with accounting.
software_solvable: partly. Orchestrating the single electronic form (DUE), bank and notary, plus post-formation compliance; but low willingness to pay and a crowded market.

title: Digital identity for companies — representative certificates, renewals and safe custody
who: all legal entities (directors and administrators), gestorías holding many clients' certificates, autónomos (personal certificate or Cl@ve).
where: national (FNMT, AEAT offices).
reality: Each company needs a representative certificate (€14 plus tax) and must renew it every 2 years. Entity types outside NIF A, B, C and D must accredit identity in person at AEAT, with an appointment. The DNIe/NFC route is unreliable. Certificates are installed per browser and shared among staff, which creates fraud risk; signatures were misused in the Kit Digital fraud.
evidence:
- €14 before tax, 2-year validity, accreditation rules, NFC warning — [FNMT, persona jurídica](https://www.sede.fnmt.gob.es/certificados/certificado-de-representante/persona-juridica)
- Cl@ve methods — [clave.gob.es](https://clave.gob.es/clave_Home/clave.html)
- Certificate identity theft — [Defensor del Pueblo 2025 §3.5](https://www.defensordelpueblo.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Defensor-del-Pueblo_Informe-anual-2025.pdf)
- Signatures used without consent — [Merca2, 14 Jun 2026](https://www.merca2.es/2026/06/14/fraude-kit-digital-supremo-las-palmas-2397192/)
scale: about 1.45M legal entities and 1.86M natural-person businesses (DIRCE 2025).
cost_impact: €14 plus VAT every 2 years; office visits; fraud exposure (vehicles registered in victims' names, fraudulent grant applications).
driver_status: Ley 39/2015 art. 14.2 (in force).
solved_today: FNMT; private certificate providers (prices not retrieved); centralised custody products such as IvSign ([Ivnosys](https://www.ivnosys.com/); no price shown); gestorías holding clients' certificates (practice not verified).
software_solvable: yes. Centralised custody with usage logs, permissions and renewal alerts.

title: Mandatory electronic notifications — the 10-day trap, embargoes and 9,000+ mailboxes
who: every SL, SA, cooperative, comunidad de bienes and other entity, of any size. Micro firms without an advisor are the most exposed.
where: national, regional and local (AEAT, Seguridad Social, DGT, regions, municipalities, courts).
reality: Notices land in DEHú or in separate electronic offices. If one is not opened within 10 calendar days it is deemed rejected, and the procedure moves on (enforcement order, account embargo, sanctions). The email alert is "obligatory", but the law says its absence does not invalidate the notice, so firms end up litigating with uncertain results.
evidence:
- Arts. 14.2, 41.6 and 43.2 — [BOE, Ley 39/2015, consolidated 6 Nov 2024](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2015-10565)
- Embargo upheld: an unopened e-notification is like an unopened letter — [TS 1927/2017, 11 Dec 2017](https://www.fiscal-impuestos.com/sites/fiscal-impuestos.com/files/NFJ068943.pdf)
- Embargo annulled for a missing alert (TSJ Murcia 396/2025, 2 Oct 2025; also STC 84/2022, SAN 78/2022, SAN 19 Apr 2023; no Supreme Court ruling yet) — [GA-P, Nov 2025](https://ga-p.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Aviso_previo_condicion_validez.pdf)
- "Sincroniza más de 9.000 sedes y evita sanciones" — [Ivnosys](https://www.ivnosys.com/) (vendor claim)
- Court summonses electronic for legal persons since 20 Mar 2024 — [Grupo2000](https://www.grupo2000.es/ya-es-posible-recibir-notificaciones-de-demandas-via-electronica) (search snippet only)
scale: about 1.45M non-natural-person businesses (3,310,824 − 1,859,925; inference from [INE DIRCE, 11 Dec 2025](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/Prensa/DIRCE2025.htm)).
cost_impact: bank-account embargoes, sanctions and enforcement surcharges (amounts not available), plus litigation costs. No national statistics found.
driver_status: Ley 39/2015 arts. 14.2, 41.6 and 43.2 (in force). Case law is evolving, with no Supreme Court ruling on the protective line as of Nov 2025.
solved_today: gestorías and asesorías acting as representatives (prices not found); notification managers such as IvNeos (no price); manual daily checks of several offices.
software_solvable: yes. Aggregation across DEHú, AEAT, Seguridad Social, regional and local offices, with alerts, legal-deadline calculation, triage, representative delegation and audit trail.
confidence: high on the mechanism and legal risk; medium on how often harm occurs.

title: Scarce appointments (cita previa) at Seguridad Social, SEPE and DGT
who: autónomos and micro employers who handle their own procedures, and their staff; driving schools and transport firms (DGT); all sizes in Madrid and Barcelona.
where: national; worst reported in Madrid (Seguridad Social, SEPE) and Barcelona (SEPE).
reality: In 2025 appointments could not be booked through any channel. Guards refused entry without one and people waited in the street. Traffic offices require compulsory appointments, and sanction files cannot be consulted online.
evidence:
- Seguridad Social blockage and guards; SEPE complaints in Madrid and Barcelona with 712 offices and 27,100 appointments a day in November 2025; DGT compulsory appointments — [Defensor del Pueblo, Informe anual 2025, pp. 108–109, 227–228, 231–232 and §3.5](https://www.defensordelpueblo.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Defensor-del-Pueblo_Informe-anual-2025.pdf) (single source; second source not found)
- Madrid's Agencia de Actividades also requires appointments for in-person help — [ADA charter 2026](https://www.madrid.es/UnidadesDescentralizadas/Calidad/CARTAS%20SERVICIOS/SistemaCartasServicio/41%20CS_de%20la%20Agencia%20de%20Actividades/DEFINITIVA/CS_ADA_2026.pdf)
scale: SEPE averages 27,100 appointments a day (November 2025).
cost_impact: delays and lost working time (not quantified).
driver_status: administrative practice of compulsory appointments. The DGT was considering moving to "recommended" appointments (2025). The Ombudsman reopened its Seguridad Social inquiry at the end of 2025.
solved_today: gestorías and *graduados sociales* using the Seguridad Social's online systems (prices not found); online procedures. Appointment resale is not verified.
software_solvable: partly. Guiding users to online alternatives and to representation removes some visits. Appointment-sniping bots are abusive and carry legal risk.

title: Immigration-office delays and inconsistent criteria — employers cannot onboard or keep foreign workers
who: employers in hospitality, agrifood, care, construction and logistics, and startups hiring non-EU talent; micro and small employers most exposed. Overlaps with the labour and HR researcher.
where: national; varies by provincial immigration office (the Ombudsman names Cádiz, Valencia and Madrid).
reality: Files pile up, offices apply different criteria and ask again for documents already submitted, and employers wait. The new Reglamento de extranjería (May 2025) added interpretive uncertainty.
evidence:
- Delays and diverging criteria with "graves consecuencias… también para sus empleadores"; RD 1155/2024 in force May 2025 with two interpretive criteria a month apart; asylum appointment system with "serias dificultades" — [Defensor del Pueblo, Informe anual 2025](https://www.defensordelpueblo.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Defensor-del-Pueblo_Informe-anual-2025.pdf)
- Foreign workers 14.1% of contributors at the end of 2025 — [Ministerio de Inclusión](https://inclusion.gob.es/gl/web/guest/w/la-seguridad-social-suma-mas-de-800.000-afiliados-extranjeros-desde-la-reforma-laboral-y-cierra-2025-en-maximos-historicos) (search snippet only)
scale: about 14% of contributors are foreign (snippet); 144,396 new asylum applications in 2025 (Ombudsman).
cost_impact: not quantified (vacancies unfilled, staff losing work permits).
driver_status: RD 1155/2024, Reglamento de la LO 4/2000 (in force since May 2025; challenges pending at the Supreme Court).
solved_today: immigration lawyers and gestorías (prices not found).
software_solvable: partly. Employer-side case tracking, office-specific checklists and renewal alerts; the root cause is staffing.

title: Autónomo contribution regularisations — surprise bills and opaque calculations
who: autónomos in every sector. Overlaps with the tax and labour researchers.
where: national (TGSS).
reality: Under the real-income contribution system, TGSS regularises the previous year's provisional bases and sends resolutions demanding the difference. Prior claims are "generally not upheld", and the Ombudsman says the method wrongly excludes months of activity.
evidence: [Defensor del Pueblo, Informe anual 2025, pp. 226–227](https://www.defensordelpueblo.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Defensor-del-Pueblo_Informe-anual-2025.pdf) (single source).
scale: proxy of 1,859,925 natural-person businesses ([INE DIRCE](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/Prensa/DIRCE2025.htm)); RETA membership not retrieved.
cost_impact: amounts payable per autónomo not available.
driver_status: RDL 13/2022 (in force; regularisations ongoing in 2025–2026).
solved_today: gestorías (prices not found).
software_solvable: yes. Forecast the contribution band from year-to-date income, warn early, and check TGSS calculations.

title: Kit Digital — overpricing, weak control and identity misuse that leave SMEs exposed
who: autónomos and micro and small firms (0 to fewer than 50 employees per Red.es), all sectors.
where: national; Catalonia examples; fraud case in Gran Canaria and Málaga.
reality: SMEs chose among more than 10,000 agents. Offers bundled hardware or inflated software (an invoicing tool billed against a €2,000 voucher was worth about €330), and contracts were hard to exit. Some applications were filed in SMEs' names without their consent, and those SMEs may now face repayment demands.
evidence:
- More than 900,000 aids, €3,067M, ended October 2025 — [Red.es](https://www.red.es/es/iniciativas/proyectos/kit-digital)
- Overpricing, lack of control, kitdigital.cat look-alike, VAT dispute — [Ara, 9 Jun 2025](https://en.ara.cat/economy/the-ups-and-downs-of-the-digital-kit-overpricing-and-poor-control_1_5405825.amp.html)
- Free iPhones; only 2.4% of SMEs had tried to apply (2022) — [Xataka, 29 Sep 2022](https://www.xataka.com/empresas-y-economia/regalar-iphones-no-digitalizacion-kit-digital-gobierno-cae-problemas-campanas-pasadas)
- Fraud case and repayment risk — [Merca2, 14 Jun 2026](https://www.merca2.es/2026/06/14/fraude-kit-digital-supremo-las-palmas-2397192/)
scale: more than 900,000 aids (Red.es); more than 930,000 beneficiaries ([CEOE, Jun 2026](https://www.ceoe.es/sites/ceoe-corporativo/files/content/file/2026/06/26/104/informe-ejecucion-fondos-europeos-junio-2026.pdf)).
cost_impact: overpricing (example above); repayment exposure; the Tribunal de Cuentas reportedly found only 25% of the budget paid out (single source via Merca2).
driver_status: Orden ETD/1498/2021 (bases). The programme **closed in October 2025**; the criminal case is open (Supreme Court order of 1 Jun 2026 sending it to Las Palmas).
solved_today: checking one's file on Acelera Pyme with a certificate or Cl@ve, lawyers, complaints to Red.es (the Ombudsman refers people there).
software_solvable: partly, and only as residual work: auditing past files and assembling evidence for repayment defence. The programme itself is over.

title: Kit Digital — intermediated justification and slow payment squeezing small IT vendors (agentes digitalizadores)
who: small IT, web and marketing agencies and freelancers that acted as agents (micro and small).
where: national.
reality: Agents delivered first and were paid by Red.es only after the Cámaras de Comercio validated the justification. That meant excessive and arbitrary corrections, no deadline and slow payment.
evidence:
- Up to 10 months to get paid; "se ha cobrado menos del 20%"; arbitrary *subsanaciones* — [Afectados Kit Digital press note, May 2023](https://theobjective.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/notadeprensa.afectadoskit-digital1.pdf)
- Payment problems for smaller agents — [Xataka, 2022](https://www.xataka.com/empresas-y-economia/regalar-iphones-no-digitalizacion-kit-digital-gobierno-cae-problemas-campanas-pasadas)
- Pimec: justification "could have been made easier" — [Ara, 2025](https://en.ara.cat/economy/the-ups-and-downs-of-the-digital-kit-overpricing-and-poor-control_1_5405825.amp.html)
scale: more than 10,000 agents (Ara); about 400 in the complaint group.
cost_impact: cash-flow strain; some agents considered closing (qualitative).
driver_status: Orden ETD/1498/2021. The programme closed in October 2025; residual payments and controls are ongoing (status in 2026 not verified).
solved_today: in-house administrative staff, lawyers.
software_solvable: partly. Automating justification evidence; but the market is shrinking because the programme ended.

title: NextGenerationEU — complex access, slow payments and repayment risk for SMEs at the end of the Recovery Facility
who: SMEs, mid-caps and deep-tech startups applying for strategic projects (PERTE), energy, digital and housing-renovation lines.
where: national, with regional management.
reality: The paperwork favours large firms, and administrative timelines do not match investment cycles. Payments lag, loans were unattractive and required collateral beyond most SMEs' reach. Now that the 31 Aug 2026 deadline has passed, beneficiaries fear repayment if execution slips.
evidence:
- All CEOE figures: 1.46M beneficiaries, 70% SMEs but 43% of funds; €27bn gap between called and awarded funds (EsadeEcPol); 2025 payments 18.7% of available credits; loans cut 73% (€83.2bn to €22.7bn); collateral out of reach for most SMEs; 223 milestones pending; about €32bn at risk (Funcas) — [CEOE, Jun 2026](https://www.ceoe.es/sites/ceoe-corporativo/files/content/file/2026/06/26/104/informe-ejecucion-fondos-europeos-junio-2026.pdf)
- Seventh and final payment request of €25,861M — [planderecuperacion.gob.es, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://planderecuperacion.gob.es/)
scale: 1,460,000 beneficiaries.
cost_impact: SMEs captured 43% of awarded volume. Repayment risk covers grants whose execution runs past 2026.
driver_status: EU Recovery and Resilience Facility, Regulation (EU) 2021/241 (milestone deadline 31 Aug 2026, now passed; the final request is pending EU assessment). Beneficiaries' justification continues, and CEOE asks for execution until 2028.
solved_today: grant consultancies (fees not found), tools such as Fandit (€56–€600/month), in-house teams.
software_solvable: partly. Justification and audit-trail tooling for double national and EU traceability; the window for new applications is closing.
confidence: high on figures (CEOE citing EsadeEcPol and Funcas; official homepage); medium on SME-level pain.

title: Grant justification and repayment exposure, including intermediated schemes (MOVES III)
who: autónomos and SMEs receiving grants (energy efficiency, EV charging, digitalisation, hiring), and the installers acting as participating firms.
where: national and regional (Andalucía example).
reality: Files stay unresolved. Where a participating installer handles the application and justification, the beneficiary is stuck if that firm disappears. Businesses ask for justification guides earlier, less up-front documentation, easier corrections and advance payments.
evidence:
- Unresolved MOVES III files; justification only by the participating firm (Andalucía) — [Defensor del Pueblo 2025, pp. 277–278](https://www.defensordelpueblo.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Defensor-del-Pueblo_Informe-anual-2025.pdf)
- Demands for earlier justification guides, less up-front documentation, easier corrections, advances, and no repayment for delays caused by the administration — [CEOE, Jun 2026](https://www.ceoe.es/sites/ceoe-corporativo/files/content/file/2026/06/26/104/informe-ejecucion-fondos-europeos-junio-2026.pdf)
scale: not quantified.
cost_impact: delays, liquidity strain (SMEs carry costs until paid), repayment risk.
driver_status: Ley 38/2003 General de Subvenciones (not re-verified this session); RD 266/2021 (MOVES III); Andalusian resolution of 7 Jul 2021.
solved_today: consultants and installers doing the paperwork (fees not found).
software_solvable: yes/partly. Justification workflows, evidence vault, deadline tracking, beneficiary-side visibility of intermediated files.

title: Grant discovery — tens of thousands of calls from thousands of administrations
who: all SMEs, autónomos and startups, and their advisors.
where: national, regional, provincial and local.
reality: Calls appear across hundreds of bulletins and websites. SMEs miss them or pay consultants and tools to monitor.
evidence: 81,665 grants, more than 8,500 administrations, more than 25,000 companies; prices €56–€600/month — [Fandit](https://www.fandit.es/), [Fandit precios](https://www.fandit.es/precios/) (single, commercial source).
scale: 81,665 grants (vendor count).
cost_impact: €56–€600/month subscriptions; consultant fees unknown.
driver_status: decentralised grant-making (structural).
solved_today: Fandit and similar tools, consultancies, gestorías, Cámaras.
software_solvable: yes, but it is already served (competitive).

title: Public tenders — thin competition and structural barriers for SMEs
who: SMEs in services (cleaning, maintenance, IT, consulting), supplies and works.
where: national, regional and local contracting authorities.
reality: Few firms bid (2.94 on average). Two in five lots attract a single bidder, and one in thirteen gets no award. Tender documents often lack the required cost breakdown, legal uncertainty concentrates in execution, and appeals are frequent.
evidence:
- 2.94 bidders (3.99 in 2020); 7.63% of lots unawarded; 117.47 days average processing; 5,053 appeals; cost breakdown missing in 49.50% (services) and 58.75% (supplies) — [OIReScon IAS 2025, 22 Dec 2025](https://www.hacienda.gob.es/rsc/oirescon/informe-anual-supervision-2025/ias2025-resumen-ejecutivo-es.pdf)
- 40.69% single bidder (85,029 of 208,962 lots) — [OIReScon Module I](https://www.hacienda.gob.es/RSC/OIReScon/informe-anual-supervision-2025/ias2025-modulo1.pdf)
- Second independent source not retrieved (the EU Single Market Scoreboard returned 403).
scale: 206,242 tenders; €113.1bn base budget (2024).
cost_impact: lost opportunities; appeal costs; cost of preparing bids (not quantified).
driver_status: LCSP, Ley 9/2017 (in force); Estrategia Nacional de Contratación Pública 2023–2026.
solved_today: tender consultants and services (licitaciones.es offers ROLECE registration help, an AI document assistant and competitor analysis; no public prices).
software_solvable: partly. Bid/no-bid analytics, DEUC and document automation, competitor and price intelligence; solvency and classification rules are legal.
confidence: high on competition metrics; the SME share is unknown.

title: Finding tenders across fragmented platforms, with contratos menores invisible
who: SMEs wanting public-sector customers, especially micro and small local suppliers.
where: PLACSP plus 7 regional platforms (Cataluña, País Vasco, La Rioja, Comunidad de Madrid, Galicia, Andalucía, Navarra), plus minor contracts that are barely published.
reality: Firms must watch several platforms with inconsistent data. Minor contracts (below €15,000 or €40,000), the natural entry point for micro firms, have no aggregated data, and auditors keep finding contracts split to stay under the thresholds.
evidence:
- Platform list; lack of homogeneity; "sería deseable contar con una única fuente" — [OIReScon Module I](https://www.hacienda.gob.es/RSC/OIReScon/informe-anual-supervision-2025/ias2025-modulo1.pdf)
- No aggregated minor-contract data; misuse through splitting — [OIReScon executive summary](https://www.hacienda.gob.es/rsc/oirescon/informe-anual-supervision-2025/ias2025-resumen-ejecutivo-es.pdf)
- Thresholds — [BOE, LCSP art. 118](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2017-12902)
scale: 206,242 tenders in 2024, plus an unknown number of minor contracts.
cost_impact: monitoring time and missed bids (not quantified).
driver_status: LCSP arts. 118 and 347 (in force).
solved_today: licitaciones.es (alerts, AI; no public prices), Euroalert (EU focus) and others (not verified).
software_solvable: yes (aggregation and matching), but it is a crowded category.

title: Contract execution friction — unforeseen modifications, appeals and missing subcontractor information
who: SME contractors and subcontractors in works and services.
where: national.
reality: After winning, firms face changes not foreseen in the tender documents, price-revision disputes and appeals. Subcontractors cannot verify whether the main contractor's payment obligations are being supervised.
evidence: modifications 22.45% of 2024 consultations (+37.5%); execution topics 32.65%; 93.08% of supervised SARA works contracts had unforeseen modifications; subcontracting information optional, so art. 217 payment checks cannot be supervised; execution is the least-documented phase — [OIReScon IAS 2025](https://www.hacienda.gob.es/rsc/oirescon/informe-anual-supervision-2025/ias2025-resumen-ejecutivo-es.pdf) (single source).
scale: 5,053 special appeals (2024).
cost_impact: not quantified. Late payment by administrations is covered by the cash-flow researcher.
driver_status: LCSP (in force).
solved_today: lawyers and in-house contract managers.
software_solvable: partly. Contract-execution logs, change-order documentation and subcontractor payment evidence.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Large customers impose long payment terms and pay late
who: Suppliers in all sectors that sell to large corporates. Hardest hit: autónomos, micro (<10) and small (10–49) firms.
where: National. On-time payment is worst in Canarias and Melilla and best in Navarra, País Vasco and La Rioja.
reality: Large clients write 60–90-day terms into their contracts and then pay later still. The supplier finances the client, chases payment, and cannot push back for fear of losing the account. Reported verbatim: "Las empresas que más tardan en pagar son las grandes" (The companies that take longest to pay are the large ones).
evidence:
- PMcM: private-sector PMP 67 days in 2025; only 15% of large clients pay within the legal period; 60% of suppliers have >60-day contracts; 33% face abusive clauses — [PMcM, Apr 2026](https://pmcm.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Informe-Morosidad-2025_PMcM-VF.pdf)
- 85% of large companies exceed the legal deadline — [PMcM, 22 Oct 2026](https://pmcm.es/pmcm-cinco-compromisos-contra-morosidad/)
- Cepyme: PMP 80.5 days in H2 2025 — [AyE, 12 Apr 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/pymes/pymes-solo-cobran-cada-tres-facturas-tiempo-ultimo-observatorio-morosidad/20260410165245053056.html)
- Informa: large firms 14.00 days late on average in Q3 2026 — [Empresa Exterior, 17 Oct 2026](https://empresaexterior.com/el-retraso-en-los-pagos-se-enquista-por-encima-de-los-14-dias-y-lastra-al-tejido-empresarial-espanol/)
scale: More than 2.9M pymes and autónomos (Cámara de Comercio, cited by [AyE, 20 Nov 2025](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/pymes/reglamento-que-sancionara-empresas-pagar-tarde-autonomos-podria-estar-listo-2026/20251119125557046617.html)); 60% of surveyed suppliers have contracts beyond the legal term.
cost_impact:
- €1,957M financial burden on pymes in 2025 — [Cepyme](https://cepyme.es/el-esfuerzo-financiero-de-las-pymes-como-consecuencia-de-la-morosidad-se-cifra-en-1-957-millones-de-euros/)
- About €3,100M direct cost — [Informa via Empresa Exterior](https://empresaexterior.com/el-retraso-en-los-pagos-se-enquista-por-encima-de-los-14-dias-y-lastra-al-tejido-empresarial-espanol/)
- Unpaid invoices equal to 3.3% of sales — [PMcM](https://pmcm.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Informe-Morosidad-2025_PMcM-VF.pdf)
driver_status:
- Ley 3/2004 as amended by Ley 15/2010 (60-day maximum): **in force, no sanctions**.
- The 2020 Junts bill on sanctions: **stalled**. No bill is pending after the Cortes were dissolved on 6 October 2026.
- EU Late Payment Regulation COM(2023) 533: **blocked in the Council** (formal withdrawal not verified).
- Crea y Crece: the subsidy condition for grants above €30k is in force, and e-invoice payment-status reporting arrives 2027–2029 (upcoming).
solved_today:
- External financing is the first choice of 71% (credit lines, factoring and confirming; Novicap etc., prices on quote).
- 19% stretch their own payables.
- Collection agencies (5–25%), gestorías and lawyers.
- Complaint: 43% of suppliers think even an EU 30-day cap "won't be complied with" — [PMcM](https://pmcm.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Informe-Morosidad-2025_PMcM-VF.pdf)
software_solvable: Partly. Software cannot change bargaining power, but it can monitor contract terms against the law, document breaches, automate claims, and score payers.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Late payment along subcontracting chains (construction and industrial services)
who: Construction subcontractors and trades, plus installation and maintenance firms. Mostly autónomos, micro and small (10–49) firms. Overlaps with the construction researcher.
where: National.
reality: The main contractor waits to be paid by its client, sometimes a public body, and only then pays subcontractors. Subcontractors carry wages and materials for about three months.
evidence:
- Contractor-to-subcontractor PMP 87 days in 2025 — [PMcM](https://pmcm.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Informe-Morosidad-2025_PMcM-VF.pdf); 88 days in 2024 — [AyE, 20 Nov 2025](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/pymes/reglamento-que-sancionara-empresas-pagar-tarde-autonomos-podria-estar-listo-2026/20251119125557046617.html)
- Construction PMP 96.5 days in H2 2025 — [AyE / Cepyme, 12 Apr 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/pymes/pymes-solo-cobran-cada-tres-facturas-tiempo-ultimo-observatorio-morosidad/20260410165245053056.html)
scale: Construction accounted for 15.4% of insolvent companies in Q4 2025 — [Registradores](https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/np-epc-4t-2025b). I found no count of subcontractors affected.
cost_impact: Not quantified separately.
driver_status: Ley 3/2004, in force without sanctions. The blocked EU proposal would have required administrations to check that contractors pay subcontractors on time — [AyE, 20 Nov 2025](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/pymes/reglamento-que-sancionara-empresas-pagar-tarde-autonomos-podria-estar-listo-2026/20251119125557046617.html). Public-procurement rules on paying subcontractors (LCSP) were not verified in this session.
solved_today: Confirming offered by the main contractor (the subcontractor pays to be paid early), factoring, lawyers.
software_solvable: Partly. Payment tracking along the chain and early-payment marketplaces are feasible. Whether subcontractors get paid sooner still depends on main contractors.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Statutory late-payment interest and the €40 compensation go unclaimed
who: All suppliers, especially autónomos and micro firms.
where: National.
reality: Overdue invoices are chased for the principal only. Firms rarely calculate or add the statutory interest or the €40 per-invoice compensation, out of fear of upsetting the customer, lack of awareness, or the hassle.
evidence:
- 89% never or almost never claim interest; 94% don't claim the €40; 30% don't know the law — [PMcM 2025](https://pmcm.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Informe-Morosidad-2025_PMcM-VF.pdf)
- In 2024 the figures were 84% and 92% — [AyE, 20 Nov 2025](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/pymes/reglamento-que-sancionara-empresas-pagar-tarde-autonomos-podria-estar-listo-2026/20251119125557046617.html)
scale: About 9 in 10 suppliers surveyed.
cost_impact: Money left uncollected. Illustration: about €168 on a €10,000 invoice paid 45 days late, at 10.40% interest plus €40 — [Novicap, 15 Oct 2026](https://novicap.com/blog/morosidad-en-espana-2026/) (single source for the rate).
driver_status: Ley 3/2004, arts. 7–8 (interest and €40 compensation), **in force**. The rate is reset each half-year by BOE resolution (H2 2026 resolution not verified).
solved_today: Manually by lawyers and collection agencies once a claim is under way. I found no evidence that invoicing tools automate it.
software_solvable: Yes. Calculation, notices and evidence can be fully automated. The barrier is behavioural (fear for the relationship), so the feature should be optional and offered as a settlement lever.
confidence: High for the data; medium for willingness to use it.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Public-sector late payment concentrated in specific regions and cities
who: Suppliers to regional and local government: health suppliers, cleaning, maintenance, IT and social services. Micro, small and medium (50–249) firms.
where: Regional: Illes Balears, Región de Murcia, Cantabria, Asturias, Cataluña. Cities: Palma, Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Murcia, A Coruña, Sevilla, plus 11 local entities above 60 days.
reality: Invoices go into FACe (the public e-invoicing portal) but wait for approval. Suppliers carry public clients for two months or more, and local councils are seen as the slowest.
evidence:
- Official August 2026 PMP: Balears 53.42 days, Murcia 42.38, Cantabria 38.51, Asturias 32.86, Cataluña 32.00; Palma 51.69, Las Palmas GC 48.40, Murcia city 36.38, A Coruña 30.64, Sevilla 30.37; 25.48% of local entities above 30 days and 7.01% above 60 — [Hacienda, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.hacienda.gob.es/es-es/prensa/noticias/paginas/2026/20261022-np-pmp-agosto.aspx)
- Supplier survey: public sector 70 days, local administration named slowest by 55% — [PMcM 2025](https://pmcm.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Informe-Morosidad-2025_PMcM-VF.pdf)
scale: Commercial debt of €4,817.6M (which I infer refers to the CCAA) — [Hacienda](https://www.hacienda.gob.es/es-es/prensa/noticias/paginas/2026/20261022-np-pmp-agosto.aspx).
cost_impact: Not quantified. 19% of companies reportedly avoid public tenders because of late payment — [Xornal21, 14 Aug 2026](https://xornal21.com/art/72938/la-morosidad-aboca-a-la-quiebra-a-empresas-viables-advierte-la-pmcm) (attribution uncertain).
driver_status: Ley 3/2004's 30-day limit for administrations and PMP monitoring by Hacienda, both **in force**. The regulation behind Hacienda's PMP methodology was not verified.
solved_today: Factoring public receivables, waiting, Hacienda's procedure for reporting PMP breaches ("Comunicaciones por incumplimiento del PMP").
software_solvable: Partly. Software can track invoices in FACe, raise alerts and offer financing, but cannot make administrations approve invoices faster.
confidence: High for the regional data; medium for the size of the pain, because official and survey figures conflict.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Collection dates are unpredictable, which breaks cash planning
who: Everyone, most acutely micro firms and autónomos, hospitality, agriculture and energy.
where: National. Worst in Canarias (23.16 days late) and Melilla (23.56).
reality: Fewer than half of invoices are paid on the due date, so owners cannot know whether they will cover payroll, Social Security contributions and VAT. They juggle overdrafts and delay their own suppliers.
evidence:
- 41.51% paid on time in Q3 2026 (43.94% in Q1); micro firms 16.79 days late; hospitality 23.89 — [Empresa Exterior, 17 Oct 2026](https://empresaexterior.com/el-retraso-en-los-pagos-se-enquista-por-encima-de-los-14-dias-y-lastra-al-tejido-empresarial-espanol/); [Novicap, 15 Oct 2026](https://novicap.com/blog/morosidad-en-espana-2026/)
- 30.4% of invoiced amounts collected on time (Cepyme) — [AyE, 12 Apr 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/pymes/pymes-solo-cobran-cada-tres-facturas-tiempo-ultimo-observatorio-morosidad/20260410165245053056.html)
scale: National. The Informa sample covered invoices worth €18,617M.
cost_impact: About €3,100M direct cost (Informa); 5.23% of payments more than 60 days late.
driver_status: Market practice; no specific regulation.
solved_today: Excel and gestorías (assumed; no survey found), credit lines, and treasury tools: Banktrack €59–119 a month, Qonto from €9–19 a month, Agicap on quote.
software_solvable: Yes. Forecasting each customer's payment date from its history, plus automatic reminders. The data advantage grows once e-invoice payment statuses arrive in 2027–2029.
confidence: High for the data; medium for the solution fit.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: The mandatory pre-litigation step (MASC) before claiming unpaid invoices
who: All creditors, especially autónomos and micro firms with small claims, and homeowners' associations.
where: National. Madrid monitorios −31.3%; Audiencia Provincial de Málaga ruling of June 2025.
reality: Before filing a monitorio or a verbal claim, the creditor must send a documented negotiation offer that can be proven (burofax, certified email or SMS, notary or mediation) and wait up to a month. A WhatsApp message or phone call does not count. Filing without a valid attempt is an incurable defect and the claim is rejected.
evidence:
- LO 1/2025 in force since 3 April 2025 — [Hay Derecho, 31 Mar 2025](https://www.hayderecho.com/2025/03/31/la-ley-de-eficiencia-procesal-y-los-masc-capitulo-i/); [BOE](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2025-76)
- Valid and invalid methods, the one-month rule, incurable defect — [Grupo Intercobros, 2026](https://www.grupointercobros.com/masc-y-reclamacion-de-deudas/)
- Courts apply the requirement to the monitorio — [vLex](https://vlex.es/vid/proceso-monitorio-masc-1121357868)
- Monitorios −20.7% year-on-year in Q2 2026 — [Moncloa.com / CGPJ, 16 Oct 2026](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/10/16/cgpj-desahucios-lanzamientos-concursos-acreedores-3449594/)
scale: 179,846 monitorios in Q2 2026 alone, each of which now needs a MASC attempt.
cost_impact: An extra certified communication (burofax price not verified), legal fees (RedClaimer from €99.90 per file; a GW Abogados consultation €110), and about a month of delay. Rejections when the attempt is not valid.
driver_status: Ley Orgánica 1/2025, **in force since 3 April 2025**.
solved_today: Lawyers, collection agencies (Intercobros, RedClaimer), certified-communication providers (BuroMail/BuroSMS). Complaint: confusion over which methods are valid, and claims rejected for a missing MASC — [ETL Ilia](https://etl-ilia.es/blog-asesoria-legal/masc-monitorio-comunidades-propietarios/).
software_solvable: Yes. Software can generate a compliant offer, send it by a certified channel, track deadlines (one month to qualify, one year of validity), assemble the evidence pack and pass the file straight to the monitorio.
confidence: High for the law; medium for the size of its effect.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Monitorio and court friction, and backlogs during the efficiency reform
who: Creditors in all sectors, especially micro and small firms.
where: National. Madrid's backlog grew 10.4% in 2025.
reality:
- In a monitorio, a debtor who cannot be located cannot be notified by public notice, so the file is archived.
- Any opposition turns the case into a declarative procedure.
- Enforcing more than €2,000 needs a lawyer and a procurador.
- Courts are being reorganised (tribunales de instancia), and lawyers are holding back filings.
evidence:
- No notice by publication; opposition converts the case — [GW Abogados, 20 Sep 2026](https://www.gwabogados.es/blog/morosidad-y-cobro/la-muerte-del-procedimiento-monitorio)
- Lawyer and procurador required above €2,000 — [BOE LO 1/2025](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2025-76) (search summary)
- Madrid: incoming cases −5.3%, backlog +10.4%, the president's caution about the fall — [Moncloa.com, 15 Jul 2026](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/07/15/tsj-madrid-ley-eficiencia-descenso-asuntos-3399983)
scale: About 180,000 monitorios a quarter; 825,114 pending cases in Madrid.
cost_impact: Lawyer and procurador fees (not verified), and months of delay.
driver_status: LO 1/2025, in force. The tribunales de instancia rollout happened in 2025–2026.
solved_today: Lawyers, collection agencies, skipping the monitorio for a declarative claim, writing debts off.
software_solvable: Partly. Software can prepare the case, find the debtor's address and send status alerts. Court times are outside its control.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Collection services are uneconomic for small invoices
who: Autónomos and micro firms with many small receivables.
where: National.
reality: Agencies take a percentage or set minimum claim sizes, so invoices of a few hundred euros are chased by the owner or written off.
evidence:
- Fees from 5–6% — [Absolut](https://absolutabogados.com/empresa-recobro/); [Debitura](https://www.debitura.com/countries/debt-collection-agency-spain)
- "10–25%" is typical, and a flat €99.90 per file — [RedClaimer](https://redclaimer.es/productos/burofax/)
- Minimum €1,500 per debtor file — [Recobrarte](https://recobrarte.es/)
scale: Unpaid invoices average 3.3% of sales — [PMcM](https://pmcm.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Informe-Morosidad-2025_PMcM-VF.pdf)
cost_impact: 5–25% of the amount recovered, or €100 or more per file.
driver_status: Market. MASC adds a mandatory step (see FIN-06).
solved_today: Owners send their own reminders and burofaxes, use agencies, or write the debt off.
software_solvable: Yes. Automated reminders, plus the MASC step and filing at a low fixed cost.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Checking a customer's solvency is fragmented and paid
who: Any supplier giving trade credit. Medium (50–249) and small (10–49) firms in wholesale, industry and services.
where: National.
reality: To vet a customer, firms buy bundled bureau reports (eInforma, Informa, Experian) that include ASNEF Empresas, RAI and EBE. RAI covers only companies, for debts of €300 or more.
evidence:
- ASNEF Empresas only accessible inside reports; listings last up to six years — [eInforma](https://www.einforma.com/informacion-empresas/asnef-empresas)
- RAI: debts of €300 or more, legal persons only, paid access — [Novicap guide](https://novicap.com/guia-financiera/registro-aceptaciones-impagadas-rai-que-es/); [Creditolab, 2026](https://creditolab.com/es/blog/ficheros-de-morosos-espana-2026)
scale: Unknown.
cost_impact: Prices are not public (gap).
driver_status: A few credit bureaus control the data, under data-protection rules (not verified here).
solved_today: Bureau reports, credit insurance (not priced), word of mouth.
software_solvable: Partly. Payment-behaviour scores could be built from receivables and e-invoice data from 2027 to 2029.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Working capital is squeezed and short-term finance is getting more expensive
who: Pymes that sell on credit, especially to large clients, and hospitality autónomos. Small and medium firms.
where: National.
reality: To bridge late collections, firms draw on credit lines, discount invoices or accept customers' confirming programmes. In 2026 the rates are rising.
evidence:
- 51.2% of pymes had financing needs in 2025 (+3.5 points), with working-capital demand up — [CESGAR](https://cesgar.es/xv-informe-sobre-financiacion-de-la-pyme-de-sgr-cesgar-mas-de-la-mitad-de-las-pymes-ha-tenido-necesidades-de-financiacion-en-2025/)
- A net 43% of euro-area SMEs reported higher bank rates in Q2 2026 — [ECB SAFE, 20 Jul 2026](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/ecb_surveys/safe/html/ecb.safe202607.en.html)
- 71% would first seek external finance when short of liquidity — [PMcM](https://pmcm.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Informe-Morosidad-2025_PMcM-VF.pdf)
scale: More than 1.8M companies with financing needs (CESGAR).
cost_impact: €1,957M financial burden of late payment on pymes — [Cepyme](https://cepyme.es/el-esfuerzo-financiero-de-las-pymes-como-consecuencia-de-la-morosidad-se-cifra-en-1-957-millones-de-euros/)
driver_status: Market force (bank lending rates rising in 2026 per SAFE).
solved_today:
- Bank credit lines.
- ICO lines, with margins set by the bank — [ICO](https://www.ico.es/web/guest/ico-empresas-y-emprendedores)
- SGR guarantees, €3,084M in 2025 — [CESGAR](https://cesgar.es/las-sociedades-de-garantia-inyectaron-3-084-millones-de-euros-a-pymes-y-autonomos-en-2025-un-14-mas-que-el-ano-anterior/)
- Invoice-finance fintechs (Novicap, prices on quote).
software_solvable: Partly. Embedded invoice finance and comparison of financing options are feasible; the cost of credit is set by banks.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Public guarantee and credit schemes are fragmented and go through the banks
who: Pymes and autónomos needing guarantees; businesses hit by disasters.
where: National (ICO); regional SGRs (Iberaval in Castilla y León, Aval CLM, Aválam in Murcia, AvalCanarias, Elkargi in País Vasco, among others); emergency lines in Andalucía, Extremadura and Valencia.
reality: Firms must work out which ICO, SGR, regional or emergency line applies, then apply through a bank, which sets the margin, and meet line-specific deadlines (for example 30 November 2026 for the Andalucía/Extremadura emergency line).
evidence:
- ICO line conditions — [ICO](https://www.ico.es/web/guest/ico-empresas-y-emprendedores); [ICO emergency line](https://www.ico.es/web/guest/linea-avales-emergencias-andalucia-y-extremadura)
- SGR 2025 figures — [CESGAR](https://cesgar.es/las-sociedades-de-garantia-inyectaron-3-084-millones-de-euros-a-pymes-y-autonomos-en-2025-un-14-mas-que-el-ano-anterior/)
- DANA ICO line: 3,470 operations — [Moncloa info-DANA, 19 Oct 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/info-dana/Paginas/2026/191026-datos-seguimiento-actuaciones-gobierno.aspx)
scale: 186,877 companies used SGR guarantees and 25,075 guarantees were issued in 2025; ICO approved €10,265M in 2025 — [ICO](https://www.ico.es/)
cost_impact: Guarantee commissions not found; ICO margins are set by banks with no published cap.
driver_status: ICO 2026 lines **in force**. RDL 5/2026 emergency line **in force, deadline 30 November 2026**.
solved_today: Bank branches, gestorías and advisers, the SGRs themselves.
software_solvable: Partly. An eligibility-matching and application-tracking tool is feasible, but SAFE shows only 3% of firms report financing obstacles, so demand may be thin.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Payment and invoice fraud (fake IBANs, business email compromise, phishing)
who: All businesses. Most exposed: autónomos and micro firms with no IT staff, and the admin and finance staff of small (10–49) firms.
where: National. Canarias data shows 244 company queries to the 017 helpline.
reality:
- A "supplier" emails new bank details.
- Someone impersonates the boss and demands an urgent transfer.
- Bank credentials are phished, or an email session is hijacked.
- The money is gone, and bank complaint routes are slow and often go the bank's way.
evidence:
- INCIBE 2025: 45,445 online-fraud cases (+19%) including 25,133 phishing; 017 helpline queries +44.9% — [INCIBE, 9 Feb 2026](https://www.incibe.es/incibe/sala-de-prensa/incibe-detecto-mas-de-122000-incidentes-de-ciberseguridad-en-2025)
- BdE: fraud is the main focus of complaints — [BdE MSR 2025](https://www.bde.es/f/webbe/Secciones/Publicaciones/PublicacionesAnuales/MemoriaServicioReclamaciones/25/MSR2025_Resumen.pdf)
- 22% of Spanish SMEs hit by invoice or payment fraud (vendor survey) — [AyE / Kaspersky, 10 Sep 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/todo-digital/ocho-cada-diez-pymes-espanolas-han-sufrido-ciberataque-muchos-descuidos-empleados/20260909151304055801.html)
scale: 122,223 incidents nationally in 2025 (all types of victim).
cost_impact: No euro figure for SMEs found. BdE refunds across all complaints totalled only €6.8M in 2025.
driver_status:
Criminal market force.
- Verification of Payee under Regulation (EU) 2024/886, mandatory from 9 October 2025: **unverified**.
- PSD3/PSR: not verified.
solved_today: The free INCIBE 017 helpline, banks' strong customer authentication, IT providers, cyber insurance (not priced).
software_solvable: Yes, partly. Checking bank details against supplier records, two-person payment approval, and anomaly alerts in accounts payable and banking.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Card and POS acceptance costs and juggling payment methods in small shops
who: Retail, hospitality and personal services (overlaps with those researchers). Autónomos and micro firms.
where: National.
reality: Shops must accept cash, card, mobile and Bizum, and online sellers must handle chargebacks. Fees are modest but add up.
evidence:
- Cash is the main method for 57% of consumers; cards accepted in 94% of small shops and hospitality businesses, mobile in 88% — [BdE, 12 Nov 2025](https://www.bde.es/f/webbe/GAP/Secciones/SalaPrensa/NotasInformativas/25/presbe2025_110.pdf)
- Fees: SumUp 1.49% or €19/€49 plans — [SumUp](https://www.sumup.com/es-es/precios/); Stripe 1.5% + €0.25 and €20 per dispute — [Stripe](https://stripe.com/es/pricing); Qonto 0.8–1.2% — [Qonto](https://qonto.com/es/pricing)
scale: Bizum has 31.5M users and 120,000 online merchants — [Bizum](https://bizum.com/es/)
cost_impact: 0–1.5% of card volume; €20 per chargeback.
driver_status: Market. The EU interchange-fee caps were not re-verified.
solved_today: SumUp, Stripe, Qonto, bank POS terminals on Redsys (prices not collected).
software_solvable: Yes, but the market is commoditised and crowded.
confidence: Medium (prices verified; weak evidence that it is a serious pain).

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Bank fees and disputes with banks
who: Autónomos and micro firms. Most evidence comes from consumers.
where: National. Madrid has the highest complaint rate (10 per 10,000 people).
reality: Fees are charged even on accounts with no balance, products are cancelled, and frauds are disputed. Only about a third of complaints to the Banco de España are admitted (the bank's own customer service must be used first).
evidence:
- 30,970 complaints, 10,856 admitted; 39% favourable to the bank and 20% to the customer; fees and cancellations among the main triggers; new criterion on fees for empty accounts — [BdE MSR 2025, 21 Jul 2026](https://www.bde.es/f/webbe/Secciones/Publicaciones/PublicacionesAnuales/MemoriaServicioReclamaciones/25/MSR2025_Resumen.pdf)
- Neobank benchmark: €0–199 a month — [Qonto](https://qonto.com/es/pricing)
scale: Banks' own customer-service departments handled more than one million complaints in 2025.
cost_impact: Average refund €625 per admitted complaint.
driver_status: Banking-transparency regulation, in force (details not verified).
solved_today: Switching to neobanks (Qonto) or negotiating with the branch. I found no evidence on business account-opening problems.
software_solvable: Partly (fee monitoring and comparison); limited value.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Autónomo insolvency and the complexity of Segunda Oportunidad
who: Autónomos, who are personally liable for business debts, and former autónomos with personal guarantees.
where: National. Cataluña, Madrid, Valencia and Andalucía lead in volume.
reality: An autónomo owing banks, suppliers, Hacienda and Social Security must go through a concurso, usually one with no assets, to seek discharge (EPI). Whether public debts can be discharged is legally contested.
evidence:
- 1,605 individual entrepreneurs declared insolvent in Q4 2025 (+14.5% year-on-year; +28.2% over 2025) — [Registradores](https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/np-epc-4t-2025b)
- CGPJ Q2 2026: 672 individual-entrepreneur concursos (−10.8%) — [Moncloa.com](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/10/16/cgpj-desahucios-lanzamientos-concursos-acreedores-3449594/)
- STS 450/2025: public debts dischargeable through a payment plan, but the TRLC is unamended — [Economist & Jurist, 1 Oct 2025](https://www.economistjurist.es/articulos-juridicos-destacados/el-fin-del-blindaje-publico-el-reciente-viraje-jurisprudencial-sobre-la-exoneracion-de-deuda-publica-en-la-segunda-oportunidad/)
scale: About 1,600 individual entrepreneurs a quarter, plus about 14,000 individuals without activity a quarter (many of them former business owners; share unknown).
cost_impact: Legal fees not found; five-year risk of the discharge being revoked.
driver_status: TRLC as reformed by Ley 16/2022, **in force**. STS 450/2025 case law applies; the code's wording is unchanged.
solved_today: Specialist Segunda Oportunidad law firms (many online) and legal aid.
software_solvable: Partly. Document preparation and creditor lists can be automated; the court process remains.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: The micro-enterprise insolvency procedure works almost only as a liquidation route
who: Micro firms (fewer than 10 employees, turnover under €700k or liabilities under €350k): commerce, construction, hospitality, professional services.
where: National. Used heavily in Madrid (212 in Q4 2025) and Valencia (116), rarely in Cataluña (30).
reality: Owners file only when already insolvent. 96% of cases end in liquidation. Liquidation is forced if 85% or more of the debt is public or tax and Social Security are not up to date. The debtor needs a lawyer and a procurador.
evidence:
- 1,427 procedures in 2025, of which 52 continuations; 970 liquidations concluded with a median of 169.5 days — [Registradores Anuario 2025](https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/anuario-concursal-2025)
- 511 openings in Q4 2025 — [Registradores](https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/np-epc-4t-2025b)
- Forced-liquidation rule — [AEAT](https://www3.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/normativa-criterios-interpretativos/analisis/El_credito_publico_en_el_procedimiento_especial_para_microempresas.html)
- Lawyer and procurador required — [Cámara de Comercio de Toledo](https://camaratoledo.com/procedimiento-especial-para-micro-empresas/)
scale: 22.5% of company insolvency procedures in 2025.
cost_impact: The business is closed in about 96% of cases. Professional fees not found.
driver_status: Ley 16/2022, Book III of the TRLC, **in force since 1 January 2023**.
solved_today: Lawyers, plus the Justice Ministry's electronic service with standard forms for micro-enterprises.
software_solvable: Partly. Early warning and preparation of filings are feasible; a continuation plan still needs creditors and public bodies to agree.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Directors' personal liability when losses trigger the legal dissolution cause
who: Owner-managers of limited companies (SLs). SLs are 93.2% of company concursos — [Registradores](https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/np-epc-4t-2025b).
where: National.
reality: Owners do not track net equity against share capital and miss the two-month window to call the shareholders. Creditors then sue the directors personally for debts incurred in the meantime.
evidence: Supreme Court STS 1477/2026 — [AyE, 23 Oct 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/pymes/supremo-confirma-que-autonomos-societarios-pueden-asumir-deudas-sl-actuan-tiempo/20261022150439056494.html) (single source).
scale: Unknown frequency of such claims.
cost_impact: Personal liability for company debts. The case concerned a €42,000 claim, and the article gives a €20,000 debt as an example.
driver_status: Ley de Sociedades de Capital dissolution rules (article numbers not verified here) and STS 1477/2026. **In force.**
solved_today: Gestorías and accountants (when they notice), lawyers.
software_solvable: Yes. Automatic alerts from accounting data when net equity falls below half of share capital, a deadline countdown, and template meeting notices.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Young, tiny firms fail early, and autónomos quit for economic reasons
who: Hospitality, commerce and professional services; startups and businesses under four years old; autónomos.
where: National. Commerce lost 763 autónomos in September 2026. Castilla y León, Galicia and Aragón lost autónomos that month.
reality: Thin margins and fixed costs (rent, the monthly social-security contribution, taxes) exhaust cash within a few years. Owners exit, often through a no-asset concurso or simply by deregistering.
evidence:
- Hospitality: 59.1% of insolvent firms under four years old; 61.7% of all insolvent firms eight years or younger; 46.8% with turnover of €250k or less — [Registradores Q4 2025](https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/np-epc-4t-2025b)
- 90% of those leaving RETA do so for economic reasons, earning €900–1,166.7 a month — [AyE / ENA 2024, 31 Oct 2024](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/noticias-de-empresa/cada-diez-autonomos-que-dan-baja-reta-hacen-motivos-economicos/20241030121727039138.html)
- September 2026 RETA flows — [AyE / ATA, 23 Oct 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/info-ata/septiembre-sumaron-mas-400-autonomos-dia-sigue-sangria-sectores-como-comercio/20261002153557056144.html)
scale: 3,483,645 autónomos; about 6,300 company insolvency procedures in 2025.
cost_impact: Closures; personal debts.
driver_status: Market forces (costs, demand). Tax and social contributions were cited as barriers by 27.1% and 25.6%.
solved_today: Gestorías; no dedicated tool found.
software_solvable: Partly. Cash runway and break-even tools are feasible; weak demand is a structural problem.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: DANA 2024 business recovery — business claims settle slowly and aid is fragmented
who: Shops and warehouses, industrial firms on industrial estates, offices and autónomos. Micro, small and medium firms.
where: Valencia province: Paiporta, Catarroja, Algemesí, Aldaia, Alfafar, València city, Benetússer, Massanassa, Sedaví, Picanya, Riba-roja de Túria, Albal, Beniparrell, Torrent, Chiva, among others.
reality: Two years on, some business claims are still being assessed, especially industrial ones. Firms deal with several aid channels at once (AEAT, ICO, ERTE, cessation benefit, regional calls), each with its own procedure, and some calls are first come, first served.
evidence:
- 23,348 business claims, 3.0% still pending, 4.6% of industrial claims pending (June 2026) — [CCS, 30th note](https://www.consorseguros.es/documents/10184/0/TRIGESIMA_nota_informativa_DEFINITIVA.pdf/e156c23e-f3a8-a031-0c46-bbd5c9d47001?t=1780910871713)
- Aid figures: 27,466 AEAT direct-aid payments; 4,169 ERTE companies; 5,295 cessation benefits — [Moncloa, 19 Oct 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/info-dana/Paginas/2026/191026-datos-seguimiento-actuaciones-gobierno.aspx)
- EMDANA second call, €3.26M, first come, first served — [AyE, 15 Sep 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/ayudas-subvenciones/comunidad-valenciana-abre-nuevas-ayudas-20000-euros-autonomos-afectados-dana/20260914161820055856.html)
scale:
- CCS business claims: 16,861 shops and warehouses, 5,336 industrial, 1,076 offices; 4,685 lost-profit claims.
- AEAT aid to 16,035 autónomos and 11,431 companies.
cost_impact:
- CCS paid €1,148.5M to shops and warehouses, €928.0M to industrial risks and €40.9M to offices.
- AEAT direct aid totalled €347.5M (about €5k per autónomo and €23.4k per company; my calculation).
driver_status:
- CCS extraordinary-risk insurance: in force.
- State aid decrees: in force; their numbers were not verified.
- RDL 10/2026 tax exemption of aid: reported (single source).
solved_today: Insurers, brokers and CCS loss adjusters; gestorías for aid applications; banks for ICO loans. I found no documented complaints about these services.
software_solvable: Partly. Claim documentation and an aid-eligibility and deadline tracker are feasible; settlement speed depends on loss adjusters.
confidence: High for the data; medium for the size of the residual pain.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Catastrophes keep recurring in 2026, and each brings a claims burden
who: Businesses in areas exposed to floods and earthquakes, mostly micro and small firms.
where:
- DANA Adam (16–18 October 2026): Valencia province (Oliva 2,760 claims), Alicante 847, Almería 163, Málaga 136, Illes Balears 127.
- Granada metropolitan area: earthquakes in August 2026.
- Andalucía and Extremadura: floods in February 2026.
reality: After each event, owners must report the policy and bank details, photograph or keep damaged goods, keep repair invoices and wait for a loss adjuster. Lost profits are paid only if insured.
evidence:
- 6,528 claims by 22 October and the CCS's conditions — [CCS DANA Adam note, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.consorseguros.es/documents/10184/0/PRIMERA_NOTA_DANA_ADAM_Def.pdf/6910f08d-ae58-d3d5-4a79-f780620b21a3?t=1792654884208)
- Granada notes — [CCS news](https://www.consorseguros.es/noticias)
- RDL 5/2026 emergency line — [ICO](https://www.ico.es/web/guest/linea-avales-emergencias-andalucia-y-extremadura)
scale: 6,528 claims within four days of DANA Adam, and still rising.
cost_impact: Not yet known for 2026 events.
driver_status: CCS regime **in force**. ICO emergency line **deadline 30 November 2026**.
solved_today: Insurers and brokers; the CCS phone line 900 222 665 and website.
software_solvable: Partly. Claims documentation, guidance on which events are covered, and business-continuity checklists.
confidence: High for the facts; medium for the pain.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Underinsurance and missing business-interruption cover
who: Micro and small firms, especially in commerce and hospitality.
where: National; the evidence comes from Valencia.
reality: Firms without a policy get nothing from the CCS. Firms whose policy lacks lost-profit cover absorb the closure period themselves.
evidence:
- The CCS pays only if a policy is in force, and lost profits only if insured — [CCS, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.consorseguros.es/documents/10184/0/PRIMERA_NOTA_DANA_ADAM_Def.pdf/6910f08d-ae58-d3d5-4a79-f780620b21a3?t=1792654884208)
- 37,384 DANA claims denied as duplicates or for lack of cover; 4,685 lost-profit claims — [CCS, 30th note](https://www.consorseguros.es/documents/10184/0/TRIGESIMA_nota_informativa_DEFINITIVA.pdf/e156c23e-f3a8-a031-0c46-bbd5c9d47001?t=1780910871713)
- Munich Re: €10.7bn damage, €4.1bn insured — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Spanish_floods) (aggregator)
scale: No SME-specific statistic was found.
cost_impact: My derivation: about 60% of DANA damage was uninsured (including public assets).
driver_status: Market (voluntary insurance) and the CCS rules, in force.
solved_today: Brokers and insurers. I found no evidence on documented complaints or on price levels.
software_solvable: Partly. Coverage-gap checks and broker leads; the policy itself is still sold by insurers.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: The April 2025 blackout left business losses uncompensated
who: Hospitality, retail and industry, nationally.
where: All of mainland Spain.
reality: About 10 hours without power. Card terminals stopped working, perishable stock was lost and production stopped. No compensation channel was identified.
evidence: CEOE estimate of €1.6bn; RDL 7/2025 revoked in July 2025; ENTSO-E final report of 20 March 2026 — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Iberian_Peninsula_blackout) (single aggregator source).
scale: National.
cost_impact: €1.6bn (CEOE estimate).
driver_status: One-off grid failure. RDL 7/2025 **revoked**; no compensation scheme found.
solved_today: Firms absorbed the losses. Whether insurance applied was not verified.
software_solvable: Mostly no. Offline-payment and continuity planning help only at the margin.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Cash forecasting and seeing all bank accounts in one place
who: Micro and small (10–49) firms with several bank accounts; startups.
where: National.
reality: Cash positions are pieced together from bank apps and spreadsheets, or sent by the gestoría after the fact. Collections are unpredictable (see FIN-05).
evidence:
- Tool prices: Banktrack €59 and €119 a month — [Banktrack](https://www.banktrack.com/precios); Qonto forecasting from €9–19 a month — [Qonto](https://qonto.com/es/pricing); Agicap annual contracts priced on quote — [Agicap](https://agicap.com/es/precios/)
- Usage of Excel or gestorías: not found.
scale: Unknown.
cost_impact: €700–1,400 a year for Banktrack, at monthly list price.
driver_status: Market.
solved_today: Excel (assumed), gestorías, neobanks, Banktrack, Agicap, Embat (for mid-sized firms and above).
software_solvable: Yes, but the market is already served. Differentiation would come from predicting payment dates and linking forecasts to collection actions.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Cash crunches from tax and Social Security debts (deferrals, seizures)
who: Autónomos and micro firms. Overlaps with the tax researcher.
where: National.
reality: When collections are late, owners defer VAT or Social Security payments, run into seizures of refunds, and fall out of good standing. That then blocks subsidies and forces liquidation in the micro-enterprise procedure.
evidence:
- Social Security has eased deferrals for small debts — [AyE, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/seguridad-social/autonomos-pequenas-deudas-tienen-ahora-mas-facil-lograr-aplazamientos-seguridad-social/20261019174524056408.html)
- Seizure of tax refunds — [AyE, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/hacienda/hacienda-puede-embargar-devoluciones-impuestos-autonomos-teac-abre-via-reclamar/20261019170607056403.html)
- Forced liquidation if not up to date with tax and Social Security — [Registradores Anuario 2025](https://www.registradores.org/documents/d/guest/anuario-concursal-2025)
scale: Unknown.
cost_impact: Default surcharges and seizures (not quantified).
driver_status: General Tax Law (LGT) and Social Security collection rules, in force. The October 2026 easing is reported but not verified in the BOE.
solved_today: Gestorías.
software_solvable: Partly. Deferral-request assistants and tax-cash planning.

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing with payment-status reporting (upcoming)
who: All businesses. First those with turnover above €8M, then the rest, including autónomos. Overlaps with the invoicing researcher.
where: National.
reality: From 2027 to 2029, invoice recipients must report acceptance or rejection and the actual payment date of each invoice. Accounts-payable teams take on a new reporting task, and the government gains real data on payment dates.
evidence:
- RD 238/2026 and Orden HAC/1028/2026 (BOE 5 Oct 2026); deadlines 6 October 2027, 6 October 2028 and 6 October 2029 — [Sánchez Garrido Abogados](https://www.sanchezgarridoabogados.com/factura-electronica-obligatoria-plazos)
- Status reporting framed "para reforzar la lucha contra la morosidad" (to reinforce the fight against late payment) — [Lealtadis](https://www.lealtadis.es/factura-electronica-b2b-estados-pago-pymes/)
scale: All B2B invoice issuers and recipients.
cost_impact: The cost of adapting software and processes (not quantified).
driver_status: Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), RD 238/2026 and Orden HAC/1028/2026. **Upcoming deadlines:** 6 October 2027 (above €8M) and 6 October 2028 (rest), with status reporting required for smaller filers from 6 October 2029.
solved_today: Not yet in force. ERP and invoicing vendors are preparing.
software_solvable: Yes, and it is a data source for late-payment analytics.
confidence: High on the dates (two law-firm sources; the BOE was not read directly).

track: Cash flow, finance, insurance and insolvency
title: Proving payment-period compliance to get subsidies above €30k
who: Small and medium (50–249) companies applying for subsidies, especially those that must file a full profit-and-loss account and therefore need an auditor. Overlaps with the subsidies researcher.
where: National.
reality: To receive a subsidy above €30k, a firm must certify that it meets Ley 3/2004 payment periods. Firms that file abbreviated accounts self-certify; others need an auditor's certificate or an agreed-upon procedures report, usually within 10 working days of the provisional award.
evidence: Art. 13.3 bis of the LGS, added by Ley 18/2022 and amended by RDL 5/2023 — [BOE consolidated LGS](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2003-20977)
scale: Unknown number of applicants.
cost_impact: Auditor fees (not found). Risk of losing the subsidy.
driver_status: Ley 18/2022, art. 11 (amending the LGS). **In force since 19 October 2022.**
solved_today: Auditors and gestorías.
software_solvable: Yes. Calculating the payment-period ratio continuously from the payables ledger.

title: Valencia DANA 2024, a slow and fragmented business recovery with heavy aid paperwork
who: all sectors, especially autónomos (16,035 AEAT aid recipients), micro and small firms (11,431 company recipients), and industrial estates in l'Horta Sud and the Ribera.
where: Comunitat Valenciana, province of Valencia (metro towns south and west of València: Paiporta, Catarroja, Sedaví, Benetússer, Picanya, Algemesí and others).
reality: two years on, businesses are still dealing with several parallel aid and insurance channels (AEAT direct aid, ERTE, ICO, CDTI, Consorcio, Reinicia Auto+), each with its own forms and evidence. Some lines are still being evaluated or were rejected.
evidence:
- AEAT direct aid: 27,466 applications with a payment order and €347,518,000 paid ([La Moncloa, 19 Oct 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/info-dana/Paginas/2026/191026-datos-seguimiento-actuaciones-gobierno.aspx)).
- CDTI LIC/LICa: 70 applications, of which 31 were approved, 13 are still in evaluation and 26 were rejected (same source).
- Consorcio: 251,940 claims and €4.66bn paid (same source).
- Net employer exits in 2026Q2 in several DANA towns, e.g. Algemesí −3.50% and Benetússer −2.39%, against Valencia province +0.79% ([INE 82132](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82132), retrieved 23 Oct 2026).
- This is primarily a single official source for the aid figures; INE provides independent dynamics.
scale: 27,466 business and autónomo aid recipients; 4,169 companies with a force-majeure ERTE covering 33,642 workers; 5,295 autónomos on extraordinary cessation benefit ([La Moncloa, 19 Oct 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/info-dana/Paginas/2026/191026-datos-seguimiento-actuaciones-gobierno.aspx)).
cost_impact: average AEAT aid was about €23,400 per company and about €5,000 per autónomo. These are my calculations from €267.288M ÷ 11,431 and €80.23M ÷ 16,035 (same source). Damage totals per business were not retrieved.
driver_status: the October 2024 DANA disaster, handled through Real Decreto-ley aid packages and the Consorcio's extraordinary-risk cover. Status in October 2026: in force and still paying; 852 Consorcio claims and 13 CDTI files are still pending (same source).
solved_today: government portals (AEAT, SEPE, ICO, Consorcio); the Generalitat's own lines were not retrieved; gestorías (tax and admin agencies). No € prices captured. Overlap: the insurance and finance researcher covers claims in depth.
software_solvable: partly. Evidence capture, dossier assembly and multi-programme application tracking can be digitised; the payouts depend on the administrations.
