confidence: high for scale; medium for "recovery" inferences.

title: Repeat flood shock, the dana Adam of October 2026 (Safor and Marina Alta)
who: households, commerce, hospitality, the primary sector and autónomos in coastal tourist towns.
where: Comunitat Valenciana, 27 municipalities in Safor (Valencia province) and Marina Alta (Alicante province), plus claims in Alicante, the Balearics, Almería and Málaga.
reality: one week after the floods, businesses do not know what aid they will get. The first €23.5M package covers only households and town councils, and business aid is left to a later package with no amounts.
evidence:
- 27 municipalities declared affected, a €23.5M first package, and a second package announced for vehicles, the primary sector, commerce and hospitality ([elDiario.es, 21 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/comunitat-valenciana/gobierno-valenciano-aprueba-paquete-ayudas-23-5-millones-euros-afectados-dana-adam_1_13603195.html)).
- 6,528 Consorcio claims in 3 days, 2,760 from Oliva ([elDiario.es, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/comunitat-valenciana/consorcio-compensacion-seguros-recibe-6-500-solicitudes-indemnizacion-dana-adam_1_13605957.html)).
- Single outlet, two articles.
scale: 6,528 claims so far, with no split for businesses; 5,007 of them are in Valencia province and 847 in Alicante (same source).
cost_impact: not yet estimated, "Todavía es pronto para estimar el alcance de los daños" ("it is still too early to estimate the extent of the damage") (same source).
driver_status: an extreme-weather event. The *zona catastrófica* declaration has been announced ([elDiario.es, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/comunitat-valenciana/gobierno-declarara-zona-catastrofica-municipios-afectados-dana-adam-promete-recursos-reconstruccion_1_13600720.html)). Business aid is still to be designed as of 23 Oct 2026.
solved_today: a single online application at the Generalitat's e-office, in-person help at town halls and PROP offices, and free legal and notarial help for dealing with insurers ([elDiario.es, 21 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/comunitat-valenciana/gobierno-valenciano-aprueba-paquete-ayudas-23-5-millones-euros-afectados-dana-adam_1_13603195.html)).
software_solvable: partly. Damage inventories, photo and evidence logs, flood-alert linked continuity plans and claim trackers are digitisable; the hazard itself is not.

title: Madrid ZBE fines hit unlabelled vehicles registered outside the city, such as metro-area trades and vans
who: autónomos and micro firms in trades, delivery and services whose old, unlabelled vans and cars are registered outside Madrid city; also any driver entering the Distrito Centro and Plaza Elíptica special zones.
where: city of Madrid (Comunidad de Madrid).
reality: camera-enforced fines arrive by post for each entry. Crossing the M-30 briefly can bring two fines, about €400 ([Motorpasión](https://www.motorpasion.com/furgonetas-y-caravanas/compras-furgoneta-camper-porque-buscas-libertad-no-tiene-etiqueta-mejor-no-pasar-madrid-escapada-te-puede-costar-400-euros-multas); known only from a search-result summary, not fetched, date not captured; single source, low confidence). Vehicles registered in Madrid that pay the local circulation tax (IVTM) may keep circulating ([RACE, 10 Dec 2025](https://www.race.es/etiqueta-b-madrid)).
evidence:
- H1 2025: 261,115 fines and €52,223,000 for entering a ZBE without a label, against 134,113 fines in H1 2024 (+94.6%).
- Distrito Centro ZBEDEP: 208,942 fines and €41.8M. Plaza Elíptica: 32,615 fines and €6.5M.
- Total from improper ZBE access: €100,534,400 ([Híbridos y Eléctricos, 11 Nov 2025](https://www.hibridosyelectricos.com/coches/191347190-en-multas-madrid-logra-record-historico-en-espana-por-acceso-sin-etiqueta-zbe_83375_102.html), citing the drivers' association AEA; single source for the counts).
- Fine of €200, or €100 if paid promptly ([RACE, 10 Dec 2025](https://www.race.es/etiqueta-b-madrid)).
scale: 261,115 unlabelled-access fines in six months (above). The split between business and private vehicles is unknown.
cost_impact: €200 per infraction; €52.2M for unlabelled access in H1 2025 (above).
driver_status: the Ordenanza de Movilidad Sostenible (Madrid 360), under Ley 7/2021 (art. 14) and RD 1052/2022. In force; since 2025 it restricts unlabelled vehicles not registered in Madrid ([RACE, 10 Dec 2025](https://www.race.es/etiqueta-b-madrid)). No label-B ban has been announced. I could not verify this against the official Madrid site (flag).
solved_today: the DGT label lookup, renewing the vehicle, parking in public car parks for the Centro zone, and authorisation lists for workers in the zone (RACE). No € prices for tools were captured. Complaint: AEA contrasts the €200 fine in Madrid with €68 in Paris (Híbridos y Eléctricos, above).
software_solvable: partly. Per-vehicle compliance checks before routing a job, fine monitoring and appeal workflows, and fleet-renewal TCO comparisons.

title: Barcelona ZBE Rondes, with van bans, day-pass rationing and stop-start enforcement
who: trades, delivery and light-transport autónomos and micro firms with unlabelled N1 vans (diesel before Euro 4, petrol before Euro 3).
where: the ZBE Rondes de Barcelona, covering Barcelona, L'Hospitalet, Sant Adrià and parts of Esplugues and Cornellà (Catalonia).
reality: unlabelled vans cannot drive on weekdays from 7:00 to 20:00 unless the owner registers one of 24 day-passes a year in the AMB registry. Rules changed suddenly when the Generalitat asked towns to suspend restrictions during the January 2026 rail crisis and then restored them on 16 March 2026.
evidence:
- Vans (N1) restricted since 1 April 2021; up to 24 day-passes a year; label B currently free to drive ([zbe.barcelona, vehicles page](https://www.zbe.barcelona/zones-baixes-emissions/vehicles-afectats.html), undated official page).
- Suspension via Resolució TER/194/2026 of 27 Jan 2026 (DOGC 9592, 28 Jan 2026) and restoration of normal enforcement ([Generalitat communication, Mar 2026](https://docs.amb.cat/alfresco/api/-default-/public/alfresco/versions/1/nodes/9af54c92-86a1-4dde-842f-1baaf76d5d32/content/20260311_activa_ZBE_dcr.pdf?attachment=false&mimeType=application/pdf&sizeInBytes=219623); [zbe.barcelona home](https://www.zbe.barcelona/)).
- Label B restriction in Catalonia from 2028, following a Govern recommendation ([Motor16, 23 Sep 2026](https://www.motor16.com/las-ultimas-noticias/zonas-bajas-emisiones-flotas)). The official ZBE page lists no future label-B restriction (conflict noted).
scale: no current count of affected vans was found; a 2019 figure from a search snippet is outdated and not used.
cost_impact: fines not retrieved from the official page; nationally the infraction is classed as serious at €200 ([elDiario.es, 29 May 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/motor/ciudades-obligatorio-distintivo-ambiental-pm_1_13259160.html)).
driver_status: municipal ZBE ordinances, the Decret 132/2024 air-quality plan (horizon 2027), Ley 7/2021 and RD 1052/2022. In force again since 16 Mar 2026. The label-B step in 2028 is a plan, not yet law (flag).
solved_today: the AMB ZBE registry (zberegistre.ambmobilitat.cat) for day-passes and exemptions; the T-verda free transport card for people who scrap a vehicle; P+R car parks (zbe.barcelona). No € prices captured.
software_solvable: yes for the admin side (day-pass budgeting across vehicles, registry automation, alerts for pollution episodes and suspensions); no for the cost of renewing vehicles.
confidence: high for current rules (official); medium for the 2028 horizon.

title: Housing costs undermine staff recruitment and retention in tourist, island and high-rent cities
who: hospitality, retail, construction and care employers (micro to medium), mostly in F&B-heavy provinces.
where: Canary Islands (Las Palmas, Santa Cruz), Balearics (Palma), Málaga, the Basque Country, Madrid; national.
reality: employers report vacancies they cannot fill. Unions call strikes over housing and wages, and young workers spend most of their income on rent. Hospitality and construction are the sectors most affected by shortages.
evidence:
- EBAE 2026Q2: labour shortages affect 57.8% of hospitality firms and 58.7% of construction firms ([BdE, 18 Jun 2026](https://www.bde.es/f/webbe/GAP/Secciones/SalaPrensa/NotasInformativas/26/presbe2026-52.pdf)). BdE Q3 2026: about 60% of construction firms, above 50% since mid-2023 ([BdE, 9 Oct 2026](https://www.bde.es/wbe/en/publicaciones/analisis-economico-investigacion/proyecciones-macro-informe-trimestral/proyecciones-e-informe-trimestral-de-la-economia-espanola-tercer-trimestre-2026.html)).
- Canary Islands general strike for housing ([Canarias Ahora](https://www.eldiario.es/canariasahora/sociedad/ugt-ccoo-canarios-huelga-general-vivienda-mejores-salarios_1_13606867.html), headline) and zero protected homes started in H1 2026 ([Canarias Ahora](https://www.eldiario.es/canariasahora/politica/sola-vivienda-protegida-inicio-canarias-primer-semestre-2026_1_13606562.html), headline).
- Young Basque rent-aid applicants pay €9,289 on an income of €15,205 ([elDiario.es](https://www.eldiario.es/euskadi/jovenes-vascos-piden-ayudas-alquiler-cobran-media-15-204-81-euros-anuales-pagan-renta-9-288-96_1_13589105.html), headline).
- Málaga protected-rental income band of €23,300–24,418 criticised ([elDiario.es, 7 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/andalucia/malaga/corto-margen-alquilar-nuevas-vpo-malaga-minimo-23-300-euros-tope-24-418-reirse-cara_1_13575766.html)).
scale: 43.1% of firms nationally report labour shortages ([BdE, 9 Oct 2026](https://www.bde.es/wbe/en/publicaciones/analisis-economico-investigacion/proyecciones-macro-informe-trimestral/proyecciones-e-informe-trimestral-de-la-economia-espanola-tercer-trimestre-2026.html)). The link to housing is partly inferred.
cost_impact: not quantified per business in the sources found.
driver_status: a market force (housing deficit, tourism demand). State and regional housing laws belong to other researchers' scope. Ongoing.
solved_today: not researched here (see the labour/HR and hospitality researchers). No € prices captured.
software_solvable: partly. Recruiting, scheduling and staff-housing matching tools can ease the operational side, but not the shortage of homes.
confidence: medium. Labour shortage is high-confidence; the housing causality comes from headlines and inference.

title: Extreme seasonality in the Balearics, with large swings in the business register
who: hospitality, retail, construction and transport employers and autónomos (micro and small).
where: Illes Balears (Palma, and Ibiza per the press).
reality: firms register employees and autónomos en masse for the season and deregister in autumn. Cash flow, hiring and permits are compressed into a few months. A weak August (per an op-ed) hits the whole year.
evidence:
- Balearic employer-unit net growth of +6.2% in Q1 2026 and +11.56% in Q2, against national +0.69% and +1.49%. Autónomos +1.48% and +5.3% against +0.11% and +0.92% ([INE 82131](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82131); [INE 82138](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82138), retrieved 23 Oct 2026).
- Palma employer units +2.13% and +3.82% ([INE 82132](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82132)).
- Short-term survival of young employer units in the Balearics is 84.8%, below the national 85.59% ([INE 82128](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82128)).
- Op-ed on a poor August ([Última Hora, 16 Oct 2026](https://www.ultimahora.es/noticias/economico/2026/10/16/2729127/turismo-vive-uno-peores-agostos-historia.html)).
scale: 43,559 employer units and 105,235 autónomos in the Balearics at 2026Q2 ([INE 82131](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82131); [INE 82138](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82138)).
cost_impact: not quantified in the sources found.
driver_status: a market force (tourism seasonality). Ongoing.
solved_today: not researched. No € prices captured.
software_solvable: partly. Seasonal workforce planning, rehiring of *fijos discontinuos* (permanent seasonal staff), and season-based cash-flow forecasting.
confidence: high for the seasonality data; low for the impact of the "bad August".

title: Insularity freight and fuel surcharges plus the de minimis aid cap (Balearics, by analogy the Canaries)
who: hauliers, wholesalers, retail and construction suppliers, and industrial SMEs on the islands.
where: Illes Balears (Menorca, Mallorca). The Canaries have an analogous structural issue, but no 2026 figures were captured.
reality: shipping lines raise the BAF (bunker adjustment factor) mid-contract, so hauliers and their clients must pass on 20–25% increases quickly. Firms juggling several aid lines hit the €300,000 de minimis ceiling and postpone investment.
evidence:
- Diesel up more than 33% since the conflict began (to 30 Sep 2026); trailer rates about €200 higher, or +20–25%; fuel up to 30% of haulier costs ([Última Hora, 23 Oct 2026](https://www.ultimahora.es/noticias/economico/2026/10/23/2734153/joaquin-bisbal-encarecimiento-del-transporte-problema.html)).
- The de minimis cap of €300,000 per company over three years limits investment ([Última Hora, 23 Oct 2026](https://www.ultimahora.es/noticias/economico/2026/10/23/2733963/insularidad-deberia-penalizar-nuestras-empresas.html), opinion).
- Energy costs limit activity for 63.2% of firms nationally ([BdE, 9 Oct 2026](https://www.bde.es/wbe/en/publicaciones/analisis-economico-investigacion/proyecciones-macro-informe-trimestral/proyecciones-e-informe-trimestral-de-la-economia-espanola-tercer-trimestre-2026.html)), an independent corroboration of the fuel shock.
scale: not quantified for the islands.
cost_impact: about €200 more per trailer per crossing (above).
driver_status: a market force (the 2026 Iran conflict and oil prices). EU de minimis regulation in force; the Balearic special regime (REB) applies.
solved_today: the cost is passed on to clients; there are calls to relax de minimis (Última Hora). No tools or prices captured.
software_solvable: partly. Automatic surcharge pass-through in quotes and invoices, freight-cost tracking and de minimis aid-ceiling tracking.
confidence: medium (one trade association plus one opinion piece; macro corroboration).

title: Zaragoza and Aragón data-centre boom, with competition for grid capacity and local fiscal tension
who: industrial and logistics SMEs needing new or larger grid connections; municipalities; possibly local labour and housing markets (not evidenced).
where: Aragón (Calatorao, San Mateo de Gállego, the AWS sites), the Zaragoza metro area; national grid.
reality: large data-centre access requests reserve node capacity and stop nearby demand from connecting. Policy keeps shifting: a draft decree, a CNMC report, opposition from the regional government, and elections.
evidence:
- About 1,600 MW of permits renounced by data centres (CNMC); more than 1,000 MW of transmission and 1,700 MW of distribution capacity freed by anti-hoarding measures; current requirements "drenan capacidad" in shared nodes and prevent other demand from connecting nearby ([elDiario.es, 17 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/economia/gobierno-mira-irlanda-medidas-significativo-riesgo-apagones-culpa-centros-datos_1_13584339.html)).
- The draft decree would require data centres of 1 MW or more to cover 80% of consumption hour by hour with new renewables; the sector says €9bn of investment is at risk (same source).
- Blackstone's Calatorao campus approved ([elDiario.es, 30 Sep 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/aragon/sociedad/luz-verde-obras-campus-centros-datos-blackstone-calatorao-mayores-espana_1_13548934.html)).
- No SME-specific connection denials were found (single outlet).
scale: unknown for SMEs.
cost_impact: unknown for SMEs.
driver_status: the data-centre decree is a **draft**; it may not be approved before the 29 Nov 2026 elections (same source). Grid access rules are set by the CNMC.
solved_today: not researched.
software_solvable: partly or no. Grid-capacity information exists from network operators (not verified here); the bottleneck is physical and regulatory.

title: Zaragoza's municipal SME aid was mis-executed and then cut (city-level subsidy administration)
who: micro firms and autónomos in retail, services and hospitality applying for municipal digitalisation and Verifactu-equipment grants.
where: city of Zaragoza (Aragón).
reality: applicants to the 2025 call waited while the call was returned twice for processing failures. The 2026 call is 60% smaller, with a 20-day application window.
evidence: - 2025 call of €1M "returned twice" by Intervención (the internal auditor); 2026 call of €400,000, of which €325,000 is for competitiveness and €75,000 for Verifactu-compliant tills and e-invoicing; 20 calendar days to apply ([elDiario.es, 29 Jul 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/aragon/economia/gobierno-zaragoza-rebaja-60-ayudas-pymes-autonomos-fiasco-anterior-convocatoria_1_13414648.html)). Single source.
scale: not stated.
cost_impact: €600,000 less aid (above).
driver_status: municipal grant ordinances. The 2026 call was being published around August 2026. Note that Verifactu itself has been postponed to October 2028 ([elDiario.es, 5–6 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/economia/gobierno-retrasa-entrada-vigor-verifactu-octubre-2028_1_13562620.html)).
solved_today: online application at the city council. Overlap with the subsidies researcher.
software_solvable: partly (grant-discovery and application tools for micro firms; grant-management tools for councils).

title: Bilbao and Bizkaia, a stagnating business base and industrial distress
who: industrial suppliers (steel, tubes), their subcontractors, and retail autónomos (21.1% of Bizkaia's autónomos are in retail).
where: Bizkaia, País Vasco (Bilbao, Sestao, the Margen Izquierda industrial belt).
reality: the number of companies is flat to falling and autónomo exits exceed entries. Large industrial employers are laying staff off or need rescue, which squeezes local suppliers.
evidence:
- DIRCE companies 71,086 at 1-1-2025 against 71,204 a year earlier (−0.2%), the only decline among the 15 provinces studied ([INE 73022](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=73022)).
- Autónomos net growth −0.24% in 2026Q2, against national +0.92% ([INE 82138](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82138)).
- Bilbao city employer units −0.25% in Q1 2026 ([INE 82132](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82132)).
- Vicinay to cut about 60 jobs; Tubos Reunidos with only the October payroll guaranteed ([elDiario.es](https://www.eldiario.es/euskadi/rescatada-vicinay-plantea-despedir-60-personas-mitad-plantilla-erte-julio-resto_1_13606403.html); [elDiario.es](https://www.eldiario.es/euskadi/interesados-salvar-tubos-reunidos-reuniran-sindicatos-plantilla-fija-nomina-octubre_1_13604355.html), headlines, Oct 2026).
scale: 78,602 autónomos and 26,385 employer units in Bizkaia ([INE 82131](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82131); [INE 82138](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82138)).
cost_impact: not quantified.
driver_status: market forces (industrial restructuring, energy costs). Basque fiscal specifics (TicketBAI/Batuz) are out of scope.
solved_today: not researched.
software_solvable: no (structural and macro); at most partly, through customer diversification and B2B marketplaces for suppliers.
confidence: high for the demographic data; low for the causal story.

title: Weak or negative net business formation in Valladolid, Sevilla, Murcia, Las Palmas and Vigo
who: employer micro firms and autónomos across sectors.
where: Valladolid (Castilla y León), Sevilla (Andalucía), Murcia (Región de Murcia), Las Palmas de G.C. (Canarias), Vigo (Galicia).
reality: in 2026, more employer units closed than opened in these cities in at least one quarter, at a time when the national register grew.
evidence:
- Valladolid −0.94% (−0.05% in Q1).
- Sevilla −0.65%.
- Murcia −0.60%; Murcia autónomos −1.07%.
- Las Palmas −0.58% in Q1 and −0.08% in Q2.
- Vigo −0.43% in Q1 and −0.07% in Q2.
- Sources: [INE 82132](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82132) and [INE 82139](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82139), retrieved 23 Oct 2026; single official source, two quarters only.
scale: see the provincial stocks in Table A.
cost_impact: not quantified.
driver_status: market forces; drivers not established.
solved_today: n/a.
software_solvable: no (diagnostic indicator, not a pain in itself).

title: ZBE patchwork across municipalities, with divergent calendars, exemptions and litigation (multi-city van fleets)
who: trades (plumbers, electricians, builders), delivery and last-mile firms, sales reps, mobile services; autónomos and micro to medium fleets.
where: national; the 68 municipalities with an active ZBE, of 149 obliged. The key cases are Madrid, Barcelona metro, Málaga, Bilbao, Valencia, Vigo, Palma, Valladolid and Santa Cruz.
reality: before taking a job in another city, a van owner has to work out whether their label is allowed there, at that hour, with which exemption or pass. The rules change with court rulings (Málaga, Guadalajara), suspensions (Catalonia, January–March 2026) and phase dates (Málaga label B on 30 Nov 2026, Vigo and Palma label B in 2027, Catalonia label B in 2028).
evidence:
- 68 active out of 149 obliged ([Motor16, 26 Sep 2026](https://www.motor16.com/las-ultimas-noticias/zonas-bajas-emisiones-68-ciudades/)).
- Professional and loading exemptions are not detailed in all municipalities ([Motor16, 23 Sep 2026](https://www.motor16.com/las-ultimas-noticias/zonas-bajas-emisiones-flotas)).
- TSJA annulment in Málaga ([elDiario.es, 11 Jun 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/andalucia/malaga/justicia-rechaza-malaga-multe-vehiculos-fuera-circular-zona-bajas-emisiones_1_13295489.html)).
- Catalan suspension ([Generalitat, Mar 2026](https://docs.amb.cat/alfresco/api/-default-/public/alfresco/versions/1/nodes/9af54c92-86a1-4dde-842f-1baaf76d5d32/content/20260311_activa_ZBE_dcr.pdf?attachment=false&mimeType=application/pdf&sizeInBytes=219623)).
- Valencia exempts economic-activity vehicles ([valencia.es, 21 Oct 2025](https://www.valencia.es/cas/actualidad/-/content/val%C3%A8ncia-aprueba-la-ordenanza-de-zona-de-bajas-emisiones)).
- Madrid's fine volume ([Híbridos y Eléctricos, 11 Nov 2025](https://www.hibridosyelectricos.com/coches/191347190-en-multas-madrid-logra-record-historico-en-espana-por-acceso-sin-etiqueta-zbe_83375_102.html)).
- Multiple independent sources.
scale: 19.5 million label-B and label-C vehicles potentially affected ([Motor16, 23 Sep 2026](https://www.motor16.com/las-ultimas-noticias/zonas-bajas-emisiones-flotas)); 261,115 unlabelled-access fines in Madrid in H1 2025 (above). The number of commercial vehicles is unknown.
cost_impact: €200 per infraction (€100 if paid promptly) ([elDiario.es, 29 May 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/motor/ciudades-obligatorio-distintivo-ambiental-pm_1_13259160.html); [RACE](https://www.race.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones)); van renewal costs not captured.
driver_status: Ley 7/2021 art. 14, RD 1052/2022 and each municipal ordinance. As of October 2026 the status is mixed: in force in Madrid, Barcelona, Málaga, Bilbao and Valencia; information phase in Santa Cruz (18 months) and Vigo (one year); postponed in Zaragoza (2030) and Cuenca (2028); annulled in Guadalajara and partly in Málaga; upcoming steps in Málaga (30 Nov 2026, uncertain), Palma and Vigo (2027) and Catalonia (2028).
solved_today: municipal registries (AMB ZBE registry, free), the DGT label lookup, RACE and Motor16 explainers, and advice to "consultar cada ordenanza local" ("check each local ordinance") (Motor16). No € prices captured; the fleet-software market belongs to the transport researcher.
software_solvable: yes. A maintained ZBE rules database or API with per-vehicle route checks, pass and quota budgeting, change alerts and fine tracking. The renewal cost is not software-solvable.
confidence: high that the patchwork exists; medium on individual city dates.

title: Municipal waste-fee rollout (Ley 7/2022), a new charge followed by court annulments, refunds and appeal windows
who: all premises holders (shops, bars, offices, workshops) and landlords; all sizes, though most of the evidence is about households.
where: national; documented in Madrid, Las Palmas de G.C., Vélez-Málaga (Málaga) and Bétera (Valencia).
reality: a new or redesigned local fee appears on the tax calendar. When it is annulled, payers must file appeals or wait for refunds. In Madrid the 2025 fee is still before the Supreme Court while the 2026 fee is already being charged.
evidence:
- The legal duty in art. 11.3 ([BOE](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2022-5809)).
- Madrid: TSJM annulment, Supreme Court appeal, about 130,000 appeals in 2025 and a 1–30 December appeal window for the 2026 fee ([elDiario.es, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/madrid/somos/almeida-debe-pasta-psoe-lanza-campana-recurrir-tasa-basuras-madrid_1_13599033.html)).
- Las Palmas: TSJC annulment and refunds from October 2026 ([elDiario.es, 13 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/canariasahora/sociedad/tasa-basura-las-palmas-gran-canaria-inicia-devolucion-importes_1_13582838.html)).
- Vélez-Málaga resignation ([elDiario.es, 14 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/andalucia/malaga/dimite-alcalde-velez-malaga-polemica-politica-vecinal-desatada-nueva-tasa-municipal-basura_1_13584080.html)).
- Bétera claims ([elDiario.es, 11 Aug 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/comunitat-valenciana/comarcas/campana-reclamaciones-vecinales-exige-restitucion-inmediata-cobros-ilegales-tasa-residuos-betera_1_13439808.html)).
- Single outlet, several independent cases.
scale: every municipality is obliged (BOE); 130,000 appeals in Madrid in 2025 (above). The number of businesses affected is unknown.
cost_impact: amounts not found (gap).
driver_status: Ley 7/2022 art. 11.3, deadline 10 Apr 2025. In force; municipal ordinances are being litigated (Madrid before the Supreme Court; Las Palmas final and refunding).
solved_today: appeals to the municipal economic-administrative court (TEAM) in Madrid, using free templates from political campaigns (Más Madrid, PSOE); refunds in Las Palmas (above). No € prices for professional services captured.
software_solvable: partly. Local-tax calendars, notification capture, appeal and refund automation, and cost allocation between landlord and tenant.

title: Energy and input-cost shock from the 2026 Iran war
who: all sizes, worst in agriculture, transport, industry and energy, trade and hospitality; autónomos included.
where: national; amplified on the islands (CITY-07).
reality: suppliers, fuel and shipping raise prices repeatedly. Firms must decide whether to pass costs on (68.9% of autónomos raised prices) or absorb them (27.3%), often without contract clauses that allow it.
evidence:
- Energy is a limiting factor for 63.2% of firms in 2026Q3, up from 42% in Q1 ([BdE, 9 Oct 2026](https://www.bde.es/wbe/en/publicaciones/analisis-economico-investigacion/proyecciones-macro-informe-trimestral/proyecciones-e-informe-trimestral-de-la-economia-espanola-tercer-trimestre-2026.html); [BdE, 18 Jun 2026](https://www.bde.es/f/webbe/GAP/Secciones/SalaPrensa/NotasInformativas/26/presbe2026-52.pdf)).
- 81.1% of autónomos saw costs rise ([Bolsamanía/ATA, 13 Apr 2026](https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/economia/economia--solo-el-56-de-los-autonomos-considera-suficientes-las-medidas-adoptadas-por-la-guerra-de-iran-segun-ata--22277520.html)).
- Diesel up more than 33% ([Última Hora, 23 Oct 2026](https://www.ultimahora.es/noticias/economico/2026/10/23/2734153/joaquin-bisbal-encarecimiento-del-transporte-problema.html)).
- Three independent sources.
scale: 63% of firms (EBAE) and 81% of autónomos (ATA).
cost_impact: 23.9% of autónomos with rising costs report increases above 16% (ATA). Freight is up 20–25% for the islands.
driver_status: a geopolitical market force. Government relief measures exist but are judged insufficient by 45.2% of autónomos (ATA). Ongoing as of October 2026.
solved_today: price increases, absorbing costs, government measures. No tools or prices captured.
software_solvable: partly. Energy-tariff monitoring and switching, automatic cost pass-through in quotes and price lists, and margin alerts.

title: Policy and regulatory uncertainty, with "regulation" rising as a top problem
who: all SMEs and autónomos, especially those planning investment and hiring.
where: national.
reality: the rules keep moving. Verifactu dates have shifted, the 2027 autónomo contribution reform has stalled, the data-centre decree is a draft, and the Cortes are dissolved before the 29 Nov 2026 elections. Firms delay decisions and struggle to keep compliance calendars current.
evidence:
- Policy uncertainty limits 57.6% of firms in Q3 2026 (62% in Q2) ([BdE, 9 Oct 2026](https://www.bde.es/wbe/en/publicaciones/analisis-economico-investigacion/proyecciones-macro-informe-trimestral/proyecciones-e-informe-trimestral-de-la-economia-espanola-tercer-trimestre-2026.html)).
- Regulation as Spanish SMEs' most pressing problem rose from 10.9% in 2023-H1 to 14.9% in 2025-H2, against 13.6% in the euro area ([ECB SAFE data](https://data.ecb.europa.eu/data/datasets/SAFE/SAFE.H.ES.SME.A.0.0.0.Q0.ZZZZ.P3.AL.WP)).
- 87.4% of autónomos say instability hurts them ([Bolsamanía/ATA, 13 Apr 2026](https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/economia/economia--solo-el-56-de-los-autonomos-considera-suficientes-las-medidas-adoptadas-por-la-guerra-de-iran-segun-ata--22277520.html)).
- Verifactu moved to October 2028 ([elDiario.es, 5–6 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/economia/gobierno-retrasa-entrada-vigor-verifactu-octubre-2028_1_13562620.html)).
scale: majority of firms (EBAE).
cost_impact: uncertainty hurts investment at 40.9% of firms (BdE Q3 2026).
driver_status: the political cycle and EU convergence (ViDA). Elections on 29 Nov 2026.
solved_today: gestorías and asesorías (tax and admin advisers), associations' alerts. No prices captured.
software_solvable: partly. Personalised regulatory-change alerts and compliance calendars; the uncertainty itself is not solvable.

title: Labour and skills shortage, concentrated in construction, hospitality and agriculture
who: construction (58.7–60% of firms), hospitality (57.8%), agriculture (47.5%); SMEs and autónomos who hire.
where: national; most acute in tourist and island provinces (inference, see CITY-05).
reality: vacancies stay open, jobs take longer, firms turn work down. 17.9% of hiring autónomos could not hire at all.
evidence:
- 43.1% of firms limited by labour shortages in Q3 2026; construction about 60% ([BdE, 9 Oct 2026](https://www.bde.es/wbe/en/publicaciones/analisis-economico-investigacion/proyecciones-macro-informe-trimestral/proyecciones-e-informe-trimestral-de-la-economia-espanola-tercer-trimestre-2026.html)).
- Sector rates for Q2 ([BdE, 18 Jun 2026](https://www.bde.es/f/webbe/GAP/Secciones/SalaPrensa/NotasInformativas/26/presbe2026-52.pdf)).
- SAFE: skilled staff is the top problem for Spanish SMEs at 25.0% in 2025-H2 ([ECB SAFE data](https://data.ecb.europa.eu/data/datasets/SAFE/SAFE.H.ES.SME.A.0.0.0.Q0.ZZZZ.P3.AL.WP)).
- 29.8% of hiring autónomos had difficulty ([Bolsamanía/ATA, 13 Apr 2026](https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/economia/economia--solo-el-56-de-los-autonomos-considera-suficientes-las-medidas-adoptadas-por-la-guerra-de-iran-segun-ata--22277520.html)).
- CEPYME: "dificultades para cubrir las vacantes" ("difficulty filling vacancies") ([CEPYME, 5 Jan 2026](https://cepyme.es/storage/2026/01/NdP-CEPYME-alerta-de-los-riesgos-de-los-nuevos-incrementos-de-costes-laborales-para-la-evolucion-del-empleo-en-las-pymes.pdf)).
scale: about 43% of firms; 25% of SMEs rank it first.
cost_impact: not quantified.
driver_status: demographics, housing and skills mismatch (market force). Ongoing.
solved_today: overlap with the labour/HR researcher; no prices captured.
software_solvable: partly (recruiting reach, scheduling and retention tools; does not create workers).

title: Rising cost of credit and tighter access to finance, with SMEs more exposed to interest costs
who: SMEs with variable-rate or short-term debt; investing firms.
where: national.
reality: interest bills rise and banks tighten conditions. SMEs report a "somewhat greater impact" from borrowing costs.
evidence:
- Access to finance limits 18.2% of firms (+5.4 pp) and borrowing costs 26.8% (+2.5 pp) in Q3 2026 ([BdE, 9 Oct 2026](https://www.bde.es/wbe/en/publicaciones/analisis-economico-investigacion/proyecciones-macro-informe-trimestral/proyecciones-e-informe-trimestral-de-la-economia-espanola-tercer-trimestre-2026.html)).
- SMEs 15.4% against large firms 9.7% on financing in 2025Q4 ([Forbes España, 23 Dec 2025](https://forbes.es/economia/849872/empresas-espanolas-preven-un-alza-de-facturacion-en-la-recta-final-del-ano-tras-retroceso-del-tercer-trimestre/)).
- SAFE: access to finance is the most pressing problem for only 5.0% of SMEs ([ECB SAFE data](https://data.ecb.europa.eu/data/datasets/SAFE/SAFE.H.ES.SME.A.0.0.0.Q0.ZZZZ.P3.AL.WP)).
- Only 3% of autónomo credit applications were refused ([Bolsamanía/ATA, 13 Apr 2026](https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/economia/economia--solo-el-56-de-los-autonomos-considera-suficientes-las-medidas-adoptadas-por-la-guerra-de-iran-segun-ata--22277520.html)).
scale: 18–27% of firms.
cost_impact: not quantified.
driver_status: tightening financial conditions (market force). Overlap with the finance researcher.
solved_today: bank and ICO lines (finance researcher).
software_solvable: partly (cash-flow forecasting, financing comparison).
confidence: high (survey); medium on severity, since it remains a minority concern.

title: Late payment affects 38% of autónomos (brief; covered in depth by the finance researcher)
who: autónomos and micro firms selling to businesses and public bodies.
where: national.
reality: invoices are paid late, mostly by private clients.
evidence: 38.3% affected (private only 19.6%, both 10.4%, public only 8.3%) ([Bolsamanía/ATA, 13 Apr 2026](https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/economia/economia--solo-el-56-de-los-autonomos-considera-suficientes-las-medidas-adoptadas-por-la-guerra-de-iran-segun-ata--22277520.html)). Single source here; the finance researcher has more.
scale: about 38% of autónomos.
cost_impact: not quantified here.
driver_status: the late-payment law (Ley 3/2004 as amended) is in force; see the finance researcher.
solved_today: see the finance researcher.
software_solvable: yes (dunning, receivables tracking, e-invoicing status), within the limits of client power.

title: Administrative time sink for autónomos (brief; overlaps the bureaucracy and tax researchers)
who: autónomos and micro firms.
where: national; quantified for Asturias.
reality: hours each week go on paperwork (tax, Social Security, the working-time register, new rules), outside billable work.
evidence:
- 226 hours a year per autónomo, worth €3,390, and 40.7% name bureaucracy as the top priority to fix ([elDiario.es, 14 Aug 2026](https://www.eldiario.es/asturias/carga-burocratica-70-559-autonomos-asturiano-226-horas-trabajo-ano-239-millones-euros-tramites_1_13446790.html), ATA Asturias, methodology not disclosed).
- €10bn a year in bureaucracy costs for autónomos (ATA's Amor in [CEOE/CEPYME, 16 Jun 2026](https://cepyme.es/storage/2026/06/260616-NP-CEOE_Encuentro-Empresarial-Absentismo.pdf)).
- SAFE "regulation" rising (CITY-15).
- Partly two sources, both from ATA.
scale: about 3.19 million autónomos nationally ([INE 82138](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82138)).
cost_impact: about €3,390 per autónomo a year (ATA Asturias estimate).
driver_status: an accumulation of rules (tax, labour, EU AI Act, working-time register); see the other researchers.
solved_today: gestorías; see the software-market researcher.
software_solvable: yes, partly (automation and consolidation of filings).

title: Absenteeism cost through temporary sick leave (IT), as reported by employer bodies (brief; overlaps the labour researcher)
who: employers of all sizes; CEPYME says SMEs are hit harder proportionally.
where: national.
reality: unplanned absences disrupt small teams that have no cover.
evidence: €33bn total cost in 2025, €17bn borne by companies, 1.4 million people absent all year ([CEOE/CEPYME, 16 Jun 2026](https://cepyme.es/storage/2026/06/260616-NP-CEOE_Encuentro-Empresarial-Absentismo.pdf)). Single source (employer lobby).
scale: national.
cost_impact: €17bn borne by companies (above).
driver_status: the temporary incapacity (IT) rules; reform demanded; see the labour researcher.
solved_today: see the labour researcher.
software_solvable: partly (absence tracking, cover scheduling).

title: Fragile young micro-employers and a falling number of employers and individual entrepreneurs
who: micro employers with 1–5 employees up to 5 years old; autónomos under 30.
where: national; worst survival in Extremadura, Navarra, Castilla-La Mancha, the Balearics and Comunitat Valenciana.
reality: about one in six young micro-employers disappears from the employer register within six months. The number of employers and individual entrepreneurs is shrinking even as total employment grows.
evidence:
- 83.36% two-quarter survival for young units with 1–5 employees, against 97.6% for units with 10–99 ([INE 82128](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82128)).
- 85.54% for autónomos under 30 ([INE 82135](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82135)).
- Employers −2.9% y/y and individual entrepreneurs −4.0% y/y in Q2 2026 ([CEPYME, 28 Jul 2026](https://cepyme.es/storage/2026/07/NdP-CEPYME-valora-el-compromiso-de-las-empresas-con-el-empleo-y-recuerda-la-necesidad-de-impulsar-la-actividad-de-las-pymes.pdf)).
- GEM closure or transfer rate 3.7% ([Emprendedores, 4 Jun 2026](https://emprendedores.es/actualidad/informe-gem-2025-2026/)).
scale: 415,649 employer units up to 5 years old at 1 Jan 2026 ([INE 82128](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=82128)).
cost_impact: not quantified.
driver_status: costs, the minimum wage and labour costs, demand (per CEPYME). Market and regulatory mix.
solved_today: n/a.
software_solvable: partly (early-warning cash, margin and pricing tools; the drivers themselves are macro).
confidence:
high for the data; medium for interpretation (deregistration is not always closure).
---

title: The micro-firm digital gap: 36% have a website, 12% sell online, 21% use AI
who: micro firms and autónomos with fewer than 10 employees, especially retail, hospitality and personal services.
where: national; the regional gap is in CITY-23.
reality: most micro firms run without a website, online sales or back-office software, and depend on social media and walk-in trade.
evidence: website 36.2%, social media 32.1%, AI 21.4%, e-commerce sales 11.8% ([INE, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/Prensa/ETICCE20251T2026.htm)). The prior year was 37.0%, 37.8%, 13.4% and 8.6% ([INE, 22 Oct 2025](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/Prensa/ETICCE20241T2025.htm)). Two INE editions.
scale: about 3.15 million companies have fewer than 10 employees: 1,800,443 with none plus 1,348,909 with 1–9 ([INE 73022](https://www.ine.es/jaxiT3/Tabla.htm?t=73022)).
cost_impact: lost online sales not quantified.
driver_status: market force (capacity, cost, skills). Public programmes such as Kit Digital belong to other researchers' scope.
solved_today: see the software-market researcher; no prices captured here.
software_solvable: yes (simple web, booking, e-commerce and AI-assistant bundles), with adoption being the bottleneck.

title: Regional laggards on CRM and ERP (Castilla-La Mancha, Murcia, Canarias, Baleares, Andalucía)
who: firms with 10+ employees in lagging regions.
where: Castilla-La Mancha (CRM 25.0%), Murcia (CRM 27.4%, AI 24.6%), Canarias (ERP 49.4%), Baleares (ERP 47.3%), Andalucía (ERP 53.5%), against Madrid (CRM 41.4%) and Cataluña (ERP 68.2%).
reality: back-office processes such as stock, invoicing and customer follow-up stay manual or in spreadsheets more often outside Madrid and Cataluña.
evidence: regional table above ([INE, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/Prensa/es/ETICCE20251T2026.pdf)). Single official source.
scale: not quantified per region in counts.
cost_impact: not quantified.
driver_status: market force.
solved_today: see the software-market researcher.
software_solvable: yes (sector-specific, low-cost ERP and CRM localised for island and seasonal businesses).
confidence:
high for the gap; medium for its business impact.
---

title: Skilled-labour shortage and ageing site workforce
who: Construction firms of every size, but mainly micro (<10) and small (10–49) builders and renovation contractors. Also trades: bricklayers, formworkers, site foremen, crane operators.
where: National. The sources give no regional breakdown.
reality: Firms cannot staff sites, especially with site foremen (*encargados*) and bricklayers (*albañiles*). The workforce is older and increasingly foreign, and few young people come in. The CNC presents this as a brake on housing delivery.
evidence:
- The CNC says about 700,000 workers are missing to build the housing that PSOE and PP proposed. It blames an ageing workforce and lower qualifications among new entrants, and asks for vocational-training (FP) reform and for immigrants to be regularised or recruited — [merca2, 20 Jan 2025](https://www.merca2.es/2025/01/20/la-escasez-de-mano-de-obra-en-el-sector-de-la-construccion-agrava-la-crisis-de-la-vivienda-segun-la-cnc-2119541/).
- The same figure was repeated in 2026: "carencia de 700.000 albañiles y operarios cualificados" ("a shortfall of 700,000 bricklayers and skilled operatives") — [El Español, 30 May 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/sociedad/20260530/juan-arquitecto-anos-experiencia-faltan-albaniles-espana-vez-mano-obra/1003744261899_0.html).
- Caveat: the 700k figure is a CNC estimate that has stayed the same since 2021. It is a single, self-interested source.
- In the CNC's first labour report, based on about 500 member firms, 65% found it "extremadamente difícil" ("extremely difficult") to hire site foremen. The hardest roles to fill were foremen, bricklayers, formworkers, concrete placers, carpenters, façade installers and crane operators — [Interempresas, 19 Apr 2022](https://www.interempresas.net/Construccion/386526-CNC-avisa-que-65-por-ciento-constructoras-ve-extremadamente-dificil-contratar-encargados.html). This predates 2024 and is context only.
- FLC 2025 data:
- 10.8% of workers are under 30, against 15.1% across all sectors.
- 25.3% are foreign, against 15.7%.
- 51.8% have lower-secondary education or less.
- Source: [IFEMA/FLC, 26 May 2026](https://www.ifema.es/construtec/noticias-sector/observatorio-construccion-informe-empleo-2025).
- Average age was 45.1 in 2025, up from 42.4 in 2015, and 22% of workers are 55 or older — [Alimarket on FLC "Radiografía del empleo en construcción 2025"](https://www.alimarket.es/construccion/noticia/426443/el-empleo-en-construccion-aumenta-un-4-5--en-la-comparativa-anual--siendo-el-sector-que-mas-crece); [IFEMA](https://www.ifema.es/construtec/noticias-sector/informe-fundacion-laboral-construccion) (snippet-level).
- El Español reports that the 55+ group could retire within ten years, and that the under-30 share was 11.1% in Q1 2026 — [El Español, 1 Aug 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/ciencia/20260801/pascual-albanil-no-relevo-generacional-necesito-jovenes-quieran-aprender-no-encuentras/1003744335404_0.html) (snippet-level).
scale: 1.53 million construction workers ([FLC 2025](https://www.ifema.es/construtec/noticias-sector/observatorio-construccion-informe-empleo-2025)). I found no source for the number of firms affected.
cost_impact: No euro figure found. The CNC links the shortage to housing undersupply ([merca2, Jan 2025](https://www.merca2.es/2025/01/20/la-escasez-de-mano-de-obra-en-el-sector-de-la-construccion-agrava-la-crisis-de-la-vivienda-segun-la-cnc-2119541/)). In 2022 it warned the shortage could slow EU-funds execution ([Interempresas, 2022](https://www.interempresas.net/Construccion/386526-CNC-avisa-que-65-por-ciento-constructoras-ve-extremadamente-dificil-contratar-encargados.html)).
driver_status: A demographic and market force, not a regulation. The causes are baby-boomer retirements and young people's preference for non-manual jobs ([El Español, May 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/sociedad/20260530/juan-arquitecto-anos-experiencia-faltan-albaniles-espana-vez-mano-obra/1003744261899_0.html)). Ongoing. I did not verify the status of any immigration or FP measures.
solved_today:
- FLC training. The 2022 CNC report cited 80,000 students a year ([Interempresas, 2022](https://www.interempresas.net/Construccion/386526-CNC-avisa-que-65-por-ciento-constructoras-ve-extremadamente-dificil-contratar-encargados.html)).
- Foreign hiring, which makes up 25.3% of the workforce.
- Subcontracting.
- I found no data on software spending.
software_solvable: Partly. Matching, crew scheduling and productivity tools can stretch scarce crews further, but they cannot create workers.
confidence: High that the shortage exists. Medium on the 700k figure.

title: CAE document platforms charge subcontractors once per client platform (RD 171/2004)
who: Subcontractors and autónomos in construction, installation and industrial maintenance, mostly autónomos, micro and small firms. Also the principal contractors that impose the platforms.
where: National.
reality: Each client or main contractor chooses its own CAE (*Coordinación de Actividades Empresariales*) platform. Subcontractors must register and pay on each one. They then upload the same prevention (PRL) paperwork, such as training, medical fitness, insurance and Social Security filings, and keep it current on every platform. Clients can tie site access or payment to the documents being validated.
evidence:
- OCU public complaint, 11 Jul 2025. A subcontractor says Nalanda:
- "tiene un precio elevadísimo" ("has an extremely high price");
- "cambia sus tarifas cuando quiere, sin avisar" ("changes its rates whenever it wants, without warning");
- and "si quieres trabajar con tus clientes estás OBLIGADO a pagarlo porque ellos son los que eligen a Nalanda" ("if you want to work with your clients you are OBLIGED to pay, because they are the ones who choose Nalanda").
- No company reply is shown — [OCU reclamación pública, 11 Jul 2025](https://www.ocu.org/reclamar/lista-reclamaciones-publicas/mal-servicio-y-descuido-al-cli/882aec16fbadc4b4f3).
- Nalanda has a TrustScore of 1.3/5 from 135 reviews, 97% of them one-star — [Trustpilot, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/www.nalandaglobal.com). These are unverified user reviews:
- Oct 2026: fees went from "300 y pico" ("300-odd") to "más de 1400 euros" ("over 1,400 euros").
- Oct 2026: "una cuota de 1400 euros para 100 trabajadores" ("a 1,400-euro fee for 100 workers").
- 19 Oct 2026: "en una factura de 2000 euros anuales no puedo dar de alta más que a 15 trabajadores" ("for a 2,000-euro annual bill I can only register 15 workers").
- Oct 2026: "50 eur por atención telefónica" ("50 euros for phone support").
- 4 Dec 2025: automatic renewal "duplicando el precio" ("doubling the price").
- Nalanda's own marketing tells clients they can condition "payments to your subcontractors to their correct documentary situation" — [Nalanda](https://nalandaglobal.com/en/?p=5276). Vendor source.
- Published prices, from a competitor's comparison (prices checked 20 Oct 2026; vendor-authored, not neutral) — [DocuPRL, Jun 2026, updated Oct 2026](https://docuprl.es/blog/mejores-plataformas-cae-2026.html):
- Dokify: from €490/yr for the principal; from €102.90/yr plus €15.44 per employee or machine for contractors (excl. VAT).
- DocAcces: €32/month for up to 5 subcontractors, rising to €99 for up to 25.
- UCAE: from €80/month.
- PlayCAE: announced €199/month, with no cost to subcontractors.
- Nalanda: price on request.
- Legal basis: RD 171/2004 governs coordination when several companies share a workplace. The principal company answers for external workers' PRL compliance and Social Security registration — [Interempresas (Dokify-sponsored article)](https://www.interempresas.net/Logistica/612265-Gestion-de-subcontratas-como-garantizar-cumplimiento-normativo-y-evitar-riesgos-legales.html) (date not shown).
scale: Not quantified. I found no data on how many subcontractors are registered on these platforms.
cost_impact:
- About €100 to over €2,000 a year per platform per subcontractor, from published prices and reviews.
- Duplicated office hours, not quantified.
- Risk of payment or site access being blocked.
driver_status: RD 171/2004 (CAE, implementing art. 24 of Ley 31/1995 PRL) is in force. For construction, Ley 32/2006 and RD 1109/2007 are also in force. No law requires any particular platform; the choice is the principals' market practice.
solved_today:
- Platforms: Nalanda, Dokify, plus Ctaima, e-coordina, Obralia and Metacontratas, whose prices and complaints I could not verify.
- External prevention consultancies.
- Office staff uploading documents by hand.
- Documented complaints exist only for Nalanda, as above.
software_solvable: Yes. An "upload once, sync to every client platform" document wallet with expiry alerts and connectors is pure software. A flat-fee model paid by the principal is another option.
confidence: High on the pain. Medium on price levels, which come from reviews and competitor sources.

title: Subcontracting-chain compliance under Ley 32/2006 (REA, Libro de Subcontratación) with joint liability
who: Main contractors and subcontractors, from micro to medium. Autónomos are barred from subcontracting.
where: National. REA registration is handled by the regional labour authority where the company has its registered office.
evidence:
- Ley 32/2006 sets these rules — [BOE consolidated text, last updated 30 Dec 2021](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-18205):
- Art. 4: subcontractors need their own organisation, PRL-trained staff and REA registration. Regular subcontractors need a minimum share of permanent staff: 10% in the first 18 months, 20% in months 19–36 and 30% from month 37.
- Art. 5.2.d: "El tercer subcontratista no podrá subcontratar" ("the third-level subcontractor may not subcontract"). Autónomos cannot subcontract either.
- Art. 8: the Libro must stay on site, listing every subcontract in date order.
- Art. 7.2: breaches trigger "responsabilidad solidaria" (joint liability) for labour and Social Security obligations.
- REA registration lasts three years and must be renewed in the six months before it expires — [Invoice Data Extraction blog](https://invoicedataextraction.com/blog/spain-rea-subcontratista-construccion) (commercial, undated; single source).
- The Libro follows the model in Annex III of RD 1109/2007 and is validated (*habilitado*) by the labour authority — [BOJA 2007](https://www.juntadeandalucia.es/boja/2007/249/d2.pdf).
scale: Every construction site that uses subcontractors. No counts found.
cost_impact:
- Joint liability for subcontractors' debts.
- Fines from the Labour Inspectorate (ITSS) under LISOS, whose amounts I did not verify.
driver_status: Ley 32/2006 and RD 1109/2007 are in force. The consolidated text was last changed by RDL 32/2021, effective 31 Dec 2021 ([BOE](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2006-18205)). I found no changes in 2024–26.
solved_today:
- CAE platforms (see CON-02).
- The Libro itself.
- Gestorías and prevention consultants.
- No prices verified.
software_solvable: Yes. A digital Libro, automated REA and quota checks, and chain-level alerts are all possible, though they depend on access to regional REA data.
confidence: High on the obligations. Low on enforcement intensity and cost.

title: Construction deaths rising while other sectors fall; safety paperwork and inspection exposure
who: Construction firms of every size. Inference: exposure is concentrated on micro and small sites.
where: National. Regional alarms have been raised in Granada (Andalucía) and Canarias.
reality: Firms manage safety plans, coordinator instructions, training records and Labour Inspection visits. A serious accident brings an inspection and possible criminal or civil liability.
evidence:
- Provisional 2025 figures: 584 deaths during working hours nationally (−9.6%). Construction was the exception: "con 29 muertos más, aumentó un 21,5%" ("with 29 more deaths, it rose 21.5%") — [INSST, 11 Feb 2026](https://www.insst.es/noticias-insst/cae-la-siniestralidad-laboral-y-se-reducen-un-9-6-por-ciento-los-accidentes-mortales).
- El Español adds — [8 Jul 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/ciencia/20260708/oficial-muertes-accidentes-construccion-elevado-gobierno/1003744313511_0.html):
- Construction's fatal-incidence index was 11.3 per 100,000 workers (+18%).
- Total work deaths including commuting were 735, down from 796.
- Accidents with sick leave totalled 620,386 (−1.3%).
- Unions are calling for updated prevention rules and a stronger Labour Inspectorate.
- Conflict: El Español writes "29 workers died", which contradicts INSST's "+29". INSST is the primary source.
- Up to July 2025, construction had the most deaths of any sector: 103 including commuting, 21 more than a year earlier — [RTVC, 8 Oct 2025](https://rtvc.es/la-construccion-el-sector-que-concentra-el-mayor-numero-de-muertes-8-de-octubre-2025/) (snippet-level).
- The Junta de Andalucía and builders met to discuss rising accidents in Granada as activity picks up — [Última Hora, 16 Oct 2025](https://www.ultimahora.es/noticias/comunidades/2025/10/16/2492169/junta-constructores-analizan-soluciones-para-reducir-siniestralidad-granada-ante-despegue-actividad.html).
scale: 1.53 million workers. Inference: an increase of 29 at +21.5% implies roughly 135 construction deaths during working hours in 2024 and about 164 in 2025.
cost_impact: Human cost and legal liability. I found no euro figures, for example for penalty surcharges on benefits (*recargo de prestaciones*) or fines.
driver_status: Ley 31/1995 PRL and RD 1627/1997 (construction sites) are in force. Unions want reform, but I found no draft.
solved_today: External prevention services, health-and-safety coordinators and CAE platforms. No prices found.
software_solvable: Partly. Digital site inspections, permits to work and training-record tracking cut paperwork, but controlling physical risk needs people on site.

title: Late payment down the subcontracting and installer chain
who: Subcontractors, electrical, telecom and HVAC installers, and suppliers, mainly micro and small firms.
where: National.
reality: Large contractors pay beyond the legal limits, often through confirming (a bank-intermediated supplier payment scheme), and small firms end up financing the chain. Few claim the late-payment interest they are owed.
evidence:
- PMcM "Estudio Plazos de Pago en España 2025" — [Forbes, 16 Apr 2026](https://forbes.es/economia/907227/el-85-de-las-grandes-empresas-incumple-los-plazos-legales-de-pago-segun-pmcm/):
- Private sector paid in 67 days on average (legal maximum 60); the public sector in 70 (legal maximum 30). Both rose by 3 days.
- 85% of large companies exceed the legal terms.
- 89% of suppliers do not claim late-payment interest, and 94% do not claim the legal compensation.
- Subcontracting averaged 87 days — [esDiario, 16 Apr 2026](https://www.esdiario.com/economia/260416/185240/85-grandes-empresas-incumple-plazos-legales-pago.html) (snippet-level).
- FENIE, the electrical and telecom installers' federation — [Interempresas, 4 Jun 2026](https://www.interempresas.net/Electricidad/634041-Fenie-destaca-la-reduccion-de-la-morosidad-en-el-sector-instalador.html):
- The installer default ratio fell to 3.5%, about half the previous year's.
- Public administrations pay installers in 45 days (20 fewer).
- Builders' and large firms' terms remain "alejados de los límites legales" ("far from the legal limits"), especially with confirming.
- 90% want a sanctions regime.
- Older or undated context:
- The PMcM accused Ibex construction groups of average payment periods of 536 days (Ferrovial), 425 (Acciona) and 337 (Sacyr) — [Vozpópuli, date not shown](https://www.vozpopuli.com/economia/empresas/constructoras-pagos-morosidad-constructoras-pagos-morosidad_0_852814755.html).
- Banco de España data put construction at 120 days and real estate at 140 — [idealista PMcM tag page, undated](https://www.idealista.com/news/etiquetas/pmcm).
scale: Not quantified.
cost_impact: Working-capital strain. No euro figure found.
driver_status: Ley 3/2004 on late payment is in force. A sanctions regime is being demanded but is not in force. Overlap: the cash-flow researcher covers this in depth.
solved_today: Confirming, factoring, credit insurance and manual chasing. No prices verified.
software_solvable: Partly. Tracking progress certificates (*certificaciones*) and invoices, plus automated interest claims, would help, but the power imbalance remains.

title: Municipal works-licence bottlenecks
who: Developers, builders, renovation contractors and architects; homeowners commissioning work.
where: City level. The best data covers Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia and Málaga (a 2020 study). Valencia developers have complained.
reality:
- Major-works (*obra mayor*) licences take about a year instead of the legal three months.
- First-occupation licences add months more.
- Renovation firms must work out, municipality by municipality, whether they need a licence, a sworn statement (*declaración responsable*) or a prior notice (*comunicación previa*).
evidence:
- ASPRIMA–EY — [EY press release, May 2020](https://www.ey.com/es_es/newsroom/2020/05/el-retraso-en-la-concesion-de-licencias-de-obra-nueva-tiene-un-sobrecoste-medio-para-el-comprador-de-casi-13-000-euros-por-vivienda). This predates 2024; I found no 2024–26 update.
- New-build licences take about 12 months on average, against a guideline of 3 months for major works and 1 month for minor works.
- First occupation takes about 3 months.
- Delay and cost per home, by city:
| City | Delay | Cost per home | Share of price |
|---|---|---|---|
| Madrid | 12 months | €28,606 | 6.56% |
| Barcelona | 12 months | €26,145 | 5.76% |
| Valencia | 12 months | €9,679 | 4.37% |
| Málaga | 8 months | €7,272 | 3.11% |
- The Ministry of Housing published a "Guía de Recomendaciones y Buenas Prácticas en materia de Licencias Urbanísticas en el Ámbito Residencial". It contains 20 recommendations, promotes digitising files and analysed 30 municipalities — [idealista/Europa Press, 29 Dec 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/12/29/878158-vivienda-publica-una-guia-para-ayudar-a-las-administraciones-a-agilizar-la).
- A former Madrid councillor launched a consultancy claiming it can cut licence times by 40% — [idealista tag page, 25 Jan 2024](https://www.idealista.com/news/etiquetas/licencias-de-obra).
- Valencia: "mantiene el embudo en las licencias de obra pese a los cambios en Urbanismo" ("the bottleneck in works licences persists despite changes in the planning department") — [Valencia Plaza, date not verified](https://valenciaplaza.com/valenciaplaza/embudo-pese-a-los-cambios-en-urbanismo).
scale: Not quantified.
cost_impact: €7,000 to €29,000 per new home (2020 figures).
driver_status: Municipal capacity and procedures. The state guide (Dec 2025) is not binding. I did not verify the regional declaración-responsable laws.
solved_today: Planning consultancies and architects' permit services. No prices verified.
software_solvable: Partly. Applicant-side preparation and tracking tools help, but the bottleneck is municipal staffing.
confidence: Medium on the problem. Low on current figures.

title: NextGenerationEU rehabilitation grants: years of processing and pre-financing risk
who: Renovation contractors acting as rehabilitation agents or managers (*agentes/gestores de la rehabilitación*); owners' communities; homeowners; *administradores de fincas*.
where: Regional, since each autonomous community runs its own calls. Documented cases are in Aragón, Alicante (Comunitat Valenciana) and Euskadi.
reality: Applicants wait years for approval and then for payment. When owners assign the grant to the contractor, the contractor carries the cash gap and the risk that the project collapses.
evidence:
- Justicia de Aragón (regional ombudsman), case Q26/763/09, 15 Jun 2026 — [Justicia de Aragón](https://eljusticiadearagon.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Q25-753-08.pdf):
- A grant under the PRTR (Spain's NextGenerationEU recovery plan), Programme 4, Orden VMV/1018/2022, took 30 months to be approved (29 May 2025).
- It then went about 10 more months unpaid after the corrected documents were filed (11 Jun 2025): "superior a los 3 años desde la solicitud" ("more than 3 years since the application").
- The regional government cited an "elevado volumen de solicitudes" ("high volume of applications") and the "complejidad de los procedimientos de gestión y fiscalización" ("complexity of the management and audit procedures"). It pays in batches (*por lotes*).
- In Euskadi, beneficiaries can assign collection of the grant to the rehabilitation agent or manager, who must put the full amount into the works — [Gobierno Vasco](https://www.euskadi.eus/web01-a2next/es/contenidos/informacion/fnext_personas_benefici/es_def/index.shtml) (undated).
- In Urbanova (Alicante), a €12m project that depended on about €9m of NextGen funds was abandoned. The contractor, appointed as rehabilitation agent, is claiming about €2m in lost profit — [Alicante Plaza, date not verified](https://alicanteplaza.es/laempresadelarehabilitaciondeurbanovaexigiraellucrocesantetrasabortarseelproyecto).
- Administradores de fincas say the state housing plan's goals do not match what communities can manage, given bureaucracy and constant rule changes. Handling "ayudas, certificaciones y requisitos administrativos" ("grants, certifications and administrative requirements") is getting harder — [idealista/Conversia, 17 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/06/17/901380-administradores-de-fincas-el-cambio-estructural-que-esta-redefiniendo-la-gestion-de).
scale: Not quantified. I found no national figures on applications or backlogs.
cost_impact: Cash gaps lasting several years, and one claim of about €2m.
driver_status: The PRTR residential-rehabilitation programmes funded by NextGenerationEU. I did not verify the final 2026 deadlines.
solved_today:
- Rehabilitation agents.
- Rehabilitation offices at the colegios de arquitectos and aparejadores, which Aragón points applicants to ([Justicia de Aragón](https://eljusticiadearagon.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Q25-753-08.pdf)).
- Tinsa's Agentia-R platform exists ([Tinsa](https://www.tinsa.es/sala-de-prensa/agentia-r/lanzamiento-agentiarplus/), not opened; price unknown).
software_solvable: Partly. File and evidence management, payment tracking and cash-flow forecasting would help, but software cannot speed up the administration.
confidence: Medium. The evidence is one official case plus press reports.

title: Solar self-consumption installers: demand slump plus tariff and permitting friction
who: Solar PV installers and electricians, mostly micro and small.
where: National.
reality: Residential and small-business jobs are down from the 2022 peak, industrial sales cycles are longer, and the fixed part of electricity tariffs erodes customers' savings.
evidence:
- UNEF figures for 2024 — [Energías Renovables, 23 Jan 2025](https://www.energias-renovables.com/autoconsumo/ya-hay-mas-de-8-000-megavatios-20250123); [Smartgridsinfo, 27 Jan 2025](https://smartgridsinfo.es/2025/01/27/autoconsumo-fotovoltaico-supera-umbral-8-gw-instalados-espana-segun-datos-unef):
- 1,182 MW of self-consumption installed, −31% against 2023 and −53% against 2022.
- Cumulative capacity of 8,137 MW.
- Industrial installations of 674 MW (−34%).
- UNEF figures for Q1 2025 — [Energías Renovables, 13 Jun 2025](https://www.energias-renovables.com/autoconsumo/el-mercado-del-autoconsumo-solar-cae-un-20250613):
- The installation pace fell 17% against the 2024 quarterly average: residential −14%, commercial −17%, industrial −20%.
- Reaching the PNIEC target of 19,000 MW by 2030 needs at least 1,810 MW a year.
- UNEF blames the 75% fixed / 25% variable split of network tolls.
- It asks for simplified processing up to 500 kW, a 5 km maximum distance, and a permit exemption under 15 kW (PV plus batteries). A new self-consumption decree was under review by MITECO (the energy ministry).
scale: Not quantified. I found no census of installers.
cost_impact: I found no data on closures or jobs.
driver_status: Electricity prices returning to normal and higher financing costs (UNEF). RD 244/2019 is in force. The new self-consumption decree was under review in June 2025; I did not verify its status as of October 2026.
solved_today: Moving into batteries and industrial work. I found no prices for design or proposal software.
software_solvable: Partly. Faster proposals and permit filing would help, but the demand drop is macroeconomic.
confidence: Medium. The 2024–Q1 2025 data is solid; the later status is unknown.

title: Quoting, measurements and change orders run on heavy or costly tools
who: Micro and small builders, renovation contractors, trades and technical studios.
where: National.
reality: Budgets (measurements, BC3 price databases), progress certificates and change orders are prepared by technical staff in Presto or Arquímedes. Inference: micro firms use spreadsheets instead. The leading tools are seen as complex.
evidence:
- Prices claimed by a competitor (OneEstimate, not verified) — [OneEstimate, 2 May 2026](https://oneestimate.ai/es/blog/mejores-software-presupuestos-construccion):
- Presto: about €100/month, or a perpetual licence from about €2,000. Drawbacks listed: "steep learning curve", "dated interface", "costly for freelancers".
- Arquímedes (CYPE): about €70/month; "requires advanced technical skills".
- Procore: "typically $10,000+ USD/year".
- A Presto 21 training course costs €471 (COIIM) — [Aprendemas](https://www.aprendemas.com/es/curso/curso-de-presto-21-1188673/) (undated).
- Presto is the public-sector default: the Junta de Andalucía and the city of Zaragoza put out tenders for Presto licences and updates — [Junta de Andalucía](https://www.juntadeandalucia.es/haciendayadministracionpublica/apl/pdc_sirec_documentacion/rest/descargar/documento/337743); [Zaragoza](https://www.zaragoza.es/sede/servicio/contratacion-publica/anuncio/19595/document.pdf).
scale: Not quantified.
cost_impact: €70–€100 per month per seat, plus training. I found no data on hours lost or on disputes over change orders or unpaid private clients.
driver_status: A market force. E-invoicing and Verifactu add invoicing requirements, which the tax researcher covers.
solved_today: Presto, Arquímedes, Excel and general invoicing apps. I could not verify field-service app prices: the vendor pages returned 404 or 403.
software_solvable: Yes.
confidence: Low. Prices come from a competitor and I found no user survey on the pain.

title: Energy performance certificate (CEE) rule changes ripple through every transaction
who: Technicians and certifiers (architects, engineers and now other qualified professionals), real estate agencies, landlords and sellers, and installers doing energy upgrades.
where: National, with regional registries.
reality:
- Agencies must display the CEE (*certificado de eficiencia energética*) when they rent or sell.
- Since August 2025, a valid registered CEE is needed before a mortgage valuation.
- The rules on who can certify are changing.
evidence:
- RD 659/2025 of 22 Jul 2025 amends RD 390/2021 — [idealista, 23 Jul 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/construccion/2025/07/23/854394-ampliado-el-abanico-de-profesionales-que-pueden-emitir-certificados-energeticos):
- More professionals can certify existing buildings after a two-module training course.
- Accreditation is by sworn statement (*declaración responsable*) and is valid nationwide.
- It creates a Registro Administrativo Centralizado de Técnicos Competentes (central register of qualified technicians), with 8 months to build the central system and 12 months for regions.
- Real estate companies must display the CEE of properties they rent or sell.
- Orden ECM/599/2025 of 10 Jun 2025 requires a valid registered CEE for mortgage valuations from 12 Aug 2025, and registry or cadastral certificates no more than three months old. A CEE has been required to sell or rent since 1 Jun 2013 — [idealista, 14 Aug 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/08/14/856865-un-notario-avisa-en-vigor-la-obligacion-de-contar-con-el-certificado-energetico-si).
- Only about 10% of purchase demand targets A-rated homes. E-rated homes account for 39.7% and G-rated for 15.4% — [idealista, 26 Jun 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/06/26/850719-solo-el-10-de-la-demanda-en-compraventa-se-dirige-a-viviendas-con-etiqueta-a).
scale: Every sale and rental. No counts found.
cost_impact: I could not find CEE prices. Fines of up to €6,000 for certifying without a site visit come from a 2021 article and are outdated — [idealista CEE tag page](https://www.idealista.com/news/etiquetas/certificado-energetico).
driver_status: RD 390/2021, RD 659/2025 and Orden ECM/599/2025 are all in force. I could not verify whether Spain has transposed the recast EPBD, Directive (EU) 2024/1275.
solved_today: Independent and online certifiers. No prices verified.
software_solvable: Partly. Ordering CEEs and tracking their expiry for agencies and landlords is software; the certificate itself needs a technician's visit.

title: Ley 12/2023 shifted rental agency fees to landlords; disguised tenant fees now face fines
who: Real estate agencies (micro and small), rental-management firms and rent-guarantee companies; landlords, who now bear the fee.
where: National. Enforcement comes from the Ministerio de Consumo, and in Madrid complaints were passed to the Comunidad de Madrid.
reality: Agencies can no longer charge tenants a fee. Some rebranded the charge as a "solvency study", a "tenant service" or an "additional guarantee". Consumer authorities and tenant groups now pursue them.
evidence:
- LAU art. 20.2, as currently consolidated: real estate management costs "no podrán ser repercutidos al arrendatario, ni directa ni indirectamente" ("may not be passed on to the tenant, directly or indirectly"). The housing law of May 2023 made the landlord pay these costs. Art. 20 was amended by Ley 12/2023 (DF 1.4, in force 26 May 2023) and rewritten again by RDL 29/2026 (art. 3.12, in force 8 Oct 2026) — [BOE consolidated LAU](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1994-26003); [Maldita, 20 Jun 2023](https://maldita.es/malditateexplica/20230620/inmobiliaria-vivienda-honorarios-trucos/).
- Consumo proposed a €3,600,902 fine on Alquiler Seguro. The case was opened in March 2025 after a FACUA complaint (Nov 2023), and the fine is not final — [Noticias de Navarra, 27 Oct 2025](https://www.noticiasdenavarra.com/economia/2025/10/27/consumo-propone-multar-alquiler-seguro-10269149.amp.html).
- El Salto's account of the same case — [El Salto, 30 Oct 2025](https://www.elsaltodiario.com/vivienda/multa-3-6-millones-alquiler-seguro-sacude-impunidad-inmobiliarias-saltarse-ley):
- Six "very serious" infractions and one "serious". The fine breaks down as €1m for the "Servicio de Atención al Inquilino" clause, €1m for home insurance that was effectively compulsory, and €1.5m for three more infractions.
- Disguised fee names included "garantía adicional" (additional guarantee), "estudio de solvencia" (solvency study) and "asesoramiento jurídico" (legal advice). One 82-year-old tenant paid a €1,400 "garantía adicional".
- Tecnocasa and RedPiso were also accused, with no fine reported.
- About ten Madrid intermediaries reported by the Sindicato de Inquilinos were referred to the Comunidad de Madrid.
- Fines range from €10,001 to €100,000 and can reach four to six times the unlawful profit. The Madrid agents' federation AMADEI argues these charges are legal as "atypical contracts" — [idealista, undated](https://www.idealista.com/news/taxonomy/term/27931).
- Earlier tactics included renaming fees as "estudio de viabilidad o solvencia económica" (viability or solvency study) — [Maldita, 20 Jun 2023](https://maldita.es/malditateexplica/20230620/inmobiliaria-vivienda-honorarios-trucos/).
scale: Agencies are involved in about 70% of transactions (FADEI, via [idealista, 29 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/node/904122)). I found no count of agencies.
cost_impact: Lost tenant-side income. Inference: the market norm for a rental was one month's rent, the minimum the MLS cartel enforced ([eldiario, 9 Dec 2021](https://www.eldiario.es/economia/cnmc-multa-idealista-remax-look-find-fijar-precios-operaciones-inmobiliarias_1_8562945.html)). Fines of up to €3.6m have been proposed.
driver_status: Ley 12/2023 is in force. RDL 29/2026 amended art. 20 again; it has been in force since 8 Oct 2026 and awaits a convalidation vote.
solved_today: Landlord-paid fee models, rent-guarantee products and legal advice. No prices verified.
software_solvable: Partly. Compliant contract and fee templates and landlord-side billing are software, but the underlying problem is how fees are regulated.

title: Long-term rental inventory is shrinking and shifting to seasonal leases
who: Agencies with rental portfolios, rental managers and landlords.
where: National. The fall is steepest in tense zones: San Sebastián, A Coruña, Bilbao, Pamplona, Vitoria, Tarragona, Lleida and Barcelona. Other cities: Alicante, Valencia, Málaga, Madrid, Palma. Las Palmas is up slightly.
reality: Fewer long-term listings to manage. More seasonal and room contracts, which carry higher legal risk (see CON-19).
evidence:
- Idealista's permanent-rental listings fell from 902,664 in 2018 to 510,091 in 2025 (about −44%). This counts adverts, not physical homes — [Artículo14, 7 Oct 2026](https://www.articulo14.es/economia/la-oferta-de-alquiler-se-desploma-un-44-desde-2018-casi-393-000-anuncios-menos-en-siete-anos-20261007.html) (snippet-level).
- Observatorio del Alquiler (Fundación Alquiler Seguro), long-term stock at end-2025 — [Forbes, 28 Jan 2026](https://forbes.es/economia/864744/la-oferta-de-alquiler-pierde-33-400-viviendas-al-cierre-de-2025-y-se-ralentiza-el-ritmo-de-encarecimiento/):
- Stock fell 4.7% (−33,418) to 683,920.
- Barcelona accounts for 34.7% of the fall (−11,594). Sevilla fell 13%.
- Madrid (+0.21%) and Málaga (+0.10%) were flat. Las Palmas fell because the tense-zone debate "ha retraído a los arrendadores" ("has made landlords hold back").
- Idealista, Q3 2026 — [idealista, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/10/20/919563-la-oferta-de-alquiler-permanente-cae-un-10-en-un-ano-y-la-de-temporada-ya-supone-un):
- Permanent supply −10% year on year; seasonal supply +7%; seasonal leases are 34% of the market.
- Permanent supply by city: San Sebastián −52%, A Coruña −41%, Bilbao −41%, Pamplona −33%, Vitoria −32%, Tarragona −31%, Lleida −29%, Barcelona −22%, Alicante −22%, Valencia −12%, Málaga −11%, Madrid −6%, Palma −2%, Las Palmas +2%.
- Seasonal share by city: San Sebastián 62%, Bilbao 59%, Barcelona 57%, Madrid 35%, Valencia 35%, Sevilla 33%, Alicante 31%, Palma 25%, Zaragoza 12%, Valladolid 11%.
- Idealista spokesman Francisco Iñareta: "la intervención en el mercado sigue generando escasez allí donde se aplica" ("market intervention keeps creating scarcity wherever it is applied").
- The ministry estimates 1.15 million people live in seasonal or room rentals, of whom about 422,000 would prefer a regular lease — [idealista, 7 Sep 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/finanzas/economia/2026/09/07/912998-consumo-estima-que-mas-de-un-millon-de-personas-vive-en-alquiler-de-temporada-o-de) (snippet-level).
- Tourist and seasonal surpluses account for only about 46% of the rental stock that has disappeared (idealista analysis with AirDNA and ministry data). This comes from a search snippet summarising idealista-based coverage; the exact article was not confirmed. Likely in [Artículo14, 7 Oct 2026](https://www.articulo14.es/economia/la-oferta-de-alquiler-se-desploma-un-44-desde-2018-casi-393-000-anuncios-menos-en-siete-anos-20261007.html) or [The Objective, 28 Jan 2026](https://theobjective.com/economia/2026-01-28/oferta-alquiler-larga-duracion-pierde-inmuebles-ano/). Low confidence.
scale: 683,920 long-term homes on the market at end-2025 (Observatorio). 1.15 million people in seasonal or room rentals.
cost_impact: A smaller rental-management revenue base for agencies. I found no euro figure.
driver_status: Rent controls in tense zones (CON-17), the seasonal-lease rules (CON-19) and the October 2026 decrees (CON-18). Idealista warns that Q3 data does not yet reflect the decrees' effect.
solved_today: Agencies shift towards sales, seasonal or coliving products, and rental management charged at 6–10% of rent (per inmho; [idealista, 30 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/empresas/2026/07/30/906830-50-empresas-compradas-al-ano-y-menos-del-3-de-cuota-asi-es-inmho-en-el-sector)).
software_solvable: No for the supply shortage itself. Partly for helping agencies retain landlords with compliance and management tools.

title: Lead overload and tenant screening in a supply-starved rental market
who: Agencies and individual landlords who advertise rentals.
where: National, with peaks in Barcelona, Girona, Baleares, Vizcaya, Las Palmas, Zaragoza, Tarragona, Valencia and Madrid.
reality: Each rental listing draws more than a hundred enquiries within days. Agencies have to triage leads, check solvency and document their selection without charging the tenant for the work.
evidence:
- The average home drew 135 interested people in 10 days in 2025, up from 124. By province: Barcelona 462 (a record), Girona 140, Baleares 137, Vizcaya 134, Las Palmas 121, Zaragoza 109, Tarragona 109, Valencia 104, Madrid 103 — [Forbes/Observatorio del Alquiler, 28 Jan 2026](https://forbes.es/economia/864744/la-oferta-de-alquiler-pierde-33-400-viviendas-al-cierre-de-2025-y-se-ralentiza-el-ritmo-de-encarecimiento/).
- Tenants spend almost 40% of their net income on rent — same source.
- Charging tenants for a "solvency study" is one of the disguised fees targeted in the Alquiler Seguro case — [El Salto, 30 Oct 2025](https://www.elsaltodiario.com/vivienda/multa-3-6-millones-alquiler-seguro-sacude-impunidad-inmobiliarias-saltarse-ley).
- The industry warns that excessive guarantees demanded from tenants mean "solo acceden prácticamente los que no necesitan acceder" ("practically only those who don't need access get in") — [idealista/inmho, 30 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/empresas/2026/07/30/906830-50-empresas-compradas-al-ano-y-menos-del-3-de-cuota-asi-es-inmho-en-el-sector).
scale: All rental listings. I found no count of agencies.
cost_impact: Agent hours per listing, not quantified. Risk of discrimination or data-protection problems in screening (inference).
driver_status: A market force plus Ley 12/2023's fee rule (in force). RDL 29/2026 caps guarantees (see CON-18).
solved_today: Portal lead tools and CRMs (prices unverified, see CON-16) and manual screening.
software_solvable: Yes. Lead triage, standardised solvency verification paid by the landlord, and an audit trail of how tenants were selected.
confidence: Medium-high on lead volume. Low on how much time it costs.

title: Anti-money-laundering duties for agencies, tightening under the EU AMLR from July 2027
who: Real estate agencies (micro and small) and developers.
where: National, then EU-wide from July 2027.
