reality: Agencies that broker sales are obliged entities under Ley 10/2010. They must identify clients and beneficial owners, assess risk and report suspicious operations, and many small agencies are unaware they are covered.
evidence:
- Ley 10/2010 art. 2.1.l covers "Los promotores inmobiliarios y quienes ejerzan profesionalmente actividades de agencia, comisión o intermediación en la compraventa de bienes inmuebles" ("property developers and anyone professionally brokering the sale of real estate") — [SEPBLAC list of obliged entities, Oct 2024](https://www.sepblac.es/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/sujetos_obligados_ley_10_2010.pdf).
- The EU AML Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 "se aplicará desde julio de 2027" ("will apply from July 2027"). It brings stricter due diligence on all parties, beneficial-owner identification, an evidence-based risk self-assessment, sanctions and adverse-media screening, and a separate compliance officer — [finReg360 / El Confidencial, 23 Dec 2025](https://finreg360.com/el-negocio-inmobiliario-ante-las-novedades-en-la-prevencion-del-blanqueo-de-capitales/).
- SEPBLAC has flagged deficiencies in the sector, such as missing whistleblowing channels — [idealista, undated](https://www.idealista.com/news/taxonomy/term/40917) (snippet-level).
- A legal commentary argues many agencies are "el perímetro que no se sabe sujeto obligado" ("the perimeter that doesn't know it is an obliged entity") — [Economist & Jurist, undated](https://www.economistjurist.es/articulos-juridicos-destacados/inmobiliarias-joyerias-y-galerias-de-arte-el-perimetro-que-no-se-sabe-sujeto-obligado/).
scale: Every agency that brokers sales. No count found.
cost_impact: I found no sanction figures for agencies or compliance-cost data.
driver_status: Ley 10/2010 is in force. The EU AMLR applies from July 2027.
solved_today: AML training courses and consultants. No prices verified.
software_solvable: Yes. Know-your-customer and beneficial-owner workflows, risk scoring, sanctions screening and record-keeping are standard regulatory-technology (regtech) features.
confidence: Medium. The obligations are verified; the pain and enforcement intensity are weakly evidenced.

title: Patchwork of regional agent registries and licensing requirements
who: Agencies and agents, especially those working across regions.
where:
- Catalonia: mandatory registration (AICAT).
- Comunitat Valenciana: mandatory registry.
- Canarias: registry since 2022.
- Madrid: voluntary, with a mandatory registry announced in June 2026.
- Other regions not verified.
reality: Training, insurance, guarantee and office requirements differ by region, so firms expanding across regions repeat the onboarding.
evidence:
- Madrid's RAIN registry is voluntary and requires 200 hours of real estate training or 4 years' experience. On 29 Jun 2026 the Madrid regional government announced it will make registration mandatory. AMADEI and FADEI welcomed this, saying the differing rules create "ciudadanos de primera y de segunda" ("first- and second-class citizens") — [idealista, 29 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/node/904122).
- Comunitat Valenciana: a mandatory registry with location, training and solvency requirements. The competition authority (CNMC) challenged it in court as disproportionate — [Valencia Plaza](https://valenciaplaza.com/valenciaplaza/vivienda-regula-un-registro-obligatorio-para-agentes-inmobiliarios-en-la-comunitat); [Valencia Plaza, CNMC appeal](https://valenciaplaza.com/competencia-recurre-el-registro-de-agentes-inmobiliarios-de-la-generalitat) (dates not verified).
- Canarias: registry created by Decreto 11/2022 of 20 Jan 2022 — [Iberley](https://www.iberley.es/legislacion/decreto-11-2022-20-enero-crea-regula-registro-agentes-inmobiliarios-canarias-27033254).
- Catalonia: registration, professional qualification, liability insurance and a guarantee are required — [JustAnswer, weak source](https://www.justanswer.es/legal-es/sugj0-para-poder-vender-pisos-en-catalu-a-es-totalmente.html). The idealista article above implies Catalonia's registry is mandatory.
scale: Not quantified.
cost_impact: Training (200 hours in Madrid), insurance and guarantees. No euro figures.
driver_status:
- Regional decrees in force in Catalonia, Valencia and Canarias.
- Madrid's mandatory registry announced, no date.
- The CNMC's challenge in Valencia: outcome not verified.
solved_today: Association training courses (API, COAPI, AICAT) and consultants. Prices not verified.
software_solvable: Partly. Tracking compliance credentials (training hours, insurance) is software, but registration itself is a legal formality.

title: Dependence on portals and CRM/MLS tools: opaque prices and competition-law exposure
who: Agencies (micro and small) and franchise networks.
where: National.
reality: Agencies depend on paid portal packages and on CRMs for publishing listings and sharing them through MLS networks. Prices are quote-based. In 2021 the competition authority found that MLS rules built into the software had been used to fix commissions.
evidence:
- CNMC fine of 9 Dec 2021 — [eldiario, 9 Dec 2021](https://www.eldiario.es/economia/cnmc-multa-idealista-remax-look-find-fijar-precios-operaciones-inmobiliarias_1_8562945.html):
- Fines by company:
| Company | Fine |
|---|---|
| Idealista (via Idealista Tools) | €730,000 |
| Remax | €375,720 |
| Inmovilla | €83,149 |
| Look & Find | €31,486 |
| Witei | €18,925 (45% leniency reduction) |
| Anaconda | €1,749 |
- The MLS rules imposed minimum commissions of 4% on sales and one month's rent on rentals, split 50/50 between agencies.
- The software vendors built filters and controls that enforced the rules.
- Discrepancy: eldiario says the total was "more than €1.5m", but the listed amounts add up to about €1.24m. Another outlet reported €1.25m — [Economist & Jurist](https://www.economistjurist.es/economia/competencia-multa-a-siete-inmobiliarias-por-pactar-comisiones/).
- Inmovilla claims more than 3,000 agencies and 5 million active properties, with prices "bajo cotización" (on quote). Its rating is 4.2/5 from 12 reviews. Complaints mention a steep learning curve, advanced features costing extra and slowness at peak hours (Sep 2024). One 2022 review says the user paid €79 + VAT on a 6-month contract but could not upload properties without paying more — [ComparaSoftware, accessed Oct 2026](https://www.comparasoftware.es/inmovilla).
scale: More than 3,000 agencies on Inmovilla alone.
cost_impact: Portal fees were not verified (see Gaps).
driver_status: A market force. The CNMC 2021 decision was appealable to the Audiencia Nacional; I did not verify the outcome.
solved_today: Idealista (with Idealista Tools), Fotocasa, Habitaclia, Inmovilla, Witei and Mobilia. No verified prices.
software_solvable: Yes for the CRM and listing-syndication layer. No for portal market power.
confidence: Low. The key evidence is from 2021 and current fee data is missing.

title: Rent caps in declared tense zones and limits on annual updates
who: Individual landlords (autónomo-scale), large holders (*grandes tenedores*: 5 or more homes in Catalonia's zones, more than 10 nationally), agencies and property managers.
where:
- **Catalonia:** 271 municipalities, plus 53 more declared by Resolución TER/3740/2026 (DOGC 19 Oct 2026), pending publication in the BOE. Examples include Martorell, Sant Andreu de la Barca, Tordera and Vila-seca.
- **País Vasco:** 17–19 municipalities, depending on the source, including Bilbao, Vitoria-Gasteiz, Donostia, Errenteria and Irun. Pasaia, Zestoa and Arrasate were added from 28 Apr 2026.
- **Navarra:** 21 municipalities since July 2025, including Pamplona, Tudela and Zizur Mayor.
- **Galicia:** A Coruña since July 2025. Santiago from 29 Jul 2026 is reported but uncertain.
- **Asturias:** Gijón, Avilés, Llanes, Gozón and Cabrales, from 30 Jul 2026 to 30 Jul 2029, in some cases for specific neighbourhoods only.
- Sources: the regional lists come from secondary blog sources ([Arrenta](https://www.arrenta.es/blog/mercado-legislacion/listado-de-municipios-en-zonas-tensionadas-en-espana/); [Inmostats](https://inmostats.com/alquiler/zonas-tensionadas); [Vivara](https://www.vivara.io/blog/legal/zona-tensionada-alquiler/)). The official ministry page refused automated access with a 403 error ([MIVAU SERPAVI](https://www.mivau.gob.es/vivienda/alquila-bien-es-tu-derecho/serpavi/consultar-zonas-de-mercado-residencial-tensionado)).
- Idealista's Q3 2026 report classifies San Sebastián, A Coruña, Bilbao, Pamplona, Vitoria, Tarragona, Lleida, Barcelona and Girona as declared-tense markets. It treats Madrid, Valencia, Málaga, Sevilla, Alicante and Palma as not tense — [idealista, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/10/20/919563-la-oferta-de-alquiler-permanente-cae-un-10-en-un-ano-y-la-de-temporada-ya-supone-un).
reality: For each new contract, the landlord must find the last rent paid in the past five years and update it, or look up the state reference index. They must disclose both to the tenant, and they can only raise the rent by up to 10% in specific cases. Annual updates can no longer exceed the IRAV, a new official index for rent updates, and are capped at 2% unless the parties agree otherwise.
evidence:
- Catalonia rules — [OCU, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.ocu.org/fincas-y-casas/gestion/alquiler/analisis/2026/10/nuevas-zonas-tensionadas-cataluna):
- Homes rented in the last five years: the new rent is capped at the previous rent plus the legal update.
- Homes not rented in five years: capped at the reference index.
- Large holders (5 or more homes) are subject to whichever limit is stricter.
- Up to +10% is allowed for qualifying renovation, energy or accessibility works, or contracts of 10 years or more.
- Landlords must disclose the previous rent, the index and the applicable limits.
- Declarations last three years.
- LAU arts. 17.6–17.9 set the caps in tense zones. They were amended by RDL 29/2026 (art. 3.10), following Ley 12/2023. Art. 18 says updates "no podrá exceder del resultado de aplicar la variación porcentual" ("may not exceed the result of applying the percentage change") of the IRAV — [BOE consolidated LAU](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1994-26003).
- RDL 29/2026 adds — [idealista, 13 Oct 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/10/13/918359-que-cambia-para-los-propietarios-con-los-decretos-prorrogas-tope-al-alquiler-del-2):
- For updates due before 31 Dec 2027, the increase is capped at 2% unless agreed otherwise.
- If the rent already exceeds the reference index, "no procederá la aplicación de incremento alguno" ("no increase at all may be applied").
- In tense zones, permanent rental supply is falling fastest. In the year to Q3 2026: San Sebastián −52%, A Coruña −41%, Bilbao −41%, Pamplona −33%, Barcelona −22% — [idealista, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/10/20/919563-la-oferta-de-alquiler-permanente-cae-un-10-en-un-ano-y-la-de-temporada-ya-supone-un).
scale: Catalonia alone has 271 municipalities, with 53 more pending. I found no count of landlords.
cost_impact: Rent foregone. Catalan sanctions for exceeding the caps were not verified.
driver_status:
- Ley 12/2023 and the regional declarations: in force.
- RDL 29/2026's 2% cap: in force since 8 Oct 2026, pending convalidation. The Basque nationalist party (PNV) has announced support, and the article says the decree has "más visos" ("better odds") of passing.
solved_today:
- Agencies and gestorías work out caps by hand.
- SERPAVI, the state reference-price index.
- Lawyers.
- No prices.
software_solvable: Yes. An address-level cap calculator, history of the last contract, IRAV and 2% update engine, and disclosure templates. The rules change often, which makes software more valuable, not less.
confidence: High on the rules. Medium on municipality counts.

title: Rapid-fire decree changes (RDL 26–29/2026) force landlords to rewrite contracts and processes
who: All landlords, whether individuals or companies; agencies; property managers; rent-guarantee and insurance firms.
where: National.
reality:
Within three weeks, two decrees were published, repealed by Congress and re-issued. Landlords must now handle a series of new rules:
- Tenant-requested extensions.
- Small repairs that are now the landlord's job.
- No passing property tax (IBI) on to tenants.
- A tenant right to leave after six months without penalty.
- Limits on guarantees.
- A possible automatic 5/7-year renewal with compensation for refusing it.
evidence:
- RDL 29/2026 (in force 8 Oct 2026) — [idealista, 13 Oct 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/10/13/918359-que-cambia-para-los-propietarios-con-los-decretos-prorrogas-tope-al-alquiler-del-2):
- An extraordinary extension of up to two years, in annual steps, for primary-residence leases ending before 31 Dec 2028, if the tenant is up to date with payments, including the previous eight months.
- Deposit (*fianza*) of one month plus at most two months of additional guarantees. Rent-default insurance can no longer be demanded as a guarantee.
- Small repairs from ordinary use move to the landlord.
- IBI cannot be passed on to the tenant.
- The tenant can leave after six months without compensation.
- Luxury homes (over 300 m², or rent above 5.5 times the minimum wage, SMI) come under the general regime.
- Purchases by large holders and entities at under 70% of market value are restricted until 31 Dec 2030.
- Optional municipal property-tax surcharges on empty homes (up to 50%, and 100% or 150% in some cases).
- The BOE consolidated text confirms the RDL 29/2026 changes: art. 36.5 (additional guarantee "no podrá exceder de dos mensualidades", may not exceed two months' rent) and a new art. 36.7 — [BOE consolidated LAU](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1994-26003).
- RDL 28/2026 (due 15 Nov 2026) would add automatic renewal at the tenant's option: 5 years for individual landlords and 7 for companies. A landlord who refuses must pay up to 12 months' rent, or one month per year of contract if that is higher. One party needed for the vote has said it will vote against, and the interviewee in the article expects it to be "un brindis al sol" ("an empty gesture") — [idealista, 13 Oct 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/10/13/918359-que-cambia-para-los-propietarios-con-los-decretos-prorrogas-tope-al-alquiler-del-2).
scale: Every residential lease. I found no landlord count.
cost_impact:
- Re-papering contracts.
- Lost flexibility.
- Up to 12 months' rent in compensation if RDL 28/2026 enters into force.
- Rent-default insurance can no longer be used as a guarantee.
driver_status:
- RDL 29/2026: in force, pending convalidation.
- RDL 28/2026: scheduled for 15 Nov 2026, likely to fail.
- RDL 26/2026 and 27/2026: repealed on 2 Oct 2026.
- General elections on 29 Nov 2026, as reported by idealista.
solved_today: Lawyers, agencies and owners' associations. No prices found.
software_solvable: Yes. A contract-clause engine, alerts for extension requests and deadlines, and versioned templates tied to the law in force on each date.
confidence: High on content, from the BOE and idealista. Status is volatile.

title: Seasonal-rental crackdown and registration whiplash
who: Small landlords letting seasonally or by the room; seasonal and coliving operators; agencies. Tourist rentals are covered by the hospitality researcher.
where: National, plus Catalonia (regional law in force since 2 Jan 2026) and Navarra (bill registered May 2026).
reality:
- From July 2025, owners needed a registration number for seasonal and tourist rentals.
- In May 2026 the Supreme Court annulled it, and owners are now chasing refunds.
- Since 8 Oct 2026, a seasonal lease must state and prove its reason and last no more than 12 months. Otherwise it counts as a primary-residence lease, with long minimum terms and rent caps.
evidence:
- The registration system (Registro Único, RD 1312/2024) applied from 1 Jul 2025. By February 2026, about 420,000 registration numbers had been issued and more than 80,000 refused, some of them social-housing (VPO) homes — [idealista, 22 Feb 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/02/22/884998-registradores-detecta-vpo-entre-los-pisos-turisticos-que-han-solicitado-el-codigo).
- Supreme Court judgment 620/2026 (reported 21 May 2026) annulled the registry and the registration number as an invasion of regional powers. The appeal was brought by the Generalitat Valenciana. The court kept the Ventanilla Única Digital (single digital data window) and the duty for platforms to send data — [idealista, 21 May 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/05/21/898563-el-supremo-tumba-el-registro-unico-de-alquiler-de-corta-duracion-por-invadir).
- After the ruling, more than 100,000 tourist licences were reactivated. The tourist-flat association Fevitur estimates compensation claims above €160m, and owners are seeking refunds of the fees they paid — [idealista tag page (22 May and 5 Jun 2026 items)](https://www.idealista.com/news/etiquetas/alquiler-de-temporada).
- Catalonia's regulation of seasonal and room rentals took effect on 2 Jan 2026. It caps rents for all residential leases regardless of length and requires seasonal contracts to state and prove their purpose. Experts say it has already cut supply. Seasonal supply fell 63% in Girona, 58% in Tarragona and 37% in Barcelona in the year to Q3 2026 — [idealista tag page](https://www.idealista.com/news/etiquetas/alquiler-de-temporada); [idealista, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/10/20/919563-la-oferta-de-alquiler-permanente-cae-un-10-en-un-ano-y-la-de-temporada-ya-supone-un).
- RDL 29/2026 rules for seasonal and room leases — [idealista, 13 Oct 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/10/13/918359-que-cambia-para-los-propietarios-con-los-decretos-prorrogas-tope-al-alquiler-del-2):
- Seasonal leases become housing leases under Title II of the LAU.
- They need a proven reason for being temporary, last more than 31 days and generally no more than 12.
- More than 12 months without justification, or more than two consecutive contracts with the same parties, turns the lease into a primary-residence lease from signature.
- For room rentals, the rents for all rooms together cannot exceed the rent for the whole home. In tense zones and for large holders, the reference index applies.
- A Coruña appeal court overturned an eviction because the purpose of the lease, not its length, defines a seasonal rental — [idealista tag page, 6 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/etiquetas/alquiler-de-temporada).
scale: About 420,000 registration numbers issued (tourist and seasonal combined). 1.15 million people live in seasonal or room rentals ([idealista, 7 Sep 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/finanzas/economia/2026/09/07/912998-consumo-estima-que-mas-de-un-millon-de-personas-vive-en-alquiler-de-temporada-o-de)).
cost_impact: Registration fees, amount not verified. Risk of a lease being reclassified as a 5/7-year primary-residence lease under capped rent.
driver_status:
- RD 1312/2024 registry: annulled by the Supreme Court in May 2026.
- EU Regulation 2024/1028 on platform data sharing: still relevant.
- Catalan law: in force since 2 Jan 2026; its number was not verified.
- RDL 29/2026: in force, pending convalidation.
- Navarra bill: in parliament.
solved_today: Lawyers, gestorías and specialised seasonal agencies. No prices.
software_solvable: Partly. Recording the reason for the lease, tracking duration and consecutive contracts, and checking caps for room rentals.

title: Unpaid rent, slow evictions, the new negotiation step and the on-off eviction moratorium
who: Small individual landlords, agencies managing rentals, rent-guarantee firms.
where:
National. By region:
- Catalonia: 6,814 evictions (about 26.6% of the national total).
- Andalucía: 3,782.
- Comunitat Valenciana: 2,992.
- Madrid: 2,267 (−17.7%).
- País Vasco: 974 (+60.2%).
reality: After about seven months of unpaid rent, the landlord must first attempt a documented negotiation (MASC), then sue. They may then face a vulnerability-based suspension. During all of this they keep paying the mortgage, IBI and community fees.
evidence:
- CGPJ (judiciary council) data for 2025 — [CGPJ, 20 Mar 2026](https://www.poderjudicial.es/cgpj/es/Poder-Judicial/Consejo-General-del-Poder-Judicial/Oficina-de-Comunicacion/Notas-de-prensa/Las-ejecuciones-hipotecarias-y-los-concursos-registrados-en-los-organos-judiciales-crecieron-en-2025-un-30---respecto-al-ano-anterior); [Forbes](https://forbes.es/economia/893652/los-desahucios-caen-un-11-en-2025-hasta-los-25-540-segun-cgpj/):
- 25,540 evictions carried out (−11%). Of these, 18,317 (71.7%) arose from rental-law (LAU) cases (−10.9%) and 4,346 (17%) from mortgage foreclosures.
- Data note: the "other causes" figure as extracted (1,877) makes the parts add up to 24,540. The percentages fit 25,540, which suggests "other" is really 2,877.
- Q4 2025: courts received 2,732 requests to suspend an eviction for vulnerability. They granted 472 suspensions: 221 under art. 1 of RDL 11/2020, 84 under art. 1 bis, and 167 under art. 441.5 of the civil procedure law (LEC).
- País Vasco: 974 evictions (+60.2%), with rental-arrears cases up 43.8% — [CGPJ TSJ País Vasco](https://www.poderjudicial.es/cgpj/es/Poder-Judicial/Tribunales-Superiores-de-Justicia/TSJ-Pais-Vasco/En-Portada/Los-lanzamientos-practicados-en-el-Pais-Vasco-en-2025-crecieron-un-60-2--respecto-al-ano-anterior).
- Observatorio del Alquiler (Fundación Alquiler Seguro), tenant arrears in 2025 — [idealista, 5 Mar 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/03/05/887280-los-inquilinos-morosos-ya-deben-siete-meses-de-renta-una-media-de-8-490-euros-en):
- Average debt per defaulting tenant: €8,489.3, about seven months' rent.
- By region: Catalonia €11,619.9; Madrid €10,420.4; Baleares €10,354.4; Barcelona province €14,036.5. In Murcia, defaulters owe more than nine months' rent.
- Inconsistency: idealista reports +16.5% year on year. Against the 2024 average of €7,957.6 ([idealista, 21 Feb 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/02/21/832887-por-que-cataluna-es-la-region-de-espana-con-mas-inquilinos-morosos)), the rise is about 6.7%.
- Prior negotiation (MASC): Ley Orgánica 1/2025 took effect on 3 Apr 2025. Art. 5.2 makes prior negotiation a precondition for filing, exempting only the matters it lists — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2025-76):
- The exemptions include "la tutela sumaria de la tenencia o de la posesión" (summary protection of possession), the remedy used against squatters, and the juicio cambiario (bill-of-exchange claims).
- Eviction for non-payment is not exempt.
- The lawyer José Ramón Zurdo (ANA) says "los procesos se han complicado todavía más" ("the processes have become even more complicated") — [idealista, 15 Apr 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/04/15/886094-ley-antiokupas-ha-mejorado-algo-todo-lo-que-tienes-que-saber).
- Moratorium status — [BOE consolidated RDL 11/2020](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2020-4208):
- Art. 1 of RDL 11/2020 ran "hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2025" ("until 31 December 2025").
- The extension in RDL 16/2025 (23 Dec 2025) was repealed by a Congress resolution of 27 Jan 2026.
- A second attempt, RDL 2/2026 (3 Feb 2026), was repealed on 26 Feb 2026.
- RDL 29/2026 art. 2 creates a new suspension regime until 31 Dec 2030 — [idealista, 13 Oct 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/10/13/918359-que-cambia-para-los-propietarios-con-los-decretos-prorrogas-tope-al-alquiler-del-2):
- Economically vulnerable tenants evicted for non-payment: the administration must offer an alternative within two months or pay the debt, otherwise it becomes the debtor.
- Other claimants: suspensions of up to three years, reviewed every 12 months. Where the landlord is an individual, the administration covers unpaid rent, utilities and court costs, but not lost profit.
- Funds that bought homes below market value: suspension without compensation.
scale: 18,317 rental-arrears evictions in 2025. I found no count of defaulted contracts.
cost_impact:
- About €8,500 average debt, plus legal costs.
- Lawyers describe 18–24 months or more for the slow route, cited for squatters and holdover tenants (*inquiokupas*) — [idealista, 15 Apr 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/04/15/886094-ley-antiokupas-ha-mejorado-algo-todo-lo-que-tienes-que-saber).
- I found no CGPJ average duration for rental-arrears evictions.
driver_status:
- LO 1/2025 MASC: in force.
- RDL 11/2020 suspension: lapsed after 31 Dec 2025, apart from transitional cases.
- RDL 29/2026 suspension to 2030: in force since 8 Oct 2026, pending convalidation.
solved_today:
- Rent-guarantee firms such as Alquiler Seguro.
- Rent-default insurance, prices not verified, which can no longer be required as a tenant guarantee under RDL 29/2026.
- Lawyers, tenant-arrears registers and agencies.
software_solvable: Partly. Screening, early-arrears alerts, generating and logging the MASC offer (for example a *burofax*, a certified letter), and case files ready for court. Court speed is outside software's reach.

title: Squatting (okupación) risk and slow recovery
who: Small landlords with empty or second homes; sellers; agencies, since squatted homes are hard to sell.
where: National. Most civil filings come from Andalucía, ahead of Catalonia, and Barcelona is the most affected province. Squatted listings are highest in Girona (8.9% of homes for sale), then Barcelona (3.7%) and Madrid (2.4%).
reality: Fast removal is possible only for a home that is someone's dwelling (*allanamiento de morada*) and only with quick action. Otherwise recovery runs through civil or criminal courts for 18–24 months or more.
evidence:
- Civil squatting filings (CGPJ data):
- 1,401 in the first nine months of 2025 (−21%), which coincided with the new prior-negotiation rule — [idealista, 16 Dec 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/12/16/876563-los-juzgados-reciben-mas-de-1-400-demandas-por-okupacion-de-viviendas-este-ano).
- 487 in Q2 2025 (−24%), with Andalucía overtaking Catalonia — [idealista, 17 Oct 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/10/17/867671-andalucia-adelanta-a-cataluna-como-la-region-con-mas-demandas-por-okupacion-de).
- 460 in Q1 2026 (−22.3%), the lowest first quarter in the series. Experts note criminal cases are excluded and negotiations delay filings — [idealista, 15 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/07/15/906009-las-demandas-por-okupacion-de-viviendas-se-desploman-pero-el-problema-persiste-los).
- 23,010 squatted homes were listed for sale in Q3 2025, about 3% of homes for sale — [idealista, 21 Oct 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/10/21/868295-el-numero-de-viviendas-okupadas-a-la-venta-supera-las-23-000-hasta-septiembre-donde).
- The 2025 "ley antiokupas" promised removal within 15 days through fast-track trials. Lawyers say the fast route works in "dos o tres semanas" ("two or three weeks") only for dwellings and with quick action; otherwise it becomes "un auténtico calvario de un año y medio, dos años o incluso más" ("a real ordeal of a year and a half, two years or even more") — [idealista, 15 Apr 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/04/15/886094-ley-antiokupas-ha-mejorado-algo-todo-lo-que-tienes-que-saber).
- Squatting victims' group PAO: two express-eviction bills have piled up 139 extensions of the amendment deadline — [idealista, 10 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/07/10/905839-los-afectados-por-la-okupacion-denuncian-el-secuestro-parlamentario-de-las-leyes-de).
- The idealista/ARAG anti-squatting policy costs €39.85 a year. It covers up to €2,000 of urgent eviction costs and €12,000 of legal defence — [idealista, 13 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/07/13/904588-seguro-antiokupas-cuanto-cuesta-que-cubre-y-cuanto-protege) (promotional source).
scale: Inference: about 1,800–1,900 civil filings a year, based on 1,401 in nine months, plus criminal cases. 23,010 squatted listings.
cost_impact: 18–24 or more months of lost use and legal costs. Squatted homes sell at a discount (inference).
driver_status:
- LO 1/2025: in force; prior negotiation is not required for summary possession claims.
- The "ley antiokupas" (2025): I did not verify its exact legal number.
- Pending express-eviction bills: inference, they likely lapsed with the dissolution of the Cortes.
solved_today:
- Cheap insurance (€39.85 a year).
- Lawyers.
- Private eviction-mediation firms (*desokupa*), not verified.
software_solvable: Mostly no. Vacancy monitoring and legal-workflow tools help at the edges; the bottleneck is the courts.

title: Tourist-flat approvals under the new three-fifths rule (Ley de Propiedad Horizontal)
who: Owners' communities and administradores de fincas (micro firms); small landlords who want to let for tourist use.
where: National law (the LPH). Barcelona funds communities that vote to ban tourist flats. Tourist hotspots are presumably most affected (inference; not verified).
reality: Any owner who wants to start tourist letting now needs the community's express prior approval. Communities call meetings to approve, condition or ban it by a three-fifths majority, and they may set special fees.
evidence:
- The Ley de Propiedad Horizontal (LPH), as amended by Ley Orgánica 1/2025 (final provisions 1 and 4.2), effective 3 Apr 2025 — [BOE consolidated LPH](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1960-10906):
- Art. 7.3: the owner "deberá obtener previamente la aprobación expresa de la comunidad de propietarios" ("must first obtain the express approval of the owners' community").
- Art. 17.12: such resolutions need "el voto favorable de las tres quintas partes del total de los propietarios" ("the favourable vote of three fifths of all owners"), who must also hold three fifths of the ownership shares.
- The same majority can set special fees or raise the owner's share of costs by up to 20%.
- "Estos acuerdos no tendrán efectos retroactivos" ("these resolutions shall not have retroactive effect").
- Barcelona raised its budget for grants to communities that ban tourist flats from €56,000 to €256,000, up to €2,500 per community, available until 31 December — [idealista, 18 Aug 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/08/18/910490-barcelona-quintuplica-las-ayudas-a-las-comunidades-de-propietarios-para-prohibir).
- More than 80,000 national registration numbers were refused (tourist and seasonal combined; reasons not broken down) — [idealista, 22 Feb 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/02/22/884998-registradores-detecta-vpo-entre-los-pisos-turisticos-que-han-solicitado-el-codigo).
scale: Every community with a tourist flat or an application for one. Not counted.
cost_impact: Meetings, legal advice and disputes. Barcelona pays up to €2,500 per community to cover the cost of such votes.
driver_status: LO 1/2025, in force since 3 Apr 2025.
solved_today: Administradores and lawyers. Barcelona's grants pay part of the cost.
software_solvable: Partly. Calculating majorities by owners and shares, logging votes, generating minutes and certificates. Disputes stay legal.
confidence: High on the rule. Medium on scale. Overlap: the hospitality researcher covers tourist flats in depth.

title: Community arrears and the harder recovery process (special payment claim plus negotiation step)
who: Communities and administradores; also owners who don't pay.
where: National. The example ruling comes from Cantabria.
reality: Administradores chase unpaid fees and one-off levies (*derramas*), issue debt certificates and file a special fast-track payment claim (*monitorio*). Since April 2025 they probably must also try a documented negotiation first.
evidence:
- LPH art. 21 gives communities a special *monitorio* claim for unpaid fees. It needs a debt certificate signed by the secretary with the president's approval. If the owner opposes the claim, the community can obtain a preventive attachment of assets without posting a bond. The reserve fund must be at least 10% of the last ordinary budget (art. 9.1.f, Ley 10/2022) — [BOE consolidated LPH](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1960-10906).
- LO 1/2025 art. 5.2 lists the claims exempt from prior negotiation. The domestic *monitorio* is not among them; only the European payment order is exempt, in art. 5.3 — [BOE LO 1/2025](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2025-76). Interpretation: community debt claims appear to need a negotiation attempt first. I did not verify how courts apply this.
- The Audiencia Provincial de Cantabria upheld a 20% surcharge on a defaulting owner: €2,775 of debt plus €555 surcharge, with interest and costs — [idealista, 2 Sep 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/09/02/911748-un-tribunal-avala-cobrar-un-recargo-del-20-a-un-vecino-moroso).
- Unpaid *derramas* are a recurring theme in consumer coverage — [idealista, 21 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/06/21/901209-que-pasa-si-un-vecino-no-paga-una-derrama-lo-que-puedes-hacer).
scale: I found no national total for community arrears.
cost_impact: Not quantified nationally.
driver_status: LPH art. 21 and LO 1/2025, both in force.
solved_today: Administradores, lawyers and community management software (prices not verified).
software_solvable: Yes. Arrears dashboards, automated reminders, negotiation-offer generation and logging, and debt certificates.

title: Administradores' documentary and compliance burden in a fragmented, ageing profession
who: Administradores de fincas, typically micro offices with 50–60 communities each, and the consolidators buying them.
where: National.
reality: Each building creates obligations: coordination with suppliers (CAE), data protection, accessibility works, energy-renovation grants, technical certifications, maintenance deadlines, and the relationship with each supplier. All of it is tracked by hand across email, paper and separate platforms, and appointments are renewed annually by vote rather than by contract.
evidence:
- Scale and consolidation — [idealista, 30 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/empresas/2026/07/30/906830-50-empresas-compradas-al-ano-y-menos-del-3-de-cuota-asi-es-inmho-en-el-sector):
- About 1 million communities and about 16,000 administradores, most managing 50–60 communities.
- inmho manages 15,000 communities, under 3% of the market, and the second operator about half that. It bought 50 firms last year.
- Firms with more than 500–600 communities used to be "muy raro" ("very rare").
- Many administradores have managed the same buildings for decades "sin un plan de sucesión claro" ("without a clear succession plan").
- An administrador handles in cash terms about 20 times what they bill.
- Rental management commissions run 6–10% of rent.
- Burdens named by Conversia, a compliance services company, through its administradores-de-fincas director — [idealista, 17 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/06/17/901380-administradores-de-fincas-el-cambio-estructural-que-esta-redefiniendo-la-gestion-de):
- "Coordinación de actividades empresariales" (CAE with suppliers), "protección de datos", accessibility work, energy-renovation grants, certifications, "seguimiento de vencimientos" (deadline tracking), "control de cumplimiento" (compliance control) and supplier coordination.
- Information is scattered across "correos electrónicos, documentación física, múltiples plataformas independientes" ("emails, paper documents, many separate platforms").
- Any incident can become "jurídico o reputacional" (a legal or reputational matter).
scale: About 16,000 administradores and 1 million communities.
cost_impact: Not quantified: no hours or euro figures found.
driver_status: A build-up of obligations across the LPH, PRL/CAE, data protection, accessibility rules and grant rules, all in force. Consolidation is a market force.
solved_today:
- Sector software: Gesfincas, Fincas Pro and Comunidad Feliz were named in the brief, but I could not verify their prices or complaints.
- Compliance consultancies such as Conversia (prices not found).
- Consolidators.
software_solvable: Yes. A single compliance and maintenance calendar per building, onboarding suppliers' CAE documents, and portals for owners. Consolidators need standard tooling.
confidence: Medium. Scale is solid; the burden is described qualitatively by a vendor.

title: Meetings, minutes and notices: no specific legal cover for online meetings
who: Administradores and owners' communities. Owners who live elsewhere, have reduced mobility or have been affected by emergencies such as the DANA floods are most affected.
where: National.
reality: Meetings are still held mainly in person, and online attendance has no explicit legal basis. Governance disputes reach the courts: for example, the Audiencia Provincial de Bizkaia annulled a resolution that left a community without a president.
evidence:
- The LPH (arts. 16–17) does not expressly regulate online meetings. It refers only to communications by "cualquier medio que permita tener constancia de su recepción" ("any means that leaves proof of receipt") — [BOE consolidated LPH](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1960-10906).
- Congress agreed on 26 May 2026 to consider a PP bill, already passed by the Senate. It would allow online or hybrid meetings, an electronic address for notices and a digital minutes book (*Libro de Actas Digital*). The administradores' general council (CGCAFE) says the practice "carece de una cobertura legal específica" ("lacks specific legal cover") and calls the change a "demanda histórica" ("long-standing demand") of the profession. The bill was at the amendment stage — [idealista, 27 May 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/finanzas/economia/2026/05/27/899214-el-congreso-tramita-una-ley-del-pp-para-permitir-juntas-de-vecinos-telematicas-con-el).
- A community cannot be left without a president for lack of agreement (Audiencia Provincial de Bizkaia) — [idealista, 3 Aug 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/08/03/907818-una-comunidad-de-propietarios-no-puede-quedarse-sin-presidente-por-falta-de-acuerdo).
scale: About 1 million communities hold at least an annual meeting. Inference: the LPH requires one per year, a requirement not re-checked here.
cost_impact: Not quantified.
driver_status: The bill was admitted in May 2026. Inference: it likely lapsed when the Cortes were dissolved for the 29 Nov 2026 elections ([idealista, 13 Oct 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/10/13/918359-que-cambia-para-los-propietarios-con-los-decretos-prorrogas-tope-al-alquiler-del-2)).
solved_today: Hybrid meetings held informally, paper minutes books, and software from administradores' vendors (prices not verified).
software_solvable: Partly. Meeting, voting and minutes tools exist, but legal certainty depends on the law changing.
confidence: Medium-high on the gap. The bill's status is inferred.

title: Coordinating works and maintenance (lifts, accessibility, energy renovation) in communities
who: Administradores, community presidents, and contractors and installers working for communities.
where: National. Grants are regional and municipal.
reality: Communities have to approve, finance and supervise large jobs such as lifts or energy upgrades. That means running grant applications, coordinating suppliers' safety documentation, and handling neighbours who don't pay their share (see CON-23).
evidence:
- Installing a lift costs €30,000–60,000 on average and takes 2–4 months, with grants of up to 75% in some cases. It needs a simple majority — [idealista, 14 Oct 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/10/14/913707-como-instalar-un-ascensor-en-tu-edificio-paso-a-paso).
- Administradores report that energy-renovation and accessibility work is getting harder to manage because of bureaucracy and changing rules — [idealista/Conversia, 17 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/06/17/901380-administradores-de-fincas-el-cambio-estructural-que-esta-redefiniendo-la-gestion-de).
- Grant payment delays affect communities and agents (see CON-07) — [Justicia de Aragón, 15 Jun 2026](https://eljusticiadearagon.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Q25-753-08.pdf).
scale: Not quantified.
cost_impact: €30,000–60,000 per lift, plus weeks of coordination.
driver_status: Accessibility and energy policies and NextGenerationEU programmes, in force. I did not verify the new lift technical rule (RD 355/2024) or any mandatory inspection or adaptation deadlines.
solved_today: Administradores, engineering firms, rehabilitation agents and the colegios' offices.
software_solvable: Partly. Comparing quotes, tracking works and grants, and collecting suppliers' CAE documents.

title: TIE fingerprint appointment bottleneck after approval
who: non-EU foreign workers, digital nomads, students and family members after a favourable resolution; the employer HR teams and relocation agencies that manage them (companies of any size; volumes per company not quantified).
where: National. Worst in Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia (city/province offices). Málaga is mid-range; Alicante, Illes Balears and Canarias are shorter but still weeks.
reality: The permit is granted, but the card needs an in-person police fingerprint appointment. Slots appear at random times and disappear within minutes, so applicants and agencies refresh ICP+ for weeks, pay alert services, or travel to small-town stations. Without the TIE, people cannot re-enter Spain after travel (EXP-17) or get an FNMT certificate (EXP-12).
evidence:
- Barcelona: "Hay gente que lleva tres meses buscando una cita de huellas" — [Crónica Global, 30 Jun 2026](https://cronicaglobal.elespanol.com/politica/20260630/avalancha-solicitudes-regularizacion-colapsar-servicios-extranjeria-barcelona/1003742774382_0.html)
- 3–6 months in Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia — [RemoteFromSpain, 29 Jul 2026](https://remotefromspain.com/tie-appointment-shortage-spain-2026/); [IG Abogados, early 2026](https://igabogadosextranjeria.com/toma-de-huellas-en-extranjeria-2026-que-es-y-por-que-cuesta-tanto-conseguir-cita/) (both commercial)
- Manual-search estimates: Madrid 4–12 weeks; Barcelona 3–10; Málaga 3–8; Valencia, Alicante and Baleares 2–4; Las Palmas 2–3 — [HayCita, 23 Oct 2026](https://haycita.es/guia/tiempo-espera-cita-extranjeria)
- Slots detected over 138 days: Madrid 915, Barcelona 361, Alicante 204, Valencia 95, Baleares 57, Málaga 32, Santa Cruz de Tenerife 15, Las Palmas 3; "under 2 minutes" to sell out — [CitaEx, 23 Oct 2026](https://citaex.com/disponibilidad-citas)
scale: 3,497,284 general-regime residents with documents who hold or renew TIEs (31 Dec 2025) — [La Moncloa, 20 Mar 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/serviciosdeprensa/notasprensa/inclusion/paginas/2026/200326-poblacion-extranjera-con-residencia.aspx). Up to 1,174,978 regularisation applicants who will need cards if granted — [La Moncloa, 2 Jul 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/serviciosdeprensa/notasprensa/inclusion/paginas/2026/020726-balance-regularizacion-extraordinaria.aspx). Annual first-TIE issuance not found.
cost_impact: Weeks to six months of delay; black-market slots at €15–500 (EXP-02); travel blocked; a legal window of about one month or 30 working days after notification (single-source), with documented attempts accepted as justification (IG Abogados).
driver_status: Administrative practice: Policía Nacional capacity and the design of the ICP+ booking system. TIE obligations sit in RD 1155/2024 (in force since 20 May 2025). Countermeasure: police auto-assignment pilot since 8 Oct 2026 for 10% of files in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Alicante, Málaga and Murcia (pilot). Personalised codes: announced Dec 2025, unconfirmed.
solved_today: Refreshing ICP+ yourself; alert services (HayCita from €14.99; CitaEx deposit model); gestorías (full TIE service €90 incl. fee at gestoriadeextranjeria.es; €80–160 per Cirera); relocation admin packs (€400 Barcelona per Locallista; €1,200 + IVA Madrid per Relocation Angel); illegal resale. Complaints: resold slots get cancelled with no refund (ConseguirCita); vendors claim privileged channels without evidence (JuroSpain).
software_solvable: Partly. Software cannot add police capacity, but it can track the 20-day auto-assignment window, read assignment notices, pre-check documents so the visit is not wasted, and suggest alternative stations. Automated booking is legally and strategically risky.
confidence: High that the pain exists; medium on the exact waits.

title: Bot hoarding and resale of appointments ("mafias de citas")
who: Everyone who needs an ICP+ slot; low-income migrants are most exposed, but expats also pay intermediaries.
where: National. Prosecuted cases in Barcelona and Valencia (2023); Alicante (17 arrests), Murcia and Valencia (2024); Teulada, Alicante (Dec 2024).
reality: Bots scan ICP+, grab slots and resell them through TikTok, Telegram, locutorios and some gestorías. Legitimate users mostly see "no hay citas disponibles" ("no appointments available").
evidence:
- 2024 ring: 21 arrested; €15–30 a slot; about €9,000 a month per member; charges of daños informáticos and others — [Infobae / Europa Press, 27 Nov 2024](https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2024/11/27/una-veintena-de-detenidos-por-la-venta-fraudulenta-de-citas-de-extranjeria-con-bots-bloqueando-el-servidor-oficial/)
- 2023 ring: 69 arrested; €30–200 — [14ymedio](https://www.14ymedio.com/internacional/detenidas-espana-bloquear-extranjeros-revenderlas_1_1094744.html) (via search snippet)
- 2025: about €30 per slot on TikTok and Telegram, with reports of €100 — [Antinodo, 28 Jun 2025](https://antinodo.tech/p/el-mercado-negro-de-citas-para-extranjeria)
- 2026 quotes: €80–500 — [IG Abogados](https://igabogadosextranjeria.com/toma-de-huellas-en-extranjeria-2026-que-es-y-por-que-cuesta-tanto-conseguir-cita/); €50–150 — [JuroSpain, Jan 2026](https://jurospain.com/cita-previa-mafia-spain-solutions/)
- CES report on automated hoarding — [El Correo Gallego, 28 Dec 2025](https://www.elcorreogallego.es/sociedad/2025/12/28/gobierno-estudia-implantar-2026-codigos-125198426.html)
scale: The share of slots captured is unknown. The market reaches TikTok, Telegram and Wallapop (Antinodo).
cost_impact: €15–500 per slot; fraud risk; denial of a free public service ("principio de gratuidad").
driver_status: ICP+ booking is not bound to identity. Penal Code offences apply (in force). Personalised codes announced Dec 2025, unconfirmed. Police auto-assignment pilot since 8 Oct 2026.
solved_today: Police operations; workarounds through lawyers (Mercurio filing avoids appointments for applications, but not for fingerprinting); alert services.
software_solvable: No, at least not by a startup. The fix is identity binding and push assignment by the state, and anything near booking is legally exposed.

title: Regularisation surge (RD 316/2026) saturating offices, police and Mercurio, and the 2027 renewal cliff
who: Directly about 1.17M applicants. Indirectly every expat, employer and agency that shares the same Extranjería offices and police fingerprint units, plus employers of regularised workers, especially hostelería.
where: National. Applications: Cataluña 257,602; Madrid 202,424; C. Valenciana 167,286; Andalucía 161,557.
reality: About 1.17M applications in ten weeks landed on top of about 180,000 pending files, during an indefinite CCOO strike and Mercurio outages. Fingerprint appointments got scarcer, and data errors surface at the police stage. All initial permits last one year, so renewals bunch up in 2027.
evidence:
- 1,174,978 applications, 609,737 processed by 2 Jul 2026 — [La Moncloa, 2 Jul 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/serviciosdeprensa/notasprensa/inclusion/paginas/2026/020726-balance-regularizacion-extraordinaria.aspx)
- About 180,000 files pending beforehand; CCOO indefinite strike from 20 Apr 2026 — [Estrella Digital, 15 Apr 2026](https://www.estrelladigital.es/articulo/espana/caos-extranjeria-regularizacion-arranca-huelga/20260415082226445302.html)
- Mercurio outages on day 1 — [Law&Trends, 17 Apr 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/administrativo/largas-colas-en-los-consulados-y-las-caidas-de-la-plataforma-mercurio-protagonistas-de-la-primera-jornada-de-1.html)
- On 2027 renewals: "El volumen de expedientes que nos puede venir va a ser inmenso" ("the volume of files coming our way could be immense"); CCOO also reported recording errors and duplicated NIEs — [Crónica Global, 30 Jun 2026](https://cronicaglobal.elespanol.com/politica/20260630/avalancha-solicitudes-regularizacion-colapsar-servicios-extranjeria-barcelona/1003742774382_0.html)
- In Baleares, about 30% of the early-filed cases one lawyer analysed still lacked provisional authorisation in early October (her own estimate) — [Ara Balears, 22 Oct 2026](https://es.arabalears.cat/sociedad/retrasos-errores-trabas-burocraticas-complican-regularizacion-extraordinaria-migrantes_1_5886839.html)
- Counter-evidence: Catalonia's "plan de choque" cleared 99.8% of the ordinary files stuck before 16 Apr (Crónica Global).
scale: 1,174,978 applications; 159,097 new Social Security affiliates by 30 Jun 2026 (La Moncloa); 337,917 regularised affiliates by the end of Aug 2026 ([Funcas, via search snippet](https://www.funcas.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/NOTAPRENSA.pdf)).
cost_impact: Longer queues for everyone in 2026–2027. A renewal wave of up to roughly 1M one-year permits in 2027 (my inference from the one-year validity). Labour shortages are cited by employers: "Las empresas necesitan la inmigración como el agua que bebemos" ("companies need immigration like the water we drink"), Foment del Treball (Crónica Global).
driver_status: RD 316/2026 (BOE 15 Apr 2026) is in force. Filing closed on 30 Jun 2026, in-person corrections ended on 30 Sep 2026, and resolutions are ongoing. DGGM interpretive criteria were issued on 22 Apr and 18 May 2026.
solved_today: Lawyers filed 58% of e-applications, at €100–400 per file. The rest came through habilitated civil servants, gestores, free union and NGO collaborators, and 448 in-person points at Correos, Seguridad Social and Extranjería.
software_solvable: Partly. Software cannot fix capacity, but the 2027 renewal wave is a clear case for bulk tracking of renewal windows, reuse of documents and pre-validation.

title: Unpredictable, office-specific processing backlogs and missing queue data
who: Employer HR teams planning start dates; relocation agencies; foreign workers, families and students.
where: Office level. Madrid, Valencia and Illes Balears publish monthly queue PDFs. Barcelona, Málaga, Alicante, Las Palmas and Santa Cruz de Tenerife publish none.
reality: The same procedure can take 12 days in one province and 232 in another, and the biggest talent hub (Barcelona) publishes nothing. HR cannot give candidates a reliable start date.
evidence:
- Initial employee permit: Valencia 232 days against Baleares 12; reunification: Baleares 184, Valencia 76, Madrid 62; study stay: Madrid 75, Valencia 63 — [España Abogados compiling Delegación PDFs, 12 Oct 2026](https://espanaabogados.com/fechas-de-resolucion-de-tramites-de-extranjeria-en-espana/) (single compiler, but the underlying data is official)
- Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia named the hardest hit — [Jobbatical, 1 Sep 2026](https://www.jobbatical.com/blog/spain-immigration-crisis-appointment-delays)
- The Defensor del Pueblo's 2025 report lists "demoras en la tramitación de procedimientos" ("delays in processing") — [Defensor del Pueblo, via search snippet](https://www.defensordelpueblo.es/informe-anual/informe-anual-2025/)
scale: All general-regime filings (3.5M documented residents). The annual flow is not quantified.
cost_impact: Weeks to about 8 months of delay; lost or deferred hires (no hard data); "recurso" work for lawyers when deadlines lapse.
driver_status: Capacity against legal deadlines. The deadlines themselves conflict: two months with negative silence for reunification per art. 68.6 RD 1155/2024 in some sources, three months or 45 working days in others. RD 1155/2024 is in force.
solved_today: Lawyers' own trackers; blogs that compile dates (España Abogados; Parainmigrantes for Baleares); complaints to the Defensor del Pueblo.
software_solvable: Yes, for prediction and transparency. Parsing the public PDFs and adding anonymised case data from professional users yields an expected time to decision per office and procedure. Software cannot speed up decisions.

title: Divergent criteria between offices, police units and consulates
who: Lawyers, gestorías and HR teams filing in several provinces; applicants.
where: National, varying office by office (for example Baleares police units; consulates against Delegaciones).
reality: The same procedure triggers different document demands depending on the office or police unit, and offices have re-examined what a consulate had already checked.
evidence:
- The Defensor del Pueblo's 2025 work covered "la diversidad de criterios entre las oficinas de extranjería" ("the diversity of criteria between Extranjería offices") — [Defensor del Pueblo, via search snippet](https://www.defensordelpueblo.es/informe-anual/informe-anual-2025/)
- In Baleares, police offices reportedly differ on the documents they require — [Ara Balears, 22 Oct 2026](https://es.arabalears.cat/sociedad/retrasos-errores-trabas-burocraticas-complican-regularizacion-extraordinaria-migrantes_1_5886839.html)
- The DGGM issued Criterio 1/2025 (12 Sep 2025) specifically to stop consulates and Delegaciones assessing the same file twice — [Gestores Alicante PDF, via search snippet](https://www.gestoresalicante.org/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/CRITERIO-DE-GESTION-DGGM-RLOEX_DOBLE-APORTACION-DE-DOCU_MENTOS.pdf); [Polaris](https://polarisextranjeria.com/nuevo-reglamento-extranjeria-rd-1155-2024-balance-2024-2025)
scale: Not quantified.
cost_impact: Requests for more documents, repeat appointments, denials.
driver_status: Administrative practice. DGGM criteria are in force but not binding regulation.
solved_today: Local know-how held by lawyers and gestorías, which is plausibly their main moat (my inference).
software_solvable: Partly. A per-office requirements knowledge base, fed by professional users, is software; the inconsistency itself is not.

title: Fast-changing rules published through scattered channels
who: Immigration lawyers, gestorías, relocation agencies and corporate mobility teams (any size), plus well-informed applicants.
where: National (BOE, ministry pages, police, Delegaciones, DGT, AEAT), with provincial differences in practice.
reality: Rules change through BOE decrees and orders, DGGM "criterios", SEM "instrucciones", police notices circulated by bar associations, UGE threshold notes and court rulings. Professionals keep up through colegio newsletters and blogs.
evidence:
- By my count, at least 20 changes between May 2025 and Oct 2026:
- RD 1155/2024 in force (20 May 2025)
- DGT digital canje (20 May 2025)
- Criterios 1/2025, 2/2025, 4/2025 and 5/2025
- SEM 3/2025
- Criterio 1/2026 (5 Jan 2026)
- UGE thresholds (Jan and Jun 2026; Orden PJC/44/2026)
- Orden PJC/617/2025 (fees)
- Orden ISM/164/2026 (5 Mar 2026)
- RD 316/2026 (15 Apr 2026)
- Regularisation criteria (22 Apr and 18 May 2026)
- Transitional arraigo closed (20 May 2026)
- Instrucción 1/2026 (2 Jun 2026)
- Criterio of 22 Jul 2026
- STS 868/2026 (8 Jul 2026) and the second STS (29 Jul 2026), both in the BOE on 22 Sep 2026
- Criterio 2/2026 (7 Aug 2026)
- Police auto-assignment pilot (8 Oct 2026)
- Elections on 29 Nov 2026 stalling the homologación draft
- Sources: Section 3 table, mainly [Polaris](https://polarisextranjeria.com/nuevo-reglamento-extranjeria-rd-1155-2024-balance-2024-2025), [BOE](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2026-5128), [DGP notice via ICAB](https://www.icab.es/export/sites/icab/.galleries/documents-noticies/2026-INICIO-PROYECTO-PILOTO-ASIGNACION-AUTOMATICA-DE-CITA-PARA-TOMA-DE-HUELLA.pdf) and [ARC Legal](https://www.arc-legal.es/el-tribunal-supremo-anula-varios-preceptos-del-reglamento-de-extranjeria/)
- Outdated form versions after RD 1155/2024 are a common cause of document-correction requests — [GestoLab, 5 Jul 2026](https://www.gestolab.com/blog/formulario-ex-03-que-es-cuando-se-usa-y-como-rellenarlo-paso-a-paso)
- An offer below the threshold is a frequent cause of highly qualified permit denials — [Infoextranjeria, via search snippet](https://infoextranjeria.org/2026/06/11/actualizacion-del-umbral-salarial-para-profesionales-altamente-cualificados/)
scale: About 2,000 immigration lawyers in Catalonia and 5,925 ICAM lawyers on Mercurio — [Law&Trends, 17 Apr 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/administrativo/largas-colas-en-los-consulados-y-las-caidas-de-la-plataforma-mercurio-protagonistas-de-la-primera-jornada-de-1.html). The number of gestorías working in extranjería is unknown.
cost_impact: Each document-correction request adds 10 working days or more; denials when thresholds or forms are out of date; professional hours spent monitoring (not quantified).
driver_status: Multiple norms, all in force (see Section 3). The election may slow new decrees but not criteria.
solved_today: Bar association notices (ICAB, ICAM), gestores' councils, free blogs and newsletters (Infoextranjeria, Machelin Díaz, Parainmigrantes, Extranjería Legal on Substack).
software_solvable: Yes. Monitoring BOE, ministry, police and Delegación sources and mapping each change to the affected active cases is core software.
confidence: High that the rules churn; medium that buyers will pay for tracking alone (no willingness-to-pay data).

title: Form and data errors that trigger correction requests, delays and TIE failures
who: Applicants, gestorías and lawyers, HR teams; regularisation files at scale.
where: National.
reality: Common errors include a wrong EX form version, transliterated surnames or inverted dates that do not match the passport, mismatched NIE or passport numbers, a missing or wrong 790 fee receipt, and payslips that do not match bank deposits. Each triggers a document-correction request, and some only surface at fingerprinting when police data does not match.
evidence:
- List of EX-03 errors and the 10-working-day correction period — [GestoLab, 5 Jul 2026](https://www.gestolab.com/blog/formulario-ex-03-que-es-cuando-se-usa-y-como-rellenarlo-paso-a-paso)
- Errors in names, surnames, parentage or ID documents prevent the TIE, and case data sometimes does not reach the police correctly — [Ara Balears, 22 Oct 2026](https://es.arabalears.cat/sociedad/retrasos-errores-trabas-burocraticas-complican-regularizacion-extraordinaria-migrantes_1_5886839.html)
- Recording errors and duplicated NIEs — CCOO in [Crónica Global, 30 Jun 2026](https://cronicaglobal.elespanol.com/politica/20260630/avalancha-solicitudes-regularizacion-colapsar-servicios-extranjeria-barcelona/1003742774382_0.html)
- Homologación: repeated correction requests for documents already corrected, and wrongful closures for abandonment — [Defensor del Pueblo, 24 Mar 2026](https://www.diariosigloxxi.com/texto-ep/mostrar/20260324182602/defensor-avisa-colapso-homologacion-titulos-universitarios-pide-transparencia-ministerio)
- DNV: gaps between contracts and bank deposits are a frequent cause of document requests — [IG Abogados, via search snippet](https://igabogadosextranjeria.com/visado-de-nomada-digital-en-espana-requisitos-errores-comunes-y-que-documentos-presentar-correctamente-en-2025/)
scale: The share of files that get a correction request is not published.
cost_impact: Weeks per correction request; repeat appointments; denials and appeals.
driver_status: New forms under RD 1155/2024 (SEM 3/2025 replaced EX-12 with EX-00); in force.
solved_today: Manual review by gestorías and lawyers; GestoLab's AI validation and EX auto-fill; Cicerai (unverified).
software_solvable: Yes. Extracting data from documents, cross-checking fields between documents and forms, and controlling form versions are classic software tasks.

title: Digital nomad visa through the UGE: heavier evidence and scrutiny of insurance and income
who: Digital nomads (employees of foreign companies and freelancers), the foreign employers who must issue certificates, relocation agencies and law firms.
where: National (UGE electronic filing; consulates abroad). Concentrated in Barcelona (15,073 permits), Madrid (8,087) and Málaga (4,916).
reality: Applicants assemble proof of a company at least one year old, at least three months of prior relationship, months of bank statements that match payslips or invoices, and full-coverage insurance with no copayments. Requests for more documents are common, and the family income uplift is 75% for the first member and 25% per child.
evidence:
- Ley 14/2013 arts. 74 ter and 76 — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2013-10074)
- Stricter evidence since 2025 — [Polaris, 29 Sep 2026](https://polarisextranjeria.com/nuevo-reglamento-extranjeria-rd-1155-2024-balance-2024-2025)
- Insurance with copayments rejected; DGGM Criterio de Gestión 2/2025 on shorter permits — [Escalona Abogados, via search snippet](https://escalonaabogados.es/visado-para-nomadas-digitales-en-espana-guia-completa-2025-2026/)
- 16–18 working days typical, 25–45 for complex cases — [Klevvera, via search snippet](https://www.klevvera.com/blog/uge-application-spain/)
scale: 44,966 teleworker permits (Sept 2025) — [El Nacional, 12 Feb 2026](https://www.elnacional.cat/oneconomia/es/economia/barcelona-ya-supera-15000-nomadas-digitales-extracomunitarios-con-permiso-residencia_1549862_102.html); 27,875 in Dec 2024 — [The Objective, 6 Jul 2025](https://theobjective.com/economia/2025-07-06/nomadas-digitales-crecen/)
cost_impact: First-year cost €2,940–7,850 for a single applicant — [Klevvera, 22 Sep 2026](https://www.klevvera.com/blog/spain-digital-nomad-visa-cost-breakdown/); law-firm packages €900–3,900 — [Lexidy](https://www.lexidy.com/services/spain/immigration/digital-nomad/)
driver_status: Ley 14/2013 as amended by Ley 28/2022, in force. No 2025–2026 change in law found; tightening came through criteria and practice. Income threshold of 200% of the SMI; the 2026 SMI amount was not verified here.
solved_today: Law firms (Lexidy, Platinum Legal, Latitude Law, Klevvera); gestorías (DNV €498 at gestoriadeextranjeria.es); online services such as myspanishdnv.com ("Apply Online in Days", seen in search results).
software_solvable: Mostly. Evidence checklists, reconciling bank statements with payslips and checking insurance policies are software tasks, but filing still needs a representative or the applicant's own certificate.

title: Corporate UGE permits (highly qualified, EU Blue Card, ICT): moving thresholds and long end-to-end timelines
who: Employer HR and mobility teams (scale-ups to multinationals); EOR and mobility providers.
where: National (UGE-CE) plus consulates abroad. Concentrated in Barcelona (53,700 UGE permits) and Madrid (41,680).
reality: The UGE decides within 20 days or the permit is granted by positive silence. But apostilles, sworn translations, the consular visa, the padrón and the TIE stretch it to 8–14 weeks door to door. Salary thresholds are reset when INE publishes the average salary, so offers can fall below the line partway through recruitment.
evidence:
- Art. 76: 20 days and positive silence — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2013-10074)
- ICT 8–14 weeks door to door; €430–980 hard costs — [Jobbatical, via search snippet](https://www.jobbatical.com/blog/spain-intra-company-transfer-ict-permit-guide)
- Highly qualified and Blue Card 3–5 months (conflicts with the 20-day figure; probably door to door) — [Deel, 9 Jun 2026](https://www.deel.com/blog/how-to-get-a-visa-and-work-permit-in-spain/)
- Thresholds €41,356.36 and €33,085.09 from June 2026 — [Infoextranjeria, via search snippet](https://infoextranjeria.org/2026/06/11/actualizacion-del-umbral-salarial-para-profesionales-altamente-cualificados/)
scale: 47,190 executives and highly qualified professionals, 6,083 Blue Card holders and 4,592 intra-company transferees (Sept 2025) — [El Nacional, 12 Feb 2026](https://www.elnacional.cat/oneconomia/es/economia/barcelona-ya-supera-15000-nomadas-digitales-extracomunitarios-con-permiso-residencia_1549862_102.html)
cost_impact: €430–980 hard costs; legal fees from €450 (Lexmovea) to €500–1,500 (Waypoint, via search snippet); Deel's $250 documentation fee; relocation packages €1,200–3,500.
driver_status: Ley 14/2013 (in force); threshold notes from June 2026 and Orden PJC/44/2026 (in force; whether it applies to the national highly qualified permit is disputed).
solved_today: Corporate immigration law firms; EOR platforms (Deel, from $999 per permit at Tarmack); Jobbatical; relocation companies.
software_solvable: Partly. Threshold monitoring, document checklists and timeline orchestration across steps are software; the professional still files.

title: Beckham regime: hard six-month modelo 149 deadline and eligibility disputes
who: Relocating employees and executives, DNV holders, entrepreneurs; payroll teams (24% withholding); tax advisers.
where: National (AEAT, common territory). The Basque and Navarre foral regimes were not covered.
reality: The relocating person must file modelo 149 within six months of Social Security registration. Missing the date is described as final, and freelancer or nomad cases face more scrutiny. Payroll has to apply the special withholding.
evidence:
- 24% flat up to €600,000 for six years; modelo 149 within six months of registration — [INEAF](https://www.ineaf.es/tribuna/la-ley-beckham-el-regimen-para-los-impatriados/) (via search snippet); [BM Consulting, 18 May 2026](https://bm.consulting/en/insights/beckham-law-court-rulings-aeat-rejections-2026/)
- No extension; late filing denied — [Roamhub, via search snippet](https://roamhub.io/guides/beckham-law-deadline-missed/) (vendor)
- Rejections rising for DNV holders working as autónomos — vendor claims with no data (via search snippet)
- Public dispute between AEAT and Amsterdam & Partners — [Infobae, 4 Jun 2025](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2025/06/05/las-13-preguntas-que-hacienda-se-niega-a-contestar-sobre-la-ley-beckham-del-bufete-que-acusa-de-carteristas-a-los-inspectores-espanoles/)
scale: About 37,000 taxpayers in a decade; about 185 (0.5%) inspected — [El Economista, May 2025, via search snippet](https://www.eleconomista.es/economia/noticias/13349201/05/25/hacienda-responde-al-bufete-britanico-que-le-acusa-de-carterista-solo-se-inspecciona-al-05-de-los-beneficiarios-de-la-ley-beckham.html) (single-source)
cost_impact: Losing the regime means progressive rates of up to 47% instead of 24% for up to six years (my inference from the rates). Advisers charge €500–1,500 for a single person and €800–2,200 for a family — [Klevvera](https://www.klevvera.com/blog/spain-digital-nomad-visa-cost-breakdown/)
driver_status: Art. 93 LIRPF (amended by Ley 28/2022; last change 21 Dec 2024); RIRPF art. 119.4 (according to BM Consulting, unverified); Orden HFP/1338/2023. All in force; no change approved in 2025–2026.
solved_today: Tax advisers; law firms bundling it (Lexidy Gold and Platinum; Klevvera); TaxDown's Beckham calculator.
software_solvable: Yes. Software can start the deadline clock from the Social Security registration date, pre-check eligibility and pre-fill modelo 149 from contract and Social Security data. Filing is done with a certificate or by a representative.

title: Homologación and equivalence of foreign degrees: a large backlog
who: Foreign professionals in regulated professions (medicine, nursing, engineering, teaching); the hospitals, clinics and engineering firms that hire them; students.
where: National (Ministerio de Universidades), the same in every city.
reality: Files wait well over the six-month legal limit, often more than a year before the documents are even checked, with repeated requests for documents already provided. Regulated-profession hires cannot start work.
evidence:
- About 100,000 pending; more than 1,000 complaints; "muy superior a los seis meses" ("far longer than six months") — [Defensor del Pueblo via Diario Siglo XXI, 24 Mar 2026](https://www.diariosigloxxi.com/texto-ep/mostrar/20260324182602/defensor-avisa-colapso-homologacion-titulos-universitarios-pide-transparencia-ministerio)
- 72,337 pending at the end of 2025; 85,564 resolved in 2025; reform draft in limbo — [Infomigrante, 14 Oct 2026](https://infomigrante.es/2026/10/14/la-reforma-de-homologacion-de-titulos-extranjeros-en-el-limbo-ante-las-elecciones-generales/)
- 80,648 pending at 30 Jun 2025 (Tribunal de Cuentas) — [Educación Gratuita, via search snippet](https://educaciongratuita.com/noticias-educacion/homologacion-de-titulos-extranjeros)
scale: 72,000–100,000 pending files depending on the source.
cost_impact: More than six months, often more than a year, of inability to practise; employers' cost of lost hires not quantified.
driver_status: RD 889/2022 in force. The new royal decree (draft of 27 Apr 2026) is not approved and is likely stalled by the 29 Nov 2026 election.
solved_today: Specialist agencies and law firms (for example espanatehomologa.es and tuvisadoonline.com, seen in search results; prices not captured); complaints to the Defensor del Pueblo; appeals.
software_solvable: Partly. Building complete dossiers, managing translations and apostilles, and tracking status are software tasks; the backlog is not.

title: Digital-identity chicken-and-egg: the FNMT certificate and Cl@ve need a TIE or EU certificate
who: Every newcomer before the TIE arrives; HR teams that want employees to self-serve online; relocation agencies.
where: National.
reality: Without a TIE or EU registration certificate a newcomer cannot get an FNMT certificate. Many online shortcuts require Cl@ve or a certificate: DGT's digital canje, online padrón in Madrid and Barcelona, and filing on Mercurio yourself. So newcomers queue for in-person appointments or depend on paid representatives.
evidence:
- FNMT: the NIE "no es en ningún caso, elemento suficiente" ("is in no case sufficient"); the TIE or EU certificate is required — [FNMT FAQ, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://www.sede.fnmt.gob.es/registro-inicio/preguntas-frecuentes/-/asset_publisher/DKnDigPrgk4U/content/4-5-problematica-del-uso-del-nie)
- DGT canje requires Cl@ve or a certificate — [DGT, 20 May 2025](https://www.dgt.es/comunicacion/notas-de-prensa/20250520-dgt-servicio-de-canje-digital-de-permisos-de-conduccion/)
- Only 7.3% of regularisation e-applications were filed by applicants with their own certificate — [La Moncloa, 2 Jul 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/serviciosdeprensa/notasprensa/inclusion/paginas/2026/020726-balance-regularizacion-extraordinaria.aspx)
- Conflicting: Cl@ve is said to accept the NIE — [Migralis, via search snippet](https://migralis.com/blog/clave-o-certificado-digital/)
scale: Everyone waiting in EXP-01's queue; not quantified.
cost_impact: Extra in-person visits; dependence on paid representatives; the online services that would bypass appointments are closed to the people who need them most.
driver_status: FNMT identity rules and the e-administration framework (Ley 39/2015), in force.
solved_today: Representatives through the Registro de apoderamientos or lawyers; the Barcelona International Welcome Desk helps with the idCat certificate (via search snippet).
software_solvable: Partly. Software can plan the order of steps and handle representation workflows, but it cannot issue identity.

title: Driving-licence exchange (canje) and the six-month clock: US and other non-agreement drivers must retest
who: Relocating employees and families from countries without an agreement (US confirmed); HR teams for car-dependent roles.
where: National (DGT). My inference is that it matters most in car-dependent areas such as Málaga, Alicante, Baleares and Canarias.
reality: New residents can drive on a foreign licence for six months. Holders from agreement countries can exchange it, online since May 2025 with Cl@ve or a certificate. US holders must pass theory and practical tests through an autoescuela.
evidence:
- Digital canje only for agreement countries (list) — [DGT, 20 May 2025](https://www.dgt.es/comunicacion/notas-de-prensa/20250520-dgt-servicio-de-canje-digital-de-permisos-de-conduccion/)
- US: six-month rule; theory test in English; practical through an autoescuela — [Spainguru, 18 Dec 2025](https://spainguru.es/2025/12/18/spanish-drivers-license-road-test-us-residents-spain/); [Waypoint Sur, via search snippet](https://guides.waypointsur.com/us-driving-license-spain/)
- €700–1,200 total — [Autoviatest, via search snippet](https://autoviatest.com/en-US/expat-license/spain) (single-source)
- Fine of up to €500 — [Costa Luz Lawyers, via search snippet](https://www.costaluzlawyers.com/exchange-uk-driving-licence-spain-2026/) (single-source)
scale: Unknown. US students alone number 6,623 (Dec 2025, La Moncloa), as a partial indicator.
cost_impact: €700–1,200 and weeks of lessons and tests; driving illegally after six months.
driver_status: DGT bilateral agreements and the digital canje (in force since 20 May 2025). The Reglamento General de Conductores was not re-checked here.
solved_today: Gestorías and autoescuelas; some relocation packages include help switching the licence (Relocation Angel Executive; Locallista).
software_solvable: Partly. Deadline tracking, a country eligibility check and document preparation are software; the tests are not.

title: EU citizens' registration certificate (NIE verde): tight appointments on the coast
who: Relocating EU/EEA citizens (employees, nomads, retirees) and their HR teams.
where: National. Coastal provinces wait 4–6 weeks and inland ones 1–2 weeks. Madrid and Barcelona show anecdotal saturation.
reality: Registration is in person at a police office. The appointment is the hard part; the certificate is then usually issued on the spot.
evidence:
- 4038 waits — [HayCita, 23 Oct 2026](https://haycita.es/guia/tiempo-espera-cita-extranjeria) (single-source, commercial)
- Issued on the spot in Barcelona — [Barcelona International Welcome, via search snippet](https://www.barcelona.cat/internationalwelcome/en/procedure/certificate-registration-eu-national-green-nie)
- Reader reports of saturation — [Parainmigrantes, Dec 2024, via search snippet](https://www.parainmigrantes.info/certificado-de-registro-de-ciudadano-de-la-u-e/)
scale: 3,804,191 EU/EFTA registration certificates (31 Dec 2025) — [La Moncloa, 20 Mar 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/serviciosdeprensa/notasprensa/inclusion/paginas/2026/200326-poblacion-extranjera-con-residencia.aspx)
cost_impact: A wait of weeks; gestoría fees of €100–200 (Cirera, via search snippet); €12 fee.
driver_status: RD 240/2007, not re-checked here; administrative practice.
solved_today: DIY; gestorías; relocation packs.
software_solvable: Partly, with low value (preparation and alerts).

title: Empadronamiento: appointment scarcity and proof-of-address documents
who: All newcomers; HR teams; relocation agencies.
where: City-specific: Barcelona (OAC waits of 1–3 weeks) and Madrid (batch releases; sources disagree on walk-ins).
reality: The padrón is needed for the TIE appointment and local services. It requires a rental contract or the landlord's authorisation, and the online route requires a certificate (EXP-12).
evidence:
- Barcelona 2–3 weeks — [Jobbatical Barcelona guide, via search snippet](https://www.jobbatical.com/blog/barcelona-empadronamiento-poblenou-gracia-eixample)
- Madrid batch releases and one appointment every 30 days, but walk-ins possible in most OACs (conflicting) — [Vida en Madrid](https://vidaenmadrid.com/pedir-cita-para-empadronamiento-en-madrid/); [MJ Barba Consulting](https://www.mjbarbaconsulting.com/guias/cita-padron-madrid-sin-disponibilidad/) (via search snippet)
- Padrón needed for the TIE — [XPath, via search snippet](https://xpath.global/blog/moving-to-spain-relocation-guide-expats-employers)
scale: Every newcomer; not quantified.
cost_impact: 1–3 weeks on the critical path; the service is free but is bundled into €400–1,200 relocation packs.
driver_status: Municipal practice; the Ley de Bases de Régimen Local was not re-checked here.
solved_today: Relocation agencies; the Barcelona International Welcome Desk (free); gestorías.
software_solvable: Partly, with low value. Overlaps with the mid-term housing track on address proof.

title: Family reunification and family-member cards: long, office-dependent waits
who: Relocating employees with families; HR teams managing assignee packages.
where: Office-specific. Baleares has the longest reunification queue, with Valencia and Madrid next. Barcelona, Málaga, Alicante and Canarias publish no data.
reality: The main applicant arrives, but the family waits months for reunification. EU family-member cards also queue for 47–96 days. A consular visa is still needed afterwards.
evidence:
- Reunification: Baleares 184 days, Valencia 76, Madrid 62. EU family card: Valencia 96, Baleares 62, Madrid 47 — [España Abogados / Delegación PDFs, 12 Oct 2026](https://espanaabogados.com/fechas-de-resolucion-de-tramites-de-extranjeria-en-espana/)
- Legal deadline conflicts between 2 and 3 months — [Emigra España](https://emigraespana.com/es/herramientas/plazos-extranjeria); [GoEasy](https://es.goveasy.eu/blog/reagrupacion-familiar-espana-2026) (via search snippet)
- The Supreme Court annulled restrictive family conditions (arts. 94.1.f and 196.b, per coverage) — [ARC Legal, 24 Sep 2026](https://www.arc-legal.es/el-tribunal-supremo-anula-varios-preceptos-del-reglamento-de-extranjeria/)
scale: 523,821 EU family-member cards; 42,792 people under the family-of-Spaniards status (31 Dec 2025) — [La Moncloa, 20 Mar 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/serviciosdeprensa/notasprensa/inclusion/paginas/2026/200326-poblacion-extranjera-con-residencia.aspx). Annual reunification flows were not found.
cost_impact: 2–6 months of family separation, then a consular visa (1–2 months, sources conflict); the assignee may turn down the move (not quantified).
driver_status: RD 1155/2024, in force and partly annulled by STS 868/2026 (BOE 22 Sep 2026).
solved_today: Lawyers and gestorías (reunification €287 at gestoriadeextranjeria.es); family relocation packages (Relocation Angel, €2,400 + IVA).
software_solvable: Partly. Software can prepare the means and housing evidence and track each family member's file.

title: Unable to travel while the TIE is pending
who: Relocating employees who must travel for work; families.
where: National, plus Schengen transit.
reality: A renewal receipt lets you leave Spain but not come back. The EX-13 return authorisation lasts at most 90 days, works only at Spanish border posts, and cannot be issued while an initial application is unresolved. Airlines may refuse boarding.
evidence:
- Receipt and EX-13 rules — [España Abogados](https://espanaabogados.com/autorizacion-de-regreso/); [Immigration Lawyers Spain](https://immigrationlawyersspain.com/es/guias/autorizacion-de-regreso-viajar-renovacion) (via search snippet)
