- Instrucción 1/2026 (temporary relief 8 Jun–30 Sep 2026) and the airline boarding warning — [Machelin Díaz](https://machelindiaz.com/autorizacion-de-regreso-verano-2026/)
- Travel without a TIE is the main risk — [RemoteFromSpain, 29 Jul 2026](https://remotefromspain.com/tie-appointment-shortage-spain-2026/)
scale: Anyone in the EXP-01 queue; not quantified.
cost_impact: Cancelled business trips and family visits; extra appointments to get an EX-13.
driver_status: RD 1155/2024 and Schengen rules, in force. Instrucción 1/2026 expired on 30 Sep 2026.
solved_today: Lawyers file the EX-13; company travel policies.
software_solvable: Partly. Software can run a pre-trip risk check per employee, pre-fill the EX-13 and send alerts.

title: Consular visa appointments through outsourced centres (BLS, VFS) for hires recruited abroad
who: Employers hiring from abroad through the UGE or the general regime; students; family members.
where: Spanish consulates abroad; national policy set by the Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores.
reality: Visa-centre appointments are hard to get, reviewers report bots and multiple charges, and the outsourcing model is under investigation.
evidence:
- The Defensor del Pueblo reports frequent complaints about consular visa appointments — [Defensor del Pueblo 2025, via search snippet](https://www.defensordelpueblo.es/informe-anual/informe-anual-2025/)
- Review anecdotes about BLS — [Tripadvisor](https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g186338-d28055780-Reviews-Bls_International_Spain_Visa_Centre-London_England.html); [Trustpilot](https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/blsspainvisa.com) (via search snippet)
- Audiencia Nacional probe at the Algiers consulate, up to €25,000 per family alleged; BLS denies involvement — [VisaVerge, 24 Aug 2026](https://www.visaverge.com/visa/spain-probes-bls-international-in-25000-schengen-visa-racket/)
scale: Unknown.
cost_impact: Weeks to months; the start date slips.
driver_status: Outsourcing contract (2016; reportedly €175M), in force.
solved_today: Agencies that book consular appointments; applying through the UGE from inside Spain where eligible. According to Polaris, the Supreme Court treats deposit at a visa centre as filing (single-source).
software_solvable: Mostly no, because the bottleneck sits abroad. Advice on choosing the route (UGE from Spain or the consulate) is software.

title: International students: study-stay backlogs and confusion over the new work rules
who: International students (85,690 including family); university and business-school international offices; employers hiring graduates.
where: Madrid (75-day backlog), Valencia (63), Baleares (2). Barcelona publishes no data.
reality: Initial or extended study authorisations queue for 2–2.5 months in big offices, and students then also need a TIE (EXP-01). The new 30-hour work right and the switch from study to work under art. 190 are misunderstood, and some websites still cite the old 20-hour rule.
evidence:
- Queues — [España Abogados, 12 Oct 2026](https://espanaabogados.com/fechas-de-resolucion-de-tramites-de-extranjeria-en-espana/)
- 85,690 students and family, up 52% on the quarter — [La Moncloa, 20 Mar 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/serviciosdeprensa/notasprensa/inclusion/paginas/2026/200326-poblacion-extranjera-con-residencia.aspx)
- 30-hour rule, art. 190 and SEM 3/2025 — [Polaris](https://polarisextranjeria.com/nuevo-reglamento-extranjeria-rd-1155-2024-balance-2024-2025); [Machelin Díaz, via search snippet](https://machelindiaz.com/tienen-permiso-de-trabajo-los-estudiantes-automatica-para-todos-instruccion-sem-3-2025/)
cost_impact: 2–2.5 months of queueing plus the TIE wait; late starts to part-time work.
driver_status: RD 1155/2024 and SEM 3/2025, in force.
solved_today: University international offices; student agencies (for example Interlink's Barcelona guide and Piktalent for interns, seen in search results).
software_solvable: Partly. A B2B2C tool through universities could handle checklists and track deadlines.

title: UK residents under the Withdrawal Agreement, concentrated on the Costa Blanca, Costa del Sol and Baleares: card renewals and old green certificates
who: UK nationals (382,474 with documents; 199,469 hold a Withdrawal Agreement TIE); coastal gestorías and English-language agencies.
where: Regional: Alicante (63,937 grants, 26%), Málaga (44,179, 18%), Illes Balears (18,574, 7%).
reality: Withdrawal Agreement TIE renewals still need manual fingerprint booking. By my calculation about 183,000 UK nationals still hold pre-Brexit EU-regime certificates rather than a Withdrawal Agreement TIE. One commercial source says Brexit-related procedures saturate the windows in Torrevieja, Orihuela and Dénia.
evidence:
- Grant counts and the UK total — [La Moncloa, 20 Mar 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/serviciosdeprensa/notasprensa/inclusion/paginas/2026/200326-poblacion-extranjera-con-residencia.aspx)
- Manual booking for renewals — [Spainguru, 21 Oct 2026](https://spainguru.es/2026/10/21/tie-fingerprint-appointments/) (practitioner reports)
- Saturation claim — [HayCita Alicante, via search snippet](https://haycita.es/estado/alicante) (commercial, unsourced)
scale: 382,474 UK nationals with documents; more than 280,000 Withdrawal Agreement applications since 2020.
cost_impact: Appointment waits; uncertainty when travelling with old documents (not researched).
driver_status: Withdrawal Agreement art. 18.4, in force.
solved_today: Coastal gestorías and law firms (for example Costa Luz Lawyers).
software_solvable: Partly. Renewal reminders and document preparation are possible, but the segment is a niche of older residents who mostly use gestorías (my inference).

title: Opaque, fragmented and costly service market for each move
who: Employer HR teams (SMEs to large companies) and individuals relocating themselves.
where: National, with price lists from Madrid, Barcelona and Alicante.
reality: HR stitches together a relocation agency, a lawyer or gestoría, a tax adviser and translators. Prices range from €181.50 per procedure to €3,900 packages and €7,500 white-glove moves, with unclear inclusions and unclear IVA, and vendors make claims that cannot be checked.
evidence:
- Price table in Section 5: [Relocation Angel](https://relocationangelspain.com/corporate-relocation-services/); [Locallista, Aug 2026](https://www.locallista.com/en/bcn/relocation-companies); [Lexidy](https://www.lexidy.com/services/spain/immigration/digital-nomad/); [Klevvera, 22 Sep 2026](https://www.klevvera.com/blog/spain-digital-nomad-visa-cost-breakdown/); [gestoriadeextranjeria.es](https://gestoriadeextranjeria.es/tramites-y-precios/)
- Inconsistent vendor claims (Lexidy) and unexplained "internal channels" ([JuroSpain](https://jurospain.com/cita-previa-mafia-spain-solutions/))
scale: Total market size unknown. About 110 companies are registered under "Relocation" — [Empresite, via search snippet](https://empresite.eleconomista.es/Actividad/RELOCATION/)
cost_impact: About €2,000–6,000 of admin per non-EU move before housing (my synthesis); HR coordination time not quantified.
driver_status: Market structure; filing reserved to habilitated professionals (EXP-22).
solved_today: Bundles from EOR and mobility platforms (Deel; Jobbatical); agency–law-firm partnerships (Lexidy offering relocation extras; Lexmovea).
software_solvable: Partly. A co-pilot lowers agencies' cost per file and lets HR teams do the simple steps in-house, while regulated filing stays with professionals.

title: Who may file: representation rules shut out non-lawyer agencies and HR teams
who: Relocation agencies without lawyers or gestores; HR teams; SaaS vendors.
where: National.
reality: Only habilitated professionals under convenios, habilitated civil servants, free union and NGO collaborators, or applicants with their own certificate can file electronically. Relocation agencies must therefore subcontract filing.
evidence:
- Filing shares (lawyers 58% … graduados sociales 3.6%) — [La Moncloa, 2 Jul 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/serviciosdeprensa/notasprensa/inclusion/paginas/2026/020726-balance-regularizacion-extraordinaria.aspx)
- Collaborators must act free of charge and be unions or non-profits — [BOE Orden ISM/164/2026](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2026-5128)
- Mercurio professional access depends on the convenio — [Machelin Díaz, via search snippet](https://machelindiaz.com/mercurio-abogados-autorizacion-extranjeria/); [Abogacía Española, 25 Jan 2021](https://www.abogacia.es/actualidad/noticias/mas-del-60-de-las-solicitudes-telematicas-en-las-oficinas-de-extranjeria-a-traves-de-mercurio-las-realizan-abogados/)
scale: 977,876 e-applications in the regularisation alone.
cost_impact: Subcontracting fees and slower hand-offs (not quantified).
driver_status: Ley 39/2015 art. 5; convenios; RD 1155/2024 art. 197; Orden ISM/164/2026. All in force.
solved_today: Agencies partner with law firms or gestorías.
software_solvable: No, because this is a legal constraint. It does shape go-to-market: sell to the filers, or build a self-filing experience for applicants with Cl@ve or a certificate.

title: A fragile e-filing stack (Mercurio + Cl@ve + certificate + AutoFirma) under peak load
who: Lawyers, gestores and graduados sociales; applicants filing themselves.
where: National.
reality: Filing depends on a certificate in the browser, AutoFirma signing and Cl@ve. The platform went down repeatedly at the regularisation peak, and file packages have to be assembled by hand.
evidence:
- Outages on 16 Apr 2026 — [Law&Trends, 17 Apr 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/administrativo/largas-colas-en-los-consulados-y-las-caidas-de-la-plataforma-mercurio-protagonistas-de-la-primera-jornada-de-1.html)
- Technical requirements — [Machelin Díaz, via search snippet](https://machelindiaz.com/mercurio-abogados-autorizacion-extranjeria/)
- Electronic share up from 27% in 2020 — [Abogacía, 25 Jan 2021](https://www.abogacia.es/actualidad/noticias/mas-del-60-de-las-solicitudes-telematicas-en-las-oficinas-de-extranjeria-a-traves-de-mercurio-las-realizan-abogados/) — to 83.2% in the 2026 regularisation — [La Moncloa, 2 Jul 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/serviciosdeprensa/notasprensa/inclusion/paginas/2026/020726-balance-regularizacion-extraordinaria.aspx)
- Mandatory e-filing for some procedures under art. 197.2 — [Subdelegación Granada slides, via search snippet](https://mptmd.gob.es/content/dam/mpt/delegaciones_gobierno/delegaciones/andalucia/sub_granada/ponencias-de-la-jornada-y-seminario-sobre-el-nuevo-reglamento-de-extranjeria/Seminario_practico_Herramientas_de_Administracion_Electronica_Extranjeria.pdf)
scale: 977,876 e-applications in 2.5 months.
cost_impact: Lost professional hours; risk of missing deadlines (not quantified).
driver_status: State e-government platforms (SGAD and Mercurio), in force.
solved_today: Manual retries. GestoLab generates PDFs for review before filing through Mercurio.
software_solvable: Partly. Software can prepare validated packages in batches and track filing receipts. No official Mercurio API was found, so the filing step stays manual.

title: Consumer market contracted in 2025 despite a record player base
who: Players (22.8M) plus publishers, platform holders and retailers selling into Spain.
where: National [ES].
reality: After a record 2024, AEVI's 2025 yearbook (published July 2026) shows revenue **down 3.2%**. Digital spending fell 4% and DLC fell 27.8%, while mobile apps and subscriptions grew 15.3%. AEVI also **restated 2024 downward** from €2,408M to €2,369M, so year-on-year comparisons must use the restated base.
evidence: (1) 2025 revenue was €2,293M, −3.2% vs €2,369M in 2024. Digital was €1,419M (−4%), including mobile apps at €567M and full games plus DLC at €509M. Physical was €873M (−1.3%), including hardware at €413M. Units sold: 999,197 consoles, 5,554,203 console games and 30,772 PC games — [Menorca.info (Europa Press), 20 Jul 2026](https://www.menorca.info/actualidad/tecnologia-videojuegos-1/2026/07/20/2673835/espana-tiene-millones-personas-juegan-videojuegos-dedican-media-horas-semana-jugar.html). (2) Digital was 61.9% of revenue; apps and subscriptions grew 15.3%; DLC fell 27.8%, which the coverage attributes to "the lack of major releases compared with 2024" — [merca2, 28 Jul 2026](https://www.merca2.es/2026/07/28/espanoles-juega-videojuegos-2425797/). The same total ("casi 2.300 millones", "almost 2,300 million") also appears in [Que.es, 29 Aug 2026](https://www.que.es/2026/08/29/dia-internacional-del-videojuego/). (3) As originally published, 2024 revenue was €2,408M (+3%) — [AEVI Anuario 2024, May 2025](https://www.aevi.org.es/web/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/VDIGITAL-ANUARIO2024-comprimido.pdf). Press coverage of that yearbook gave digital €1,558M (+19.75%) and physical €850M (−18.11%) — [euribor.com.es, 5 Jun 2025](https://www.euribor.com.es/2025/06/05/la-industria-del-videojuego-en-espana-no-solo-entretiene-sino-que-tambien-impulsa-la-economia/). The outlet was identified from a search summary; verify the split, which the 2025 yearbook has also restated.
scale: €2.29bn consumer spend in 2025 and 22.8M players — [Menorca.info, 20 Jul 2026](https://www.menorca.info/actualidad/tecnologia-videojuegos-1/2026/07/20/2673835/espana-tiene-millones-personas-juegan-videojuegos-dedican-media-horas-semana-jugar.html).
cost_impact: The split is 61.9% digital and 38.1% physical. Mobile apps (€567M) are the largest single digital line; hardware is €413M — [merca2](https://www.merca2.es/2026/07/28/espanoles-juega-videojuegos-2425797/); [Menorca.info](https://www.menorca.info/actualidad/tecnologia-videojuegos-1/2026/07/20/2673835/espana-tiene-millones-personas-juegan-videojuegos-dedican-media-horas-semana-jugar.html).
driver_status: Coverage attributes the fall to a weaker release slate after 2024, with DLC collapsing. **Status in Oct 2026:** the 2025 data (published July 2026) is the latest; 2026 data is expected around mid-2027.
solved_today: Retail is led by sports and mainstream franchises. GAME Spain's 2025 top sellers across all platforms were EA Sports FC 26, Pokémon Legends Z-A, EA Sports FC 25, GTA V, Minecraft and Assassin's Creed Shadows — [Vandal, early 2026](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/1350788363/game-espana-revela-los-juegos-mas-vendidos-en-espana-durante-2025-con-un-claro-ganador/). The H1 2025 GfK top three for Spain were EA FC 25, Minecraft and AC Shadows — [Vandal, 2025](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/1350782147/no-hay-duda-estos-son-los-videojuegos-mas-vendidos-de-lo-que-llevamos-de-2025-en-espana-y-europa/).
software_solvable: none (context only). The topline is flat to declining, so a new game must take share rather than ride market growth.
confidence: high. Two outlets reproduce the same AEVI 2025 figures, and the restatement is documented.

title: Player base is broad, gender-balanced, mobile-first and near-universal among teens
who: 22.8M players, 47.5% of the population.
where: National [ES].
reality: Gaming is mass-market in Spain. Teen penetration is very high (86% of 12–17-year-olds) and seniors are a growing share. Mobile is the preferred platform, so the PC (Steam) audience is a minority of players.
evidence: (1) 54% of people aged 6–75 play; 86% of 12–17-year-olds; 28% of 65–75-year-olds. The gender split is 51% men, 48.5% women and 0.5% non-binary. Preferred platform: mobile/tablet 43%, console 29%, PC 28% — [merca2, 28 Jul 2026](https://www.merca2.es/2026/07/28/espanoles-juega-videojuegos-2425797/). (2) Players average 8.5 hours a week. The 2025 study extended its age range to 75 for the first time — [Menorca.info, 20 Jul 2026](https://www.menorca.info/actualidad/tecnologia-videojuegos-1/2026/07/20/2673835/espana-tiene-millones-personas-juegan-videojuegos-dedican-media-horas-semana-jugar.html). (3) 2024 had 22.1M players (+10.22%) — [AEVI Anuario 2024, May 2025](https://www.aevi.org.es/web/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/VDIGITAL-ANUARIO2024-comprimido.pdf). Coverage of the 2024 yearbook said more women than men played — [Que.es, 27 May 2025](https://www.que.es/2025/05/27/mas-jugadoras-videojuegos-espana/). That conflicts with the 2025 split, where women are 48.5%.
scale: 22.8M players — [merca2](https://www.merca2.es/2026/07/28/espanoles-juega-videojuegos-2425797/).
cost_impact: The sources found give no per-player spend.
driver_status: Smartphone ubiquity, and a methodology change (age cap raised to 75) that inflates the year-on-year growth. **Status in Oct 2026:** this is the latest data (July 2026).
solved_today: Mobile free-to-play leads usage. Console and PC are each under 30% preference.
software_solvable: none (context only). The 86% teen penetration makes minors' safety rules (GAM-23) central for any social or voice-chat game.

title: Development industry: €1.46bn, fragmented, slowing, Catalonia-centred and dependent on Steam
who: 815 active studios (495 incorporated) and about 10,500 workers.
where: Catalonia has 53% of revenue, 50% of employment and 32% of studios. Madrid has 23% of studios, Andalucía 13% and Comunidad Valenciana 10% [ES].
reality: Revenue growth has settled at about 3% a year since the pandemic boom. Employment growth hit a record low in 2024. Most studios are micro-businesses that self-publish on PC/Steam, while a handful of large firms hold half the jobs.
evidence: (1) **2023 data (DEV white paper, 11th edition, published May 2025):** revenue €1,425M (+3.1%) and 10,259 direct jobs. In 2024 there were 815 active studios, 495 of them incorporated. 54% of studios bill under €200k a year; 2% bill over €50M and account for 49% of employment. Business models: digital premium sales 41%, services 20%, work for third parties 16%. 88% develop their own IP and 55% self-publish. Platforms: PC 89%, Android 52%, Switch 49%. 82% of PC-focused studios use Steam as their main store. 39% need €50k–€150k for their next project, and 83% say they would be at risk if the crisis continues. Markets: Spain 44%, Europe 26%, North America 22%. DEV's president said "Los números no son para nada catastróficos" ("the numbers are not at all catastrophic") — [Forbes España (Europa Press), 27 May 2025](https://forbes.es/economia/722211/el-videojuego-espanol-facturo-1-425-millones-en-2023-y-empleo-a-mas-de-10-000-personas-de-manera-directa/). (2) **2024 data (white paper published July 2026, called the "2025 edition"):** revenue €1,464M (+2.7%) and employment +2.4%. DEV: "Registramos el menor crecimiento desde que tenemos datos, solo un 2,4%" ("we recorded the lowest growth since we have data, only 2.4%"). There are about 10,500 workers, women are 27% of them, and the forecast is over €1,650M by 2028. About half of studios say their viability is at risk if the crisis lasts another year — [Vandal, 8 Jul 2026](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/1350791499/el-videojuego-espanol-factura-1464-millones-de-euros-pero-registra-su-peor-dato-de-crecimiento-de-empleo/).
scale: €1.464bn revenue (2024), 815 studios and about 10,500 jobs — [Vandal](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/1350791499/el-videojuego-espanol-factura-1464-millones-de-euros-pero-registra-su-peor-dato-de-crecimiento-de-empleo/); [Forbes](https://forbes.es/economia/722211/el-videojuego-espanol-facturo-1-425-millones-en-2023-y-empleo-a-mas-de-10-000-personas-de-manera-directa/).
cost_impact: Premium digital sales are the leading model at 41% — [Forbes](https://forbes.es/economia/722211/el-videojuego-espanol-facturo-1-425-millones-en-2023-y-empleo-a-mas-de-10-000-personas-de-manera-directa/). A Vandal sidebar headline says only 6% of studios monetise subscriptions; the article body was not read, so this is unverified.
driver_status: Post-Covid correction, rising costs and a funding squeeze. **Status in Oct 2026:** the latest white paper (2024 data) was published in July 2026.
solved_today: Self-publishing on Steam, work-for-hire for foreign publishers, and public grants (GAM-04).
software_solvable: SaaS tool (possible). Roughly 440 micro-studios bill under €200k (54% of 815, an inference) and self-publish on Steam, which makes a defined but low-budget customer segment.
confidence: high. Two editions of DEV data were reported by two outlets.

title: Public funding comes as small national grants plus regional calls, and depends on EU recovery funds
who: Indie studios and digital creators; AEVI and DEV as co-funded event organisers.
where: National (Ministerio de Cultura) and the Madrid region; Málaga has small prizes. Catalonia (ICEC) and Valencia (IVC) could not be verified.
reality: The national "ayudas para la promoción del sector del videojuego, del pódcast y de otras formas de creación digital" (grants promoting video games, podcasts and other digital creation) are capped at about €80k per applicant and funded by the EU Recovery Plan (PRTR / NextGenerationEU). The state also co-funds B2B market access through events.
evidence: (1) The 2024 call totalled €8M, funding up to 80% of project cost with a maximum of €80k per applicant. This figure comes from a search summary of the 2024 call extract, is single-source and should be verified in the BDNS (national grants database) — [BOE-B-2024-243, 4 Jan 2024](https://www.boe.es/boe/dias/2024/01/04/pdfs/BOE-B-2024-243.pdf). (2) The 2025 call extract was published on 16 Nov 2024 (BDNS 796539), is PRTR-funded, and excludes beneficiaries of the three previous calls — [BOE-B-2024-41842, 16 Nov 2024](https://www.boe.es/boe/dias/2024/11/16/pdfs/BOE-B-2024-41842.pdf). (3) Mad Games Show 2026 (Naves de Matadero, Madrid, 28–29 Apr 2026) ran under a Ministry–AEVI–DEV agreement with a budget of €481,090. The Ministry put in up to €240,350 and AEVI up to €240,740. The budget includes €88,000 for the "Meet to Match" B2B marketplace, and is funded by PRTR component 24 — [BOE-A-2026-928, published 15 Jan 2026](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-928). (4) Comunidad de Madrid video-game project grants were resolved by Orden 2405/2025 of 9 Oct 2025 — [BOCM, 22 Oct 2025](https://www.bocm.es/boletin/CM_Orden_BOCM/2025/10/22/BOCM-20251022-21.PDF). A new 2026 call (Orden 411/2026, corrected by Orden 505/2026; BDNS 892428) was found, but its amount was not — [BOCM, 19 Mar 2026](https://www.bocm.es/boletin/CM_Orden_BOCM/2026/03/19/BOCM-20260319-25.PDF). (5) In Málaga, the Premios Iris Games 2026 handed out €44,000 in prizes (single source) — [Ayuntamiento de Málaga communiqué, 2026](https://www.malaga.eu/visorcontenido/ANUDocumentDisplayer/179107/COMUNICADO.pdf).
scale: The 2024 national pot was €8M — [BOE-B-2024-243](https://www.boe.es/boe/dias/2024/01/04/pdfs/BOE-B-2024-243.pdf). That is about 0.5% of the industry's €1.46bn revenue (inference).
cost_impact: Grants of up to €80k compare with 39% of studios needing €50k–€150k for their next project — [Forbes/DEV, 27 May 2025](https://forbes.es/economia/722211/el-videojuego-espanol-facturo-1-425-millones-en-2023-y-empleo-a-mas-de-10-000-personas-de-manera-directa/).
driver_status: PRTR/NextGenEU funding. **Status in Oct 2026:** regional 2026 calls are active (Madrid), and the national 2026 call amount is not verified. Continuity after PRTR funding winds down is an unverified risk (inference).
solved_today: Grants, trade events (Mad Games Show, GAMERGY), and ICEX internationalisation support. ICEX's representative described the sector as "resiliente, internacionalizado, con empleo cualificado y joven" ("resilient, internationalised, with skilled and young employment") — [Forbes, 27 May 2025](https://forbes.es/economia/722211/el-videojuego-espanol-facturo-1-425-millones-en-2023-y-empleo-a-mas-de-10-000-personas-de-manera-directa/). The specific ICEX programmes were not verified. DEV maintains a grants directory — [DEV ayudas](https://dev.org.es/es/servicios/ayudas).
software_solvable: none (funding context). The ticket sizes fit a small game prototype, not a platform.
confidence: medium. Amounts are partly single-source, and Catalonia and Valencia are unverified.

title: Spanish hits are rare, and 2025–26 brought layoffs and closures
who: Studios including The Game Kitchen, MercurySteam, Ubisoft Barcelona, King Barcelona, Secret 6, Aheartfulofgames and Tequila Works.
where: Seville, Barcelona and Madrid [ES].
reality: Spain has a few durable successes but saw a wave of cuts in 2025–26, from multinational studios in Barcelona to Madrid studios that closed after being acquired.
evidence: (1) Blasphemous (The Game Kitchen, Seville, released 2019) passed 5M copies sold — [Vandal, Jun 2026](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/1350791155/blasphemous-celebra-sus-mas-de-5-millones-en-ventas-y-se-confirma-como-uno-de-los-grandes-exitos-espanoles/). (2) MercurySteam (Metroid Dread) began "un proceso de ajuste de nuestra mano de obra" ("a process of adjusting our workforce") in May 2026 without disclosing the scale. Press linked this to the commercial failure of Blades of Fire and NetEase withdrawing funding — [Vandal, 13 May 2026](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/1350789773/dia-negro-para-la-industria-espanola-mercurysteam-el-estudio-de-metroid-dread-anuncia-despidos/). (3) Ubisoft Barcelona lost 51 employees in Ubisoft's 2026 restructuring and remains the main hub for Rainbow Six Siege — [VidaExtra, 2026](https://www.vidaextra.com/industria/ubisoft-va-camino-quedarse-vacia-cierran-dos-estudios-despiden-a-51-empleados-barcelona-380-puestos-corren-peligro); [Menorca.info, 11 Jun 2026](https://www.menorca.info/actualidad/tecnologia-videojuegos-1/2026/06/11/2648115/ubisoft-realiza-nuevos-despidos-afectan-equipo-barcelona-centra-desarrollo-rainbow-six-siege.html). (4) Secret 6 (Madrid) closed on 31 July with 42 staff, and Aheartfulofgames (28 staff) also closed. elDiario.es says Tequila Works "ya no existe" ("no longer exists") and that these studios were bought by larger companies before disappearing. King Barcelona faced more than 50 layoffs. This is single-source, and the article date (2025) was inferred from context — [elDiario.es](https://www.eldiario.es/1_bf4169).
scale: The layoff and closure items above total over 160 named jobs (51 + 42 + 28 + 50+), an inference that excludes MercurySteam's undisclosed number.
cost_impact: No sales figures were found for 2024–26 Spanish releases other than Blasphemous.
driver_status: Global industry contraction, rising development costs and publisher funding pullbacks. **Status in Oct 2026:** ongoing, with the latest items in May–June 2026.
solved_today: n/a.
software_solvable: none directly. It signals a pool of experienced developers in Barcelona and Madrid (inference).

title: Spain's Twitch footprint and what Spain watches
who: About 10.5M monthly Twitch users in Spain (third-party estimate) and over 1.1M active Spanish-language channels.
where: Spain for user counts and Twitch's Spain ranking; [ES-world] for language-level watch time.
reality: Twitch remains the centre of Spain's streaming culture. Twitch's own 2026 data ranks competitive titles first in Spain, while top creators mix Minecraft, simulators and new releases. The long tail is tiny.
evidence: (1) Spain is Twitch's sixth-largest market with 10.5M monthly users, 4.1% of the global audience (worldpopulationreview plus StreamsCharts, Mar 2026). Spanish is Twitch's fifth language by watch time at about 6%, or 19.5M hours a week [ES-world] (TwitchTracker/SullyGnome, Jun 2026). Four of the ten most-followed channels worldwide are Spanish — [Kolsquare, 24 Aug 2026](https://www.kolsquare.com/es/informes-y-guias/guia-marketing-influencers-twitch). (2) Twitch State of Gaming 2026 (1 Jan–1 Sep 2026): Spain's top three games are League of Legends, Valorant and Fortnite. Rubius passed 21M hours watched, and his most-streamed categories were Minecraft, TCG Card Shop Simulator and Marvel Rivals. Globally, hours watched on indie-tagged channels rose 51% year on year — [Vandal, 14 Sep 2026](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/2026257023/twitch-supera-los-8600-millones-de-horas-de-gaming-vistas-en-2026-y-revela-los-juegos-y-streamers-mas-populares/). (3) 18% of Spanish social-media users use Twitch daily (2024 data, source not named). There are over 1.1M active Spanish-language channels, and **90% of streams average three or fewer viewers** — [Que.es, 9 Jan 2026](https://www.que.es/2026/01/09/fenomeno-streaming-espana-videojuegos/). (4) Twitch's Spanish web traffic was "relatively stable" while YouTube's was volatile (Semrush) — [PuroMarketing, 2025](https://www.puromarketing.com/163/215300/youtube-recupera-terreno-mientras-twitch-resiste-cambiado-trafico-digital-espana-2025).
scale: 10.5M monthly users [ES] and 19.5M hours a week [ES-world] — [Kolsquare](https://www.kolsquare.com/es/informes-y-guias/guia-marketing-influencers-twitch).
cost_impact: See GAM-09.
driver_status: A creator-centric culture that formed during 2020–22. Que.es describes it as "en una fase de consolidación tras el boom pandémico" ("in a consolidation phase after the pandemic boom") — [Que.es](https://www.que.es/2026/01/09/fenomeno-streaming-espana-videojuegos/). **Status in Oct 2026:** Twitch remains the default platform for Spain-based top creators.
solved_today: Twitch, with simulcasts to YouTube and TikTok for big events (GAM-07).
software_solvable: game (streamer integration). Spanish creators are a credible distribution channel; for Spain, a Twitch integration matters more than Kick.
confidence: medium. The top games are first-party Twitch data; the user counts are third-party estimates.

title: La Velada del Año is the largest creator-led live event in streaming, but its peak fell in 2026
who: Ibai Llanos and invited creators/celebrities. Production by Telefónica's TBS in 2025.
where: Seville (Estadio La Cartuja in 2025 and 2026); audience [ES-world].
reality: Peak concurrent viewers rose from about 3.3M (2022) to about 9.2–9.3M (2025). In 2026 the show was simulcast on Twitch, YouTube and TikTok, and the Twitch peak fell to about 8M.
evidence: (1) Edition II (2022) peaked at 3.3M — [LevelUp, 2022](https://www.levelup.com/noticias/la-velada-del-ano-ii-ibai-la-rompe-en-twitch-con-3-millones-de-espectadores-supera-record-de-thegrefg/). Edition III (2023) peaked at about 3.45M — [LevelUp, 2023](https://www.levelup.com/noticias/ibai-vuelve-a-hacer-historia-la-velada-del-ano-iii-rompe-records-de-twitch/). Edition IV (2024) peaked at 3.7M — [LevelUp, 2024](https://www.levelup.com/noticias/ibai-llanos-y-la-velada-del-ano-4-rompieron-un-record-historico-de-audiencia-en-twitch/). (2) Edition V (26 Jul 2025, Seville) peaked at 9,334,179 according to TBS — [Señal News, 2025](https://senalnews.com/es/contenidos/tbs-de-telefonica-produjo-la-velada-del-ano-v-de-ibai-llanos), 9,189,762 according to Kolsquare (tracker data) — [Kolsquare, 24 Aug 2026](https://www.kolsquare.com/es/informes-y-guias/guia-marketing-influencers-twitch), and 9.2M according to Stream Hatchet — [Net Influencer, 18 Feb 2026](https://www.netinfluencer.com/?p=43866). The organisers claimed 144M live views and 20M unique viewers — [RTVC, Jul 2025](https://rtvc.es/velada-del-ano-v-26-julio-2025/). (3) Edition VI (25 Jul 2026, La Cartuja) peaked at about 8M on Twitch, short of the record, which the outlet attributes to simulcasting on Twitch, YouTube and TikTok (single source) — [Que.es, 27 Jul 2026](https://www.que.es/2026/07/27/velada-ano-6-roza-audiencia-twitch/). It drew more than 80,000 attendees, sold out in just over two hours, and a 2027 edition was announced — [Euronews, 25 Jul 2026](https://es.euronews.com/2026/07/25/haciendo-historia-en-el-streaming-online-desde-espana-la-velada-del-ano-6-en-directo). A later headline claims "34 millones de dispositivos" ("34 million devices"); the page returned 403 and was not read — [La Tribuna, 28 Jul 2026](https://www.latribuna.hn/2026/07/28/la-velada-del-ano-de-ibai-llanos-se-siguio-desde-34-millones-de-dispositivos/).
scale: About 8–9.3M concurrent viewers and 80,000+ in the stadium — sources above.
cost_impact: A telecom group (Telefónica/TBS) handled technical production and streaming — [Señal News](https://senalnews.com/es/contenidos/tbs-de-telefonica-produjo-la-velada-del-ano-v-de-ibai-llanos). Event revenue and sponsorship figures were not found.
driver_status: Creator-celebrity boxing as a sports-entertainment spectacle. **Status in Oct 2026:** annual, with 2027 confirmed. Multi-platform simulcast is now the norm, which spreads out per-platform peaks.
solved_today: Twitch, YouTube and TikTok, plus TV-grade production by a telecom partner.
software_solvable: platform (weak signal). It proves Spanish-speaking demand for creator-led sports entertainment, but it is a superstar phenomenon and says little about the mid-tier.
confidence: high for the 2025 peak range; medium for 2026 figures.

title: Kick in Spanish is a Latin American story; Spain-based stars stay Twitch-first
who: Latin American creators lead Kick's Spanish-language audience (Davoo Xeneize, Westcol, LaCobra). Spain-based leaders (Ibai, Rubius) remain on Twitch.
where: [ES-world]; Spain-specific Kick data was not found.
reality: Kick's Spanish-language audience is large and growing, but led by Latin America. Its credibility suffered from a viewbot purge, and it has expelled controversial Spanish streamers.
evidence: (1) In May 2026 the most-watched Spanish-speaking streamers (Streams Charts) were Davoo Xeneize (4.3M hours), Westcol (3.7M) and LaCobra (2.6M), all on Kick. Ibai was fourth with 1.9M, and only Ibai and Rubius held on among Twitch names. In the same month Kick banned more than 500 streamers for viewer-count manipulation and added an option to hide viewer counts — [Infobae, 1 Jun 2026](https://www.infobae.com/tecno/2026/06/01/estos-fueron-los-streamers-hispanos-mas-vistos-en-mayo-de-2026-davoo-westcol-y-mas/). (2) A July 2025 claim that Kick overtook Twitch in Spanish-language streaming (about 60% of viewership) traces back to **Kick's own X account**, so it is low reliability — [Tribune](https://tribune.com.pk/story/2556546/kick-overtakes-twitch-in-key-streaming-niche-with-sustained-lead-in-viewership); [EarlyGame](https://earlygame.com/es/news/gaming/kick-intenta-fichar-streamer-mas-grande-europa-twitch). (3) Stream Hatchet's 2025 report says Kick's strongest growth is among Spanish-speaking users — [Net Influencer, 18 Feb 2026](https://www.netinfluencer.com/?p=43866). (4) Kick expelled Spanish streamers Simón Pérez and Silvia Charro for rule breaches, as the company confirmed to EFE — [La Patilla (EFE), 27 Aug 2025](https://lapatilla.com/2025/08/27/que-es-kick-la-polemica-plataforma-australiana-que-ha-expulsado-a-streamers-espanoles/). (5) Ibai said Kick offered him more than double his Twitch pay for exclusivity ("me temblaba la mano", "my hand was shaking"). He was still on Twitch in 2026 (GAM-06, GAM-07) — [EarlyGame, undated](https://earlygame.com/es/news/gaming/kick-intenta-fichar-streamer-mas-grande-europa-twitch).
scale: Top Kick Spanish-language creators reach 2.6–4.3M hours a month — [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/tecno/2026/06/01/estos-fueron-los-streamers-hispanos-mas-vistos-en-mayo-de-2026-davoo-westcol-y-mas/).
cost_impact: Kick pays creators 95% of subscription revenue — [Influencer Marketing Hub, 2025](https://influencermarketinghub.com/kick-vs-twitch-vs-youtube/); [TechCrunch, 27 Jun 2023](https://techcrunch.com/2023/06/27/kick-lures-disenchanted-twitch-streamers-for-now-explained/). Its hourly-pay Creator Incentive Program reportedly opened in Feb 2025 at about $16–32 an hour — [Makeinfluence](https://www.makeinfluence.com/en/academy/kick-as-a-livestreaming-channel-for-brand-and-influencer-marketing). Reported eligibility is an average of 100 concurrent viewers and 50 hours streamed in 30 days — [Passionfruit](https://passionfru.it/?p=59979). The rates and thresholds are not confirmed by Kick.
driver_status: Creator-favourable economics (95/5 split, hourly pay, signing offers). **Status in Oct 2026:** Kick is strong in Latin America, has credibility problems (May 2026 purge), and has no confirmed exclusive signing of a top Spain-based streamer.
solved_today: Kick's public API (GAM-18) makes integrations possible.
software_solvable: game/platform. Integrate Kick for Latin American reach, but Spain distribution still runs through Twitch.

title: Streamer monetisation is thin outside the top tier
who: Small and mid-tier Spanish streamers.
where: Spain (Eurozone pricing).
reality: Spanish subscriptions are cheap. The standard split is 50/50, with better Partner Plus terms only for high performers, and most channels have almost no audience. Sponsorship is the main upside, and it is concentrated among top creators and includes gambling brands.
evidence: (1) In August 2021 Twitch cut Spain's subscription price from €4.99 to €3.99, in line with the rest of the Eurozone, and temporarily compensated streamers (100% for three months, then 25% less every three months). Streamer Xamork said nine gifted subs fell from about €16 to about €8: "Se viene una época bastante durilla" ("a rather tough period is coming") — [Genbeta, 5 Aug 2021](https://www.genbeta.com/actualidad/suscripciones-twitch-tambien-bajan-precio-espana-pagaremos-creadores-ingresaran). 3DJuegos later reported a Eurozone Tier-1 change from €3.99 to €4.99; the date was not verified — [3DJuegos](https://www.3djuegos.com/industria-gaming/noticias/twitch-cambia-precios-suscripciones-tier-1-cuanto-costara-apoyar-a-tu-streamer-favorito-cuando-se-haran-efectivos-estos-cambios). **The current Spanish price is therefore unverified.** (2) The standard Twitch split is 50/50. Under Partner Plus, holding 100 points for three months gives 60/40 and 300 points gives 70/30, effective 1 May 2024 — [LevelUp, 2024](https://www.levelup.com/noticias/772873/Twitch-nuevos-cambios-ayudaran-a-los-streamers-a-ganar-mas-dinero-pero-hay-una-mala-noticia). EOL reports a 70/30 split for creators above $100k a year, undated — [Elotrolado](https://www.elotrolado.net/noticias/internet/twitch-ingresos-creadores-cambios). (3) 90% of streams average three or fewer viewers. Revenue comes from sponsorships, subscriptions, donations and ads. Sponsor sectors include online betting and casino operators, and some creators work with unlicensed casinos (no figures) — [Que.es, 9 Jan 2026](https://www.que.es/2026/01/09/fenomeno-streaming-espana-videojuegos/).
scale: The long tail is large (over 1.1M Spanish-language channels) but mostly tiny — [Que.es](https://www.que.es/2026/01/09/fenomeno-streaming-espana-videojuegos/).
cost_impact: €3.99 (2021) sub price at a 50/50 split, versus Kick's 95/5 — sources above.
driver_status: Platform economics. **Status in Oct 2026:** Partner Plus tiers apply. Amazon Ads launched creator sponsorship formats and a free advertiser–streamer matching tool in 17 countries; Spain is not named in the available snippet — [Señal News, 2 Jun 2025](https://senalnews.com/es/digital/amazon-ads-cerro-patrocinios-para-creadores-de-twitch-con-alcance-en-mexico-y-brasil).
solved_today: Twitch subscriptions, Bits and ads; Kick incentives; agency sponsorships; Crowd Control-style paid interactivity (GAM-19).
software_solvable: SaaS tool. Mid-tier creators need engagement and monetisation tooling, but they have little ability to pay (inference).

title: Cheap co-op "friendslop" hits are huge globally and on Twitch; Spain's share is unknown
who: Small studios (semiwork/R.E.P.O., Aggro Crab and Landfall/PEAK, TVGS/Schedule I, Nuggets Entertainment/RV There Yet?) and streamers.
where: [GLOBAL]; no Spain-specific data was found.
reality: Cheap, social co-op games, often with proximity voice chat and comedic physics, became Steam's top sellers by units in 2025. Their virality is driven by streamers, led by English-language creators.
evidence: (1) Four of the ten best-selling Steam games by copies in 2025 were friendslop titles: R.E.P.O. (18.5M), PEAK (15.4M), Schedule I (9.1M) and RV There Yet? (5.7M) (GameDev Reports, cited). GameDiscoverCo (Jan 2026) gives PEAK 15.5M and R.E.P.O. 18.4M. AppMagic says these games typically cost $5–20 and that effective spend at least doubles because nobody plays them solo. All of this is secondary — [Game Industry Library, 2026](https://gameindustrylibrary.com/research/shared/6-how-has-the-friendslop-genre-evolved). (2) PEAK sold 1M copies in six days after its 16 Jun 2025 launch — [Shacknews, Jun 2025](https://www.shacknews.com/article/144826/peak-million-copies-sold-aggro-crab) — and 5M in under a month — [PCGamesN, Jul 2025](https://www.pcgamesn.com/peak/major-sales-milestone). It sells best in the USA, with Russia second — [WN Hub, 2025](https://wnhub.io/news/analytics/item-48220). (3) On Twitch, R.E.P.O. peaked at 163.8K viewers on 12 Apr 2025 and drew 2.95M hours in May 2026 — [Streams Charts](https://streamscharts.com/games/repo). Chained Together drew 1.13M hours and a 217,564-viewer peak on launch day (19 Jun 2024), led by US streamer caseoh_ — [Streams Charts](https://streamscharts.com/games/chained-together/release-stats). (4) The genre's traits are low barrier to entry, group play, common proximity chat and physics comedy, "usually costing US$20 or less" (The Verge, 20 Dec 2025) — [Wikipedia: Friendslop, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friendslop). Critics say the label gets applied to any small co-op game after Lethal Company — [AV Club](https://www.avclub.com/not-every-co-op-game-is-friendslop).
scale: Tens of millions of units [GLOBAL] — sources above.
cost_impact: Typical prices are €5–10 in Spain (GAM-13).
driver_status: Streamer virality plus group-purchase dynamics. **Status in Oct 2026:** the genre is still producing entrants (Wikipedia lists 2026 titles such as Meccha Chameleon, Yapyap and BOMBANANA!), and indie-tagged Twitch hours are up 51% (GAM-06). Saturation risk is rising (inference).
solved_today: Dozens of cheap titles; see GAM-13 for the price ladder.
software_solvable: game. The evidence supports comedic co-op/proximity-chat games, but at low prices and with global (English-led) virality rather than a Spain-specific market.
confidence: medium. Global figures are from secondary sources, and the Spain share is unknown.

title: Fact-check 1 — "massive player shift away from competitive shooters toward premium comedic co-op games with proximity voice chat"
who: Spanish players and viewers; global Steam buyers.
where: Spain (viewing and retail) compared with [GLOBAL] (Steam units).
reality: Spanish viewing and retail are still dominated by competitive and sports titles. Cheap co-op games are a large global segment that **coexists** with shooters rather than replacing them.
evidence: (1) Spain's top Twitch games for Jan–Sep 2026 are League of Legends, Valorant and Fortnite (first-party Twitch data) — [Vandal, 14 Sep 2026](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/2026257023/twitch-supera-los-8600-millones-de-horas-de-gaming-vistas-en-2026-y-revela-los-juegos-y-streamers-mas-populares/). (2) GAME Spain's 2025 top sellers were EA Sports FC 26, Pokémon Legends Z-A, EA Sports FC 25, GTA V, Minecraft and AC Shadows — [Vandal, early 2026](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/1350788363/game-espana-revela-los-juegos-mas-vendidos-en-espana-durante-2025-con-un-claro-ganador/). (3) Globally, four friendslop games were in Steam's 2025 top ten by units, but at $5–20 price points — [Game Industry Library](https://gameindustrylibrary.com/research/shared/6-how-has-the-friendslop-genre-evolved). (4) The global tier-1 competitive audience is stable: the Worlds 2025 final peaked at 6,737,568 concurrent viewers excluding China, −1.7% vs 2024 (single source, via search summary) — [wecoach.gg, 2026](https://wecoach.gg/es/blog/article/league-of-legends-player-count-and-statistics-2026).
scale: See GAM-06 and GAM-10.
cost_impact: The co-op hits are priced at €5–10, so they are not "premium" (GAM-13).
driver_status: A genuine global rise in social co-op. **Status in Oct 2026:** no Spain-specific data shows players leaving shooters.
solved_today: Competitive titles (LoL, Valorant, Fortnite, CS2) alongside cheap co-op games (R.E.P.O., PEAK and others).
software_solvable: game, if repositioned. The accurate pitch is "cheap viral co-op coexisting with shooters", not "replacing shooters".
confidence: high on the Spain viewing and retail facts; medium on the global units.

title: Fact-check 2 — "rigid, traditional esports formats are declining in engagement"
who: Spain's esports league operators (LVP/Mediapro, LastLap/Atresmedia) and clubs; Riot.
where: Spain's national tier; Zaragoza (2025 Iberian Cup final); [GLOBAL] for tier-1 comparison.
reality: Spain's national League of Legends league economy contracted in 2025–26. Engagement with top-tier esports is holding up and increasingly runs through creator co-streams and creator-owned teams.
evidence: (1) Mediapro bought LVP's parent Fandroid for about €22M and struggled to recoup it, capping spending at revenue for three years. LVP prepared an ERE (collective dismissal) for 59 employees and stepped down from organising the Superliga (Sep 2025). It stayed active until late November to run the Iberian Cup final in Zaragoza — [Sheep Esports, 16 Sep 2025](https://www.sheepesports.com/articles/sources-lvp-to-step-down-from-organizing-the-superliga/en); [Sheep Esports, Sep 2025](https://www.sheepesports.com/articles/sources-59-lvp-employees-sent-to-labor-force-adjustment-plan/en). title: Twitch and Kick integration surfaces and rules
who: Game developers and extension builders; streamers.
where: [GLOBAL] platform rules that apply in Spain.
reality: Both platforms allow chat- and event-driven integrations. Twitch explicitly forbids using its paid currency (Bits) for wagering, gambling with monetary rewards, random loot boxes, or contest entries, and forbids exchanging extension items for money.
evidence: (1) **Twitch Extensions Guidelines:** 5.2 "Extensions may not allow items to be exchanged for money or other commerce instruments." 5.3 "Awarding loot boxes that include an element of randomness is permitted so long as contents" [do not have a monetary value]. Section 6.2 restricts Bits use: 6.2.1 "To obtain access to a pay-to-play game"; 6.2.3 "If your Extension contains gambling activities that provide a reward with a monetary value"; 6.2.4 "Where Bits can be exchanged for loot boxes with unknown items that are determined randomly or by chance"; 6.2.5 "To provide the end user with an entry into a sweepstakes or contest"; 6.2.6 "For engaging in 'wagering' or 'betting,' on gameplay events, contests of chance". 4.5 says rewarding actions outside Twitch must not be a principal use case — [Twitch Developers, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/extensions/guidelines-and-policies/). The fetched page gave the 6.2 clause texts without the lead-in sentence; verify the exact wording. (2) **Predictions** use Channel Points, which have no cash value (third-party). Stakes reportedly range from 10 to 250,000 points per outcome (secondary source) — [Stream-Rise](https://stream-rise.com/blog/channel-points-predictions); [Tubefilter, 13 Nov 2020](https://www.tubefilter.com/2020/11/13/twitch-launches-predictions-feature-channel-points/). (3) **Twitch Drops** in 2026: DropsEnabled streams drew 1.6bn hours (+46%), over 7,500 campaigns ran (+20%), and 40M users claimed Drops (+15%) [GLOBAL] — [Vandal, 14 Sep 2026](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/2026257023/twitch-supera-los-8600-millones-de-horas-de-gaming-vistas-en-2026-y-revela-los-juegos-y-streamers-mas-populares/). (4) **Kick public API**, described by Kick as its "first release" with more endpoints planned. The changelog runs from Feb to Nov 2025. Endpoints cover chat (send, reply, delete), channels, livestreams, categories, a KICKs leaderboard and moderation. Webhooks cover chat messages, channel subscriptions, livestream metadata, moderation bans and `kicks.gifted`. No channel-rewards or predictions endpoints are listed, and rate limits and developer terms are not stated on the landing page — [Kick Docs, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://docs.kick.com/). Some community libraries rely on reverse-engineered endpoints that "may break without notice" (search summary of docs.rs crates).
scale: Drops reach 40M users [GLOBAL] — [Vandal](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/2026257023/twitch-supera-los-8600-millones-de-horas-de-gaming-vistas-en-2026-y-revela-los-juegos-y-streamers-mas-populares/).
cost_impact: Bits are Twitch's paid currency inside extensions, with the restrictions above. Kick's KICKs gifting is visible through the API.
driver_status: Platforms are opening APIs (Kick in 2025) while keeping gambling out. **Status in Oct 2026:** current as fetched.
solved_today: Native Predictions and Polls, Twitch extensions, Kick webhooks, Crowd Control (GAM-19).
software_solvable: game. Viewer voting on rule changes through chat, Channel Points or Bits (non-wagering) is technically and policy-feasible. A **transfer market with real-money value would breach clause 5.2** if run as a Twitch extension.
confidence: high for Twitch rule texts (primary) and Kick API scope (primary); medium for Predictions details.

Only about 10% of users are reported to pay for premium (information "leaked" by people close to the company). Fantasy Marca carries LaLiga's official sponsorship. All of this is weakly sourced and undated — [Xataka](https://www.xataka.com/aplicaciones/no-solo-de-comunio-viven-los-fantasy-sports-estas-son-sus-alternativas-y-el-futuro); [TuAppPara](https://tuapppara.com/juegos/ligas-fantasy/). (2) A 2025 fantasy site lists "Comunio, Biwenger y LaLiga Fantasy DAZN" as the three main Spanish games — [Comuniate](https://www.comuniate.com/noticias/37042/los-5-jugadores-mas-caros-de-comunio-biwenger-y-laliga-fantasy-dazn). (3) LaLiga partnered with Sorare in 2021 to issue NFT player cards for fantasy tournaments — [Euronews, 9 Sep 2021](https://www.euronews.com/next/2021/09/09/spain-s-la-liga-launches-enters-nft-and-blockchain-world-with-fantasy-football-cards-for-i); [Genbeta, 2021](https://www.genbeta.com/actualidad/laliga-lanza-nfts-todos-sus-jugadores-mano-sorare-asi-quieren-aumentar-sus-ingresos-blockchain). The UK Gambling Commission investigated whether Sorare needed a gambling licence, and Sorare said "we are very confident Sorare does not offer any forms of regulated gambling" — [City AM, 2022](https://cityam.com/?p=1777419). Sorare's CEO argued for a "new category" outside betting rules — [Decrypt, 2023](https://decrypt.co/122650/sorare-nfts-regulation-ceo-nicolas-julia).
scale: Comunio has about 1M users (weak estimate) — [Xataka](https://www.xataka.com/aplicaciones/no-solo-de-comunio-viven-los-fantasy-sports-estas-son-sus-alternativas-y-el-futuro).
cost_impact: Freemium with premium subscriptions; reportedly about 10% pay (unverified).
driver_status: A long-standing habit tied to LaLiga. **Status in Oct 2026:** active in the 2026–27 season (fantasy sites publishing tips). The DGOJ's position on Sorare-style products in Spain was not found.
solved_today: Free apps with virtual budgets, plus a premium tier.
software_solvable: platform (constrained). Spanish users already understand drafts and transfer markets, so a creator-league product must stay points- or virtual-money-only to avoid gambling classification (GAM-21) and to compete with free incumbents.
confidence: low for user numbers; medium for the Sorare facts.

title: Ley 13/2011 defines what turns predictions, virtual currencies or transfer markets into regulated gambling
who: Any operator of predictions, contests or markets with real-money value (idea b); game studios with paid randomised items.
where: National [ES] (state-level online activity).
reality: The definition of gambling turns on (a) staking money or economically valuable objects, (b) uncertain outcomes partly dependent on chance, and (c) transferability between participants. Leisure games are excluded only when they produce no economically valuable transfers. Unlicensed operation is prohibited.
evidence: All from the [BOE consolidated text (last update shown 31 Dec 2022)](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2011-9280). (1) Art. 3.a: "juego" is "toda actividad en la que se arriesguen cantidades de dinero u objetos económicamente evaluables en cualquier forma" ("any activity in which sums of money or economically valuable objects are risked in any form") on future, uncertain outcomes dependent to some degree on chance, "y que permitan su transferencia entre los participantes" ("and which allow their transfer between participants"). This applies whether skill or chance predominates, and prizes may be cash or in kind. (2) Art. 3.c: a bet ("apuesta") stakes money on the outcome of a predetermined event that is uncertain and outside the participants' control. (3) Art. 3.e: a "concurso" (contest) is offered, run and resolved through a media outlet, tied to its main activity, and requires payment or premium-rate participation. Free participation is not a concurso. (4) Art. 2.2.a excludes "juegos o competiciones de puro ocio, pasatiempo o recreo que constituyan usos sociales" ("games or competitions of pure leisure, pastime or recreation that constitute social customs") "siempre que éstas no produzcan transferencias económicamente evaluables" ("provided they produce no economically valuable transfers"). A price for the means to play is allowed "cuando éste no constituya en medida alguna beneficio económico para el promotor o los operadores" ("when it does not constitute any economic benefit for the promoter or operators"). (5) Art. 2.2.c excludes "combinaciones aleatorias con fines publicitarios o promocionales" (promotional prize draws), subject to Title VII. (6) Art. 10.1 requires a general licence (licencia general) per game category before operating; Art. 11.1 requires a singular licence (licencia singular) per game type. The text names the Comisión Nacional del Juego; in practice the DGOJ issues licences ([Focus Gaming News](https://focusgn.com/latinoamerica/dgoj-entrega-nueva-licencia-de-juego)). Art. 9.2 makes activity without a licence "prohibida" (prohibited) and sanctionable under Title VI.
scale: The licensed market is about €1.7bn in gross gaming revenue (2025; single source) — [Gambling Insider](https://www.gamblinginsider.com/es/?p=105043).
cost_impact: Licensing costs and fine amounts were not read (Title VI is beyond the portion of the text retrieved).
driver_status: Law in force since 2011. **Status in Oct 2026:** in force (BOE consolidated text). DGOJ guidance on fantasy, prediction or creator products was not found.
solved_today: Licensed operators only. Free fantasy apps and Twitch Predictions use points with no cash value or transferability (GAM-18, GAM-20).
software_solvable: none for real-money versions. A points-only design (non-purchasable or non-cashable, non-transferable, no prizes of economic value) is the viable path (inference; legal advice needed).
confidence: high for the legal text; medium for how it applies to specific designs.

title: Gambling advertising after STS 527/2024, and the influencer decree RD 444/2024
who: Gambling operators and the creators they sponsor; large influencers ("usuarios de especial relevancia", users of special relevance).
where: National [ES].
reality: The Supreme Court annulled key parts of RD 958/2020, including the celebrity ban, new-customer promotions, and restrictions on information-society services, video-sharing platforms and social networks, because they lacked legal-rank backing. Separately, RD 444/2024 treats only very large creators as audiovisual providers for advertising and minors' protection duties.
evidence: (1) STS 527/2024 of 2 Apr 2024, on an appeal by Jdigital, annulled art. 15 (celebrities in ads), art. 13.1 and 13.3 (new-customer promotions), art. 23.1 (a general ban on commercial communications in information-society services), art. 25.3 (video-sharing platforms) and art. 26.2–26.3 (social networks). Other articles were upheld — [Noticias de Navarra, 10 Apr 2024](https://www.noticiasdenavarra.com/sociedad/2024/04/10/supremo-anula-parte-real-decreto-8099748.html); [LegalToday, 11 Apr 2024](https://www.legaltoday.com/practica-juridica/derecho-publico/publico/el-tribunal-supremo-anula-varios-articulos-del-real-decreto-958-2020-de-comunicaciones-comerciales-de-las-actividades-de-juego-2024-04-11/); [vLex](https://vlex.com/vid/tribunal-supremo-anula-varios-1029883895); [ECIJA note, Apr 2024](https://ecija.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/ECIJA_Nota-Informativa-STS-RD-958-2020.pdf). Jdigital welcomed it — [Yogonet, 12 Apr 2024](https://www.yogonet.com/latinoamerica/noticias/2024/04/12/98729-). (2) Under RD 444/2024 (BOE 1 May 2024, in force 2 May 2024), a creator is a "usuario de especial relevancia" if they meet **all** of: at least €300,000 gross income from video-sharing activity in the previous year; at least 1M followers on one service or 2M in aggregate; and at least 24 videos a year. Such creators had two months to register in the State Registry (Ley 13/2022 art. 39) and become subject to that law's minors' protection and audiovisual commercial-communication rules — [BOE RD 444/2024](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2024/04/30/444). (3) Betting and casino brands sponsor Spanish streamers, and some creators work with unlicensed casinos (no figures) — [Que.es, 9 Jan 2026](https://www.que.es/2026/01/09/fenomeno-streaming-espana-videojuegos/).
scale: Only top creators meet RD 444/2024 (€300k and 1M followers); the number registered was not found.
cost_impact: n/a.
driver_status: Litigation by the gambling industry, and transposition of the audiovisual directive. **Status in Oct 2026:** the annulments stand. I found no evidence that the annulled provisions were re-enacted by law; this is unverified.
solved_today: Agencies and self-regulation (not verified).
software_solvable: none. This is a compliance factor: gambling-linked sponsorship of a creator league would draw scrutiny.

title: The minors' digital protection bill bans loot boxes for under-18s and adds age verification, but its passage is unverified
who: Game studios, platforms, device makers and large influencers; minors (86% of 12–17-year-olds play, GAM-02).
where: National [ES]; an EU draft is in parallel.
reality: The government's organic bill would ban minors' access to random reward mechanisms ("cajas botín", loot boxes), raise the digital-consent age from 14 to 16, require default parental controls on devices, and require age verification from large influencers. It was admitted for processing in September 2025 under the urgency procedure and was still in Congress in mid-2026.
evidence: (1) The draft first approved on 4 Jun 2024 includes a "prohibición expresa a que las niñas, niños y adolescentes accedan a los mecanismos aleatorios de recompensa" ("an express ban on children and adolescents accessing random reward mechanisms"). The DGOJ says loot boxes "funcionan con la lógica de las máquinas tragaperras" ("work with the logic of slot machines"), and that almost 24% of 15–17-year-olds bought loot boxes in the past year — [Ministerio de Derechos Sociales, Consumo y Agenda 2030, 4 Jun 2024](https://www.dsca.gob.es/es/comunicacion/notas-prensa/ministerio-consumo-prohibe-acceso-menores-cajas-botin-videojuegos-evitar). (2) The Council of Ministers gave second-round approval on 25 Mar 2025. The bill bars under-18s from accessing or activating random reward mechanisms in video games, raises the age of consent from 14 to 16, requires free parental controls "activated by default", and requires large influencers to warn about harmful content and to "implement effective age-verification systems" — [Osborne Clarke, 25 Apr 2025](https://www.osborneclarke.com/insights/spain-seeks-protect-minors-digital-environment-key-points-new-version-draft-law); [La Moncloa, 25 Mar 2025](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/lang/en/gobierno/councilministers/Paginas/2025/20250325-council-press-conference.aspx). (3) Congress rejected Vox's amendment to the whole bill (Sep 2025), allowing it to proceed, and it is processed by urgency — [Ministerio de Justicia, 10 Sep 2025](https://www.mjusticia.gob.es/es/institucional/gabinete-comunicacion/noticias-ministerio/100925-tramitacion-lo-proteccion-menores-entornos); [BOCG 15-A-52-2](https://www.congreso.es/public_oficiales/L15/CONG/BOCG/A/BOCG-15-A-52-2.PDF). (4) As an organic law it needs an absolute majority, and Junts' votes were reported as key (Dec 2025) — [The Local, 1 Dec 2025](https://www.thelocal.es/20251201/today-in-spain-a-roundup-of-the-latest-news-on-monday-58). The EU Better Internet for Kids profile (June 2026) says the bill is "currently under parliamentary consideration in the Congress of Deputies" — [BIK Spain Country Profile 2026](https://better-internet-for-kids.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2026-06/ES%20Country%20Profile%202026_final.pdf). Minister Sira Rego was reported to expect approval in autumn 2026 (seen only in a search summary; attribution uncertain). (5) EU level: a **leaked draft** "EU Kids Act" would require age verification for new accounts in online games, social media and AI — [Profesional Review, 15 Sep 2026](https://www.profesionalreview.com/2026/09/15/union-europea-eu-kids-act-borrador-filtrado/).
scale: About 24% of 15–17-year-olds bought loot boxes — [DSCA, 4 Jun 2024](https://www.dsca.gob.es/es/comunicacion/notas-prensa/ministerio-consumo-prohibe-acceso-menores-cajas-botin-videojuegos-evitar).
cost_impact: n/a.
driver_status: Child-protection politics. **Status in Oct 2026: final passage and BOE publication NOT verified.** Congress bulletins (BOCG-15-A-52-1 to 10) returned 403 through the research proxy, and searches found no final vote. Treat it as pending.
solved_today: Platform age gates and PEGI (not researched).
software_solvable: none (constraint). A Spain-launched game should avoid loot boxes and plan age assurance and voice-chat safety for minors. A league product should avoid any randomised paid mechanics.
confidence: medium. The content is verified; the current stage is not.

title: Indie discoverability: a Steam glut and dependence on streamers
who: Spanish indie studios (54% bill under €200k; 55% self-publish; 82% of PC studios rely on Steam).
where: Spain (studios) on a [GLOBAL] storefront.
reality: Release volume on Steam keeps hitting records, and most new games get almost no attention. Streamer virality is how the 2024–26 breakout co-op hits were discovered.
evidence: (1) Valve saw a record of nearly 19,000 releases in 2024 — [GamingOnLinux, Jan 2025](https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2025/01/valve-saw-a-record-breaking-nearly-19-000-games-released-on-steam-in-2024/). Over 18,000 games were released in 2025, half with fewer than 10 reviews — [MP1st, 2025–26](https://mp1st.com/news/18k-games-released-steam-2025-half-have-10-reviews); [WN Hub](https://wnhub.io/news/analytics/item-49561). 40% of 2025 Steam games earned less than $100 — [MP1st](https://mp1st.com/news/40-of-steam-games-in-2025-earned-less-than-100). Estimates for 2025 range from about 19,200 (SteamDB, late 2025) to 20,282 (Zukowski tally), and the first half of 2026 reportedly had 11,979 releases; these counts are estimates and vary by source — [Steam Page Analyzer](https://www.steampageanalyzer.com/blog/how-many-games-release-on-steam). (2) DEV: 82% of PC-focused Spanish studios use Steam as their main store, 55% self-publish, and 39% need €50k–€150k for their next project — [Forbes/DEV, 27 May 2025](https://forbes.es/economia/722211/el-videojuego-espanol-facturo-1-425-millones-en-2023-y-empleo-a-mas-de-10-000-personas-de-manera-directa/). (3) Discovery levers: indie-tagged Twitch hours rose 51% and Drops campaigns 20% in 2026 [GLOBAL] — [Vandal, 14 Sep 2026](https://vandal.elespanol.com/noticia/2026257023/twitch-supera-los-8600-millones-de-horas-de-gaming-vistas-en-2026-y-revela-los-juegos-y-streamers-mas-populares/). Mad Games Show 2026 budgeted €88,000 for a "Meet to Match" B2B marketplace — [BOE-A-2026-928](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-928).
scale: About 19–20k Steam releases a year [GLOBAL]; about 440 Spanish micro-studios (inference from DEV's 54% of 815).
cost_impact: 40% of 2025 Steam games earned under $100 — [MP1st](https://mp1st.com/news/40-of-steam-games-in-2025-earned-less-than-100).
driver_status: Low-friction publishing (Steam) plus attention scarcity. **Status in Oct 2026:** 2026 is on pace for another record.
solved_today: Twitch Drops (mostly large publishers), key distribution to creators, publishers, events and grants.
software_solvable: SaaS tool. A Spanish-language streamer-campaign or discovery tool for micro-studios fits the evidenced pain, though budgets are small (inference). Designing virality into the game, as idea (a) does, addresses the same pain from the product side.
confidence: medium. Release counts vary by tracker; the DEV data is solid.

title: Brands: sponsorship funds creator entertainment but concentrates on mega-events and English-language creators
who: Brands sponsoring creator events and leagues (telecoms, beverages, tech, gaming, betting).
where: Spain / [ES-world] / [GLOBAL].
reality: Sponsorship is the dominant revenue line of creator sports entertainment, but measured brand activity on Twitch skews English-language. Spanish-language demand is large while brand presence is reportedly thin, and gambling brands are a notable sponsor category in Spain.
evidence: (1) About 90% of Kings League revenue comes from sponsors (El Confidencial, undated) — [Emprendedores](https://emprendedores.es/gestion/ingresos-kings-league-pique/). (2) Stream Hatchet's 2025 report (36.4bn hours): top Twitch brands by unique chatters are Marvel (1.7M), Amazon (1.5M) and Coca-Cola (1.2M), and are "positioned toward English-language audiences". Twitch brand-mention data "shows no corresponding concentration of brand activity" in the Spanish-speaking demographic. No spend figures were given, so this is an inference by the outlet — [Net Influencer, 18 Feb 2026](https://www.netinfluencer.com/?p=43866). (3) Amazon Ads' Twitch sponsorship formats and matching tool cover 17 countries; Spain is not named in the snippet — [Señal News, 2 Jun 2025](https://senalnews.com/es/digital/amazon-ads-cerro-patrocinios-para-creadores-de-twitch-con-alcance-en-mexico-y-brasil). (4) Spanish streaming sponsor sectors include tech/gaming, energy drinks and snacks, e-commerce and subscriptions, telecoms, and betting and casino operators — [Que.es, 9 Jan 2026](https://www.que.es/2026/01/09/fenomeno-streaming-espana-videojuegos/). Telefónica's TBS produced La Velada V — [Señal News, 2025](https://senalnews.com/es/contenidos/tbs-de-telefonica-produjo-la-velada-del-ano-v-de-ibai-llanos). Mediaset dropping Kings League tournaments reportedly hurt sponsors (undated, single source) — [NTN24](https://www.ntn24.com/noticias-economia/pique-ya-no-factura-proyectos-de-la-expareja-de-shakira-estarian-pasando-por-problemas-economicos-451260).
scale: Not quantified for Spain (gap).
cost_impact: Kings League sponsorship is about €46M (90% of €51M), an inference combining two sources.
driver_status: Brands buy reach, which mega-events deliver. **Status in Oct 2026:** Kings League sponsors face a paused Spanish league (GAM-15).
solved_today: Agencies, platform ad products (Amazon Ads) and direct event deals.
software_solvable: SaaS tool (speculative). Tools that package mid-tier Spanish-language creators for brands target a claimed but unquantified gap, and gambling-ad restrictions limit one sponsor category.
confidence: low to medium. The brand-gap claim is unquantified.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Frozen insurer fee scales (baremos) squeeze self-employed doctors and the clinics that depend on insurers
who: Self-employed specialist doctors (autónomos) and micro clinics on insurer panels (Adeslas, Asisa, DKV, Sanitas, Mapfre). Also private hospitals.
where: National. Mobilisation was strongest in Sevilla in 2023, then spread to other provinces. Also Andalusia (Consejo Andaluz de Colegios de Médicos) and Madrid.
reality: Insurers send fee tables by email on a take-it-or-leave-it basis and refuse collective negotiation. A specialist first visit pays about €17–19 and a follow-up about €7–8, so practices must run high volumes to cover costs. Some doctors are leaving panels, especially in small provinces.
evidence:
- Adeslas: +3.5%, private policies only. The consultation fee went from €18 to €19, while surgery, diagnostic and emergency fees stayed frozen (per Unipromel). Asisa: +6.5% on all acts, backdated to 1 Jan 2025. Insurers refuse to negotiate with associations, citing Article 101 TFEU. Unipromel cites the European Commission's 29 Sep 2022 guidelines on collective agreements by solo self-employed people — [The Objective, 6 May 2025](https://theobjective.com/economia/2025-05-06/adeslas-asisa-suben-tarifa-medicos/). Corroborated by [OKDiario, 10 Jun 2025](https://okdiario.com/economia/admitida-demanda-medicos-contra-concurso-muface-considerarlo-nulo-discriminatorio-14913438), which reports Adeslas going from €18 to €19 over three years and Asisa raising first consultations by up to 12% and other acts by 6.5% for MUFACE/ISFAS/MUGEJU patients.
- Asisa paid €17.06 for an ophthalmology consultation and €20.71 for rheumatology (2022 scales supplied by Unipromel). Per patient, insurers pay a public hospital about five times what they pay a private doctor (Unipromel claim) — [The Objective, 15 Feb 2025](https://theobjective.com/economia/2025-02-15/medicos-autonomos-ofensiva-judicial-muface/)
- Older baseline: €7–15 per outpatient consultation and fee scales "30 años... congelados" (frozen for 30 years). Insurers account for 65% of private hospital groups' billing (ASPE) — [Vozpópuli, 10 Nov 2022](https://www.vozpopuli.com/espana/divorcio-sanidad-privada-hospitales-aseguradoras-bajas-primas-medicos.html). Per-act examples: minor surgery about €48, second consultation about €7–8, tear-duct wash €7.21 — [Vozpópuli, 3 Oct 2022](https://www.vozpopuli.com/espana/consulta-operar-fimosis-tarifas-denuncian-medicos-privada.html)
- About 1,900 Sevilla doctors stopped seeing patients from Adeslas, DKV, Asisa and Mapfre from September 2023, and the protest spread to seven provinces — [The Objective, 24 Sep 2023](https://theobjective.com/sanidad/2023-09-24/siete-provincias-ofensiva-medicos-privados-sevilla-aseguradoras/) (search summary; page not fetched; single-source)
scale: The top five insurers hold 71% of health premiums: Adeslas 27.8%, Sanitas 15.7%, Asisa 13.9%, DKV 7.0%, Mapfre 6.1% — [Infocop, 13 Jun 2023](https://www.infocop.es/?p=50249). 24% of Spaniards had private health insurance in 2022 — [Vozpópuli, 10 Nov 2022](https://www.vozpopuli.com/espana/divorcio-sanidad-privada-hospitales-aseguradoras-bajas-primas-medicos.html). No count of affected self-employed doctors was found.
cost_impact: Unipromel says fees were cut 10% in 2008–09 and not raised substantially for about 15 years, and it asks for +150% ([The Objective, 6 May 2025](https://theobjective.com/economia/2025-05-06/adeslas-asisa-suben-tarifa-medicos/)). Litigation: an appeal at the Audiencia Nacional against the MUFACE 2025–2027 contract (April 2025), admitted for processing ([OKDiario, 10 Jun 2025](https://okdiario.com/economia/admitida-demanda-medicos-contra-concurso-muface-considerarlo-nulo-discriminatorio-14913438)). The new MUFACE contract raised premiums paid to insurers by 41% (budget €4,429M) while doctors were left out of the negotiation — [The Objective, 15 Feb 2025](https://theobjective.com/economia/2025-02-15/medicos-autonomos-ofensiva-judicial-muface/). Quote: "muchos médicos en provincias pequeñas directamente se van a ir del cuadro" ("many doctors in small provinces will simply leave the panel").
driver_status: A market force (insurer concentration and individual contracts) plus competition law, which blocks collective fee bargaining for the self-employed. No specific regulation applies. Status Oct 2026: unresolved. The 2025–2027 MUFACE contract is in force and Unipromel's lawsuit is pending; outcome not found. A CNMC report was requested in March 2026; its status is unknown.
solved_today: Leaving panels, moving to private-pay patients, litigation via associations (Unipromel), and occasional small increases. Unipromel suggests patients pay up front and claim reimbursement, and proposes a "Muface Directo" model in which the state pays doctors directly. No software tools were documented.
software_solvable: Partly. Software cannot raise fees. It can support payer-mix profitability analysis, private-pay acquisition and reimbursement-claim ("reembolso") paperwork for patients.
confidence: High that the pain exists (several outlets, consistent figures). Most fee figures originate from Unipromel, an interested party.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Allied health professionals (psychology, physiotherapy, podiatry, nutrition, speech therapy) paid €5–20 per insurer session on terms set by the insurer
who: Self-employed psychologists, physiotherapists, podiatrists, dietitian-nutritionists, speech therapists and dentists working for insurers. Mostly autónomos and micro clinics.
where: National. The 2026 move to the CNMC was led by Andalusian councils together with the national physiotherapy council.
reality: The insurer fixes the tariff, caps the session length ("20 a 30 minutos por sesión, en el mejor de los casos": 20 to 30 minutes per session at best) and limits session numbers. The professional either accepts or loses the panel referrals.
evidence:
- 88.76% of respondents said insurers impose conditions unilaterally ("dicha negociación no existe": there is no negotiation). ATA says insurers pay "desde 5 a 20 euros la sesión", the professional receives "menos de un tercio" of what the insurer allocates, and tariffs have not been updated in "más de 30 años" — [Infocop, 13 Jun 2023](https://www.infocop.es/?p=50249). A related Infocop item reports a sample of 782 responses and complaints about caps on session numbers — [Infocop](https://www.infocop.es/?p=71679) (search summary; page not fetched)
- Physiotherapy: insurers paid about €5 per session regardless of condition or length (AEF, 2020) — [Redacción Médica, 13 Aug 2020](https://www.redaccionmedica.com/profesionales/20200813/los-fisioterapeutas-claman-por-las-bajas-tarifas-abonadas-mutuas/264642_0.html) (search summary; dated)
- The CGCFE (physiotherapists' council) asked the CNMC for a report on self-employed professionals' capacity to negotiate with insurers — [Redacción Médica, 24 Mar 2026](https://www.redaccionmedica.com/profesionales/20260324/fisioterapia-eleva-competencia-las-demandas-del-colegiado-autonomo/260131_0.html)
scale: 43,200 self-employed psychologists as of 31 Mar 2021 (Ministry of Labour, cited by [Infocop, 13 Jun 2023](https://www.infocop.es/?p=50249)). No counts were found for physiotherapists or podiatrists.
cost_impact: Income "often does not cover the cost of running a practice" (ATA, via Infocop 2023). Not quantified in euros.
driver_status: The same insurer concentration as PRO-01. Status Oct 2026: unresolved, with the CNMC route open.
solved_today: Accepting volume, leaving panels, private-pay or online practice. No pricing data was found for therapy marketplaces.
software_solvable: Partly. The tariff is not fixable by software. Practice tools could help professionals move away from insurer dependence (booking, payments, online sessions).
confidence: Medium. The fee figures date from 2020–2023; the 2026 source confirms the issue is current but gives no new numbers.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: No-shows and front-desk appointment work in private clinics
who: Private clinics of all kinds (dental, physiotherapy, psychology, aesthetic, podiatry, nutrition). Micro and small.
where: National. No city-level data was found.
reality: Reception staff phone or WhatsApp patients to confirm, empty slots go unfilled, and clinics hesitate to charge deposits.
evidence:
- 12–19% of booked appointments are not attended, costing €2,500–7,500 per centre per month with consultations averaging €50–150. The cited "Elsevier" studies are not named. The Klinikare CEO, a vendor, extrapolates more than €300M a year in losses — [El Independiente, 29 Sep 2025](https://www.elindependiente.com/sociedad/2025/09/29/las-ausencias-a-citas-medicas-cuestan-hasta-7-500-euros-al-mes-a-las-clinicas-privadas/). The same wire story ran in [Vozpópuli](https://www.vozpopuli.com/sanitatem/las-ausencias-a-citas-medicas-cuestan-hasta-7500-euros-al-mes-a-las-clinicas-privadas.html) and [The Objective](https://theobjective.com/actualidad/2025-09-29/ausencias-citas-medicas-clinicas-privadas/), so these are not independent sources.
- Spanish studies put no-shows at 10–20% — [Medesk blog (vendor), updated 19 Sep 2026](https://www.medesk.net/es/blog/penalizacion-a-pacientes-por-no-acudir-a-la-cita/)
- Public benchmark: Castilla y León primary care lost 752,932 of 23,586,954 appointments in 2024 (about 3.2%) — [The Objective, 11 Aug 2025](https://theobjective.com/espana/castilla-y-leon/2025-08-11/absentismo-medico-castilla-y-leon-2024/) (search summary)
scale: Doctoralia alone is present in 5,000 private clinics — [descubre.vc/El Economista, 20 Feb 2026](https://www.descubre.vc/noticia/doctoralia-factura-20m-en-espa-a-y-consolida-su-expansi-n-tecnol-gica-en-latam-y-europa-2026-02-20). No census of private clinics was found.
cost_impact: €2,500–7,500 per month per centre (vendor-originated estimate).
driver_status: Patient behaviour, a market issue. No sector regulation was found. The legality of no-show fees or deposits under Spanish consumer law was not verified; the Medesk page covers Colombia and France only.
solved_today: Clinni at €12.95/month + taxes, with reminders by email, SMS and Telegram and TicketBAI integration for the Basque Country; SMS pack prices are not published ([Clinni pricing, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://clinni.com/precios/)). Doctoralia's automated reminders "para reducir el ausentismo" (to reduce no-shows), price not published ([pro.doctoralia.es, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://pro.doctoralia.es/)). Klinikare's AI receptionist claims "hasta en un 50%" fewer no-shows (vendor claim, no price).
software_solvable: Yes, through reminders, deposits, waitlist auto-fill and two-way WhatsApp. But the market is crowded and cheap (about €13/month entry price).
confidence: Medium. The problem is real, but most numbers come from vendors.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Dependence on a dominant booking directory (Doctoralia/Docplanner) for patient acquisition, with opaque pricing
who: Self-employed specialists and micro/small clinics.
where: National.
reality: Clinics pay a subscription for visibility and online booking. There is no public price list, and prices are set after a sales call ("plan personalizado").
evidence:
- Doctoralia Spain's revenue was €20M in 2025 (+25%), and it is present in 5,000 private clinics — [descubre.vc citing El Economista, 20 Feb 2026](https://www.descubre.vc/noticia/doctoralia-factura-20m-en-espa-a-y-consolida-su-expansi-n-tecnol-gica-en-latam-y-europa-2026-02-20)
- Docplanner group: ARR of US$300M at end-2025, EBITDA-positive, 13 countries. Products include booking, telemedicine, remote payments and "Noa" AI clinical notes — [Forbes Chile, 1 Jul 2026](https://forbes.cl/negocios/2026-07-01/una-polaca-y-una-espanola-el-tripadvisor-de-los-medicos-suma-3-millones-de-visitas-al-mes-en-chile-y-hub-clave-para-ia/)
- The pro site shows no prices, only "Sesión gratuita" (free session) and "Plan personalizado" (custom plan) — [pro.doctoralia.es, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://pro.doctoralia.es/)
