- In user reviews, a Spanish endocrinologist called the product expensive and a long-time user cited unjustified price increases — [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/253301/Doctoralia-Pro/reviews/) (search summary; HTTP 403 on fetch; single-source)
scale: 5,000 clinics, plus individual specialists in unknown numbers.
cost_impact: Unknown. Inference only: €20M ÷ 5,000 clinics ≈ €4,000 per clinic per year if all revenue came from those clinics, so this is not a real per-clinic price.
driver_status: A market force (network effects). Nothing regulatory.
solved_today: Doctoralia subscription. Alternatives such as Top Doctors were not verified (no evidence found).
software_solvable: Partly. Own-booking, Google profile and reputation tools exist, but the directory's two-sided network is the hard part.
confidence: Low–medium. Prices and complaints are thinly documented.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Veterinary clinics — mandatory PRESVET antibiotic reporting and the RD 666/2023 sanctions regime
who: Companion-animal veterinary clinics (micro/small). About 16,460 clinicians are registered.
where: National, with reporting to the database of the autonomous community where the prescriber resides. Protests took place in Madrid, Sevilla, Pontevedra, A Coruña, Lugo, Valencia, Tarragona, Castilla y León (Valladolid) and Baleares (Palma).
reality: Every antibiotic prescribed or administered must be reported (drug, species, quantity, days of treatment, % of package used) at least every 15 days. Antibiotics are grouped A–D with antibiogram (lab-test) prerequisites. Vets describe the platform as "difícil de usar" (hard to use), say it "a veces se cae" (sometimes goes down), and report it rejecting digital certificates.
evidence:
- Mandatory for companion animals from 2 Jan 2025 (art. 39 RD 666/2023), at least fortnightly ("quincenal"). The MAPA report of May 2026 counts about 16,460 clinicians, about 3,220,000 prescriptions and 80% automated reporting via web services — [MAPA PRESVET](https://www.mapa.gob.es/es/ganaderia/temas/sanidad-animal-higiene-ganadera/Higiene-de-la-produccion-primaria-ganadera/medicamentos-veterinarios/Presvet.aspx) (search summary; HTTP 503 on fetch)
- The Colegio journal confirms the "plazo de 15 días" (15-day deadline). The Castilla y León vets' council says a delay or omission "está tipificado como muy grave y la sanción mínima es de 60.000 euros" (is classed as very serious, with a €60,000 minimum fine). The OCV (vets' collegiate body) assembly of 14 Feb 2025 unanimously asked for a moratorium on PRESVET and repeal of the sanctions regime. The OCV says nearly 5,000 vets demonstrated at MAPA — [Colvet "Información Veterinaria", Mar 2025](https://colvet.es/files/reportajes/informacionveterinaria_marzo_2025.pdf)
- Fines run from €600 (minor) to €1,200,000 (most serious). Quote: "Para mí es un exceso de burocracia" ("For me it is excessive bureaucracy") — [Hipertextual, 14 Feb 2025](https://hipertextual.com/2025/02/paren-veterinario-espana)
- About 2,000 vets protested at MAPA on 5 Mar 2025. The government (DG Valentín Almansa) said repeal "no tendría sentido" (would make no sense) because the decree implements EU Regulation 2019/6 — [Público/EFE, 6 Mar 2025](https://www.publico.es/sociedad/claves-sobre-protestas-veterinarios-regulacion-medicamentos.html). Clinics closed nationwide from 10:00 to 12:00 on 19 Mar 2025, and about 400 vets gathered in Madrid on 26 Mar 2025 — [El Debate, 26 Mar 2025](https://www.eldebate.com/sociedad/20250326/veterinarios-siguen-lucha-contra-ley-medicamento-gobierno-injustificada-desproporcionada_282516_amp.html). More than 1,500 vets gathered at the Congress on 7 May 2025 — [Agronews CyL](https://www.agronewscastillayleon.com/veterinarios-protesta-diput) (search summary)
scale: About 16,460 companion-animal clinicians and about 3.22M prescriptions in roughly 16 months (MAPA, May 2026; search summary).
cost_impact: Fines from €600 up to €1.2M. A minimum of €60,000 for "muy grave" applies according to the CyL council; this reading was not checked against the Ley de Sanidad Animal. The time burden is not quantified in any source.
driver_status: RD 666/2023 of 18 July (distribution, prescription, dispensing and use of veterinary medicines), which implements Regulation (EU) 2019/6. In force, and the PRESVET duty applies. Amended by RD 767/2025 of 2 Sep (BOE 3 Sep 2025, in force 4 Sep 2025), which kept PRESVET — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2025/09/02/767); [Uría Menéndez](https://www.uria.com/es/publicaciones/9470-principales-novedades-en-materia-de-medicamentos-de-uso-veterinario). In March 2025 a change to the sanctions regime was reported as "en trámite en las Cortes Generales" (going through the Cortes) ([Colvet, Mar 2025](https://colvet.es/files/reportajes/informacionveterinaria_marzo_2025.pdf)). Its current status could not be verified.
solved_today: 80% of clinics report automatically through practice-software web services (MAPA, search summary). The remaining 20% enter data manually on the web. Which vendors integrate (e.g., Qvet) and at what price could not be verified.
software_solvable: Yes for reporting, though largely solved already by integrations. The residual opportunity is compliance checking (A–D categories, antibiogram evidence, audit trail ahead of inspections). The restriction itself cannot be fixed by software.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Veterinarians cannot dispense full treatments, so owners are sent to pharmacies (partly relieved by RD 767/2025)
who: Veterinary clinics (micro/small) and pet owners.
where: National.
reality: The vet may supply only a partial dose and must prescribe the rest. Pharmacies sell packs of 20, 40 or 100 pills, leaving leftovers, and owners "recorrer farmacias" (go from pharmacy to pharmacy). Vets report delays in treatment.
evidence:
- Partial-dose rule and pack-size leftovers — [Hipertextual, 14 Feb 2025](https://hipertextual.com/2025/02/paren-veterinario-espana)
- Three vets said two animals had to be re-operated because dispensing was delayed (anecdotal) — [El Debate, 26 Mar 2025](https://www.eldebate.com/sociedad/20250326/veterinarios-siguen-lucha-contra-ley-medicamento-gobierno-injustificada-desproporcionada_282516_amp.html)
- Vets say most of the medicines they need are not stocked by pharmacies — [Público, 6 Mar 2025](https://www.publico.es/sociedad/claves-sobre-protestas-veterinarios-regulacion-medicamentos.html)
- RD 767/2025 widens "dispensación", allows dispensing of perfusion fluids, mineral supplements for perfusion, immunologicals and hormones (new Annex VI), lets the vet authorise a third party to collect exclusive-administration medicines, and requires establishments to document antibiotic-reduction measures — [Uría Menéndez](https://www.uria.com/es/publicaciones/9470-principales-novedades-en-materia-de-medicamentos-de-uso-veterinario); [Cuatrecasas](https://www.cuatrecasas.com/es/spain/farmaceutico-sanitario/art/medicamentos-veterinarios-reforma-espana)
- The Balearic vets' college (COVIB) called the changes positive but insufficient and still asks for less PRESVET bureaucracy — [Mallorca Diario](https://www.mallorcadiario.com/veterinarios-baleares-ven-avances-decreto-medicamento-exigen-mas-cambios) (article undated; may predate the final decree)
scale: All companion-animal clinics (see PRO-05).
cost_impact: Not quantified. Separately, vets complain that the 21% VAT on veterinary services, at the top rate since 2012, makes treatment more expensive ([Colvet, Mar 2025](https://colvet.es/files/reportajes/informacionveterinaria_marzo_2025.pdf)).
driver_status: RD 666/2023 together with RDL 1/2015 (Ley de garantías). The OCV demands an amendment to RDL 1/2015 so vets can retail all the medicines they need. RD 767/2025 is in force (partial relief) and the core restriction remains as of Oct 2026.
solved_today: Paper or electronic prescriptions to pharmacies and partial supply from the clinic's own stock.
software_solvable: Mostly no, because the barrier is regulatory. Software could help only with prescription routing and pharmacy stock lookup.
confidence: High on the rules, low on the cost of the impact.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Community pharmacies spend hours a week managing medicine shortages
who: Community pharmacies (micro).
where: National.
reality: Pharmacists locate alternatives, call distributors, contact prescribers about substitutions and handle frustrated patients.
evidence:
- European pharmacies spent an average of 12 h/week on supply incidents in 2025, double the figure of five years earlier. More than 600 medicines are affected, and 70% of countries report no improvement on 2024 (PGEU) — [Farmacéuticos (CGCOF magazine), 23 Mar 2026](https://www.farmaceuticos.com/revista/internacional/escasez-medicamentos-europa-farmacias-incidencias/) (subscriber-only; partial read)
- The CGCOF vice-president cites the PGEU figure of about 11 h/week. CisMED 2025: 207 medicines with incidents or alerts (285 in 2024, −27.37%), an average of 44 per week (60 in 2024), 6% non-substitutable, 101,364,392 shortage records reported (116,818,024 in 2024), and 13,483 pharmacies participating. FarmaHelp solves 7 in 10 cases for patients — [Corresponsables, updated 10 Feb 2026](https://www.corresponsables.com/actualidad/cismed-reduccion-27-medicamentos-con-incidencias-alertas-suministro-2025/)
scale: 13,483 pharmacies in CisMED.
cost_impact: About 11–12 h/week per pharmacy. This is an EU average; no Spain-specific hours figure was found.
driver_status: Market and supply chain (EU critical medicines). Improving in Spain in 2025.
solved_today: CisMED (the pharmacy profession's own shortage-monitoring platform), FarmaHelp (patient-facing) and pharmacy management software (vendors not verified).
software_solvable: Partly, and already well served by the profession's own tools.
confidence: High on the figures. Spain-specific time cost is a gap.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Health-data protection exposure for small clinics and pharmacies (GDPR/LOPDGDD, clinical records)
who: Every clinic and pharmacy, especially autónomos running on spreadsheets and WhatsApp.
where: National (AEPD).
reality: Patient data sits in Excel files or personal phones. Transparency notices and security are missing, and clinical records must be kept for at least five years after each care episode.
evidence:
- The AEPD fined a Castilla y León pharmacy owner €16,000 for keeping clients' health data in "un documento Excel" without informing them and without adequate security — [Economist & Jurist, 8 May 2025](https://www.economistjurist.es/actualidad-juridica/jurisprudencia/multa-de-16-000-euros-a-una-farmaceutica-que-recopilaba-los-datos-personales-y-relativos-a-la-salud-de-los-pacientes-en-un-excel/)
- AEPD 2025: 299 fines totalling about €40M (+14%), with no health-sector focus mentioned — [ECIJA, 27 Jan 2026](https://www.ecija.com/actualidad-insights/mas-sanciones-y-de-mayor-importe-la-aepd-sube-el-nivel-de-multas-en-2025/). This conflicts with €48.1M given in a summary of the AEPD annual report — [Usercentrics](https://usercentrics.com/es/knowledge-hub/memoria-anual-aepd-2025/) (search summary; not fetched)
- Public health bodies receive warnings rather than fines (art. 77 LOPDGDD), so the monetary risk falls on private providers — [Legiscope blog, 8 Sep 2026](https://www.legiscope.com/blog/aepd-sanciones-sanidad-salud.html) (search summary of Legiscope pages; secondary; its sector fine statistics, e.g. an "average €18,000 fine", are unverified and not used)
- Clinical records must be kept "como mínimo, cinco años contados desde la fecha del alta de cada proceso asistencial" (at least five years from discharge of each care episode) — [Ley 41/2002 art. 17.1, BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2002/11/14/41)
scale: Unknown.
cost_impact: €16,000 in the pharmacy case. No 2024–2026 fines against dental, physiotherapy, psychology or aesthetic clinics were found.
driver_status: GDPR and LOPDGDD 3/2018 (in force); Ley 41/2002 (in force). The EU European Health Data Space Regulation could not be checked in this session (EUR-Lex fetch failed).
solved_today: Clinic EHR software (Clinni etc.) and data-protection consultancies. Prices were not collected.
software_solvable: Yes, through compliant records, consent, access logs, retention and secure messaging.
confidence: Low–medium. The obligation is real, but there is little evidence of frequent enforcement against clinics.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: New duty for every health centre to keep verified staff-qualification records (RD 239/2026), due around January 2027
who: All authorised health centres and services, public and private, including dental, physiotherapy, psychology, aesthetic, podiatry and nutrition clinics.
where: National basic rule, enforced through the autonomous communities' authorisation and inspection regimes.
reality: Each clinic must hold an up-to-date file for every health professional, whatever their employment type (employee, autónomo, partner). The file must show official qualification and specialty, and the clinic must inform new staff about safe practices.
evidence:
- RD 239/2026 of 25 March (BOE no. 75, 26 Mar 2026, BOE-A-2026-6975), in force 1 Jul 2026, adds art. 7 to RD 1277/2003. Centres must guarantee care by staff with "la titulación oficial y las competencias y habilidades profesionales adecuadas" (the official qualification and appropriate professional skills) and keep updated information and a personal file for all health staff. Additional provision 1 gives six months to "disponer de la información actualizada de todo su personal sanitario" (have up-to-date information on all health staff). It also rewrites the unit definitions U.11 Nutrición y dietética and U.36 Tratamiento del dolor, and gives regions one year to adapt — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2026/03/25/239)
- Base rule: prior sanitary authorisation by the autonomous community is compulsory before any centre opens (art. 3.2 RD 1277/2003) — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2003/10/10/1277)
scale: All private health centres. No national count was found.
cost_impact: Not documented. Exposure is in regional inspections.
driver_status: RD 239/2026, in force since 1 Jul 2026. Staff-records deadline about 1 Jan 2027 (my calculation: six months after entry into force). Regional adaptation of the annexes is due about July 2027.
solved_today: No evidence was found. The likely current practice is HR folders and spreadsheets (inference).
software_solvable: Yes. A credential registry with colegiación and specialty checks, expiry alerts and an inspection-ready export.
confidence: High on the obligation (official text). Low on how painful businesses find it, since no complaints were found because it is so new.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Gestorías/asesorías cannot hire or replace qualified staff
who: Gestorías, asesorías fiscales/laborales/contables and accounting firms. Micro and small.
where: National. No city breakdown was found.
reality: Vacancies for tax, labour and accounting technicians stay open, owners are ageing, and fewer young people choose the career. Firms absorb more clients per technician during campaign peaks.
evidence:
- 7 in 10 firms have difficulty finding qualified staff. 98.4% of active professionals are over 30, most over 45 (Barómetro del Sector del Despacho Profesional). Quote from EDASE's director: "No es un problema de empleo. Hay vacantes, hay necesidad, pero no hay quien las cubra" ("It isn't a jobs problem. There are vacancies and there is need, but no one to fill them") — [Merca2, 4 Aug 2025](https://www.merca2.es/2025/08/04/los-despachos-y-gestorias-se-quedan-sin-personal-crisis-en-el-sector-espanol-2219718/) (the source, EDASE, trains and recruits staff for the sector, so it is an interested party)
- Hays Guía del Mercado Laboral 2026: 93% of Spanish companies struggle to find qualified talent, and finance/admin salaries are expected to rise 7% in 2026. INE ETIC Q1-2025: 8.7% of firms with 10–49 employees actively use AI, against 49.2% of large firms. An anecdote, without a source, of about 30 h/month spent typing invoices in a 4–8 person asesoría — [Copilot Gestoría blog (vendor), 23 Jul 2026, updated 22 Oct 2026](https://copilotgestoria.com/blog/no-encuentras-personal-asesoria-2026-automatizacion)
scale: More than 3 million SMEs and autónomos depend on these firms for tax and Social Security filings ([Merca2, 4 Aug 2025](https://www.merca2.es/2025/08/04/los-despachos-y-gestorias-se-quedan-sin-personal-crisis-en-el-sector-espanol-2219718/)). No count of gestorías was found.
cost_impact: Salary pressure (+7% expected for finance/admin, per Hays). Turnover and lost capacity are not quantified.
driver_status: A labour-market force plus growing regulatory complexity. Ongoing.
solved_today: Recruiting and training schools (EDASE trained more than 13,000 people in 2024), plus automation tools (Copilot Gestoría, a3 by Wolters Kluwer, Sage, ContaPlus). No prices were found.
software_solvable: Partly. Document capture, client portals and automated bookkeeping reduce hours per client but do not create staff.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Gestorías must plan client migrations around invoicing rules that keep shifting (VeriFactu postponed again; B2B e-invoicing countdown started)
who: Gestorías/asesorías and their micro clients, including the clinics, law firms and academies in this inventory.
where: National, except that the Basque Country and Navarra have their own foral systems. Clinni's TicketBAI integration ([Clinni](https://clinni.com/precios/)) shows the Basque route; the scope of the foral exemption was not verified in this session.
reality: Firms prepared clients for VeriFactu in 2025, then had to re-plan twice. They must now also plan B2B e-invoicing, which uses private exchange platforms plus a public solution, for every client. Clients keep asking "¿me afecta y cuándo?" ("does this affect me, and when?").
evidence:
- RDL 15/2025 of 2 Dec (BOE 3 Dec 2025, validated 11 Dec) moved VeriFactu to 1 Jan 2027 for Corporate Income Tax payers and 1 Jul 2027 for everyone else — [Legal Today, 4 Dec 2025](https://www.legaltoday.com/actualidad-juridica/noticias-de-derecho/nueva-prorroga-verifactu-no-sera-obligatorio-hasta-2027-para-sociedades-y-otros-contribuyentes-2025-12-04/); [Maldita, 3 Dec 2025](https://maldita.es/malditobulo/20251203/hacienda-retrasa-a-2027-la-entrada-en-vigor-de-verifactu-el-sistema-de-verificacion-de-facturas-para-pymes-y-autonomos)
- On 5 Oct 2026 the government announced it "se aplazarán hasta octubre de 2028" (will postpone until October 2028) the VeriFactu obligations not yet in force. No legal instrument has been identified yet — [CMS, 6 Oct 2026](https://cms.law/en/esp/publication/factura-electronica-b2b-arranca-la-cuenta-atras-y-veri-factu-se-aplaza-a-2028); [Emprendedores](https://emprendedores.es/gestion/aplazamiento-verifactu-2028/) (needs a norm with the rank of law); [TeamSystem, 7 Oct 2026](https://teamsystem.es/magazine/verifactu-se-aplaza-2028/) ("announced", with the RDL 15/2025 calendar still in force until a new norm appears). One headline calls it "el cuarto aplazamiento en tres años" (the fourth postponement in three years) — [wwwhatsnew, 6 Oct 2026](https://wwwhatsnew.com/2026/10/06/hacienda-verifactu-octubre-2028-aplazamiento-factura-electronica-2026)
- B2B e-invoicing: RD 238/2026 of 25 Mar (BOE 31 Mar 2026; in force 20 Apr 2026 per the Consejo General de Gestores) — [AEAT news, 31 Mar 2026](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/eu_es/todas-noticias/2026/marzo/31/facturacion-electronica-obligatoria.html) (search summary); [Consejo General de Gestores, 30 Apr 2026](https://www.consejogestores.org/?p=14916). Orden HAC/1028/2026 of 2 Oct (BOE 5 Oct 2026, BOE-A-2026-20587, in force 6 Oct 2026) sets 6 Oct 2027 for turnover above €8M and 6 Oct 2028 for the rest — [Garrigues, 6 Oct 2026](https://www.garrigues.com/es_ES/noticia/comienza-computo-plazos-aplicacion-factura-electronica-obligatoria-empresarios.md); consistent with [CMS](https://cms.law/en/esp/publication/factura-electronica-b2b-arranca-la-cuenta-atras-y-veri-factu-se-aplaza-a-2028)
- The draft-order calendar summarised by the Consejo General de Gestores puts the public solution (SPFE) online on 1 Aug 2027 and invoice-status reporting for firms with turnover of €8M or less on 1 Oct 2029 (draft dates; may differ in the final order) — [CGG, 30 Apr 2026](https://www.consejogestores.org/?p=14916)
scale: More than 3M SME and autónomo clients of advisory firms (Merca2, see PRO-10).
cost_impact: Not quantified; no gestoría survey of hours was found.
driver_status: RD 1007/2023 (VeriFactu) with RDL 15/2025 dates (in force: 1 Jan / 1 Jul 2027), and a postponement to Oct 2028 announced but not enacted. Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), RD 238/2026 and Orden HAC/1028/2026 are in force, with deadlines of 6 Oct 2027 and 6 Oct 2028.
solved_today: Invoicing and ERP vendors (Billin, Quipu, TeamSystem, Holded, a3, Sage). The tax/invoicing researcher covers prices.
software_solvable: Yes. A gestoría-side "compliance cockpit" could track which clients are on compliant software and the deadline for each. This overlaps with the invoicing researcher's scope.
confidence: High on status (two law firms, the Consejo de Gestores and AEAT). Medium on gestoría workload (inferred).

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Small law firms — the MASC pre-litigation requirement (since 3 April 2025) adds a documented negotiation step, risk of inadmission and cost penalties
who: Small law firms and autónomo lawyers in civil and commercial work, plus landlords and property managers in eviction cases (administradores de fincas).
where: National, but criteria differ by court. Documented cases: the Las Palmas de Gran Canaria courts' unified criteria and the Collado Villalba (Madrid) criteria.
reality: Before filing, the lawyer must send a negotiation invitation (burofax, certified email or mediation), prove that the counterparty received it at an address that belongs to them, record the outcome, and describe all of it in the claim. Otherwise the claim can be rejected. Refusing to negotiate can lead to adverse costs.
evidence:
- LO 1/2025 of 2 January (BOE 3 Jan 2025) entered into force three months after publication. A MASC (medio adecuado de solución de controversias: an approved out-of-court dispute-resolution step) is required before civil and commercial claims, excluding labour, criminal and insolvency cases and cases with public-sector parties. Accepted methods include direct negotiation, mediation, conciliation, a neutral expert opinion, a confidential binding offer and collaborative law. Under art. 10, proof is a document from the neutral third party, a document signed by both parties, or any document proving the other party received the invitation, on what date, and had access to its content. Claims must include these documents "so pena de inadmisión". Cost rules: arts. 245, 394 and 395 LEC. Fines for "abuso del servicio público de justicia" (abuse of the public justice service): art. 247 — [PwC Tax & Legal, Jan 2025](https://periscopiofiscalylegal.pwc.es/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Retos-derivados-de-los-MASC-como-requisito-de-procedibilidad.pdf)
- Evictions: the requirement applies from 3 April 2025 — [CAF Madrid PDF, May 2025](https://cafmadrid.es/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/La-negociacion-previo-como-nuevo-requisito-de-procedibilidad-de-los-juicios-de-desahucio.pdf) (search summary)
- Las Palmas courts: if the claim makes no reference to these points "la misma será inadmitida a trámite" (it will be rejected) — [Confilegal-hosted criteria, Apr 2025](https://confilegal.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/UNIFICACION-CRITERIOS-MASC-INSTANCIA-LPGC.pdf) (search summary). Collado Villalba excludes some procedures, such as cambiario (bills of exchange), summary possession and enforcement of judicial titles — [ICPM PDF](https://www.icpm.es/downDocs/2390_CRITERIOS%20MASC%20%20COLLADO%20VILLALBA_2.pdf) (search summary). Practice is therefore not uniform.
- Case-law headline: "Los MASC no se cumplen con acreditar la entrega de un correo: hay que probar que la dirección pertenece al demandado" ("MASC is not satisfied by proving an email was delivered: you must prove the address belongs to the defendant") — [Economist & Jurist (related-article headline), page dated 13 Jul 2025](https://www.economistjurist.es/?p=231084)
- Academic critique on access to justice — [Ferreiro Baamonde, InDret 2/2026](https://indret.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2006.pdf)
scale: Civil courts received 3,563,038 new cases in 2024 (about +20% on 2023); 2,688,606 were pending at the end of 2024 (CGPJ annual report 2025, cited by [InDret 2/2026](https://indret.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2006.pdf)). Most civil claims now need a MASC step, subject to the exclusions. Court-referred mediation was negligible before the reform: in 2024, 647 non-family civil referrals produced only 70 agreements (same source).
cost_impact: Risk of inadmission, adverse costs and fines for abuse. Extra billable or non-billable hours are not quantified. No statistics on inadmissions or on the fall in filings after April 2025 were found.
driver_status: LO 1/2025 (in force; MASC required since 3 Apr 2025).
solved_today: Burofax and certified-email services, mediators and lawyers' own templates. Practice software with LexNET integration includes MN Program ("desde 1 € al día", from €1 a day) and SuDespacho (from €35.95/month), both vendor prices reported by [Upliora blog, 21 Oct 2026](https://www.upliora.es/blog/ia-despachos-procuradores-abogados-lexnet-software-gestion-2026). Kmaleon, Aranzadi Fusión and Tirant do not publish prices.
software_solvable: Yes. A MASC workflow could cover invitation templates, certified delivery with proof of the counterparty's address, timeline and evidence bundle, the interruption of limitation periods, and auto-drafting the claim section describing the negotiation.
confidence: High on the regulation. Medium on the size of the operational impact (no inadmission statistics).

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Court reorganisation and LexNET notification load overwhelm small firms' deadline control
who: Small law firms, autónomo lawyers and procuradores (court agents). Labour lawyers who litigate without a procurador are especially exposed.
where: National. The Madrid bar (ICAM) has raised the issue with the Ministry of Justice.
reality: Notifications arrive through LexNET every day of the year and each one starts a deadline. After the court reform, filings go to new court inboxes. Deadlines must be calculated by hand, accounting for local holidays, August and grace days.
evidence:
- LO 1/2025 rollout: 315 Tribunales de Instancia set up from 1 Jul 2025, 16 from 1 Oct 2025 and 100 from 31 Dec 2025, 431 in total. LexNET has no documented public API for third parties. Deadline calculation "must be validated by a person" — [Upliora blog (vendor), 21 Oct 2026](https://www.upliora.es/blog/ia-despachos-procuradores-abogados-lexnet-software-gestion-2026) (single-source)
- LexNET notifies "los 365 días al año" (365 days a year), so labour lawyers without procuradores cannot take holidays, and the same applies during maternity or sick leave. The associations asked for a change in the law, and the Ministry agreed it should be regulated by law — [ICAM](https://web.icam.es/primera-reunion-en-el-colegio-con-el-ministerio-de-justicia-para-debatir-las-preocupaciones-de-la-abogacia-madrilena-en-el-uso-de-lexnet/) (page dated 2018/2020; old)
scale: Kmaleon Procuradores (Wolters Kluwer) claims more than 8,000 users (vendor claim, via Upliora).
cost_impact: Not quantified (missed deadlines lead to professional-liability claims; no data).
driver_status: LO 1/2025, with court phases completed by 31 Dec 2025, and the LexNET rules (in force). No 2025–2026 evidence of specific LexNET outages was found.
solved_today: Practice-management software with LexNET integration (MN Program, SuDespacho, Kmaleon, New Procurador V5, Aranzadi Fusión, Tirant). Prices are mostly unpublished.
software_solvable: Partly. Notification triage and deadline computation are possible with a human check, but the lack of a public LexNET API limits automation.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Driving schools — practical-exam bottleneck, slot rationing and disputed waiting lists
who: Driving schools (autoescuelas), mostly micro and small, though some chains are large (Autoescuela Lara has 65 centres in Madrid).
where: National, with hotspots in Andalusia (Sevilla, Málaga, Almería, Cádiz), Catalonia (Barcelona, Lleida), Madrid, Murcia, Valencia and Alicante, Baleares (Palma), Navarra, Tenerife and Aragón.
reality: Students who pass the theory test wait weeks or months for a practical slot. Schools keep giving paid lessons to hold students' skills, tie up cars and instructors, and lose students who give up. Slot allocation depends on each school's pass rate.
evidence:
- The DGT says the "mal llamada 'lista de espera'" (the so-called waiting list) counts everyone who passed theory and has two years to sit the practical, and that fewer than 10% were presented when unlimited exams were offered. The DGT added 130 examiner posts to reach 21 examiners per million inhabitants. Pass rates: Lleida 46.15% (51.71% in Jan–Apr), Almería 70%, Baleares more than half failed — [DGT, 16 Jun 2026](https://www.dgt.es/export/sites/web-DGT/.galleries/downloads/nota_prensa/2026/20260616-nota-de-prensa.pdf)
- DGT head Pere Navarro told the Congress "solo un 8 % de la bolsa de alumnos está en condiciones de examinarse" (only 8% of the pool is ready to sit the exam). The driving-schools confederation CNAE called this "inaceptable" (unacceptable) and the PRO plan "un parche" (a patch). Spain holds more than 1 million practical tests a year. Catalonia, Madrid, Murcia and Cádiz are the most saturated — [Motor.es, 19 May 2026](https://www.motor.es/noticias/pere-navarro-dgt-enfurece-autoescuelas-listas-espera-2026114254.html)
- Valencia has about 19,000 students in the pool, up more than 3,000 in three years. Waits for a retest are "dos o tres meses" (two or three months). In Madrid, students wait from 1.5 to 5 months. The DGT says its staffing plan is 97% covered, with about 50 new examiners a year and 732 since 2017. Each examiner does 12 tests a day, and 46% fail their first practical — [Xataka, 5 Sep 2025](https://www.xataka.com/movilidad/se-frustran-dejan-autoescuelas-denuncian-que-lista-esperar-para-examen-conducir-interminable-dgt-niega)
- Andalusia: 82,000 students (sector figure), up to 5 months for professional licences, and simultaneous protests at every DGT office in the region on 17 Jul 2026 (70–100 firms in Sevilla) — [El Español, 17 Jul 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/invertia/20260717/autoescuelas-pie-guerra-alumnos-esperan-practico-andalucia-faltan-examinadores/1003744322825_0.amp.html)
- Baleares: more than 7,000 students waiting, with 2.5-month delays for cars — [Mallorca Diario](https://www.mallorcadiario.com/autoescuelas-alertan-colapso-obliga-muchos-alumnos-examinarse-practicas-fuera-mallorca) (search summary; HTTP 403 on fetch)
- The CAPA algorithm splits each provincial office's exam capacity among driving schools according to their theory pass rates and number of candidates. Historic baseline from 2021: 704 operational examiners (almost 1,000 in 2006) and more than 2 million people waiting — [Vozpópuli, 25 Mar 2021](https://www.vozpopuli.com/economia/lista-espera-carne-conducir.html) (dated)
scale: More than 1M practical tests a year. Claimed pools of 63,000 in Barcelona, 82,000 in Andalusia and 19,000 in Valencia (all disputed).
cost_impact: Students pay extra lessons while waiting, and cars and instructors are tied up for weeks ([Motor.es](https://www.motor.es/noticias/pere-navarro-dgt-enfurece-autoescuelas-listas-espera-2026114254.html)). Students drop out ([Xataka](https://www.xataka.com/movilidad/se-frustran-dejan-autoescuelas-denuncian-que-lista-esperar-para-examen-conducir-interminable-dgt-niega)). No euro figures were found.
driver_status: Examiner capacity (DGT staffing plan, retirements, leave) and CAPA allocation. The DGT's Plan de Refuerzo Operativo (PRO) ran as a pilot in May–June 2026 and is being extended (Barcelona from 13 Jun 2026, Tenerife late June). 101 new examiners joined 46 provincial traffic offices in September 2025 (search summary; single-source). Status: ongoing as of Oct 2026.
solved_today: Saturday PRO sessions, sending students to smaller exam centres, and protests. Driving-school management software and its prices were not researched (gap).
software_solvable: Partly. Software can track readiness and pass probability (to win CAPA slots and send only ready students), schedule practical lessons and produce the verified student lists the DGT now asks for. It cannot create examiner capacity.
confidence: High that the pain exists. The magnitude is contested (sector versus DGT).

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Private 0–3 nurseries — proposed ratio cut and dependence on regional free-place schemes
who: Private early-years centres (escuelas infantiles 0–3), mostly micro and small.
where: National proposal. Regional schemes: Galicia (full free places in private centres), Madrid (cheque infantil), La Rioja (association opposing the cut).
reality: Owners fear fewer children per classroom without compensation would cut income, while fees are capped by what families can pay or by subsidy rules. Where places are free (Galicia), centres join the scheme each year and are paid by the Xunta in instalments.
evidence:
- ACADE (24 Jun 2026): if the ratios are applied "sin medidas compensatorias" (without compensating measures), the 5,345 private centres could close, leaving more than 224,000 pupils (about 50% of the stage) without places and putting more than 60,000 jobs at risk. Data source: "Las cifras de la educación en España. Curso 2023/2024 (edición 2026)" — [ACADE press release](https://educacionprivada.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/NP_ACADE_Bajada_ratios_Infantil_amenaza_cierre_escuelas_privadas_24-06-2026.pdf)
- On 27 Jul 2026 ACADE met the Secretary of State for Education and rejected the "propuesta de reducción de ratios planteada por el Gobierno y consensuada con los sindicatos" (ratio-cut proposal put forward by the Government and agreed with the unions). ACADE stresses that non-concerted private centres "no reciben financiación" (receive no public funding) — [ACADE press release, 27 Jul 2026](https://educacionprivada.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/NdP_ACADE_Reunion_Secretario_Estado_Reduccion_Ratios.pdf)
- The La Rioja association joined the opposition, citing more than 5,000 centres, about 60,000 jobs and about 224,000 pupils — [nuevecuatrouno, 3 Jul 2026](https://nuevecuatrouno.com/2026/07/03/escuelas-infantiles-rioja-alzan-contra-reduccion-ratios/) (search summary; HTTP 403 on fetch)
- Galicia has paid for free places for 100% of 0–3 pupils in private and social-initiative centres since 2022/23: €45.7M for 2024/25. Payment runs as an advance of 100% of the September–December amount, then advances of 45% and 45%, with 10% at the end of the year. Centres have one month after the call is published in the DOG to join — [Xunta, 24 Jun 2024](https://www.xunta.gal/notas-de-prensa/-/nova/003039/xunta-consolida-gratuidad-las-escuelas-infantiles-0-3-iniciativa-social-privadas). For 2025/26: more than €65M and more than 32,000 families — [Xunta press releases](https://www.xunta.gal/es/notas-de-prensa/-/nova/014503/xunta-consolida-liderazgo-galicia-educacion-infantil-con-una-nueva-orden-ayudas) (search summary; exact page not fetched)
- Madrid: a cheque infantil scheme for private centres (2020 support line) — [Comunidad de Madrid, 21 May 2020](https://www.comunidad.madrid/node/56851) (dated)
scale: 5,345 private centres, more than 224,000 pupils and more than 60,000 jobs (ACADE, using ministry statistics).
cost_impact: ACADE projects closures. This is an interested-party projection, not an observed outcome.
driver_status: A ministry proposal on 0–3 ratios, agreed with public-network unions (June–July 2026). Status: draft/proposal. No BOE text and no exact ratios were found as of 23 Oct 2026.
solved_today: Lobbying through employers' associations. Software in use (enrolment, family billing, subsidy claims) was not researched.
software_solvable: Partly. Administering subsidies and free-place claims, waitlists and fees is software territory. The ratio rule is not.
confidence: Medium (interested-party projections; regulation still a draft).

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Elderly residences — 2022 accreditation model (staff ratios, living units, single rooms) due by 2029 against low public concert prices
who: Private and concerted elderly residences (small and medium; also large groups).
where: A national framework agreement, applied by each autonomous community. Madrid has a documented price and ratio framework. CEAPs and ACRA (Catalonia) are vocal.
reality: Operators must hire more care staff (gerocultores) and restructure buildings into "home-like" units, while regional concert prices barely cover current costs. Staff rotas must meet ratio and contract-stability rules.
evidence:
- Agreement of the Consejo Territorial (28 Jun 2022, approved 10–9). At least 80% of contracts must be indefinite and 66% full-time (50% in SAD). Living units of at most 15 residents. New centres capped at 75, 90 or 120 places depending on population density. New centres need 65% single rooms for public places. Regions had nine months to legislate, with a transition until 2030 — [Público, 29 Jun 2022](https://www.publico.es/sociedad/seran-partir-residencias-mayores.html)
- Existing residences have until December 2029, and about 80% must create living units of fewer than 15 people. CEAPs: concert prices "tan bajos como 54 euros (o incluso menos)" (as low as €54 or even less) per place per day must rise to at least €75. Quote: "sin financiación suficiente" (without enough funding) the model cannot be applied — [Diari de Tarragona, 11 Jul 2022](https://www.diaridetarragona.com/sociedad/no-hay-dinero-para-aplicar-el-nuevo-modelo-de-residencias-OA11661096)
- Ratio target of 0.51 professionals per resident by 2029; about 21,071 extra residence jobs, part of a total of more than 34,000 new jobs — [Valencia Plaza](https://valenciaplaza.com/valenciaplaza/el-gobierno-preve-que-el-acuerdo-del-modelo-de-residencias-suponga-la-creacion-de-mas-de-34000-empleos) (search summary)
- Madrid: €54.51 to €74.88/day; direct care 0.42 to 0.47; gerocultores 0.33; cleaning, food and maintenance 0.15; direct-care staff cannot be subcontracted — [Comunidad de Madrid, 28 Jan 2021](https://www.comunidad.madrid/node/59061)
scale: No reliable count of residences or residents was found in this session. A search summary also attributed to CEAPs a figure of about 180,000 residents and 33,000 day-centre users paying out of pocket, but the source page could not be identified, so the figure is not used.
cost_impact: A gap of about €21 or more per place per day between low concert prices and the €75 CEAPs estimate (my calculation from the CEAPs figures).
driver_status: The 2022 Consejo Territorial accreditation agreement, with existing centres due by December 2029. Its transposition status in each region as of Oct 2026 was not verified, and the sources are from 2021–2022.
solved_today: Re-tendered framework agreements at higher prices (Madrid). Rostering, family-communication and care-record software was not researched.
software_solvable: Partly. Rostering against ratios, compliance reporting to regions and family communication can be served by software. Funding and buildings cannot.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Home-help (SAD) providers squeezed by capped hourly prices in municipal tenders that include travel time
who: SAD companies, from small regional operators to large groups, plus not-for-profits (e.g., Cruz Roja in Orihuela).
where: Municipal, funded by the region. Documented in Vigo (Galicia), El Puerto de Santa María (Cádiz), Orihuela (Alicante), Granada and Catalonia.
reality: The company bids a price per hour of care. Travel between homes, coordination, supervision and training must be covered within that price, while collective-agreement wage rises keep pushing costs up.
evidence:
- Vigo: €49.5M over 3 years (about €16M a year), hourly price rising from €16.70 to €22 "por el incremento de salarios" (because of wage increases). The mayor demands the Xunta pay it "íntegramente" (in full) — [Vigo e, 17 Mar 2025](https://vigoe.es/vigo/local/vigo-pone-en-marcha-uno-de-sus-megacontratos-y-caballero-exige-que-lo-pague-la-xunta)
- A Catalan tender states the hourly price "incluye todos los costes organizativos como desplazamientos, coordinación, supervisión y formación" (includes all organisational costs such as travel, coordination, supervision and training) — [TED 2025 notices](https://ted.europa.eu/es/notice/92082-2025/pdf) (search summary; the exact notice was not confirmed)
- Orihuela: cap of €17/h; €206,672 over 2 years — [Alicante Plaza, 15 Apr 2020](https://alicanteplaza.es/alicanteplaza/cuatro-empresas-optan-al-contrato-de-prestacion-del-servicio-municipal-de-ayuda-a-domicilio-en-orihuela) (dated)
- El Puerto de Santa María: more than €5.6M over 2 years for about 400 users, funded mainly by the Junta de Andalucía. A worker agreement caps the working week at 35 hours — [Diario Bahía de Cádiz, 19 Jul 2023](https://diariobahiadecadiz.com/el-puerto/licitado-en-el-puerto-por-un-precio-historico-el-servicio-de-ayuda-a-domicilio)
- The accreditation agreement requires at least 50% full-time contracts in SAD — [Público, 29 Jun 2022](https://www.publico.es/sociedad/seran-partir-residencias-mayores.html)
scale: Not found nationally.
cost_impact: Margins hinge on the gap between the price cap and wage rises. Loss figures were not found.
driver_status: Public procurement (Ley 9/2017 LCSP) and dependency-law funding. Ongoing.
solved_today: Re-tendering at higher prices and lobbying regions. Scheduling and route software was not researched.
software_solvable: Partly. Route optimisation to cut unpaid travel, visit verification, hours reporting to councils and rostering. The price cap itself is not fixable by software.

track: Clinics, professional services, education and care
title: Households as employers of domestic workers — risk assessment (RD 893/2024) on top of the 2022 reform's duties
who: Households employing domestic and care workers (empleadas de hogar), plus the gestorías that handle their payroll.
where: National.
reality: Each employing household must complete an online risk assessment of the home, implement measures, hand information material to the worker and keep the signed plan for labour inspectors. This comes on top of Social Security registration and contributions, including unemployment contributions since 2022.
evidence:
- The free tool on Prevencion10.es was launched on 14 May 2025. Employers "dispondrán de un plazo de seis meses" (have six months) to complete the assessment, finishing "antes del próximo noviembre" (before next November). More than 348,000 women are registered with Social Security, about 38,000 of them live-in workers, with an average salary of about €1,014/month — [INSST press release, 14 May 2025](https://www.insst.es/documents/d/portal-insst/yolanda-diaz-presenta-la-herramienta-para-evaluar-los-riesgos-laborales-de-las-trabajadoras-del-hogar-nota-de-prensa)
- Households' deadline 14 Nov 2025. Results are "no se envía a ningún lado, se guarda en la casa" (not sent anywhere, kept at home). Working-time records had not been implemented. At least a quarter of households with undocumented live-in workers will not do the assessment (claim by a workers' association) — [El Salto, 26 May 2025](https://www.elsaltodiario.com/trabajo-domestico/prevencion10-herramienta-evaluacion-riesgos-empleo-hogar)
- More than 378,000 workers registered under the special Social Security scheme against about 540,000 counted in the EPA labour-force survey (implying informal work). The sector lost 53,000 workers in a year. The employers' association AESPD says the minimum wage has risen 61% since 2018. The platform collapsed, with the Ministry reporting almost 50M access attempts in 24 h and more than 16,000 suspicious IPs blocked. The technical guide, harassment protocol and training platform promised for early 2026 were still pending in May 2026. Unions UGT and CCOO asked the labour inspectorate not to be punitive at first — [El Español, 20 May 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/mujer/estilo-vida/20260520/asesora-financiera-nueva-ley-limpiadoras-hogar-unico-consigue-nadie-contrate/1003744249353_0.amp.html)
- RD 893/2024 has been in force since 13 Sep 2024, with duties enforceable six months after the tool became available — [umivale activa report](https://umivaleactiva.es/dam/umivale-activa/novedades-normativas/2024/Informe-Externo-RD-893_2024.pdf) (search summary)
scale: About 348,000–378,000 registered workers (and roughly as many employing households). About 540,000 domestic workers in the EPA.
cost_impact: The tool is free. Fines were not quantified, as the press only mentions "amenaza de sanciones" (threat of sanctions). Opinion from an adviser: "Así lo único que conseguirán es que nadie las contrate" ("All they will achieve is that nobody hires them") (El Español, 20 May 2026).
driver_status: RD 893/2024 is in force and the household deadline (Nov 2025) has passed. The 2022 reform (RDL 16/2022, unemployment contributions) is in force (described in the INSST release and El Salto, which also cites ILO Convention 189, in force in Spain since 24 Feb 2024). The government guides were still pending as of May 2026.
solved_today: Prevencion10 (free, risk assessment only), and gestorías or advisers for payroll (e.g., Dancausas Asesores is quoted). Household-payroll platforms and their prices were not researched.
software_solvable: Yes. An all-in-one household-employer app could handle the contract, Social Security registration, monthly contributions and payslips, store the Prevencion10 output, record working time and remind employers of renewals. The free government tool covers only one step.
confidence: High (official INSST source plus two independent press sources).

title: Staff shortages, 40–60% turnover and rising absenteeism
who: Bars, restaurants, cafés and hotels of all sizes, from autónomo to medium. Micro and small firms are least able to pay premiums to attract staff.
where: National. Most acute in highly seasonal coastal and island destinations (Baleares, Canarias, Costa del Sol). A staffing startup is piloting in A Coruña.
reality: Owners cannot fill camarero de sala, cocinero, ayudante de cocina, barra, jefe de cocina and encargado roles. With 40–60% annual rotation they are always recruiting and training, owners often cover shifts themselves, and absenteeism leaves shifts uncovered at short notice.
evidence:
- Hostelería accounts for 13.37% of all hard-to-fill vacancies in Spain (SEPE Observatorio de las Ocupaciones), "sólo por detrás de algunos sectores administrativos y sanitarios". The six hardest profiles are those listed above — [El Debate, 26 Jul 2026](https://www.eldebate.com/espana/galicia/20260726/empresa-gallega-encuentra-solucion-cubrir-vacantes-hosteleria-forma-rapida_443319_amp.html) (single source for the 13.37% figure).
- Annual rotation is 40–60% in traditional establishments and above 70% in very seasonal businesses. The source notes "No existe una estadística oficial única" — [El Debate, 26 Jul 2026](https://www.eldebate.com/espana/galicia/20260726/empresa-gallega-encuentra-solucion-cubrir-vacantes-hosteleria-forma-rapida_443319_amp.html) (sector estimates, single source).
- Absenteeism in tourism firms rose to 7.7% of agreed hours in summer 2026, up from 6.6% in June. Its total cost equals 3.8% of turnover. Exceltur lists "escasez de talento y aumento del absentismo" among the adverse factors of summer 2026 — [Exceltur nº98, Oct 2026](https://www.exceltur.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/EXCELTUR-Informe-Perspectivas-N98-Balance-del-IIIT26-y-previsiones-para-IVT26.pdf)
- Tourism employment rose by 105,160 Social Security affiliates year on year. Wages rose 3.5% in hostelería against 3.0% in the rest of the economy, and 85.6% of new tourism contracts in Sep 2026 were permanent (indefinidos) — [Exceltur nº98, Oct 2026](https://www.exceltur.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/EXCELTUR-Informe-Perspectivas-N98-Balance-del-IIIT26-y-previsiones-para-IVT26.pdf)
- In 2023, Hostelería de España president José Luis Yzuel said "Faltan unos 100.000 trabajadores" ("about 100,000 workers are missing") — [Valencia Plaza (search summary; 2023 quote)](https://valenciaplaza.com/valenciaplaza/restauracion-faltan-100000-empleados-por-que-ocurre-esto-espana)
- Mallorca restaurateurs cite "high staff turnover" alongside soaring rents and no-shows — [Majorca Daily Bulletin, 17 Aug 2026](https://www.majorcadailybulletin.com/news/local/2026/08/17/145039/mallorca-bars-and-restaurants-suffer-per-cent-drop-turnover-during-the-first-half-august.html)
scale: 1.85 million jobs and more than 300,000 companies — [Hostelería de España](https://www.hosteleriadeespana.es/)
cost_impact: Absenteeism alone costs about 3.8% of turnover (Exceltur). I found no source for the cost per departure (recruiting, training, lost productivity).
driver_status: A tight labour market, unsocial hours and seasonality. On collective bargaining, unions and employers signed a modification of the VI ALEH (state labour agreement for hospitality) on 13 Apr 2026, covering LGTBI protocols, climate-risk prevention and a hearing before disciplinary dismissal — [CEHAT, 14 Apr 2026](https://cehat.com/notaprensa/sindicatos-y-patronales-dan-un-paso-decisivo-para-la-hosteleria-con-la-firma-del-nuevo-acuerdo-estatal-aleh/). Status: in force. Convenio wages and time recording belong to the labour researcher.
solved_today: Job portals, temp agencies (ETTs) and word of mouth. New on-demand matching apps are appearing, such as Rapitalento (A Coruña, launched mid-2026; requests by web or WhatsApp voice note, AI matching, free for workers, establishments pay a monthly or quarterly subscription whose price is not disclosed) — [El Debate, 26 Jul 2026](https://www.eldebate.com/espana/galicia/20260726/empresa-gallega-encuentra-solucion-cubrir-vacantes-hosteleria-forma-rapida_443319_amp.html). I verified no prices for scheduling or absence-management tools.
software_solvable: Partly. Staffing marketplaces, shift planning and absence prediction reduce friction, but pay, hours and housing (HOS-26) drive the shortage.
confidence: High that the pain is severe and widespread; medium on the exact magnitudes.

title: No-shows and the cost of guaranteeing reservations
who: Reservation-driven restaurants, mostly micro and small, in cities and tourist areas.
where: National. 2025 no-show rates: Alicante 3.1%, Valencia 3.2%, Madrid 3.3%, Málaga 3.3%, Barcelona 3.5%, Sevilla 3.7%. Mallorca restaurateurs list no-shows among their pressures.
reality: Tables are held for parties who never arrive, especially at peak services. To protect themselves, restaurants increasingly ask for a card guarantee or prepayment, which creates friction with customers and pushes them onto paid software tiers.
evidence:
- TheFork data: the national no-show rate was 3.3% in 2025, down from 3.6% in 2024. 21% of restaurants use a card guarantee (huella bancaria), double the 2023 share, and 7% use card prepayment, triple the share of two years earlier. TheFork removes users with four no-shows in 12 months; 2% of users were removed in 2025 — [Majorca Daily Bulletin, 28 Feb 2026](https://www.majorcadailybulletin.com/news/local/2026/02/28/140559/spanish-restaurants-take-stand-against-shows-balearic-sector-struggled-last-year.html); same figures in [Vinetur, 24 Feb 2026 (search summary)](https://www.vinetur.com/2026022496663/la-restauracion-espanola-reduce-la-tasa-de-no-show-al-33-en-2025-segun-thefork.html). Both reports rest on the same TheFork data, so they are not independent.
- In a 2025 TheFork survey of diners who missed a booking without cancelling, 55% said they forgot, 38% had a last-minute problem and 7% were embarrassed to call — [Vinetur (search summary)](https://www.vinetur.com/2026022496663/la-restauracion-espanola-reduce-la-tasa-de-no-show-al-33-en-2025-segun-thefork.html)
- With an average spend of €27 per diner and 2.9 diners per booking, each no-show table loses about €78.30 of potential revenue. A restaurant taking 500 bookings a month would lose more than €15,500 a year (revenue, not profit) — [ESdiario (search summary; date unclear)](https://www.esdiario.com/economia/260708/192740/coste-reservas-fantasma-restaurantes.html)
- A claim that no-shows cost affected establishments 5–20% gives no methodology — [Vinetur, 12 Aug 2025 (search summary)](https://www.vinetur.com/2025081290379/las-reservas-fantasma-afectan-a-los-restaurantes-espanoles-pese-a-la-reduccion-de-no-shows-este-verano.html) (low reliability).
scale: The number of restaurants that take bookings in Spain was not found.
cost_impact: About €78 of potential revenue per no-show table, and at least €15,500 a year for a restaurant taking 500 bookings a month (ESdiario estimate).
driver_status: A market and behavioural problem. I found no Spanish rule specifically governing no-show penalties (gap).
solved_today:
Prices from a comparison written by a competing vendor (Qamarero), updated 22 Oct 2026 — [Qamarero](https://qamarero.com/blog/mejores-software-reservas-restaurantes/):
- TheFork Manager: price on quote; the "garantías" features are only in the Performance plan.
- CoverManager: per-venue price not published; three months free for new restaurants signing by 31 Oct 2026.
- Restoo: Mini €39, Pro €79, Premium €149, Gold €249 per month excl. VAT; prepayments only in Premium.
- resmio: €0, €69.90 or €129.90 per month plus VAT, with a 12-month lock-in or €10/month extra for monthly cancellation.
- OpenTable: Core €149 or Pro €299 per month, plus €1.50 per seated diner who comes through its network.
- Last.app "The Book": a basic version is included with its POS plans.
software_solvable: Yes, through deposits, card pre-authorisation, reminders and risk scoring. But the market is crowded and the rate is already falling, so the opportunity is mainly cheaper or bundled protection.
confidence: High on the rates; low to medium on the losses.

title: Delivery-platform commissions (Glovo, Uber Eats, Just Eat)
who: Restaurants, pizzerias, fast-casual outlets and dark kitchens, mostly micro and small.
where: National, concentrated in cities (Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Sevilla, Málaga, Zaragoza, Bilbao).
reality: The platform takes 15–35% of each order, plus monthly fees, marketing fees and shared promotions, and pays out every two weeks or monthly. Restaurants either raise menu prices on the apps or absorb the margin loss.
evidence:
- Uber Eats charges 30% + VAT on its Básico plan, 25% with a 6-month lock-in (Plus) and 15–20% with a 12-month lock-in (Premium). Glovo charges 15–35% + VAT depending on zone and demand, plus €39/month for the tablet and support and 2–5% for marketing. Just Eat charges 13% + VAT if the restaurant delivers itself, or 25–35% + VAT plus €0.30 per order if Just Eat delivers — [Qamarero, 30 Sep 2025](https://qamarero.com/blog/comisiones-delivery-cuanto-cobran-realmente-las-plataformas/). This is a vendor blog that cites no sources.
- Glovo plan tiers: Marketplace 15–18%, Standard 25–28%, Premium 28–30%, Top 30–35%. Estimated all-in cost is 35–42% of revenue once VAT on the commission, about 1.5% service charges, shared promotions (for example 25% flash discounts) and refunds or disputes (1–2% of turnover) are included. Payouts are monthly — [Fooderise, 10 May 2026](https://www.fooderise.com/en/blog/integrer-glovo-restaurant-fonctionnement-commission-2026). This source is generic and multi-country, not Spain-specific.
- Payout timing conflicts: another guide says Glovo settles every 14 days — [Qamarero Glovo guide (search summary)](https://qamarero.com/blog/cuanto-cobra-glovo-restaurantes/)
scale: One claim says 78% of Spanish restaurants see commissions as their main delivery challenge — [Qamarero, 30 Sep 2025](https://qamarero.com/blog/comisiones-delivery-cuanto-cobran-realmente-las-plataformas/). It is unsourced and has low reliability.
cost_impact: 15–35% commission per order, or 35–42% of delivery revenue all-in (Fooderise estimate).
driver_status: A concentrated market. I found no Spanish or CNMC regulation of commission levels in 2025–2026 (gap). The Ley Rider employment model belongs to the labour researcher.
solved_today:
- Own online ordering plus aggregator integrators. Last.app plans include a delivery integrator covering Glovo, Uber Eats and Just Eat, with 100, 550 or unlimited orders included and extra orders at €0.25 or €0.19 each. Its online store costs up to €40/month plus 4% and €0.20 per sale, and QR ordering €25/month — [Last.app pricing, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://www.last.app/precios)
- Negotiated rates for high-volume chains, according to older press (search summary of a Xataka article, undated).
software_solvable: Partly. Direct ordering, CRM and loyalty tools can move repeat customers off the platforms, but the platforms keep control of demand aggregation.
confidence: Medium. The figures come from vendors and I found no independent 2025–26 data.

title: Margin squeeze from energy, supplies, rent and financing, with falling turnover and forecast closures in Mallorca
who: Bars, cafés and restaurants (micro and small) and leisure firms. Hotels are faring better.
where: National. Most acute in Mallorca and the Baleares in 2025–2026.
reality: Costs keep rising and prices cannot follow them fully. In island destinations tourists are spending less on eating out: owners call them "sandwich tourists", and all-inclusive hotels capture their meals.
evidence:
- Tourism firms' costs in Q3 2026: oil-linked +7.3%, energy +6.9%, supplies +6.2%, labour about +5% and interest rates +25%. 39.1% of firms report worse results and 30.6% better. Hotels did best (53.1% improved; balance +29.3), while leisure firms had a balance of −6.5 — [Exceltur nº98, Oct 2026](https://www.exceltur.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/EXCELTUR-Informe-Perspectivas-N98-Balance-del-IIIT26-y-previsiones-para-IVT26.pdf)
- Mallorca bars and restaurants saw turnover fall about 14% in the first half of August 2026, according to CAEB Restauración's Juanmi Ferrer. Causes cited include economic weakness in source markets such as Germany, all-inclusive hotels, heat, soaring rents, staff turnover and no-shows — [Majorca Daily Bulletin, 17 Aug 2026](https://www.majorcadailybulletin.com/news/local/2026/08/17/145039/mallorca-bars-and-restaurants-suffer-per-cent-drop-turnover-during-the-first-half-august.html)
- Balearic restaurants lost 4.2% of their custom in summer 2025, the largest drop of any region, according to a Delectatech report — [Majorca Daily Bulletin, 28 Feb 2026](https://www.majorcadailybulletin.com/news/local/2026/02/28/140559/spanish-restaurants-take-stand-against-shows-balearic-sector-struggled-last-year.html)
- Early-2026 reports predicted 500–600 restaurant closures in Mallorca, and said one in ten bars and cafés had closed over the last decade — [Majorca Daily Bulletin, 17 Aug 2026](https://www.majorcadailybulletin.com/news/local/2026/08/17/145039/mallorca-bars-and-restaurants-suffer-per-cent-drop-turnover-during-the-first-half-august.html) (single source; the original reports were not traced).
- A Palma restaurant owner said they would advise against opening a restaurant this year (paraphrased) — [Majorca Daily Bulletin, 28 Feb 2026](https://www.majorcadailybulletin.com/news/local/2026/02/28/140559/spanish-restaurants-take-stand-against-shows-balearic-sector-struggled-last-year.html)
scale: The whole sector (more than 300,000 companies, per Hostelería de España).
cost_impact: Costs rising 6–7% a year against tourism sales growth of 4.1% in Q3 2026 (Exceltur). Mallorca turnover −14% in early August 2026, and 500–600 closures forecast.
driver_status: Market forces: energy and fuel prices (linked to the Middle East conflict), inflation, interest rates, rents and shifting tourist spending.
solved_today: Recipe costing (escandallo), stock control and menu engineering inside POS systems, for example stock control in Last.app's Growth plan at €95/month (Last.app pricing). Energy brokers and group purchasing exist but their prices were not verified.
software_solvable: Partly. Cost control, procurement, dynamic menus and demand forecasting help, but software cannot change input prices.
confidence: Medium. I found no 2025–26 data on food-cost inflation specific to restaurants (gap).

title: Terraces — restrictive municipal ordinances, permit risk and conflict with residents over noise
who: Bars, cafés and restaurants with terraces (micro and small).
where: Madrid (new ordinance in force since 1 Jan 2026) and Valencia (2022 terrace cut in Honduras and Blasco Ibáñez). Search results also show disputes in Cádiz, Alicante (La Explanada) and Zaragoza, but these were undated or older.
reality: Terraces are a core revenue source, but ordinances cap their size by sidewalk width and limit noise and enclosures, sanctions are getting tougher, and residents' associations push for earlier closing. Disputes over terrace cuts end in protests and court cases.
evidence:
- Madrid's new terraces and kiosks ordinance applies from 1 Jan 2026. The 2022 ordinance had been annulled by the TSJ de Madrid for formal defects. The new text limits space by sidewalk width, toughens sanctions, requires low-noise materials, does not allow activity above 45 dB from 23:00 (according to FRAVM's reading), and does not cut opening hours. Madrid has more than 6,600 authorised terraces, up 20.9% since 2019; Chamberí went from about 200 in 2013 to about 700 — [El Salto, 23 Nov 2025](https://www.elsaltodiario.com/comunidad-madrid/ordenanza-terrazas-almeida-un-traje-medida-hosteleria-segun-asociaciones-vecinales)
- The ordinance is numbered "Ordenanza 7/2025" according to a search summary of an [Aparejadores Madrid document](https://www.aparejadoresmadrid.es/documents/d/aparejadores/gt884). The number was not checked in the BOCM.
- Hostelería Madrid called the initial draft "claramente perjudicial para el sector, especialmente para las pequeñas y medianas empresas" ("clearly harmful to the sector, especially small and medium businesses"). The residents' federation FRAVM submitted 43 allegations and none were accepted; only 7 of 106 allegations were incorporated overall. A 2018 CERMI report found 56% of Madrid's terraces obstructed pedestrians — [El Salto, 23 Nov 2025](https://www.elsaltodiario.com/comunidad-madrid/ordenanza-terrazas-almeida-un-traje-medida-hosteleria-segun-asociaciones-vecinales)
- Valencia (older context): a 2022 terrace cut affected 72 venues, which estimated losses of almost €200 a day, called the measure "injusta y arbitraria" and announced legal action. Citing council data, they said "apenas un 3% de las denuncias por ruido van vinculadas a la actividad de las terrazas" ("barely 3% of noise complaints are linked to terraces") — [Valencia Plaza, 2 Nov 2022](https://valenciaplaza.com/hosteleros-honduras-decretan-jornada-cierre-terrazas). This falls outside the 2024–26 window.
scale: More than 6,600 authorised terraces in Madrid alone. National figure not found.
cost_impact: About €200 a day per venue in lost revenue (Valencia 2022 claim). Fine amounts under the new Madrid ordinance were not reported.
driver_status: Municipal terrace and noise ordinances. Madrid's is in force since 1 Jan 2026. Acoustic protection zones (ZPAE/ZAS) in Madrid, Valencia (Ruzafa), Sevilla and San Sebastián were not verified (gap).
solved_today: Architects and gestorías prepare terrace licence plans; costs were not found. I identified no specialised SaaS (gap).
software_solvable: Partly. Permit and renewal tracking, layout compliance and noise-monitoring evidence can be software, but the underlying decisions are political.
confidence: Medium for Madrid; low for other cities.

title: Smoking and vaping ban on hospitality terraces (bill in Congress)
who: Bars, cafés, restaurants, beach clubs and hotels with terraces or pools; all sizes.
where: National.
reality: If the bill passes, staff will have to stop customers smoking or vaping on terraces and owners must change their signage. The sector fears losing customers at terrace times.
evidence:
- The Council of Ministers approved the bill amending Ley 28/2005 on 21 Jul 2026 and sent it to Congress, where parliamentary groups can table amendments; until it is passed the current rules apply — [INEAF](https://www.ineaf.es/tribuna/ley-antitabaco/) and [Nuevecuatrouno, 21 Jul 2026](https://nuevecuatrouno.com/2026/07/21/la-prohibicion-de-fumar-en-las-terrazas-supera-su-primer-gran-tramite/) (search summaries); confirmed by [Que.es, 25 Jul 2026](https://www.que.es/2026/07/25/ley-antitabaco-terrazas-playas/) ("el pasado martes").
- The bill bans smoking and vaping on bar and restaurant terraces, beaches, pools, bus shelters and campuses, sets 15-metre buffers around schools and health centres, and treats e-cigarettes, nicotine pouches and shisha like tobacco. Fines for businesses range from €200 to €600,000, and businesses get two months to update signage after entry into force — [Que.es, 25 Jul 2026](https://www.que.es/2026/07/25/ley-antitabaco-terrazas-playas/)
- The hospitality employers argue that a terrace ban would be an "excepción en Europa" ("an exception in Europe") — [Onda Vasca (search summary)](https://www.ondavasca.com/el-gobierno-amplia-la-prohibicion-de-fumar-a-terrazas-playas-y-piscinas/)
scale: Every establishment with a terrace (number not found).
cost_impact: Not quantified (gap). Fines of €200–€600,000 if the bill passes.
driver_status: Bill amending Ley 28/2005, approved by the Council of Ministers on 21 Jul 2026 and now in Congress. **Draft / not in force** as of Oct 2026.
solved_today: Not applicable yet.
software_solvable: No. This is a behavioural and regulatory change.
confidence: High on the status; low on the impact.

title: Fake-review attacks and reputation extortion
who: Bars, restaurants and cafés, mostly micro and small, heavily dependent on Google and Tripadvisor ratings.
where: National. Courts in Madrid and Barcelona are cited.
reality: A venue suddenly receives a burst of one-star reviews from faceless profiles, or an offer to buy positive reviews. Its rating and its visibility in Google's ranking drop before any complaint is reviewed, and the owner has little recourse.
evidence:
- One bar received 20 negative reviews from faceless profiles in under an hour and its 4.8 rating "se desploma en tiempo real". Smear campaigns cost "apenas 200 euros" and "packs de odio" are sold by click farms using VPNs. Courts in Madrid and Barcelona have awarded up to €20,000 in compensation (no cases or dates given) — [Merca2, 28 Apr 2026](https://www.merca2.es/2026/04/28/resenas-bar-google-2373862/). This is an opinion-style piece with no primary sources.
- A journalist quoted by Ara: restaurateurs have all received offers like "Tú me pagas 200 euros al mes y yo te hago veinte reseñas positivas en Tripadvisor" ("you pay me €200 a month and I write you twenty positive reviews") — [Ara (search summary; undated)](https://es.ara.cat/comer/lee-resenas-restaurante-alerta-hay-falsas_1_5373668.html)
- Since the Omnibus Directive was transposed in May 2022, fake reviews count as a serious infraction, with fines of up to €100,000 — [Merca2, 28 Apr 2026](https://www.merca2.es/2026/04/28/resenas-bar-google-2373862/); also [Puromarketing (search summary)](https://www.puromarketing.com/141/215522/ciberextorsion-falsas-resenas-amenaza-creciente-para-reputacion-imagen-negocios-empresas). Not checked against the BOE.
- In April 2025, PSOE and Sumar proposed letting companies request the removal of fake reviews; whether it passed is unknown — [Marketing4ecommerce (search summary)](https://marketing4ecommerce.net/empresas-eliminar-resenas-falsas-de-internet/)
scale: Not quantified (gap).
cost_impact: Attacks cost the attacker about €200; compensation of up to €20,000 has been awarded in court (single source).
driver_status: Platform ranking algorithms and click-farm markets. Unfair-practice rules (Omnibus transposition) in force since 2022. The 2025 removal proposal's status is unknown.
solved_today: Google's "flag as inappropriate" option and its owner review-management tool, reports to the Policía Nacional or Guardia Civil cybercrime units, unfair-competition and right-to-honour lawsuits — [Merca2](https://www.merca2.es/2026/04/28/resenas-bar-google-2373862/). Reputation-management SaaS exists, but its prices were not verified.
software_solvable: Partly. Monitoring and anomaly alerts, certified evidence capture and takedown or legal-claim workflows are software, but removal depends on Google.
confidence: Low to medium; the evidence is mostly anecdotal.

title: Food-waste law (Ley 1/2025) — leftovers, prevention plans and donation duties
who:
- All restaurants and bars: free leftovers.
- Chains and larger venues: prevention plans and donation agreements.
- Micro firms (fewer than 10 staff and no more than €2M) and establishments of 1,300 m² or less are exempt from the plan and donation duties.
where: National. Sanctions are enforced by the autonomous communities, which may set higher thresholds.
reality: Restaurants must tell diners they can take leftovers home free, and supply food-grade reusable or easily recyclable containers at their own cost. Larger operators must document a prevention plan, apply the priority hierarchy (donation first) and sign donation agreements.
evidence:
- From the law itself — [BOE, Ley 1/2025 (published 2 Apr 2025)](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2025/04/01/1):
- Art. 8: hospitality businesses must let customers take uneaten food at no extra cost (buffet libre excepted), say so clearly and visibly, preferably on the menu, and use food-grade, reusable or easily recyclable containers.
- Art. 6.4: a prevention plan and donation agreements are required.
- Art. 6.4(c): hospitality establishments of 1,300 m² or less are exempt, unless several premises under the same tax ID add up to more.
- Art. 6.6: micro firms are excluded from all art. 6 duties.
- Sanctions (art. 21): minor infractions up to €2,000 (or a warning), serious €2,001–€60,000, very serious €60,001–€500,000. Serious infractions include having no plan when one is required and deliberately destroying edible food (art. 20); very serious means repeating a serious infraction within two years — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2025/04/01/1); matching ranges in [Andersen alert, Apr 2026](https://es.andersen.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Andersen-Ley-de-desperdicio-alimentario_alerta.pdf)
- Timing: final provision 20 reads "La presente ley entrará en vigor el 2 de enero de 2025" ("this law enters into force on 2 January 2025"), a drafting oddity since the law was published in April. The mandatory art. 6 measures apply "transcurrido el plazo de un año desde la publicación" ("one year after publication"), so from about 3 Apr 2026 — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2025/04/01/1); [Andersen](https://es.andersen.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Andersen-Ley-de-desperdicio-alimentario_alerta.pdf)
- Press framing: "desde el 3 de abril de 2026" restaurants "deberán ofrecer las sobras de la comida en tápers gratis"; serious fines start at €2,001 — [El Español, 15 Apr 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/sociedad/20260415/entrado-vigor-multas-restaurantes-no-ofrezcan-tapers-gratis-sobras/1003744204930_0.html)
- **Discrepancy:**
- The one-year deferral in final provision 20 covers only art. 6. The leftovers duty in art. 8 has no deferral of its own, so it arguably applied earlier than April 2026 (my reading).
- The list of infractions in art. 20 contains no specific infraction for failing to offer a container. Press stories about fines for "no tupper" appear overstated unless regional regimes add one.
scale: Every restaurant for the leftovers duty. The plan and donation duties hit mainly chains and large venues.
cost_impact: Container costs, which are not quantified. Fines of €2,001–€60,000 for a missing plan.
driver_status: Ley 1/2025. **In force**; art. 6 obligations apply from April 2026.
solved_today: Hostelería de España runs a compliance help service at hosteleriacircular.es ([HdE website](https://www.hosteleriadeespana.es/)). Consultants and law firms advise larger operators. Surplus-food apps exist but were not verified.
software_solvable: Partly. Waste measurement, plan documentation and donation-traceability logs suit chains. For small restaurants the burden is mostly packaging cost.

title: Food-safety self-control records (APPCC) and allergen information
who: Every bar, restaurant, café, hotel kitchen and caterer.
where: National. Inspections are run by regional health authorities.
reality: Kitchens must keep temperature, cleaning, pest-control, traceability and allergen records up to date for health inspections. Allergen information for each dish must be available in writing, or given orally if it is backed by a written or electronic record. Every menu change means updating the allergen matrix.
evidence:
- The legal basis for APPCC is Reglamento (CE) 852/2004 art. 5 ("Sí: necesitas crear, aplicar y mantener procedimientos basados en APPCC"), RD 1021/2022 art. 20 for bars and restaurants (which repealed RD 3484/2000), and RD 1086/2020 art. 30 on temperatures for prepared meals. Required records cover temperatures, cleaning, pests, maintenance, traceability (Reglamento 178/2002 arts. 18–19), allergen sheets, and frozen-food temperatures kept for at least one year (Reglamento 37/2005) — [Qamarero, updated 6 Oct 2026](https://qamarero.com/blog/appcc-hosteleria/) (vendor blog; the norms cited are real but were not each re-checked).
- Allergens for non-prepacked food: RD 126/2015 art. 4.1(b) requires allergen information. Art. 6.2 requires it in writing on labels or signs. Art. 6.5(a) allows oral information if it is "registrada de forma escrita o electrónica" (recorded in writing or electronically) and easily accessible to staff, inspectors and customers. Art. 6.5(b) requires signs telling customers where the information is — [BOE, RD 126/2015](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2015/02/27/126)
- Food-safety sanctions under Ley 17/2011 art. 52: minor up to €5,000, serious €5,001–€20,000, very serious €20,001–€600,000. Very serious cases can also lead to "cierre temporal del establecimiento... por un plazo máximo de cinco años" (temporary closure for up to five years) — [BOE, Ley 17/2011](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2011/07/05/17); the same range is quoted by a vendor blog — [Qamarero, Jul 2025](https://qamarero.com/blog/como-hacer-una-carta-con-alergenos-para-un-restaurante-o-bar/)
scale: Every food-service establishment (more than 300,000 hospitality companies).
cost_impact: Fine exposure of up to €600,000 plus closure. Actual inspection frequency and the number of fines imposed were not found (gap).
driver_status: Reglamento (CE) 852/2004, RD 1021/2022, RD 126/2015 and Ley 17/2011, all **in force**.
solved_today: APPCC consultancies, which draft the plan and train staff (prices not verified); paper logbooks; digital APPCC apps and temperature sensors (prices not verified); allergen-menu builders inside POS and menu tools.
software_solvable: Yes. Digital logs with sensors, recipe-based allergen matrices and inspection-ready exports.
confidence: High on the legal duty; low on how often it is enforced.

title: A costly, fragmented tech stack (POS, reservations, delivery integration) and moving fiscal-software deadlines
who: Bars, restaurants and cafés, from autónomo to small chain.
where: National. Basque Country (TicketBAI) and Navarra have their own fiscal-software regimes; that topic belongs to the tax researcher.
reality: A typical venue pays separately for a POS, a reservation tool, a delivery integrator, a kitchen display and an online store, each priced per location, with setup fees and add-ons. Repeated postponements of Verifactu leave owners unsure whether and when to change their POS.
evidence:
- Last.app charges €50 (Starter), €95 (Growth) or €175 (Unlimited) per location per month on annual billing, plus €500 setup. A kitchen display costs €35/month and extra delivery orders €0.19–0.25 each — [Last.app pricing, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://www.last.app/precios)
- Reservation tools cost €39–€299/month, plus per-diner fees in some cases (see HOS-02) — [Qamarero, 22 Oct 2026](https://qamarero.com/blog/mejores-software-reservas-restaurantes/)
- Verifactu: the previous deadlines were 1 Jan 2027 for companies and 1 Jul 2027 for autónomos. A postponement to October 2028 has been announced but the change was not yet published as of 5 Oct 2026, and "the obligation remains" — [Qamarero, 5 Oct 2026](https://qamarero.com/blog/verifactu-retraso-octubre-2028/) (vendor, single source; to be verified by the tax researcher).
scale: Whole sector.
cost_impact: From about €600 to more than €2,100 a year per location for the POS alone, before reservations, payment fees and hardware.
driver_status: A market problem, plus Verifactu (RD 1007/2023): postponement to Oct 2028 announced, but its formal publication was not verified.
solved_today: All-in-one POS suites (Last.app, Qamarero, Revo, Ágora, Glop, Cuiner). Revo, Ágora and Glop pricing pages could not be retrieved (gap).
software_solvable: Yes. This is a software-cost and integration problem, but the market is crowded.

title: Municipal waste fee (tasa de residuos) and the free tap-water duty (Ley 7/2022)
who: Bars and restaurants, which are heavy waste generators.
where: Set by each municipality.
reality: Municipalities had to introduce a waste fee covering the full real cost of the service by 2025, so food-service premises face new or higher bills. Separately, restaurants must offer free tap water.
evidence: Ley 7/2022 art. 11.3 requires local entities to establish, "en el plazo de tres años", a "tasa... específica, diferenciada y no deficitaria" (a specific, separate fee that covers its cost) that enables pay-as-you-throw. Art. 18.3 obliges hostelería and restauración to offer "la posibilidad de consumo de agua no envasada de manera gratuita" (free non-bottled water). The law entered into force on 10 Apr 2022, so the fee deadline fell around Apr 2025 (my calculation) — [BOE, Ley 7/2022](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2022/04/08/7)
scale: Increases in specific cities for hospitality premises were **not found** (gap).
driver_status: Ley 7/2022, **in force**; the fee deadline has passed.
solved_today: Gestorías handle appeals against fee assessments (not verified).
software_solvable: Mostly no. Waste measurement could reduce pay-as-you-throw bills.
confidence: Low on impact; high on the legal duty.

title: SES.Hospedajes traveller-data reporting (RD 933/2021)
who: Hotels, hostales, hostels, campsites, tourist apartments, VUT owners and property managers. Non-professional hosts must still report even though they are exempt from keeping the register. Micro and small businesses dominate.
