where: National, except Catalonia (Mossos d'Esquadra) and the Basque Country (Ertzaintza), which run their own reporting systems.
reality: For every booking, cancellation and check-in, the operator must send a report (parte) within 24 hours. Each one carries guest identity, contact and address details, kinship for minors, contract data and payment data. Guests over 14 must sign. Records must be kept for 3 years. A platform outage does not extend the deadline, and small errors such as a missing document support number get the report rejected.
evidence:
- From the decree — [BOE, RD 933/2021](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2021/10/26/933):
- Entry into force 27 Apr 2022.
- Art. 6.3: data must be sent "de manera inmediata, y en todo caso en un plazo no superior a 24 horas" (immediately, and within 24 hours at most).
- Art. 5.3: retention for "tres años".
- Art. 4.2: every guest "mayor de catorce años" (over 14) must sign.
- Annex I.A (professional lodging): about 43 data fields, including 5 payment fields (type, payment-method identification, holder, card expiry date, payment date). This is my tool-assisted count.
- Use of the SES.Hospedajes platform has been mandatory since 2 Dec 2024. Other operational rules — [net2rent guide, published 11 Dec 2025, updated 18 Sep 2026](https://net2rent.com/guia-completa-ses-hospedajes/) (PMS vendor):
- The 24-hour clock is triggered by the booking, its cancellation and the check-in, and "Una caída de la plataforma no amplía el plazo" (an outage does not extend the deadline).
- Common errors: the document support number (número de soporte) is missing, or the operator did not tick "web service" at enrolment, which forces re-registration establishment by establishment.
- Old Hospederías/WebPol credentials no longer work, and acknowledgement receipts must be kept for inspections.
- The number of data points rose "de nueve a 42" (from nine to 42). The sector called it "inaceptable" and studied legal action. Fines of €30,000 are mentioned — [Economist & Jurist, 2 Dec 2024](https://www.economistjurist.es/actualidad-juridica/entra-en-vigor-el-registro-de-viajeros-que-incrementa-de-nueve-a-42-los-datos-que-la-industria-hotelera-recurrira-en-los-tribunales/)
- Fines under LO 4/2015 (citizen-security law): minor €100–€600 per report (incorrect, incomplete or late data); serious €601–€30,000 (failing to register as a provider or to communicate, or giving false data). Inspections are "cada vez más habituales" (increasingly common), a claim with no source given — [net2rent](https://net2rent.com/guia-completa-ses-hospedajes/); same ranges in [Chekin (search summary)](https://chekin.com/blog/registro-de-viajeros-ses-hospedajes-2025/)
- **Conflict on payment data:** one vendor FAQ says the card number, IBAN and expiry date are not mandatory and only the payment method must be given — [Chekin, 12 Mar 2025](https://chekin.com/blog/preguntas-frecuentes-sobre-ses-hospedajes/). But Annex I.A lists the card expiry date ([BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2021/10/26/933)), and net2rent says the data-protection authority (AEPD) reportedly considers the last four card digits proportionate. Operators face ambiguous guidance.
- Data-minimisation conflict: the AEPD fined €2,000 for scanning guests' ID cards — [Cuatrecasas, Nov 2023 (search summary)](https://www.cuatrecasas.com/es/spain/propiedad-intelectual/art/registro-datos-personales-establecimientos-hoteleros)
- The European Commission announced infringement procedure INFR(2026)4005 against Spain on 4 Jun 2026, citing proportionality, data minimisation and the three-year retention ("desproporcionado"). CEHAT is demanding that RD 933/2021 be repealed and a dialogue table set up — [CEHAT, 5 Jun 2026](https://cehat.com/notaprensa/cehat-recoge-el-aval-de-bruselas-el-expediente-sancionador-a-espana-por-el-registro-de-viajeros-confirma-que-la-norma-era-inaplicable-y-vulneraba-el-derecho-europeo/). The stage of the procedure was not stated; this is a single source and an interested party.
- The BOE consolidated text shows no amendments or annulments (latest version 27 Oct 2021) — [BOE consolidated text](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2021-17461)
- A Zaragoza council motion (filed by Vox) says the sector rejected the rule unanimously, that the sanctions are disproportionate, and that 95% of those affected are pymes and micropymes — [Ayuntamiento de Zaragoza, VOX motion (search summary; undated; partisan)](https://www.zaragoza.es/cont/paginas/organizacion/plenos/mociones/VOX-10519.pdf)
scale: About 341,000 listed tourist homes (INE, May 2026) plus hotels, hostels and campsites; Booking alone lists about 200,000 hotels and accommodations in Spain.
cost_impact: €100–€600 per faulty report and up to €30,000 for serious breaches. Staff minutes per check-in and data-security liability were not quantified (gap).
driver_status: RD 933/2021 and LO 4/2015. **In force and unamended** as of Oct 2026. EU infringement INFR(2026)4005 opened in June 2026; its outcome is pending. I could not verify a Supreme Court ruling on the industry's challenge (gap).
solved_today:
- Manual web form, signed in with a digital certificate, DNIe or Cl@ve.
- PMS web-service integrations (net2rent; Smoobu includes online check-in in plans from €29 to €55 a month for the first unit, plus €9.60 per additional unit).
- Dedicated check-in and compliance tools such as Chekin, from €3.95/€5.95/€7.95 per property per month. Annual billing saves up to 20%, minimum unit counts are stated inconsistently (3, 10 or 20), and deposits cost 1.5% + €0.30 — [Chekin pricing, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://chekin.com/en/pricing/)
- Documented complaints: outages, the 24-hour clock, lost credentials, re-enrolment and email-only support (net2rent).
software_solvable: Yes. Data capture, validation, transmission, retention and audit trail can all be automated, but the space is already crowded (Chekin and PMS vendors), so differentiation would be price, reliability and multi-system coverage (SES, Mossos, Ertzaintza).

title: The short-term-rental registry (Registro Único de Arrendamientos, NRUA, RD 1312/2024) — fees, revocations, delistings, annulment and refund claims
who: VUT owners (autónomos and private owners), property managers, owners of seasonal and room rentals, and platforms.
where: National. Revocations were concentrated in Andalucía, Canarias, Cataluña and the Comunitat Valenciana. Cities with the most revoked applications: Sevilla, Marbella, Barcelona, Málaga, Madrid, Benalmádena, Adeje, Valencia, Torrevieja, Fuengirola.
reality: Since 1 Jul 2025 owners have needed a €27 code per unit and per rental type to advertise. The application portal (registradores.org) failed at launch, about one in five applications was revoked (missing licence, no owners'-community approval, protected housing), and platforms delisted units. After the Supreme Court annulled the procedure in May 2026, owners are back to regional codes and arguing over refunds and damages.
evidence:
- Launch week: StayAlliance reported the portal "experimentó fallos persistentes que impidieron a numerosas empresas completar el procedimiento" (suffered persistent failures that stopped many businesses completing the procedure) and estimated that fewer than 50% of units had registered. Each code cost €27, so a unit used for both tourist and seasonal rental could need three codes (€81). Platforms had 48 hours to remove a listing once notified — [idealista, 4 Jul 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/07/04/851896-de-las-incidencias-a-las-denuncias-asi-ha-sido-el-estreno-del-registro-de)
- Main reasons for revocation: no tourist licence, no 3/5 owners'-community approval, or the property is protected housing. As of 4 Jul 2025 there were 255,172 applications and 22,368 revocations — [idealista, 7 Jul 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/07/07/852282-los-motivos-que-provocan-mas-revocaciones-del-codigo-obligatorio-para-los)
- In July–August 2025, 34,529 of 68,594 applications were revoked. Over the first eight months of 2025 there were 260,595 applications and 51,692 revocations — [Europa Press via Bolsamania, 2 Sep 2025](https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/empresas/economia--el-nuevo-registro-de-alquileres-turisticos-obtuvo-68500-solicitudes-en-verano-y-la-mitad-fueron-rechazadas--20818271.html)
- 53,876 revoked tourist-rental applications were notified to platforms for delisting. By city: Sevilla 2,289, Marbella 1,802, Barcelona 1,564, Málaga 1,471, Madrid 1,257. By region: Andalucía 16,740, Canarias 8,698, Cataluña 7,729, Comunitat Valenciana 7,499 — [idealista/Europa Press, 15 Sep 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/09/15/859916-el-gobierno-notifica-mas-de-53-500-pisos-turisticos-ilegales-para-que-se-retiren)
- As of 8 Jan 2026: 400,362 applications, 299,754 approved and 84,250 revoked (about 21%). Tourist rentals were 72% of applications and temporary rentals 14.7%. Definitive codes by province: Málaga more than 36,000 (10,327 revoked), Alicante 35,916 (8,309 revoked), Barcelona 30,092, Las Palmas 20,962, Madrid 18,899, Santa Cruz de Tenerife 17,693, Baleares 16,672 — [idealista, 20 Jan 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/01/20/879570-una-de-cada-cinco-viviendas-de-alquiler-de-corta-estancia-se-quedan-sin-el-codigo)
- Final totals: more than 467,000 applications, about 373,600 approved and about 20% rejected. The base fee was €27.05 per application — [idealista, 17 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/06/17/902074-se-avecinan-demandas-contra-el-registro-unico-de-alquileres-los-registradores-no)
- **The annulment:**
- Supreme Court ruling 620/2026 of 19 May 2026, on an appeal by the Generalitat Valenciana, annulled "los preceptos del Real Decreto impugnado referidos al procedimiento de registro único de arrendamientos" (the provisions on the single registration procedure) for lack of state competence. It was published in the BOE on 8 Jun 2026 — [Notarios y Registradores, 21 May 2026](https://www.notariosyregistradores.com/web/participa/noticias/el-ts-anula-registro-arrendamientos-corta-duracion/)
- Ruling 629/2026 of 21 May 2026, on an appeal by Apartur and ATA (corrected by an order of 11 Jun 2026), annulled arts. 2(f) and (i), 5, 8, 9, 10 and 12(b), and the references to the procedure and the registration number in arts. 1, 2(j) and 6 — [BOE-A-2026-13893, 26 Jun 2026](https://www.boe.es/boe/dias/2026/06/26/pdfs/BOE-A-2026-13893.pdf)
- Aftermath:
- About 111,000 rejected homes were unblocked. Fevitur puts the average loss per affected owner at about €33,000 and possible collective claims above €160M (lobby estimate). The Ministry of Housing (MIVAU) asked the regions to "refuercen los controles" (tighten controls), and Andalucía asked for an analysis of compensation — [idealista, 22 May 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/05/22/898792-el-fin-del-registro-de-viviendas-de-corta-estancia-reabre-100-000-licencias)
- Lawyers argue the nullity "sí tiene efectos retroactivos" (is retroactive), so fees should be refunded. The Colegio de Registradores says it "no tiene efectos retroactivos" and that existing codes "son válidos" (remain valid) — [idealista, 17 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/06/17/902074-se-avecinan-demandas-contra-el-registro-unico-de-alquileres-los-registradores-no)
- Fee refunds can be claimed for unjust enrichment within one year of the ruling becoming final — [Chekin, 2 Jun 2026](https://chekin.com/blog/real-decreto-1312-2024/) (vendor).
- **What remains:**
- The Ventanilla Única Digital (the state data-exchange window) still operates. Platforms must still share monthly data under EU Regulation 2024/1028, applicable since 20 May 2026; platforms with fewer than 4,250 listings may report quarterly.
- Listings now display regional codes (RTA, HUT, RTV, VUT, REAT, ETV, VV).
- The annual informative return (Orden VAU 1560/2025) remains.
- Spain has not adopted the state penalty regime the EU regulation requires — [Chekin, 2 Jun 2026](https://chekin.com/blog/real-decreto-1312-2024/) and [Chekin, 3 Jun 2026](https://chekin.com/blog/reglamento-ue-2024-1028/) (vendor; single source).
- Exceltur says the annulment "urge un sistema alternativo eficaz y jurídicamente sólido de control de la oferta ilegal de VUT" (makes an effective, legally sound alternative system for controlling illegal tourist-flat supply urgent) — [Exceltur nº98, Oct 2026](https://www.exceltur.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/EXCELTUR-Informe-Perspectivas-N98-Balance-del-IIIT26-y-previsiones-para-IVT26.pdf)
scale: About 467,000 applications nationally; about 111,000 rejected homes.
cost_impact: €27.05 per code (×1–3 per unit); lost bookings during blocking (Fevitur: about €33,000 per affected owner, a lobby figure); possible €160M in claims.
driver_status: RD 1312/2024 is **partially annulled** (rulings of 19 and 21 May 2026). EU Regulation 2024/1028 has been **in force since 20 May 2026**, but the national penalty regime is pending. I found no replacement decree as of Oct 2026.
solved_today: Gestorías and real-estate lawyers, whose fees were not found; PMS and channel tools that store and display the registration number (Smoobu, Chekin, net2rent); now also refund-claim lawyers.
software_solvable: Partly. Tracking regional codes against each platform listing, packaging EU 2024/1028 data, and automating refund claims are software tasks, but the regime itself is legal and political.

title: OTA dominance — Booking.com parity and commissions, the CNMC fine, hotel damages claims, and Airbnb's host-only fee
who: Independent and small or medium hotels, hostels, tourist apartments and VUT managers.
where: National. The CNMC complaint originated with the Madrid hotel association, per a search summary.
reality: Hotels depend on Booking for a large share of their bookings, pay higher commissions for visibility programmes (Preferente, Genius), and until 2024 faced price-parity constraints. Contracts are English-only under Dutch law with Amsterdam courts. VUT managers using a PMS are being moved onto Airbnb's 15.5% host-only fee.
evidence:
- On 30 Jul 2024 the CNMC fined Booking €413.24M (two fines of €206.62M) for abuse of dominance since 1 Jan 2019. The conduct sanctioned:
- parity clauses;
- unilateral price cuts;
- opaque Preferente, Preferente Plus and Genius programmes;
- English-only contracts under Dutch law with Amsterdam courts;
- ranking by total bookings, which pushes hotels to concentrate sales on Booking.
- Source: [Genbeta, 1 Aug 2024](https://www.genbeta.com/actualidad/booking-com-culpable-abuso-posicion-dominante-cnmc-impone-multa-record-413-millones-euros)
- Booking's share of hotel OTA intermediation in Spain was 70–90% in 2019–2022, and Booking is appealing to the Audiencia Nacional — [Vozpópuli, 31 Jul 2024](https://www.vozpopuli.com/economia/empresas/multa-booking-reservas.html); the CNMC said the share was "cercana al 90% en algunos años" (close to 90% in some years) — [Forbes, 19 Sep 2024](https://forbes.es/turismo/502788/la-cnmc-ve-un-impacto-positivo-de-la-multa-historica-de-413-millones-a-booking-para-el-tejido-empresarial/)
- Civil damages claims:
- More than 1,700 hotels have joined an initiative run by the litigation firm Eskariam with the Asociación Española de Directores de Hoteles, and about 1,200 have supplied documents.
- Total claim about €1,000M; the first lawsuit alone is above €300M. The claimed damage is 1.65% to just over 2% of turnover over the 20 years affected.
- Parity clauses applied in Spain from 2004 until June 2024, when Booking dropped them after its DMA gatekeeper designation.
- Filings were due in H1 2026, with first rulings expected between late 2027 and early 2028.
- CEHAT signed a separate agreement with CSS Abogados in Nov 2024.
- Source: [Vozpópuli, updated 30 Dec 2025](https://www.vozpopuli.com/legal/un-millar-de-hoteles-espanoles-buscara-recuperar-1000-millones-de-booking-en-pleitos-desde-2026.html)
- Airbnb: under the split-fee model hosts pay 3% and guests 14.1–16.5%. The host-only fee is 15.5% for most hosts and is required for hotels and for hosts using property-management software, and Airbnb is moving all home hosts to it — [Airbnb Help Center, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857)
- Counter-trend: hotels' direct-channel revenue was up 19% year on year in summer 2026 — [CEHAT/PwC, 1 Jul 2026](https://cehat.com/notaprensa/el-sector-hotelero-mantiene-unas-perspectivas-favorables-para-verano-y-otono-impulsado-por-la-fortaleza-de-la-demanda-turistica/)
scale: Booking has about 200,000 hotel and accommodation partners in Spain; more than 1,700 hotels are in the damages claims.
cost_impact: Claimed overcharge of 1.65–2% of turnover (claimants' expert estimate). Typical 2025–26 Booking and Expedia commission percentages could not be verified (gap).
driver_status: The CNMC decision is **under appeal at the Audiencia Nacional**. A reported suspension of the fine appeared in a search summary that I could not trace to a dated source (gap). The DMA has applied to Booking since 2024. Civil claims are being filed in 2026.
solved_today: Booking engines and metasearch (Cloudbeds says it adds no commission on its booking engine; it charges metasearch commission only after the stay), revenue-management tools, and litigation funders such as Eskariam.
software_solvable: Partly. Direct-booking stacks, CRM and loyalty tools reduce dependence; assembling evidence for claims (historical rate-parity and commission data) is also a software task.
confidence: High on the fine and the claims; medium on commission levels.

title: Multiplying tourist taxes and the burden of collecting them (Catalonia doubled in 2026; Basque Country from 2027; Galician cities)
who: Hotels, hostels, campsites, VUT owners and managers. The establishment collects and pays the tax as "sustituto del contribuyente".
where:
- Catalonia: Barcelona plus a regional rate elsewhere.
- Basque Country: Gipuzkoa including San Sebastián, Bizkaia including Bilbao, and Álava.
- Galicia: Santiago, A Coruña and Vigo.
- Baleares: since 2016.
- None in Madrid, Andalucía or Canarias. The Comunitat Valenciana's tax was repealed in Nov 2023.
reality: Operators must charge each guest a per-night amount that varies by establishment type, municipality and season, apply exemptions (minors, long stays) and night caps, keep per-property records and file returns, quarterly in Gipuzkoa. Managers with portfolios across several regions face a different regime in each.
evidence:
- Catalonia — Ley 2/2026 de 6 de marzo:
- The Parlament approved the bill on 25 Feb 2026 with PSC, ERC and Comuns, effective 1 Apr 2026. The maximum Barcelona municipal surcharge rises from €4 to €8, and other councils can add up to €4 — [Forbes, 25 Feb 2026](https://forbes.es/economia/879865/el-parlament-aprueba-la-ley-que-incrementara-la-tasa-turistica-a-partir-del-1-de-abril/)
- The Barcelona rate is roughly doubled, youth hostels get a new tariff, the rate in force at booking applies if the tax is paid then, the surcharge also applies to cruise stays of 12 hours or less, and 25% of revenue goes to housing policy — [Cuatrecasas, 2 Apr 2026](https://www.cuatrecasas.com/es/global/fiscalidad/art/cataluna-impuesto-estancias-establecimientos-turisticos)
- Rates in the rest of Catalonia rise 50% from Apr 2026 and 100% from Apr 2027 — [net2rent (search summary)](https://net2rent.com/tasa-turistica-en-cataluna-que-es-cuanto-se-paga-y-como-gestionarla/)
- Combined Barcelona rates: 5-star €11, 4-star €7.40, tourist flat €8.50, other establishments €6 — [DonPorqué, 30 Jul 2026](https://donporque.com/tasa-turistica-espana-2026/) (secondary source)
- **Conflict:** Forbes gives both a Barcelona maximum of €4.50 until March 2027 and €6 after, and "7 € for the top category"; the exact figures must be read from the DOGC tables (images, not retrieved).
- Gipuzkoa — Norma Foral 3/2026, de 12 de junio (BOPV nº119, 25 Jun 2026) — [BOPV](https://www.euskadi.eus/bopv2/datos/2026/06/2602836a.pdf):
- Minimum–maximum rates per night: hotels 5-star €4.50–6.50, 4-star €3.50–5.50, 3-star €1.50–3.50, 2-star €1.00–2.50, 1-star €0.75–1.75; tourist apartments €1.50–3.50; campsites, rural houses and hostels €0.75–1.75; agroturismos €0.50–1.25; VUT, whole or by rooms, €4.50–6.50; cruises €6.00–7.00.
- Charged for at most 6 nights per stay.
- Municipal surcharge of up to 50% where a municipality has 750 or more bed places, or 5,000 or more residents with tourist intensity of 10% or more. A 100% rebate applies where there are 25 places or fewer.
- The establishment files a quarterly self-assessment (autoliquidación).
- **Takes effect 1 Jan 2027**; bookings made before 5 Feb 2026 are exempt.
- Basque Country as a whole: all three territories start on 1 Jan 2027, after a summer-2026 start was dropped; municipalities have six months to adapt their ordinances — [Chekin, 10 Jun 2026](https://chekin.com/blog/tasa-turistica-pais-vasco/)
- **Contradicted claim:** a report that San Sebastián already charged "hasta 7,50 euros por noche" in summer 2026 — [Moncloa.com, 10 Jun 2026 (search summary)](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/06/10/san-sebastian-donostia-tasa-3383636/) — is contradicted by the official text, which takes effect on 1 Jan 2027.
- Galicia: Santiago and A Coruña have charged a voluntary municipal tax of €1–€2.50 since late 2025 — [DonPorqué, 30 Jul 2026](https://donporque.com/tasa-turistica-espana-2026/). Vigo starts in October; the year was not confirmed — [Xataka (search summary)](https://www.xataka.com/magnet/vigo-empieza-a-cobrar-tasa-turistica-octubre-importante-no-precio-sino-intencion)
- Baleares (Impuesto de Turismo Sostenible), high season 1 May–31 Oct: 5-star €4, 4-star €3, 3-star and apartments €2 — [DonPorqué, 30 Jul 2026](https://donporque.com/tasa-turistica-espana-2026/) (single secondary source)
scale: Every lodging establishment in Catalonia, the Baleares, the Basque Country (from 2027) and the participating Galician municipalities. Catalonia had 51,300 listed tourist homes and the Baleares 21,304 in May 2026 (INE via [idealista](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/06/24/903471-estos-son-los-municipios-con-mas-viviendas-turisticas-en-espana)).
cost_impact: Rates of €1–€11 per person per night make price competition harder, and collection and filing add administrative work every quarter.
driver_status: Catalonia: Ley 2/2026, **in force from 1 Apr 2026**, with a second step on 1 Apr 2027. Gipuzkoa: Norma Foral 3/2026, **upcoming on 1 Jan 2027**; Bizkaia and Álava are aligned to the same date, but their norm numbers were not verified. Galicia: municipal ordinances, in force.
solved_today: Chekin includes tourist-tax handling in all plans; PMS modules; gestorías file the returns.
software_solvable: Yes. A multi-jurisdiction engine covering rates, exemptions, night caps, surcharges, collection at booking and return preparation.
confidence: High for Catalonia's status and Gipuzkoa; medium for exact Barcelona amounts.

title: Costly, fragmented PMS, channel-manager and compliance subscriptions for small hotels and VUT managers
who: Small hotels, hostels and VUT managers with roughly 1–200 units.
where: National.
reality: Managers combine a PMS, a channel manager, online check-in and police reporting, tourist-tax handling, deposits, dynamic pricing and messaging. Most are priced per unit with add-ons and minimum commitments, and the larger PMS vendors publish no prices.
evidence:
- Smoobu: the listed prices are per month and scale "por número de unidades seleccionadas" (by number of units selected): Flex €29 plus 0.9% per booking, Prepago €35 (€31.50 billed annually), Pro+ €55 (€49.50 annually). Each additional unit costs €9.60/month and extra write-access accounts €12/month. The FAQ quotes €28 for the first unit, which conflicts with the price table. Police reporting is not mentioned — [Smoobu pricing, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://www.smoobu.com/es/precios/)
- Chekin: from €3.95/€5.95/€7.95 per property per month, with inconsistently stated minimums and transaction fees (1.5% + €0.30 on deposits; damage protection $2.50–$4.00) — [Chekin pricing](https://chekin.com/en/pricing/)
- Mews is priced "on a per-room basis" on custom quotes, with payments, POS and add-ons extra — [Mews pricing](https://www.mews.com/en/pricing). Cloudbeds' Flex, One, Experience and Enterprise plans are all quote-only — [Cloudbeds pricing](https://www.cloudbeds.com/pricing/)
- Lodgify's pricing page returned 403 and could not be read. Avantio, Hostaway and Avirato pricing was not retrieved (gap).
scale: About 341,000 listed tourist homes and about 200,000 Booking partners, most of them small operators.
cost_impact: Indicatively, a 10-unit manager on Smoobu Prepago pays about €35 + 9 × €9.60 ≈ €121/month, plus Chekin at €3.95–€7.95 per property (≈ €40–€80/month). That is roughly €1,950–€2,400 a year (my calculation; the pricing pages are ambiguous), before payment fees, dynamic-pricing tools or a hotel channel manager.
driver_status: A market problem, plus regulatory add-ons (SES, tourist taxes, registration numbers, EU data sharing).
solved_today: Bundled PMSs with built-in compliance (net2rent, Smoobu) and point tools (Chekin).
software_solvable: Yes. This is pure software consolidation and pricing, but the market is crowded.

title: Andalusia's new mandatory electronic complaints system (Hoj@)
who: Every business selling in Andalusia, including hotels, apartments, VUT and property managers. Its application to restaurants was not stated in the source.
where: Andalucía (Málaga, Sevilla, Granada, Cádiz, Costa del Sol).
reality: Businesses must register on the Hoj@ platform, designate authorised people, display a QR poster, keep paper complaint forms and answer electronic complaints within 10 working days.
evidence: An Order of 24 Apr 2026 (BOJA nº82, 30 Apr 2026), implementing Decreto 82/2022, entered into force on 20 May 2026. Registration is mandatory by 20 Nov 2026 for large firms (more than 250 staff, turnover above €50M or more than 20 establishments in Andalucía) and by 20 May 2027 for everyone else. A complaint counts as received when opened or after 10 calendar days, and the business has 10 working days to reply. Failing to reply is an infraction under art. 71.8.3ª of Ley 13/2003 — [Chekin, 9 Jun 2026](https://chekin.com/blog/boja-andalucia-nuevo-sistema-hoj-de-quejas-y-reclamaciones/) (vendor, single source; the BOJA text was not checked).
scale: All Andalusian accommodation businesses (90,649 listed tourist homes in Andalucía in May 2026, INE via [idealista](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/06/24/903471-estos-son-los-municipios-con-mas-viviendas-turisticas-en-espana)).
cost_impact: Fine amounts not stated.
driver_status: Andalusian Order of 24 Apr 2026. **Upcoming deadlines** on 20 Nov 2026 and 20 May 2027. This overlaps with cross-sector consumer compliance.
solved_today: Not yet solved; there is no evidence of tools.
software_solvable: Yes. Complaint inbox, deadline alerts and response templates, ideally integrated into a PMS or helpdesk.
confidence: Medium-low until checked against the BOJA.

title: Barcelona — all 10,101 tourist-flat licences (HUT) lapse in November 2028
who: HUT owners (many autónomos), property managers, and cleaning, laundry and maintenance suppliers.
where: Barcelona city.
reality: Licensed operators have a fixed end date. No new licences are issued, so they must plan exits, conversions or moves to other uses while paying a doubled tourist tax (HOS-15).
evidence:
- Mayor Collboni announced in July 2024 that the licences of "los 10.101 apartamentos actualmente aprobados" would end by November 2028. The Supreme Court rejected an owners' appeal around 13 Mar 2025 — [Genbeta, 14 Mar 2025](https://www.genbeta.com/actualidad/barcelona-va-ganando-airbnb-booking-tribunal-supremo-apoya-que-prohiba-pisos-turisticos-hay-fecha-para-ello)
- The Constitutional Court upheld the Catalan decree-law in 2025 (exact date not given). Collboni: "10.000 pisos turísticos se convertirán en viviendas residenciales" ("10,000 tourist flats will become homes"). Apartur says tourist flats are "apenas el 0,77% del parque residencial" (barely 0.77% of the housing stock) and that eliminating them would cost about 40% of the city's tourist accommodation capacity (lobby figure) — [Moncloa.com, 12 Jun 2026](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/06/12/barcelona-collboni-pisos-3384249/)
- Mechanism: the Catalan decree-law requires municipalities to approve specific planning before 2028 for tourist flats to continue, and Barcelona will not do so — [Hosteltur (search summary)](https://www.hosteltur.com/165598_apartur-barcelona-prohibe-pisos-turisticos-pero-permitira-mas-hoteles.html)
scale: 10,101 licences; 8,231 listings in May 2026 (INE).
cost_impact: Loss of the business in 2028. Effects on cleaning and maintenance jobs were not quantified (gap).
driver_status: Catalan Decreto-ley 3/2023 and Barcelona planning. **In force; deadline November 2028.** Upheld by the Constitutional Court (2025, per press) and the Supreme Court (March 2025).
solved_today: Lawyers and associations (Apartur). Some owners are moving to seasonal or medium-term rentals, but that route is also being regulated (see Gaps).
software_solvable: No for the ban itself. Partly for the transition: portfolio planning and compliance with seasonal-rental rules.
confidence: High on the policy; low on the knock-on effects.

title: Madrid — Plan Reside, the licence freeze and escalating fines
who: VUT owners and managers in the historic centre and in upper floors anywhere in the city.
where: Madrid city. Historic centre (APE 00.01, written "AP-01" in the source) plus city-wide rules.
reality: No new dispersed VUT are allowed in residential buildings in the centre. Elsewhere only ground or first floors (and basements, per idealista) with independent access qualify. Inspections and coercive fines push illegal flats out, and appeals are pending.
evidence:
- The City approved the plan at an extraordinary plenary on 21 May 2025. It ends dispersed VUT in the historic centre, requires independent access city-wide, limits VUT to basement, ground or first floor, sets fines of up to €190,000 per home, and keeps the licence suspension in place since Apr 2024 — [idealista, 21 May 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/05/21/845876-aprobado-el-plan-reside-de-madrid-prohibe-viviendas-turisticas-dispersas-en-el)
- The Comunidad de Madrid approved it on 27 Aug 2025. Listings fell from 16,959 (Jul 2025) to 14,297 (7 Nov 2025), down 15.7% (Inside Airbnb data cited by the council). Fines escalate to €30,001, €60,001 and €100,001 for repeated non-compliance under art. 204 of the regional land law. 1,423 flats stopped tourist use under an agreement with the Colegio de Administradores de Fincas — [Forbes, 11 Nov 2025](https://forbes.es/economia/825920/los-pisos-turisticos-en-la-ciudad-de-madrid-caen-un-157-desde-la-aprobacion-del-plan-reside/)
- The council claims a 40% fall in tourist flats between Aug 2024 and May 2026 (INE), against 15% for Spain — [Madrid City Council press release (title and search summary only; page returned 403)](https://diario.madrid.es/blog/notas-de-prensa/madrid-lidera-a-nivel-nacional-la-reduccion-de-los-pisos-turisticos-caen-un-40-en-la-capital-frente-al-15-del-conjunto-de-espana/)
- Litigation:
- The TSJ de Madrid admitted the PSOE's appeal and asked for the administrative file. The PSOE claims the plan could let up to 73% of central buildings become tourist accommodation (party estimate) — [Brains RE News, 20 Oct 2025](https://brainsre.news/justicia-revisa-plan-reside-madrid-tras-recurso-psoe/)
- The earlier Plan Especial de Hospedaje faces 14 appeals (search summary).
- A Madrid court annulled a €30,001 fine on a tourist flat for wrong legal classification (3 Feb 2026, not final; headline only) — [idealista tag page](https://www.idealista.com/news/etiquetas/normativa-alquiler-turistico)
scale: 10,836 listings in May 2026 (INE); 14,297 in Nov 2025 (Inside Airbnb).
cost_impact: Fines of €30,001–€190,000 per home; loss of the business for non-compliant flats.
driver_status: Plan Reside (a PGOU modification). **In force since Aug–Sep 2025, appealed** at the TSJ de Madrid with no ruling found.
solved_today: Urban-planning consultants and lawyers; moving to whole-building tourist use, which the plan allows.
software_solvable: Mostly no. Partly through compliance checks on licences against listings and inspection-risk alerts.

title: Andalusia — Málaga's 43-barrio ban, mass revocations in Sevilla and the Costa del Sol
who: VUT owners and managers (many autónomos), cleaning and laundry firms.
where: Málaga city, Sevilla, Marbella, Benalmádena, Fuengirola, Mijas; Granada and Cádiz not verified.
reality: In saturated barrios new registrations are blocked. Elsewhere units need independent access and services. Thousands of applications were revoked and delisted in 2025, and Málaga province carries the country's largest VUT stock.
evidence:
- Málaga's PGOU amendment, based on Andalusian Decreto 31/2024 (which lets councils limit VUT), sets three bands: no new VUT in 43 barrios where VUT exceed 8% of housing; new VUT capped at 8% in 32 barrios; and new VUT allowed in 296 others only with independent access and services. The study counted 11,559 registered VUT, 7,035 of them on platforms. Initial approval was given in October 2024, pending plenary approval and publication in the BOP — [idealista, 24 Oct 2024](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2024/10/24/820750-malaga-prohibe-nuevas-viviendas-turisticas-en-43-barrios-de-la-ciudad). Final approval and 2026 status were not verified (gap).
- Revoked registry applications notified for delisting (Sep 2025): Sevilla 2,289 (the most of any city), Marbella 1,802, Málaga 1,471, Benalmádena 926, Fuengirola 686; Andalucía 16,740 in total — [idealista, 15 Sep 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/09/15/859916-el-gobierno-notifica-mas-de-53-500-pisos-turisticos-ilegales-para-que-se-retiren)
- In Andalucía, more than 90,000 registry applications produced 66,643 approvals and 21,294 rejections. Málaga province had more than 36,000 definitive codes and 10,327 revocations — [idealista, 20 Jan 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/01/20/879570-una-de-cada-cinco-viviendas-de-alquiler-de-corta-estancia-se-quedan-sin-el-codigo)
- Andalucía appealed the national registry (May 2025, headline) and after the annulment asked for an analysis of compensation for affected operators — [idealista, 22 May 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/05/22/898792-el-fin-del-registro-de-viviendas-de-corta-estancia-reabre-100-000-licencias)
scale: Málaga province 45,176 listings; Sevilla city 6,937 (INE, May 2026).
cost_impact: Lost registrations and bookings; Hoj@ duties come on top (HOS-17).
driver_status: Decreto 31/2024 (Junta de Andalucía), **in force**. Málaga's PGOU amendment had initial approval in 2024; final status not verified. Sevilla's own caps were not verified (gap).
solved_today: Gestorías handle registration with the Registro de Turismo de Andalucía (RTA); PMSs display the RTA code.
software_solvable: Partly. Checking zone and cap eligibility before buying or listing, and tracking registrations.

title: Comunitat Valenciana — Valencia and Alicante moratoria and the largest supply drop
who: VUT owners and managers, and investors in whole-building apartments.
where: Valencia city (Cabanyal-Canyamelar), Alicante city, Torrevieja; Benidorm not verified.
reality: Licence suspensions spread barrio by barrio and to whole buildings. The Comunitat Valenciana lost the most listings, and one in three of the listings sanctioned in Airbnb's €64M fine were located there.
evidence:
- Valencia extended its May 2024 moratorium in Cabanyal-Canyamelar, suspending building permits for new tourist apartments after licence applications rose more than 220%. Compromís asked for a one-year extension — [idealista, 28 Jan 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/01/28/829610-valencia-suspende-las-licencias-para-nuevos-pisos-turisticos-en-el-barrio-del)
- Alicante (22 Jul 2025) extended its moratorium to whole blocks, pensions and tourist hostels for two years. Aptur CV is suing, claiming the council's own report found no excess of tourist flats, and citing €220M of economic impact and 2,500 jobs in 2024 (lobby figures) — [idealista, 22 Jul 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/07/22/854283-alicante-aprueba-ampliar-la-moratoria-a-licencias-de-pisos-turisticos-en-bloques)
- Registry revocations: Valencia city 731, Torrevieja 700, Comunitat Valenciana 7,499 — [idealista, 15 Sep 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/09/15/859916-el-gobierno-notifica-mas-de-53-500-pisos-turisticos-ilegales-para-que-se-retiren). Alicante province had 35,916 definitive codes and 8,309 revocations — [idealista, 20 Jan 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/01/20/879570-una-de-cada-cinco-viviendas-de-alquiler-de-corta-estancia-se-quedan-sin-el-codigo)
- One in three of the 65,122 listings in Airbnb's fine were in the Comunitat Valenciana, followed by Canarias and Galicia — [RTVC/Europa Press, Dec 2025 (search summary)](https://rtvc.es/consumo-sanciona-64-millones-airbnb-anunciar-viviendas-sin-licencia/)
- It was the Generalitat Valenciana's appeal that won Supreme Court ruling 620/2026 against the national registry — [Notarios y Registradores](https://www.notariosyregistradores.com/web/participa/noticias/el-ts-anula-registro-arrendamientos-corta-duracion/)
scale: Comunitat Valenciana 51,268 listings (about −12,000 year on year); Alicante province 32,148; Valencia city 5,393 (INE, May 2026).
cost_impact: Moratoria freeze new supply; existing operators face delisting risk.
driver_status: Municipal moratoria, **in force** (Alicante for two years from Jul 2025). Regional Decreto-ley 9/2024 and Valencia's city-wide 2024–25 rules were not verified (gap).
solved_today: Lawyers (Aptur CV litigation); registration with the regional tourism register (RTV).
software_solvable: Partly, through eligibility and zoning lookup and compliance monitoring.

title: Baleares (Palma/Mallorca) and Canarias — bans, caps and island-level delisting deals
who: VUT owners and managers, hostels and vacation-home (vivienda vacacional) owners.
where: Palma and Mallorca; Canarias (Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Adeje, Arona, La Oliva); Ibiza not verified.
reality: Palma announced a ban on any new tourist rental and on new hostels. Island authorities are getting Airbnb to delist units without the island registration number. Canarias is legislating a hard cap on vacation homes.
evidence:
- Palma's mayor announced on 14 Oct 2025 a ban on new tourist rentals "en cualquiera de sus modalidades" (in any form) across the municipality, to be approved in plenary, with three months' retroactive effect. The city's 639 legal tourist homes would be kept, and new hostels would also be banned — [idealista, 14 Oct 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/10/14/867487-palma-prohibira-nuevos-alquileres-turisticos-en-cualquiera-de-sus-modalidades). Final approval was not verified (gap).
- Airbnb removed more than 2,300 Mallorca listings that lacked the Consell de Mallorca number, the second phase of an agreement with the Consell; a councillor said "no habrá tregua" (there will be no truce) — [idealista, 27 Oct 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/10/27/869388-airbnb-elimina-mas-de-2-300-anuncios-en-mallorca-que-no-cuentan-con-numero-de)
- The Canarias draft law (March 2025) would:
- cap vacation homes at 10% of residential buildable area per settlement (20% in La Palma, La Gomera and El Hierro);
- require a minimum of 35 m² and 10 years of age;
- allow no new vacation homes until municipal planning permits them, for five years.
- The CNMC warned it could wipe out supply — [idealista, 19 Mar 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/03/19/837355-cnmc-avisa-a-canarias-de-que-su-ley-para-regular-el-alquiler-turistico-puede-acabar)
- The final law's number, date and transition terms were not verified (gap).
- Airbnb removed unregistered Canarias listings under an April 2025 agreement with the regional government; registered listings rose more than 45% between 1 Jan and 31 Aug 2025 — [idealista, 30 Sep 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/09/30/862069-airbnb-elimina-anuncios-de-alquileres-a-corto-plazo-en-canarias-que-no-completaron)
- In some parts of Canarias, obsolete tourist accommodation is being converted into substandard housing (infravivienda) — [Exceltur SolyTUR 2024, Apr 2025](https://www.exceltur.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Exceltur_Solytur-2024_230425.pdf)
scale: Baleares 21,304 listings; Canarias 48,356; Las Palmas province 26,998; Tenerife 21,358 (INE, May 2026). Canarias had 8,698 registry revocations in Sep 2025.
cost_impact: Frozen new supply; delisting of non-compliant units.
driver_status:
- Palma: ban **announced** (Oct 2025); adoption not verified.
- Canarias: vacation-rental law, draft in March 2025; the final law was not verified.
- Balearic "contención turística" decree-laws were not verified.
solved_today: Registration with the island or regional registers (ETV, VV codes); lawyers.
software_solvable: Partly, through compliance monitoring and eligibility checks.
confidence: Medium-low because of the status gaps.

title: Owners' communities can veto new tourist flats by a 3/5 majority (reform of the Ley de Propiedad Horizontal)
who: Prospective VUT owners and managers in apartment buildings.
where: National.
reality: Since April 2025, opening a new VUT in an apartment building requires explicit approval by three-fifths of the owners, representing three-fifths of the participation quotas. Many units fail to get it, and missing approval was one of the main reasons registry codes were revoked.
evidence:
- From 3 Apr 2025 new tourist flats need "el visto bueno expreso" (express approval) of three-fifths of owners and quotas, without amending the title deed or statutes — [idealista, 2 Apr 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/finanzas/economia/2025/04/02/839265-las-comunidades-de-vecinos-tendran-la-ultima-palabra-sobre-los-pisos-turisticos)
- Ley Orgánica 1/2025 has applied since 3 Apr 2025, and licences granted before that date keep their acquired rights — [Moncloa.com, 12 Jun 2026](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/06/12/barcelona-collboni-pisos-3384249/)
- Missing 3/5 community approval was one of the three main reasons for revoking registry codes — [idealista, 7 Jul 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/07/07/852282-los-motivos-que-provocan-mas-revocaciones-del-codigo-obligatorio-para-los)
scale: Every new VUT in a multi-unit building nationwide.
cost_impact: Blocked openings and community disputes. I could not verify the reported option for communities to raise fees by up to 20% (gap).
driver_status: LO 1/2025 (justice-efficiency law) amending Ley 49/1960. **In force since 3 Apr 2025.** The exact article text was not retrieved because the BOE page was too long.
solved_today: Community administrators (administradores de fincas) and lawyers.
software_solvable: Partly. Community voting and minutes and evidence of acquired rights are digitisable, but the veto itself is legal.

title: Enforcement through platforms and consumer law — exposure for managers and knock-on effects on the service ecosystem
who: Property managers (gestoras), hosts, cleaning and maintenance suppliers, and platforms.
where: National. Most sanctioned listings were in the Comunitat Valenciana, Canarias and Galicia.
reality: Listings vanish when platforms act on government orders or regional agreements. Large managers are investigated for presenting themselves as private hosts or giving misleading information. Lobbies warn of large losses for owners and service firms.
evidence:
- Consumo fined Airbnb €64,055,311 (signed in Dec 2025) over 65,122 listings, mainly for advertising unlicensed properties or showing registration numbers that did not match official records. The TSJ de Madrid denied Airbnb's request for interim suspension in March 2026. In July 2025 Airbnb had removed 65,000 listings — [Ministerio de Derechos Sociales, Consumo y Agenda 2030, 22–23 Mar 2026](https://www.dsca.gob.es/es/comunicacion/notas-prensa/justicia-obliga-airbnb-pagar-64-millones-euros-previstos-multa-que-le); also [RTVC (search summary)](https://rtvc.es/consumo-sanciona-64-millones-airbnb-anunciar-viviendas-sin-licencia/)
- Consumo opened proceedings against large tourist-flat managers (names not disclosed) for misleading information (art. 5 of the unfair-competition law) and for presenting a company as a private individual (art. 27). Fines can reach €100,000, or four to six times the illicit profit — [idealista, 20 Feb 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/02/20/833191-consumo-abre-expedientes-a-grandes-gestoras-de-pisos-turisticos-por-posibles)
- The consumer association CECU complained that Airbnb still allowed listings without a number and that Booking blocked new ones but had not removed existing listings — [idealista, 4 Jul 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/07/04/851896-de-las-incidencias-a-las-denuncias-asi-ha-sido-el-estreno-del-registro-de)
- Lobby estimates, which were not borne out (see Noise): Fevitur predicted the registry would remove 70% of supply and cost €13,737M between July and December 2025 — [idealista, 16 Jun 2025](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2025/06/16/849309-fevitur-avisa-el-registro-unico-de-alquileres-de-corta-duracion-eliminara-el-70-de). In practice listed supply fell 10.7% year on year by May 2026 (INE).
scale: 65,122 sanctioned listings; 341,001 listed units nationally.
cost_impact: Delisted units lose all platform revenue. Managers face fines of up to €100,000 or 4–6× profit. Cleaning and maintenance revenue losses were not quantified (gap).
driver_status: TRLGDCU consumer law and unfair-competition law, enforced by Consumo. The Airbnb fine is final in the administrative route and under appeal at the TSJ de Madrid, with interim relief denied. The proceedings against managers had no outcome found.
solved_today: Lawyers; platform-compliance staff inside large managers.
software_solvable: Partly. Continuous listing audits (does the code match the official register, is the host's trader status disclosed), cross-platform compliance dashboards and automated disclosure texts.
confidence: High on enforcement; low on knock-on effects.

title: Activity and tour operators — weak spending at destination, OTA dependence and booking-software fees
who: Tour, activity and experience operators and guides (autónomos and micro firms).
where: National, especially city and coastal destinations. City-specific guide rules were not verified.
reality: Operators depend on marketplaces (Viator, GetYourGuide, Civitatis) and pay booking-software fees per transaction, while tourists trim spending on extras. Seasonality compresses income into a few months.
evidence:
- Bókun's plans: FREE (1 user); START $49/month plus a 1.5% booking fee; PLUS $149/month plus 1.25% (the plan card says 1%); PREMIUM $499/month plus 1%. There is no Bókun fee on Viator bookings, and channel-manager pricing is on request — [Bókun pricing, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://www.bokun.io/pricing)
- FareHarbor and TuriTop pricing pages did not load (gap). Viator, GetYourGuide and Civitatis commission rates were not verified (gap).
- Weak 2026 demand for leisure: see Cited Findings above (Exceltur).
scale: Not quantified (gap).
cost_impact: Software fees of 1–1.5% per booking plus a monthly fee; marketplace commissions unknown.
driver_status: Market forces (spending restraint, OTA concentration). Regional licensing of tour guides and municipal free-tour rules (Madrid, Barcelona, Sevilla, San Sebastián, Granada) were not verified (gap).
solved_today: Bókun, FareHarbor, TuriTop, Regiondo and direct websites. Complaints were not researched.
software_solvable: Partly. Direct booking, channel management and dynamic pricing help, but demand and licensing are external.

title: Seasonal staffing and worker housing in island and coastal destinations
who: Hotels, restaurants and beach clubs in seasonal destinations (micro to medium), and their seasonal workers.
where: Baleares (Mallorca, Ibiza), Canarias, Costa del Sol (Málaga), Costa Blanca (Benidorm).
reality: Businesses must rehire much of their staff every season. Workers struggle to find affordable rentals where tourist flats and second homes absorb housing, so recruitment fails and turnover rises.
evidence:
- Turnover above 70% a year in very seasonal businesses — [El Debate, 26 Jul 2026](https://www.eldebate.com/espana/galicia/20260726/empresa-gallega-encuentra-solucion-cubrir-vacantes-hosteleria-forma-rapida_443319_amp.html)
- Mallorca restaurateurs cite soaring rents and high staff turnover — [Majorca Daily Bulletin, 17 Aug 2026](https://www.majorcadailybulletin.com/news/local/2026/08/17/145039/mallorca-bars-and-restaurants-suffer-per-cent-drop-turnover-during-the-first-half-august.html)
- Destination-level housing pressure from VUT growth and conversions of old tourist accommodation into substandard housing in parts of Canarias — [Exceltur SolyTUR 2024](https://www.exceltur.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Exceltur_Solytur-2024_230425.pdf)
- Exceltur names "escasez de talento" (talent shortage) as a persistent adverse factor in summer 2026 — [Exceltur nº98](https://www.exceltur.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/EXCELTUR-Informe-Perspectivas-N98-Balance-del-IIIT26-y-previsiones-para-IVT26.pdf)
scale: Not quantified for workers specifically (gap).
cost_impact: Not quantified: no data on rents paid by seasonal workers, employer-provided housing costs or unfilled posts.
driver_status: Housing scarcity and the concentration of activity in one season. Balearic and Canarian measures on worker housing were not verified (gap).
solved_today: Not verified. Employer-leased staff housing and housing allowances are reported anecdotally but were not sourced here.
software_solvable: Partly. Staff-housing marketplaces, pre-season rehiring pipelines and planning for fixed-discontinuous (fijo discontinuo) staff could help, but the root cause is housing supply.
confidence: Low to medium. The pain is very likely real, but worker-specific evidence was not captured.

title: Time-recording compliance in limbo (paper legal today, digital mandate pending)
who: All employers, from autónomos with one employee to medium firms. The pain is heaviest in hostelería, retail, building caretakers, field and mobile staff, and split shifts.
where: National.
reality: Owners keep paper sheets, Excel or a basic app. They don't know whether to invest now or wait for the decree, and they are exposed if an inspector or an ex-employee challenges the hours.
evidence:
- Paper or electronic records are valid today; the fine is €751–7,500 per infraction — [RegistraHora, 13 Oct 2026](https://www.registrahora.es/noticias/registro-horario-digital-aplazado-septiembre-2026); [ControlHorarioLegal, 23 Oct 2026](https://controlhorariolegal.com/normativa-fichaje-2026).
- The Consejo de Estado estimates 1.35M companies affected at €867M a year and says "no procede aprobar" (should not be approved) — [El Español, 23 Mar 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/invertia/economia/empleo/20260323/consejo-critica-tumba-registro-horario-yolanda-diaz/1003744181041_0.html).
- Postponed on 24 Jul 2026; not approved as of 23 Oct 2026.
scale: 1.35M companies (Consejo de Estado figure, via El Español).
cost_impact:
- €867M a year estimated compliance cost if the decree passes, about €640 per firm (my inference).
- Fines up to €7,500 per infraction.
- Registro-specific fines of €2.99M in 2024 (1,869 infractions) — [El Derecho/EP, 7 Feb 2025](https://elderecho.com/inspeccion-de-trabajo-elevo-un-9-las-multas-por-infracciones-por-tiempo-de-trabajo-en-2024).
driver_status:
- Art. 34.9 ET (RDL 8/2019): **in force**.
- Digital-registration royal decree (draft): **pending / postponed**. Urgent processing was authorised 30 Sep 2025, the Consejo de Estado opinion was unfavourable on 23 Mar 2026, and the decree was missing from the agendas of 6, 13 and 20 Oct 2026. The Government aims to approve it before 29-N, with a 6- or 12-month transition for pymes under discussion.
solved_today:
- Paper or Excel.
- Apps: Woffu Lite from €1.5 per user per month (10 or fewer employees); Sesame €4.75–8 (15-seat minimum); Factorial from €5–5.5; Timu (Nimbo), priced by employees.
- Complaint: Factorial clock-ins "tarda en registrarlos" (are slow to register) — [Trustpilot, 30 Sep 2026](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/factorialhr.com).
software_solvable: Yes. Tamper-proof digital records, correction audit trails, worker access and ITSS export are exactly what software does; sector edge cases (caretakers, mobile staff) need tailored capture.
confidence: High on rules and status; medium on the cost estimate (one official-opinion figure reported by the press).

title: Working-time and overtime inspections and unpaid-overtime lawsuits
who: Micro, small and medium firms with long or irregular hours: hostelería, retail, logistics, care, construction, and startups with "always-on" cultures.
where: National. Euskadi has its own inspection data showing more than 60% of inspections find irregularities.
reality: Overtime is often unrecorded or paid informally. When a worker leaves, they claim back overtime; without a record the employer cannot rebut it if there was no fixed schedule.
evidence:
- 2024 ITSS working-time and overtime fines €17.2M (13,681 infractions, 38,686 actions) — [El Derecho/EP, 7 Feb 2025](https://elderecho.com/inspeccion-de-trabajo-elevo-un-9-las-multas-por-infracciones-por-tiempo-de-trabajo-en-2024).
- 2025: 14,728 infractions and 252,500 workers affected — [Finantres, 25 Aug 2026](https://finantresnoticias.com/negocios-y-autonomos/multas-por-incumplir-horario-se-triplican-deben-revisar-ahora-pymes/) (single source).
- Euskadi 2025: 1,490 actions, 417 infractions — [Onda Vasca, 16 Feb 2026](https://www.ondavasca.com/trabajo-sigue-detectando-un-60-de-anomalias-en-las-inspecciones-por-horarios-de-trabajo-en-euskadi/).
- STS 372/2026 sets the burden-of-proof rules; a butcher's-shop case involved €11.7k claimed — [RRHH Digital, 13 May 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/legal/794593/el-tribunal-supremo-pone-limites-a-las-reclamaciones-de-horas-extra/).
scale: About 2.4–2.5M unpaid overtime hours a week nationally — [El Independiente, 1 Apr 2024](https://www.elindependiente.com/economia/2024/04/01/multas-registro-jornada-horario-3-millones-euros/amp/); [Onda Vasca, 9 Sep 2026](https://www.ondavasca.com/trabajo-asegura-que-el-registro-horario-se-aprobara-con-caracter-inmediato-tras-incorporar-cambios-juridicos/).
cost_impact: Back-pay claims in the thousands of euros per worker, plus grave-infraction fines. Wage claims (reclamaciones de cantidad) run at 32–35k a quarter nationally — [Law&Trends/EFE, 16 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/laboral/las-demandas-por-despido-marcan-record-en-el-segundo-trimestre-con-45-230-procedimientos-1.html).
driver_status: Arts. 34–35 ET and LISOS (in force); STS 372/2026 (15 Apr 2026) case law.
solved_today: Time-recording apps (see LAB-01), gestoría advice, and labour lawyers or graduados sociales once a claim arrives (fees not found).
software_solvable: Partly. Records, overtime alerts and compensation within 4 months (per Finantres) are automatable; disputes still need lawyers.

title: SMI hikes, the absorption/compensation puzzle and retroactive payroll fixes
who: Micro and small employers in low-wage sectors (retail, hostelería, cleaning, care, agriculture, domestic employers) and the gestorías that run their payroll.
where: National. Most beneficiaries are in Andalucía, Madrid, C. Valenciana and Cataluña.
reality: Each year the SMI arrives late and retroactively, so payroll must be re-run for months already paid. Firms must test annually whether supplements can absorb the rise, and a union-backed decree-law threatens to ban absorbing some supplements.
evidence:
- RD 126/2026: €1,221 × 14, retroactive to 1 Jan, approved 18 Feb 2026; compensable income is measured as of 20 Feb 2026; an anti-absorption decree-law was pending — [PwC, 19 Feb 2026](https://periscopiofiscalylegal.pwc.es/se-fija-la-cuantia-del-smi-el-problema-ahora-es-como-aplicarlo/).
- About 2.5M beneficiaries; approved without employers — [Consejo General de Gestores, Feb 2026](https://www.consejogestores.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Novedades-destacadas-91.pdf).
scale: About 2.5M workers; the SMI is up 66% since 2018.
cost_impact:
- +€518 per worker per year in gross pay.
- An SMI worker costs €22,589.72 a year in total — [Gestoria247, 7 Sep 2026](https://gestoria247.com/blog/cuanto-cuesta-un-trabajador-a-la-empresa-2026).
- Re-processing January payroll.
- ASNALA warns pymes may struggle to absorb the rises — [Law&Trends, 14 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/abogacia/ana-gomez-presidenta-de-asnala-es-necesario-recuperar-el-dialogo-social-para-resolver-los-grandes-problemas-del-1.html).
driver_status: RD 126/2026 (in force, retroactive). The anti-absorption decree-law is announced but its status is unverified as of Oct 2026.
solved_today: Gestorías (€15–20 per payslip) and payroll software (a3innuva and others) re-run payroll; employers' associations issue circulars, e.g. [FADE Circular laboral 1/2026](https://fade.es/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Circular-laboral-1-2026.-SMI.-19Feb2026.pdf) (search result).
software_solvable: Partly. Annual absorption tests and retroactive recalculation can be automated; the cost itself cannot.

title: Rising employer contributions and total labour cost (MEI, solidarity quota, maximum base, short-contract surcharge)
who: All employers. In practice micro and small firms feel the total cost; the solidarity quota mainly hits startups and medium firms with high salaries.
where: National.
reality: Contribution rates and bases change every January, sometimes before the official order is published. Short contracts carry an extra charge. Total cost per employee rises about 4% a year.
evidence:
- Maximum base €5,101.20; €33.62 surcharge for contracts of 30 days or less — [Seguridad Social, 2026](https://www.seg-social.es/wps/portal/wss/internet/Trabajadores/CotizacionRecaudacionTrabajadores/36537).
- MEI 0.90% and solidarity quota at 1.15%, 1.25% and 1.46% by band — [CopilotGestoria, 28 Mar 2026](https://copilotgestoria.com/blog/cuota-solidaridad-2026-calcular-nomina-tramos-ejemplos-guia-gestorias), which conflicts with the official page's 0.80% (apparently not updated).
- Labour cost +4.0% and Social Security contributions +4.2% year on year — [INE, 17 Sep 2026](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/Prensa/es/ETCL2T26.htm).
scale: All employers. The maximum base matters only for salaries above about €61k a year.
cost_impact:
- Employer rate about 32.15% for a permanent office job (33.35% temporary) — [Gestoria247](https://gestoria247.com/blog/cuanto-cuesta-un-trabajador-a-la-empresa-2026).
- +€74.73 a month for an executive earning €8,500 a month — [CopilotGestoria](https://copilotgestoria.com/blog/cuota-solidaridad-2026-calcular-nomina-tramos-ejemplos-guia-gestorias).
- 5.8% of establishments without vacancies cite high hiring costs — [INE](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/Prensa/es/ETCL2T26.htm).
driver_status: Ley 21/2021 and RDL 2/2023 MEI schedule; DT 42ª LGSS solidarity quota (2025–2045); Orden PJC/297/2026. All **in force**.
solved_today: Gestorías and payroll software updates; cost simulators on gestoría and vendor blogs.
software_solvable: Partly. Cost simulation and automatic rate updates are possible; the cost itself is not reducible.
confidence: High on direction; medium on exact 2026 MEI and solidarity rates (secondary sources).

title: Record absenteeism (IT) cost and sick-leave management with mutuas
who: All sizes. The impact is acute for micro and small firms without cover staff; industry, postal, building services and care are worst hit.
where:
- National.
- Highest rates: País Vasco (Bilbao), Canarias (Las Palmas) and Cantabria, at 9.6%.
- Largest costs: Cataluña (Barcelona) €11.6bn, Madrid €10.3bn, Andalucía (Sevilla, Málaga) €7.4bn.
- Lowest rates: Baleares (Palma) 6.2% and Madrid 6.6%.
reality:
- The owner learns of a sick-leave note (parte de baja) the same morning and scrambles for cover.
- The firm pays statutory days and convenio supplements, and juggles communication with the mutua and the INSS.
- Long mental-health leaves are increasingly common.
- Employers feel powerless on suspected abuse, since surveillance is legally limited.
evidence:
- 7.6% absenteeism, 5.95% IT rate, €59.1bn cost, mental-health leave +111% in 5 years — [Adecco, 14 Jul 2026](https://www.adeccogroup.com/-/media/project/adecco-group/adeccogroup/spain-content/2026-press-releases/2026-07-14-ndp-xv-informe-anual-adecco-empresa-saludable-gestion-absentismo.pdf); [El Derecho/EP, 14 Jul 2026](https://elderecho.com/el-absentismo-laboral-alcanza-un-maximo-historico-del-76-en-2025).
- 9.1M IT processes; €16,115M of €33,280M IT cost borne by companies; 1,407,819 absent — [Law&Trends, 9 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/laboral/las-empresas-necesitan-herramientas-para-gestionar-mejor-sus-bajas-medicas-y-reducir-sus-niveles-de-absentismo-1.html) (single source).
scale: About 1.4M workers absent; 9.1M IT processes a year.
cost_impact: €16.1bn borne directly by companies in 2025; Cataluña companies alone €3.07bn.
driver_status:
- Structural (ageing, health-system waits).
- Ley 2/2025 (in force 1 May 2025) and the INSS–INGESA 2025–2028 agreement (in force).
- No adopted "flexible return / partial IT" reform found (status unknown).
solved_today:
- Mutuas (e.g., Unión de Mutuas) for monitoring.
- AMAT/CEOE follow-up on repeat claimants.
- Private investigators within legal limits.
- Absence modules in HR suites (e.g., Sesame "Vacaciones y Ausencias" from €4.75 per employee per month — [Sesame](https://www.sesamehr.es/precios/)).
- Graduados sociales and lawyers.
software_solvable: Partly. Absence tracking, return-to-work workflows, convenio supplement calculation, analytics and mutua paperwork can be automated; root causes cannot.
confidence: High on scale (Adecco plus multiple outlets); medium on the company-cost split (single source).

title: Permanent-incapacity "reasonable adjustment" duty (Ley 2/2025)
who: All employers, especially micro and small firms (under 25 workers) in physically demanding sectors.
where: National.
reality: When a worker is declared permanently incapacitated, the contract no longer ends automatically. The worker has 10 days to ask to stay. The employer then has 3 months to adapt the post or find a vacancy, or to justify in writing that this is an excessive burden before terminating.
evidence:
- Ley 2/2025 (BOE 30 Apr 2025; in force 1 May 2025).
- For firms under 25 workers, the burden is excessive if the adaptation cost (net of subsidies) exceeds the greater of the art. 56.1 ET severance or 6 months' salary.
- The prevention service determines the scope of adjustments.
- Source: [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2025/04/29/2); the change is also highlighted by [Adecco, 14 Jul 2026](https://www.adeccogroup.com/-/media/project/adecco-group/adeccogroup/spain-content/2026-press-releases/2026-07-14-ndp-xv-informe-anual-adecco-empresa-saludable-gestion-absentismo.pdf).
scale: Not quantified; number of permanent-incapacity declarations not found.
cost_impact: Adaptation costs, SPA involvement, and litigation risk if the procedure is mishandled (urgent procedure under art. 120 LRJS).
driver_status: Ley 2/2025, **in force**.
solved_today: SPA plus labour lawyers; no dedicated tools found.
software_solvable: Partly. Deadline tracking (10 days and 3 months), documentation, and a calculator comparing adaptation cost with the severance threshold.
confidence: High on rules; low on scale.

title: Technical and trade talent shortages and persistent vacancies
who: Industrial SMEs, installers, maintenance, logistics and transport, energy, plus tech startups needing software and AI profiles.
where: National. Vacancies are concentrated in Cataluña (Barcelona), Madrid and Andalucía (Sevilla, Málaga), with sector campaigns elsewhere (e.g., Valencia agriculture, Pontevedra automotive — RRHH Digital headlines).
reality: Positions stay open for months. SMEs compete with large firms and ETTs (temp agencies) for electromechanics, welders, refrigeration technicians and C+E drivers, and often train people in-house.
evidence:
- 151,736 vacancies, 87.4% in services — [INE, 17 Sep 2026](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/Prensa/es/ETCL2T26.htm).
- Maintenance technicians are more than 30% of technical vacancies; driver shortage; CNC roles "especialmente compleja" — [RRHH Digital, 15 Aug 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/mercado-laboral/800825/los-siete-perfiles-tecnicos-mas-buscados-este-verano/).
- Transport seeks 1,000 drivers — [RRHH Digital, 31 Aug 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/mercado-laboral/801076/el-sector-del-transporte-busca-1-000-choferes/) (headline).
scale: About 152k vacancies at any time (INE). Spain's vacancy count is low relative to unemployment, so the pain is concentrated in specific trades.
cost_impact: Lost output and overtime (not quantified); 5.8% of no-vacancy firms cite hiring cost — [INE](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/Prensa/es/ETCL2T26.htm).
driver_status: Market force (demographics, training mismatch, heat-driven refrigeration demand). Ongoing.
solved_today: ETTs and recruiters (Adecco, Randstad, Gi Group, ILUNION campaigns), technical training providers (Tecnio). Fees not found.
software_solvable: Partly. Recruiting, training-to-hire and skills matching help; the structural shortage is not software-solvable.
confidence: Medium. Vacancies are high-confidence; the profile list comes from vendor and agency analysis.

title: Hiring foreign workers through overloaded immigration offices (Reglamento 2025, regularisation 2026)
who: Agriculture, hostelería, care, construction and logistics SMEs; autónomo employers (including domestic employers); startups hiring non-EU talent.
where:
- National.
- Documented bottlenecks: Zaragoza (Aragón), La Rioja (Logroño), Tarragona, and Madrid (202,424 regularisation applications).
reality:
- Employers wait months for permits or arraigo resolutions and need two appointments for residence cards.
- They rely on immigration lawyers.
- They risk heavy fines if they employ someone whose authorisation has lapsed.
evidence:
- RD 1155/2024 in force about 20 May 2025; arraigo sociolaboral requires a contract on initial-permit terms — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2024/11/19/1155).
- Zaragoza: +25% workload and 6-month average delays — [CSIF Aragón, 11 Feb 2026](https://www.csif.es/es/noticia/portada/aragon/articulo/85294).
- La Rioja: more than 1,000 pending — [Nuevecuatrouno, 9 Mar 2026](https://nuevecuatrouno.com/2026/03/09/csif-rioja-colapso-extranjeria-mil-expedientes-pendientes-tramitacion/) (search summary).
- RD 316/2026 window 16 Apr–30 Jun 2026, about 500k expected — [Diari de Tarragona, 16 Apr 2026](https://www.diaridetarragona.com/tarragona/257385/posible-invisibilidad-tarragona-vuelca-regularizacion-extraordinaria_amp.html).
- More than 1.17M applications — [Law&Trends, 4 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/abogacia/los-expertos-avalan-a-una-abogacia-leal-pero-firme-que-ha-ayudado-a-regularizar-a-mas-de-1-2-millones-de-inmigrantes-1.html).
scale:
- More than 1.17M regularisation applications.
- Zaragoza alone handles about 34,000 files a year.
- ITSS found 18,655 unauthorised foreign workers in 2025 — [El Derecho/EP, 7 Oct 2026](https://elderecho.com/?p=489934).
cost_impact: €187.7M proposed fines in 2025, about €10k per unauthorised worker (my inference); months of delay; lawyer fees (not found).
driver_status:
- RD 1155/2024: **in force** since about 20 May 2025.
- RD 316/2026: application window **closed** 30 Jun 2026; resolutions and card issuance ongoing.
solved_today: Immigration lawyers (58% of Madrid online filings), gestorías, Correos (17%), individuals (11%) — [Law&Trends, 4 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/abogacia/los-expertos-avalan-a-una-abogacia-leal-pero-firme-que-ha-ayudado-a-regularizar-a-mas-de-1-2-millones-de-inmigrantes-1.html).
software_solvable: Partly. Case preparation and tracking, document checklists, and permit-expiry and right-to-work monitoring; the office-capacity bottleneck is not software-solvable.

title: Record dismissal litigation and wage claims
who: Micro, small and medium employers of all sectors; startups after funding cuts.
where:
- National.
- Largest volumes: Cataluña (Barcelona) 9,075, Madrid 8,040, Andalucía (Sevilla, Málaga) 7,302 and C. Valenciana (Valencia, Alicante) 5,885 in Q2 2026.
- Fastest growth: Galicia (Vigo, A Coruña) +27.8%.
reality: Almost any dismissal is challenged. The firm faces a mandatory SMAC conciliation, then a 3–4-year wait for trial in big cities. The usual choice is to settle at SMAC (pre-trial conciliation service) or carry the uncertainty.
evidence:
- Q2 2026: 45,230 claims, a record — [Law&Trends/EFE, 16 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/laboral/las-demandas-por-despido-marcan-record-en-el-segundo-trimestre-con-45-230-procedimientos-1.html).
- Q1 2026: 42,572 — [Forbes/EP, 22 Jun 2026](https://forbes.es/?p=961605).
- Q1 2025: 41,116 — [Bolsamanía/EP, 16 Jun 2025](https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/economia/economia--los-concursos-de-acreedores-mantienen-su-tendencia-al-alza-y-crecen-un-37-en-el-primer-trimestre-segun-cgpj--20017952.html).
- Q2 2025: 40,680 — [Bolsamanía/EP, 15 Oct 2025](https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/economia/economia-los-concursos-de-acreedores-mantienen-su-tendencia-al-alza-y-crecen-un-19-en-el-segundo-trimestre-segun-cgpj--21045150.html).
scale: About 170k dismissal claims and about 135k wage claims a year (my inference from quarterly run-rates); H1 2026 +7.3% year on year.
cost_impact: Statutory compensation is fixed by tariff, and no judicial top-ups are allowed (STS 1350/2024; STS 736/2025) — [Law&Trends, 23 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/laboral/el-supremo-cierra-la-puerta-a-aumentar-la-indemnizacion-por-despido-improcedente-1.html). Legal fees and settlement averages were not found.
driver_status: ET arts. 49–56 and LRJS (in force). Litigation volume is rising in 2026 (market and macro force).
solved_today: Graduados sociales and labour lawyers; SMAC settlements; settlement agreements (pactos transaccionales) — [RRHH Digital, 30 Sep 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/legal/802554/los-pactos-transaccionales-tras-un-despido-requisitos-para-garantizar-su-eficacia/) (headline). Prices not found.
software_solvable: Partly. Severance and risk calculators, pre-dismissal checklists, document generation and case management for advisers; the litigation itself needs professionals.
confidence: High on volumes; low on costs.

title: Labour-court backlogs pushing trials to 2029–2030
who: Every employer in a dispute, especially those in Madrid and Barcelona.
where: Documented in Madrid and Barcelona. Other cities (Sevilla, Valencia, Málaga, Bilbao) were not verified in 2026 sources.
reality: A contested dismissal or wage claim stays an open liability for years, complicating provisioning, sale of the business and audits.
evidence:
- Madrid trials set for 2029–2030, judgments 6–10 months after the hearing, 80–90 vacancies — [Law&Trends/EFE, 21 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/abogacia/abogados-laboralistas-exigen-soluciones-ante-los-retrasos-en-los-juicios-de-lo-social-1.html).
- Barcelona "citaciones para el año 2030" (court dates in 2030) — [Law&Trends, 2 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/laboral/el-colegio-de-graduados-sociales-de-barcelona-girona-y-lleida-alerta-del-impacto-del-rd-723-2026-en-la-gestion-y-el-1.html).
scale: Tens of thousands of pending cases (no exact backlog figure found).
cost_impact: Uncertainty and contingent liabilities (not quantified).
driver_status: Judicial staffing; the court-structure reform into Tribunales de Instancia is operating — [Grant Thornton, Jun 2026](https://www.grantthornton.es/contentassets/4730b6c010d04ea29770da8a29bc5b94/labour-newsjunio-retos-aun-pendientes-y-nuevos-limites-en-materia-laboralgrant-thornton.pdf). Ongoing.
solved_today: Settlement and mediation, e.g. a new court-annexed mediation protocol between the Audiencia Nacional and SIMA-FSP — [RRHH Digital, 5 Mar 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/legal/790517/el-novedoso-protocolo-de-mediacion-intra-judicial-entre-la-audiencia-nacional-y-el-sima-fsp/) (headline).
software_solvable: No. Court capacity is the constraint; only settlement-support tools help at the margin.
confidence: Medium (two press sources, Madrid and Barcelona only).

title: Dismissal procedure traps (pre-dismissal hearing, retaliation nullity, notice-pay contributions, net back pay)
who: Owner-managed micro and small firms without HR staff; autónomo employers.
where: National.
reality: The owner fires someone with a letter template. They skip the pre-dismissal hearing, or dismiss shortly after the worker complained, or pay notice in lieu without contributions. Each mistake turns a defensible dismissal into an unfair or null one, or into a Social Security debt.
evidence:
- Hearing requirement since the 2024 change in case law — [Law&Trends, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/laboral/un-tramite-que-puede-cambiarlo-todo-cuando-un-despido-disciplinario-puede-ser-declarado-improcedente-1.html).
- STS 526/2026 on retaliation nullity before any formal claim — [RRHH Digital, 15 Jul 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/legal/799602/el-supremo-refuerza-la-proteccion-frente-al-despido-represalia-incluso-antes-de-una-reclamacion-formal/).
- TGSS RED 8/2026 makes notice pay contributable — [RRHH Digital, 22 Jul 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/legal/799952/la-tgss-cambia-el-criterio-la-compensacion-por-falta-de-preaviso-en-el-despido-objetivo-ya-cotiza/).
- Back pay (salarios de tramitación) is subject to income-tax and Social Security withholding, and clauses allowing unilateral schedule changes are null (STS 491/2026) — [Grant Thornton, Jun 2026](https://www.grantthornton.es/contentassets/4730b6c010d04ea29770da8a29bc5b94/labour-newsjunio-retos-aun-pendientes-y-nuevos-limites-en-materia-laboralgrant-thornton.pdf).
scale: Applies to every disciplinary or objective dismissal; tens of thousands a quarter are litigated (LAB-09).
cost_impact: Unfair-dismissal compensation instead of none; nullity means readmission plus back pay; supplementary contributions on notice pay; ITSS proposed €459,587 for improper probation terminations in 2025 — [El Derecho/EP, 7 Oct 2026](https://elderecho.com/?p=489934).
driver_status: Case law 2024–2026 and TGSS criteria (July 2026). **In force.**
solved_today: Gestorías and labour lawyers; articles from law firms (Augusta Abogados) serve as guidance. No dedicated SME tools found.
software_solvable: Yes or partly. A guided dismissal workflow (hearing, letter, timing check against recent complaints, correct CRA coding of notice pay, net back-pay calculation) is very automatable.

title: Labour Inspectorate enforcement at record intensity
who: All sizes. Sector focus includes temporary contracts, part-time, platforms, foreign labour and hiring before registration with Social Security.
where: National, plus the Basque inspectorate.
reality: Firms receive ITSS letters, requirements and visits, often triggered by anonymous complaints. Small firms lack documentation ready to produce.
evidence:
- ITSS 2025 annual report: €858.26M in proposed sanctions (+58.62% vs €541M); €1,212.3M in Social Security contributions claimed; 1,206,028 actions; 427,495 workplaces; 131,645 irregular jobs surfaced; 96,194 registrations made by the ITSS itself; 70,163 contracts converted to permanent; 11,824 anonymous complaints (+17.5%) — [El Derecho/EP, 7 Oct 2026](https://elderecho.com/?p=489934).
- Euskadi 2025: €10.4M in penalties from 20,191 actions — [Onda Vasca, 16 Feb 2026](https://www.ondavasca.com/trabajo-sigue-detectando-un-60-de-anomalias-en-las-inspecciones-por-horarios-de-trabajo-en-euskadi/).
scale: About 427k workplaces inspected a year, and about 1.03M workers directly protected by inspections.
cost_impact: €858M in proposed fines in 2025.
driver_status: LISOS; ITSS strategic plans and anti-fraud campaigns. In force and intensifying.
solved_today: Gestorías and asesorías, labour lawyers, compliance audits (prices not found).
software_solvable: Partly. A continuous compliance self-audit, document vault and ITSS-requirement response workflow.
confidence: High (official report via Europa Press), though single-source.

title: Bogus self-employment (falsos autónomos) and bogus internships, especially at startups and platforms
who: Startups, digital platforms, delivery, professional services and media using freelancers or interns as staff.
where: National; startup hubs in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia and Málaga (inference; no city data).
reality: Early-stage companies contract "freelancers" with fixed hours or use unpaid or underpaid interns. The ITSS reclassifies them, with back contributions and fines.
evidence: ITSS 2025 regularised 47,143 bogus self-employed (vs 7,234 in 2024) and 601 bogus interns (vs 220) — [El Derecho/EP, 7 Oct 2026](https://elderecho.com/?p=489934) (single source; the jump may reflect a few large platform cases, unverified).
scale: 47k workers reclassified in 2025.
cost_impact: Back contributions (part of the €1.21bn claimed in total) plus fines.
driver_status: ET art. 1 presumption of employment and LISOS; ITSS campaigns. In force.
solved_today: Lawyers; employer-of-record and freelancer platforms (not researched here).
software_solvable: Partly. A contractor-classification risk checklist and conversion-cost simulator.

title: Temporary, part-time and fijos-discontinuos contract misuse risk
who: Seasonal and variable-demand SMEs (hostelería, agriculture, retail, events, education services).
where: National, with seasonal regions such as Baleares, Canarias, Málaga and Valencia (inference).
reality: Since the 2021 reform, temporary contracts need a specific justification. Seasonal staff must be "fijos discontinuos" (permanent seasonal workers) with formal call-ups. Part-time hours must match reality. Contracts of 30 days or less trigger a surcharge.
evidence:
- ITSS 2025: 70,163 contracts converted to ordinary permanent ones (temporary and fijos discontinuos) and 18,804 part-time contracts extended — [El Derecho/EP, 7 Oct 2026](https://elderecho.com/?p=489934).
- €33.62 surcharge on terminating contracts of 30 days or less — [Seguridad Social, 2026](https://www.seg-social.es/wps/portal/wss/internet/Trabajadores/CotizacionRecaudacionTrabajadores/36537).
- RD 723/2026 now requires stating the justification for any temporary contract in writing — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2026/09/09/723).
- Euskadi: 1,788 contracts converted to permanent full-time out of 26,959 reviewed — [Onda Vasca, 16 Feb 2026](https://www.ondavasca.com/trabajo-sigue-detectando-un-60-de-anomalias-en-las-inspecciones-por-horarios-de-trabajo-en-euskadi/).
