scale: About 70k conversions a year nationally.
cost_impact: Fines per contract (amounts not verified here), conversion to permanent, surcharges.
driver_status: RDL 32/2021 labour reform (in force), RD 723/2026 (in force 5 Oct 2026).
solved_today: Gestorías and Contrat@ (the public employment service's online contract-filing system).
software_solvable: Partly. A contract-type rules engine, call-up management for fijos discontinuos and part-time hours reconciliation with time records.
confidence: Medium. I found no data on fijos-discontinuos litigation.

title: New written-information duties under RD 723/2026 (from 5 Oct 2026)
who: All employers, including autónomo employers; startups using algorithmic management.
where: National.
reality: Every new hire must get, before starting, a detailed written statement covering pay items, schedule, probation, convenio code, protocols, equality measures and algorithmic systems, delivered with proof. Changes must be notified by the day they take effect. Existing staff can demand the statement, with 30 working days to respond.
evidence:
- Rules as above — [BOE, RD 723/2026](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2026/09/09/723).
- Guidance on what employers must now provide — [RRHH Digital, 18 Sep 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/legal/802273/las-empresas-tendran-que-informar-con-mas-detalle-a-sus-empleados-sobre-sus-condiciones-de-trabajo-desde-octubre/).
- Graduados sociales expect more ITSS complaints; EU infringement case (€7.54M lump sum plus €266,772 a day sought) — [Law&Trends, 2 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/laboral/el-colegio-de-graduados-sociales-de-barcelona-girona-y-lleida-alerta-del-impacto-del-rd-723-2026-en-la-gestion-y-el-1.html).
scale: Every new contract longer than 4 weeks (all employers, roughly 1.35M by the Consejo de Estado count).
cost_impact: Administrative time per hire and change; complaint and litigation risk. Sanctions are not set in the decree.
driver_status: RD 723/2026 (transposes Directive 2019/1152). **In force since 5 Oct 2026.** The SEPE model document was due within 20 days of 15 Sep 2026; publication not verified.
solved_today: Gestoría contract packs; HR suites with e-signature (Factorial Core includes e-signature — [Factorial](https://factorial.es/pricing)).
software_solvable: Yes. Auto-generating the information document from contract and convenio data, e-delivery with proof, change notifications and a 30-day request tracker.

title: Pay register for all and the delayed pay-transparency transposition
who: Pay register: all employers. Pay-transparency draft: 50+ (Spanish draft) and 100+ (Directive). Medium firms and scale-ups are most affected.
where: National.
reality: Firms keep a nominal pay register, often only on paper. They don't know when salary ranges in job adverts, the ban on pay-history questions, gap reports and joint pay assessments will apply, or in what form.
evidence:
- Deadline of 7 Jun 2026 missed — [Grant Thornton, Jun 2026](https://www.grantthornton.es/contentassets/4730b6c010d04ea29770da8a29bc5b94/labour-newsjunio-retos-aun-pendientes-y-nuevos-limites-en-materia-laboralgrant-thornton.pdf); [Que.es, 9 Jun 2026](https://www.que.es/2026/06/09/transparencia-salarial-ofertas-pospuesta/).
- Draft royal decree amending RD 902/2020 consulted 4–24 Aug 2026; duties from 50 employees; not in the BOE — [Talentup, 10 Sep 2026](https://talentup.io/insights/es/pay-transparency/spain/) (single source).
- Ministry promised the text "en los próximos días o semanas"; more than a third of companies not ready — [RRHH Digital, 10 Jun 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/legal/797519/la-directiva-de-transparencia-retributiva-el-plazo-vencio-ayer-y-espana-aun-no-la-ha-traspuesto/).
scale: All employers for the register; 50+ firms for the draft duties (count not found).
cost_impact: Future joint pay assessments and litigation (a Supreme Court magistrate expects disputes in court) — [Law&Trends, 23 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/laboral/espana-ante-el-reto-de-la-igualdad-y-transparencia-salarial-las-mujeres-cobran-de-media-5-000-euros-anuales-menos-que-1.html).
driver_status:
- RD 902/2020 pay register: **in force**.
- Directive 2023/970: transposition **overdue and in draft**. The Directive's first gap report for 150+ employees is due by 7 Jun 2027.
- The elections make law-rank elements unlikely before 2027 (my inference).
solved_today: Equality and HR consultants and HR software pay-register modules (prices not found).
software_solvable: Yes or partly. Pay-register and gap analytics, salary-band publication and right-to-information request handling; job-evaluation methodology needs consultants.
confidence: Medium on status (consistent across sources, but draft details are single-source).

title: Equality plans (50+) and REGCON registration friction
who: Medium firms (50–249) and some small firms that crossed the threshold.
where: National.
reality:
- The firm must form a negotiating commission, carry out a diagnosis and a pay audit, negotiate the plan and register it in REGCON.
- The administration has rejected registrations on substantive grounds, forcing litigation.
- Plans must be adapted and renewed periodically.
evidence: TS 519/2026 (28 May 2026) and STS 461/2025 (27 May 2025) limit REGCON to formal control — [Grant Thornton, Jun 2026](https://www.grantthornton.es/contentassets/4730b6c010d04ea29770da8a29bc5b94/labour-newsjunio-retos-aun-pendientes-y-nuevos-limites-en-materia-laboralgrant-thornton.pdf).
scale: Not found (no REGCON count retrieved). Only 52% of SMEs say they apply equality policies — [RRHH Digital, 1 Mar 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/pymes/790309/por-primera-vez-mas-de-la-mitad-de-las-pymes-espanolas-aplica-politicas-de-igualdad/).
cost_impact: Consultancy fees (not found) and LISOS fines (not verified here).
driver_status: LO 3/2007 and RD 901/2020 (in force since 2022 for 50+). The pay-transparency draft would fold into this framework.
solved_today: Equality consultants (prices not found); templates.
software_solvable: Partly. Diagnosis data extraction, pay audit, plan templates and monitoring; the negotiation is human.
confidence: Medium on the friction; low on scale and cost.

title: Harassment protocols (all employers) and LGTBI measures and protocol (50+)
who:
- Harassment procedures: all employers, including micro firms and autónomo employers.
- LGTBI measures: firms with more than 50 workers.
where: National.
reality: Micro firms often lack any written harassment procedure. Firms over 50 had to negotiate LGTBI measures within 3 to 6 months of October 2024, or apply the decree's default measures. Complaint handling is rare but high-stakes when it happens.
evidence:
- LO 10/2022 art. 12 — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/lo/2022/09/06/10).
- RD 1026/2024 (in force 10 Oct 2024; commission within 3 or 6 months; protocol mandatory) — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2024/10/08/1026).
- ITSS LGTBI campaign 2025: 196 actions, 101 requirements — [El Derecho/EP, 7 Oct 2026](https://elderecho.com/?p=489934).
- RD 723/2026 requires informing workers about the harassment protocol and LGTBI measures — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2026/09/09/723).
scale: All employers for harassment procedures; 50+ firms for LGTBI measures.
cost_impact: Low inspection intensity so far (196 actions); reputational and litigation risk in individual cases.
driver_status: LO 10/2022 (in force); RD 1026/2024 (in force; deadlines passed in early 2025).
solved_today: Consultancy templates and gestoría packs (prices not found).
software_solvable: Partly. Protocol generation, training records, confidential complaint intake and case management.
confidence: Medium on obligations; low on how acute the pain is.

title: Internal whistleblowing channel (Ley 2/2023, 50+)
who: Private employers with 50+ workers; regulated entities of any size.
where: National.
reality: The firm keeps a channel and a named, independent system manager notified to the authority, and handles the occasional report under confidentiality and anti-retaliation rules.
evidence: Threshold, 1 Dec 2023 deadline for those with 249 or fewer workers, and fines up to €1M for legal persons — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2023/02/20/2).
scale: All 50+ employers (count not found).
cost_impact: High theoretical fines; enforcement evidence not found.
driver_status: Ley 2/2023, **in force**; deadlines passed.
solved_today: Whistleblowing-channel SaaS and law-firm services (prices not found).
software_solvable: Yes, and already commoditised.
confidence: High on rules; low on pain intensity (see Noise).

title: Occupational risk prevention (PRL), SPA dependence and heat-stress duties
who:
- All employers from the first worker.
- Micro firms with up to 10 workers, or up to 25 with one workplace, may self-manage prevention, but not health surveillance.
- Construction, agriculture and outdoor work are most exposed to heat.
where: National. Heat plans matter most in Andalucía (Sevilla, Córdoba), Murcia, Extremadura and Valencia (inference).
reality:
- The owner signs an SPA contract, receives a generic risk assessment and schedules medical exams.
- Each summer the ITSS e-mails heat-protocol reminders.
- Climate emergencies trigger the 4-day paid leave.
evidence:
- RD 39/1997 arts. 10–11 — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1997-1853).
- Plan Estival 2026 (9 Jun 2026), ITSS e-communications, RDL 8/2024 4-day leave — [Grant Thornton, Jun 2026](https://www.grantthornton.es/contentassets/4730b6c010d04ea29770da8a29bc5b94/labour-newsjunio-retos-aun-pendientes-y-nuevos-limites-en-materia-laboralgrant-thornton.pdf).
- 76 immediate stoppages in 2025 — [El Derecho/EP, 7 Oct 2026](https://elderecho.com/?p=489934).
- PRL is mandatory from the first worker — [Gestoria247, 7 Sep 2026](https://gestoria247.com/blog/cuanto-cuesta-un-trabajador-a-la-empresa-2026).
scale: All employers (about 1.35M).
cost_impact: SPA prices not found. Sources only say "más costes de prevención" (plus prevention costs) — [Billeo, 22 Jun 2026](https://www.billeo.es/blog/cuanto-te-cuesta-de-verdad-contratar-a-tu-primer-empleado).
driver_status: Ley 31/1995, RD 39/1997 and RDL 8/2024: **in force**. A broader PRL reform was not verified.
solved_today: SPA contracts (Quirónprevención, Cualtis, Preving and others; prices not found) or employer self-management for micro firms.
software_solvable: Partly. Risk assessment, training records, heat-alert protocols and SPA document management; health surveillance needs medical services.
confidence: Medium on obligations; low on cost data.

title: Payroll administration complexity and gestoría dependence
who: Micro and small employers and autónomo employers (outsourced payroll); gestorías and asesorías laborales as intermediaries.
where: National. Convenios are often provincial, so the work is province-specific (e.g., Barcelona, Madrid, Valencia, Sevilla, Bizkaia).
reality: The monthly cycle runs: gather incidents (absences, overtime, IT) → gestoría calculates payslips under the applicable convenio → Social Security filings through RED/SILTRA → contracts on Contrat@ → corrections whenever rules change mid-year.
evidence:
- Gestoría prices: €20 per worker per month and minimum €250 a month — [PayFit, 17 Jun 2026](https://payfit.com/es/contenido-practico/software-de-nominas-vs-asesor-laboral/); €20 per payslip, from €15 at volume — [Billeo, 22 Jun 2026](https://www.billeo.es/blog/cuanto-te-cuesta-de-verdad-contratar-a-tu-primer-empleado); from €49 a month for 2 workers — [Gestoria247, 7 Sep 2026](https://gestoria247.com/blog/cuanto-cuesta-un-trabajador-a-la-empresa-2026).
- Rule churn: retroactive SMI — [PwC](https://periscopiofiscalylegal.pwc.es/se-fija-la-cuantia-del-smi-el-problema-ahora-es-como-aplicarlo/); 2026 rate changes and correcting January–March filings — [CopilotGestoria](https://copilotgestoria.com/blog/cuota-solidaridad-2026-calcular-nomina-tramos-ejemplos-guia-gestorias); RED 8/2026 — [RRHH Digital, 22 Jul 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/legal/799952/la-tgss-cambia-el-criterio-la-compensacion-por-falta-de-preaviso-en-el-despido-objetivo-ya-cotiza/); convenio-specific rulings on shifts and holidays — [Grant Thornton, Jun 2026](https://www.grantthornton.es/contentassets/4730b6c010d04ea29770da8a29bc5b94/labour-newsjunio-retos-aun-pendientes-y-nuevos-limites-en-materia-laboralgrant-thornton.pdf).
scale: All employers that outsource payroll (count of gestoría clients not found).
cost_impact: About €900–1,200 a year for a 5-person firm at €15–20 per payslip (my inference); error and surcharge risk.
driver_status: LGSS, the annual contribution order, convenios and TGSS bulletins: **in force and continuously changing**.
solved_today:
- Gestorías on a3innuva and similar engines (Sesame integrates with a3innuva — [Sesame](https://www.sesamehr.es/precios/)).
- PayFit software; complaints about ticket-only support — [Trustpilot](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/payfit.com).
software_solvable: Yes or partly. Rules engines, convenio tables and change alerts for gestorías; automated incident capture from SMEs.
confidence: Medium. Prices come from three vendor sources, broadly consistent.

title: Leave and permit entitlement tracking (19-week birth leave, per-event care leave, force-majeure and climate leave)
who: All employers. The pain is hardest for micro firms where one absence matters and for shift-based sectors.
where: National.
evidence:
- RDL 9/2025 — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rdl/2025/07/29/9).
- TS 753/2026 (25 Sep 2026) — [RRHH Digital, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/legal/804055/el-tribunal-supremo-confirma-que-el-permiso-por-cuidados-familiares-no-tiene-un-limite-anual-de-cinco-dias/).
- Shift-staff leave counted on the real shift (TS, 27 May 2026) and RDL 8/2024 — [Grant Thornton, Jun 2026](https://www.grantthornton.es/contentassets/4730b6c010d04ea29770da8a29bc5b94/labour-newsjunio-retos-aun-pendientes-y-nuevos-limites-en-materia-laboralgrant-thornton.pdf).
- A Supreme Court doctrine on the 8-week parental leave and a warning on force-majeure leave — [RRHH Digital, 1 Apr 2026 and 13 May 2026](https://www.rrhhdigital.com/secciones/legal/792157/el-tribunal-supremo-fija-doctrina-sobre-el-permiso-parental-semanas-completas-si-perdida-de-vacaciones-no/) (headlines).
scale: All workers with family-care events (not quantified).
cost_impact: Mis-applied caps lead to claims and conflicts (not quantified).
driver_status: ET arts. 37 and 48; RDL 5/2023, 8/2024 and 9/2025; TS case law 2026: **in force**.
solved_today: HR suites with leave modules (Sesame, Factorial, Woffu) and gestorías.
software_solvable: Yes. A per-event entitlement engine kept current with case law.

title: FUNDAE training-credit bureaucracy and under-use
who: Micro and small firms, which have small credits and high administrative overhead.
where: National.
reality: Firms have a training credit, financed by the 0.60% vocational-training contribution, that they can recover through contribution rebates. Using it requires notifying courses, certifying and justifying costs, so many don't bother or delegate it to training providers.
evidence:
- 290,747 companies using their credit (Oct 2026); new 2026 cost-justification application and guides (22 Oct 2026) — [FUNDAE](https://www.fundae.es/).
- Vocational-training contribution: 0.60% employer + 0.10% worker — [Seguridad Social](https://www.seg-social.es/wps/portal/wss/internet/Trabajadores/CotizacionRecaudacionTrabajadores/36537).
scale: About 290k users vs about 1.35M employers, roughly 21% usage (my inference; bases differ).
cost_impact: Unused training credit (not quantified).
driver_status: Ley 30/2015 (in force; not re-verified here). Overlaps with the subsidies researcher.
solved_today: Training companies acting as "entidad organizadora" (organising entity) handle the paperwork, often bundled with the course (prices not found).
software_solvable: Partly. Credit tracking, course notification and justification workflows.

title: HR and payroll software that fits micro firms poorly (minimum seats, support, gestoría hand-off)
who: Micro firms (under 10), autónomo employers and small firms (10–49).
where: National.
reality: The leading suites price per employee with minimums or annual commitments and leave payroll to the gestoría. Support is often ticket-only. Micro owners end up with paper, WhatsApp and a gestoría.
evidence:
- Sesame 15-employee minimum — [Sesame](https://www.sesamehr.es/precios/).
- Woffu Lite for 10 or fewer employees from €1.5, other plans annual-only — [Woffu](https://www.woffu.com/es/precios).
- Factorial: slow support, unannounced changes — [Trustpilot](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/factorialhr.com).
- PayFit: ticket-only support — [Trustpilot](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/payfit.com).
scale: Micro firms are the bulk of employers (count not retrieved here).
cost_impact: €1.5–9 per employee per month list prices; switching friction after annual commitments (e.g., a Sesame reviewer: "En cuanto pase el año me cambio" — as soon as the year is up I'm switching — [Trustpilot](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/sesamehr.es), tiny sample).
driver_status: Market structure, ongoing.
solved_today: Woffu Lite, Factorial, Sesame, PayFit and gestorías.
software_solvable: Yes. This is a product-design and pricing gap.

title: Regulatory whiplash and election-driven uncertainty
who: All employers and their advisers.
where: National.
evidence:
- 37.5-hour bill rejected 10 Sep 2025 — [Periódico de Ibiza, 11 Sep 2025](https://www.periodicodeibiza.es/noticias/nacional/2025/09/11/2467647/congreso-tumba-reduccion-jornada-laboral-prosperar-veto-vox-junts.html).
- Registro decree postponed — [RegistraHora](https://www.registrahora.es/noticias/registro-horario-digital-aplazado-septiembre-2026).
- Pay transparency overdue — [Que.es, 9 Jun 2026](https://www.que.es/2026/06/09/transparencia-salarial-ofertas-pospuesta/).
- RD 723/2026 four years late (Directive deadline 2022) — [Law&Trends, 2 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/laboral/el-colegio-de-graduados-sociales-de-barcelona-girona-y-lleida-alerta-del-impacto-del-rd-723-2026-en-la-gestion-y-el-1.html).
- SMI lateness reduces legal certainty — [PwC](https://periscopiofiscalylegal.pwc.es/se-fija-la-cuantia-del-smi-el-problema-ahora-es-como-aplicarlo/).
- Elections called — [Euronews, 6 Oct 2026](https://es.euronews.com/2026/10/06/calendario-elecciones-generales-29n-fechas-clave-voto-correo-campana).
scale: Universal.
cost_impact: Wasted preparation or late compliance; adviser workload — ASNALA asks for "periodos de transición razonables" (reasonable transition periods) — [Law&Trends, 14 Oct 2026](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/abogacia/ana-gomez-presidenta-de-asnala-es-necesario-recuperar-el-dialogo-social-para-resolver-los-grandes-problemas-del-1.html).
driver_status: Political fragmentation; Cortes dissolved 6 Oct 2026; elections 29 Nov 2026.
solved_today: Adviser newsletters (Grant Thornton, PwC), Colegio de Graduados Sociales training (e.g., Madrid sessions on transparency and absenteeism — [Law&Trends](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/laboral/ley-de-transparencia-y-absentismo-laboral-proximos-encuentros-formativos-del-colegio-de-graduados-sociales-de-madrid-1.html), headline).
software_solvable: Partly. A regulatory-change tracker mapped to each firm's size, sector and convenio, with checklists.

title: Mandatory pre-litigation negotiation (MASC): proving the attempt, inadmission risk and delay
who: all sectors. Autónomos, micro, small and medium firms, and startups, both as claimants (unpaid invoices, supplier or customer contract claims, lease claims) and as recipients of MASC invitations.
where: national, with **city-specific admissibility criteria** (Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Valencia, Sevilla, Cádiz, Zaragoza, Teruel, Barcelona, Madrid).
reality: before suing, the business must send a provable negotiation request (burofax, certified email, mediator or conciliation), wait 30 days to 3 months, and attach proof plus a description to the claim. If the court considers the proof inadequate, the claim is inadmitted and the process restarts. Incoming invitations must be answered, or the business risks a costs penalty.
evidence:
- In force since 3 Apr 2025 — [Economist & Jurist, 3 Apr 2025](https://www.economistjurist.es/?p=223479)
- Refusing MASC counts against the refuser on costs — [Osborne Clarke, 20 Jan 2025](https://www.osborneclarke.com/es/insights/ley-organica-12025-cambios-en-la-jurisdiccion-civil-nueva-estructura-de-la-oficina)
- ICAM survey (1,164 lawyers): 49.3% had problems proving the attempt; 71.7% see inconsistent interpretation. No official channel or registry; private solutions' validity "not guaranteed in advance" — [Moncloa.com, 6 Oct 2026](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/10/06/requisito-masc-lo-1-2025-juzgados-3443197) (single source for the survey)
- Divergent local rules (e.g. WhatsApp and SMS excluded in Sevilla and Cádiz; MASC required in monitorio in Las Palmas; omission incurable in Valencia) — [Martínez Bernabéu, 7 May 2025](https://martinezbernabeu-abogados.com/acuerdos-de-jueces-y-laj-sobre-la-lo-1-2025-y-los-masc-2/)
- Adds 30–90 days — [Legal Pigeon, 7 May 2026](https://www.legalpigeon.com/masc-un-ano-despues-mediacion-ley-1-2025/) (vendor)
- MASC "generally not free"; ICAM asks for it to become voluntary — [ICAM, 6 Apr 2026](https://web.icam.es/reforma-ley-1-2025-balance-icam/)
scale: applies to most of the 3,287,980 civil cases filed in 2025 — [CGPJ, 30 Mar 2026](https://www.poderjudicial.es/cgpj/es/Poder-Judicial/En-Portada/Los-organos-judiciales-recibieron-en-2025-un-3-2---menos-asuntos-que-el-ano-anterior-y-aumentaron-en-un-2---su-capacidad-de-resolucion). The SME share is not quantified. Pre-deadline rush: about 90,000 claims queued in Madrid and Barcelona — [Economist & Jurist, 3 Apr 2025](https://www.economistjurist.es/?p=223479)
cost_impact: private certified MASC €110–150 + VAT per file, plus €100–120 + VAT per mediation session — [Moncloa.com](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/10/06/requisito-masc-lo-1-2025-juzgados-3443197). Free LAJ conciliation takes about 6 months. Inadmission means repeating the whole step. Penalty risk on costs.
driver_status: LO 1/2025 (arts. 5, 7, 10; additional provision 3 on official MASC services). **In force; official channel still pending; Supreme Court has not unified the case law** (Oct 2026).
solved_today: lawyers sending burofax or buromail; mediators registered with the Ministry of Justice; notarial demands; online MASC platforms (Legal Pigeon: certificate in under 30 days, no public prices; an unnamed eIDAS platform at €110 + VAT). Documented complaints: inconsistent acceptance by courts; ICAM calls the requirement disproportionate; no supplier can guarantee court acceptance.
software_solvable: **yes.** Certified electronic delivery, timers for waiting periods, a city-aware admissibility checklist, a negotiation log and an automatic evidence pack are all workflow and document problems.

title: Slow, congested civil courts and enforcement backlog (winning does not mean collecting)
who: all sectors and sizes, as creditors, landlords, buyers and sellers.
where: national. Worst: Murcia, Madrid, Sevilla. Middle: Málaga, Palma, Bilbao, Alicante, Barcelona, A Coruña, Las Palmas, Valencia. Best: Vigo/Pontevedra, Valladolid, Zaragoza.
reality: an ordinary civil claim takes about 11 months at first instance and another 9–10 months on appeal. The firm then joins an enforcement queue of more than a million files. Meanwhile it carries the receivable, the dispute and legal fees. The court reorganisation added misrouted filings and LexNET returns.
evidence:
- Civil first-instance duration 10.3 → 11.0 months; appeals 8.3 → 9.6 months — [CGPJ Indicadores Anual 2025, Mar 2026](https://www.poderjudicial.es/stfls/SALA%20DE%20PRENSA/DOCUMENTOS%20DE%20INTERES/Indicadores%20a%20Nivel%20Nacional%20-%20Anual%202025.pdf)
- 1,384,591 enforcement files pending in first-instance courts; civil pendency rate Madrid 1.02 vs Zaragoza 0.52 — [CGPJ Anual 2025 PDF, Mar 2026](https://www.poderjudicial.es/stfls/SALA%20DE%20PRENSA/DOCUMENTOS%20DE%20INTERES/Datos%20Nacionales%20Anual%202025.pdf)
- Madrid civil pending +15.4% to 557,824 (Q3 2025) — [CGPJ Madrid, 17 Dec 2025](https://www.poderjudicial.es/portal/site/cgpj/menuitem.65d2c4456b6ddb628e635fc1dc432ea0/?vgnextoid=d12a6a4253b2b910VgnVCM1000004648ac0aRCRD&vgnextchannel=0470825dd79f0310VgnVCM1000006f48ac0aRCRD&vgnextfmt=default&vgnextlocale=es&perfil=1)
- LexNET automatic returns, duplicate inboxes, staff shortages — [ICAM, 6 Apr 2026](https://web.icam.es/reforma-ley-1-2025-balance-icam/)
scale: 2,672,464 civil cases pending nationwide at end-2025 — [CGPJ, 30 Mar 2026](https://www.poderjudicial.es/cgpj/es/Poder-Judicial/En-Portada/Los-organos-judiciales-recibieron-en-2025-un-3-2---menos-asuntos-que-el-ano-anterior-y-aumentaron-en-un-2---su-capacidad-de-resolucion)
cost_impact: months of locked-up working capital; legal fees (not quantified); court fees for legal persons (2012 schedule €100–€1,200 fixed plus variable; current amounts unverified) — [BOE Ley 10/2012](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2012/11/20/10)
driver_status: structural shortage of judges and staff, plus the LO 1/2025 reorganisation into tribunales de instancia. **Ongoing.**
solved_today: lawyers and procuradores; debt-collection agencies and legal-expenses insurance (covered by other researchers). No prices collected here.
software_solvable: **partly.** Software cannot speed courts up. It can help with settlement (MASC offers), deciding which forum to use or whether to sue at all, and tracking enforcement.

title: Congested commercial courts, the venue for partner, IP, unfair-competition and transport disputes
who: small and medium firms and startups in partner or shareholder disputes, IP or unfair-competition conflicts, or transport claims. Also insolvency, which is out of scope here.
where: national; one or more commercial courts per province, mainly in the big cities. City durations not available.
reality: corporate and IP disputes go to commercial courts whose intake rose sharply in 2025 while their resolution rate stayed below 1, so backlogs are growing.
evidence: 119,564 new cases (+18.6%), 94,963 pending (+11.4%), resolution rate 0.92, congestion 1.87, 34,588 enforcement files pending — [CGPJ Anual 2025 PDF, Mar 2026](https://www.poderjudicial.es/stfls/SALA%20DE%20PRENSA/DOCUMENTOS%20DE%20INTERES/Datos%20Nacionales%20Anual%202025.pdf). Single statistical source; no breakdown by case type.
scale: 121 courts. The share of partner, IP and unfair-competition cases is unknown and probably smaller than insolvency (inference).
cost_impact: not quantified.
driver_status: rising insolvency (personal insolvency in particular, another researcher's scope) crowding the same courts. **Ongoing.**
solved_today: corporate lawyers; mediation and arbitration (no data); shareholder agreements.
software_solvable: **partly.** Shareholder-agreement and cap-table tools prevent some disputes; litigation itself is not software-solvable.
confidence: medium (volume growth is solid; the attribution to SME dispute types is weak)

title: Cost and cost-risk of litigating (court fees for companies, paid MASC, costs penalty for refusing to negotiate)
who: all sectors. Companies (sociedades) pay court fees; autónomos as natural persons are exempt (2015 reform, **unverified current text**).
where: national.
reality: a company chasing a debt above €2,000 faces court fees, lawyer and procurador fees, and now MASC costs. Refusing an opponent's negotiation proposal can backfire on costs if the judgment ends up close to that proposal.
evidence:
- 2012 fee schedule: verbal €150, ordinario €300, monitorio €100, appeal €800, cassation €1,200, plus 0.5% variable (max €10,000); claims of €2,000 or less exempt; 60% refund on settlement. **Original text, partly annulled later** — [BOE Ley 10/2012](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2012/11/20/10)
- Costs exoneration or moderation linked to rejected offers; "abuso del servicio público de justicia" — [Osborne Clarke, 20 Jan 2025](https://www.osborneclarke.com/es/insights/ley-organica-12025-cambios-en-la-jurisdiccion-civil-nueva-estructura-de-la-oficina)
- MASC prices €110–150 + VAT — [Moncloa.com, 6 Oct 2026](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/10/06/requisito-masc-lo-1-2025-juzgados-3443197)
- ICAM opposes the costs consequence — [ICAM, 6 Apr 2026](https://web.icam.es/reforma-ley-1-2025-balance-icam/)
scale: not quantified.
cost_impact: hundreds to thousands of euros per claim before lawyer fees (not quantified).
driver_status: Ley 10/2012 (partly annulled by STC 140/2016; natural persons exempted by RDL 1/2015) and LO 1/2025 costs rules. **In force; current fee amounts need verification.**
solved_today: legal-expenses insurance (another researcher's scope), collection agencies, lawyers on success fees. No prices collected.
software_solvable: **partly.** A litigation cost and recovery estimator plus a MASC offer engine can steer decisions; the costs themselves stay.

title: Complaint-driven data-protection exposure (record AEPD complaints, slow procedures)
who: every business handling personal data, all sizes; most exposed are B2C retail, hospitality, health, property management and online services.
where: national (AEPD); Catalonia and the Basque Country also have regional authorities for the public sector (not covered).
reality: a customer, neighbour or ex-employee files a complaint and the SME receives an AEPD information request or a sanction procedure that drags on for months. Appeals rarely succeed.
evidence:
- 30,931 complaints (+64%); resolution rate 76%; 23,361 resolved — [Legal Today, 7 May 2026](https://www.legaltoday.com/actualidad-juridica/noticias-de-derecho/la-aepd-recibio-mas-de-30-000-reclamaciones-en-2025-un-64-mas-que-el-ano-anterior-2026-05-07/)
- Procedures +45% longer; 325 fines; commerce, transport and hospitality fines €10.76M (+1,653%) — [BDO, May 2026](https://es-admin.bdo.global/getattachment/29fdc619-d1c8-40fd-af4f-57757c6ceb21/AEPD-2025.pdf?lang=es-ES)
- 76% of Audiencia Nacional appeals inadmitted or dismissed — [Legal Today](https://www.legaltoday.com/actualidad-juridica/noticias-de-derecho/la-aepd-recibio-mas-de-30-000-reclamaciones-en-2025-un-64-mas-que-el-ano-anterior-2026-05-07/)
scale: 30,931 complaints a year; 126,176 notified DPOs (116,007 private) — [Legal Today](https://www.legaltoday.com/actualidad-juridica/noticias-de-derecho/la-aepd-recibio-mas-de-30-000-reclamaciones-en-2025-un-64-mas-que-el-ano-anterior-2026-05-07/)
cost_impact: SME fines are usually €600–€3,000 — [Lawwwing, 13 Jul 2026](https://lawwwing.com/aepd-sanciones-2025/). The headline average of about €148k is driven by large firms — [BDO](https://es-admin.bdo.global/getattachment/29fdc619-d1c8-40fd-af4f-57757c6ceb21/AEPD-2025.pdf?lang=es-ES). Plus lawyer time (not quantified).
driver_status: GDPR and LOPDGDD (LO 3/2018). **In force; enforcement volume rising.**
solved_today: AEPD free tools (Facilita 51,979 accesses, Gestiona RGPD 29,304); outsourced consultancies (PymeLegal claims over 5,000 clients, no public prices); SaaS (Lawwwing €9.9–€79/month).
software_solvable: **partly.** Records, policies and procedures for responding to complaints and rights requests can be automated; behaviour and physical setups cannot.

title: CCTV / video-surveillance non-compliance (signs, camera angle, retention, staff monitoring)
who: shops, bars and restaurants, workshops, gyms, offices, residential-community administrators. Autónomos to small firms.
where: national.
reality: cameras are installed by security firms or the owner, often filming the street or a neighbour, with no or an outdated sign, footage kept indefinitely and staff recorded without notice. A neighbour or employee complains.
evidence:
- Video surveillance is the #2 complaint area with 4,050 complaints (+19%) — [BDO, May 2026](https://es-admin.bdo.global/getattachment/29fdc619-d1c8-40fd-af4f-57757c6ceb21/AEPD-2025.pdf?lang=es-ES)
- The most common area of finished procedures (81) — [Legal Today, 7 May 2026](https://www.legaltoday.com/actualidad-juridica/noticias-de-derecho/la-aepd-recibio-mas-de-30-000-reclamaciones-en-2025-un-64-mas-que-el-ano-anterior-2026-05-07/)
- Typical cases: misaimed cameras or no sign — [WebLegal, 31 Jul 2026](https://weblegal.ai/es/blog/multas-aepd-donde-caen-los-48-millones/)
- "Cámaras mal instaladas" listed as an everyday error — [PymeLegal, 22 May 2026](https://www.pymelegal.es/noticias/aepd/las-sanciones-rgpd-mas-altas-en-espana-en-2025-la-aepd-endurece-su-actuacion-ante-brechas-de-seguridad-y-tratamientos-ilicitos)
- AEPD guide (Feb 2025): signs, 30-day retention, record of processing — [PymeLegal, 17 Mar 2025](https://www.pymelegal.es/noticias/aepd/nueva-guia-sobre-el-uso-de-videocamaras-para-seguridad-y-otras-finalidades)
scale: 4,050 complaints in 2025 (see above).
cost_impact: typical fine amounts for small businesses **not found** (gap).
driver_status: GDPR, LOPDGDD art. 22, AEPD video-surveillance guide (updated Feb 2025). **In force.**
solved_today: security installers' templates, LOPD consultancies, the AEPD guide. No prices collected.
software_solvable: **partly.** A guided "camera compliance kit" (sign generator, notice to staff, retention settings check, record entry) is software; correcting camera angles is physical.

title: Website legal compliance (cookies, privacy policy, legal notice under the e-commerce law LSSI)
who: every business with a website or online shop; startups. All sizes.
where: national.
reality: website templates and agencies leave non-technical cookies firing before consent, reject buttons that do not work, and privacy policies that are missing or identify the wrong company. Competitors or users complain to the AEPD.
evidence:
- 2025 fines (cookies, missing privacy policy, wrong controller): MaxPower €1,600; Amor Ideal €600; Inmo-master €1,000; Wallapop €3,000; El Debate €3,000 — [Lawwwing, 13 Jul 2026](https://lawwwing.com/aepd-sanciones-2025/)
- Internet services: >5,100 complaints (+63%); fines €11.38M — [BDO](https://es-admin.bdo.global/getattachment/29fdc619-d1c8-40fd-af4f-57757c6ceb21/AEPD-2025.pdf?lang=es-ES)
- The EU cookie-relief proposal (Digital Omnibus) is still in European Parliament committee — [OEIL 2025/0360(COD)](https://oeil.europarl.europa.eu/oeil/en/procedure-file?reference=2025/0360(COD))
scale: not quantified (the number of SME websites is not sourced).
cost_impact: €600–€3,000 per fine (above).
driver_status: LSSI art. 22.2 (cookies), GDPR arts. 13–14 and AEPD cookie guidance. **In force; EU simplification is only a draft.**
solved_today: consent-management platforms, e.g. Cookiebot (free to 50 subpages, then €7–€90/month) — [Cookiebot](https://www.cookiebot.com/en/pricing/); Lawwwing (€9.9–€79/month including legal texts) — [Lawwwing](https://lawwwing.com/precios/). The fines themselves document misconfigured banners ("rechazo ineficaz", ineffective reject option).
software_solvable: **yes, and largely already solved cheaply.** The remaining gap is configuration audits and monitoring.

title: Everyday data slips (emails without BCC, WhatsApp with clients or staff, internal snooping, employee data)
who: all sectors; especially autónomos and micro firms, clubs and event organisers, clinics, property managers.
where: national.
reality: staff send group emails with every address visible, use personal WhatsApp groups for customers or employees, or look up records without need. One annoyed recipient files a complaint.
evidence:
- Trueba Sport fined €1,200 for an email to more than 300 people without BCC — [Lawwwing, 13 Jul 2026](https://lawwwing.com/aepd-sanciones-2025/)
- "Uso indebido de WhatsApp" and unauthorised internal access listed as common errors; "Relaciones laborales" is the #7 complaint area — [PymeLegal, 22 May 2026](https://www.pymelegal.es/noticias/aepd/las-sanciones-rgpd-mas-altas-en-espana-en-2025-la-aepd-endurece-su-actuacion-ante-brechas-de-seguridad-y-tratamientos-ilicitos)
scale: not quantified.
cost_impact: around €1,000-level fines (single example).
driver_status: GDPR art. 5.1.f (confidentiality). **In force.**
solved_today: training from LOPD consultancies; AEPD "Gestiona RGPD" (29,304 accesses) — [Legal Today](https://www.legaltoday.com/actualidad-juridica/noticias-de-derecho/la-aepd-recibio-mas-de-30-000-reclamaciones-en-2025-un-64-mas-que-el-ano-anterior-2026-05-07/). No prices.
software_solvable: **partly.** Email BCC enforcement, compliant business messaging and micro-training help, but behaviour drives the risk.

title: Personal-data breaches and security incidents leading to AEPD procedures
who: any business holding customer or patient data, especially e-commerce, health, retail and SaaS startups. Small to medium firms.
where: national.
reality: ransomware, misconfigured databases or lost devices trigger the 72-hour notification duty. Missing documentation of security measures turns an incident into a fine.
evidence:
- Breach-related procedures 30 → 77 (+157%), worth €19.84M (about 40% of all fines) — [Legal Today, 7 May 2026](https://www.legaltoday.com/actualidad-juridica/noticias-de-derecho/la-aepd-recibio-mas-de-30-000-reclamaciones-en-2025-un-64-mas-que-el-ano-anterior-2026-05-07/)
- GDPR arts. 5.1.f + 32 appear in at least 7 of the 12 fines above €1M — [BDO, May 2026](https://es-admin.bdo.global/getattachment/29fdc619-d1c8-40fd-af4f-57757c6ceb21/AEPD-2025.pdf?lang=es-ES)
- Comunica-Brecha tool: 15,214 accesses in 2025 — [Legal Today](https://www.legaltoday.com/actualidad-juridica/noticias-de-derecho/la-aepd-recibio-mas-de-30-000-reclamaciones-en-2025-un-64-mas-que-el-ano-anterior-2026-05-07/)
scale: number of breach notifications not obtained.
cost_impact: large fines are concentrated in big firms; SME breach fines not quantified.
driver_status: GDPR arts. 32–34. **In force.**
solved_today: AEPD's free Comunica-Brecha and Asesora-Brecha; managed security providers and cyber insurance (other researchers). No prices collected.
software_solvable: **partly.** An incident-response playbook, 72-hour clock, notification drafting and a register of security measures are software; prevention needs security services.

title: Opaque outsourced data-protection compliance market
who: autónomos and micro and small firms buying "adaptación LOPD/RGPD" or an outsourced DPO.
where: national.
reality: SMEs buy one-off document packs or subscriptions from consultancies, often with no published price and unclear deliverables. Many rely on the AEPD's free tools instead.
evidence:
- PymeLegal claims over 5,000 companies or clients and 500 partners, with no public price list (accessed 23 Oct 2026) — [PymeLegal](https://www.pymelegal.es/)
- Heavy use of free AEPD tools (Facilita 51,979; Facilita Emprende 6,571) — [Legal Today, 7 May 2026](https://www.legaltoday.com/actualidad-juridica/noticias-de-derecho/la-aepd-recibio-mas-de-30-000-reclamaciones-en-2025-un-64-mas-que-el-ano-anterior-2026-05-07/)
- Self-serve SaaS prices €9.9–€79/month — [Lawwwing](https://lawwwing.com/precios/)
scale: 116,007 private-sector DPOs notified (a proxy for organisations with a formal DPO) — [Legal Today](https://www.legaltoday.com/actualidad-juridica/noticias-de-derecho/la-aepd-recibio-mas-de-30-000-reclamaciones-en-2025-un-64-mas-que-el-ano-anterior-2026-05-07/)
cost_impact: **not quantified.** Consultancy prices not found; complaints and scams (fake inspectors, FUNDAE-funded "LOPD gratis") not verified.
driver_status: GDPR and LOPDGDD. **Mature market.**
solved_today: consultancies, gestorías bundling LOPD, SaaS, AEPD free tools.
software_solvable: **partly.** A transparent, guided self-service product with optional expert review is feasible, but it competes with free AEPD tools and cheap SaaS.

title: Commercial phone calls: mandatory 400 prefix (blocking since 17 Oct 2026), consent, and void contracts
who: businesses that sell by phone: energy and telecom resellers and agents, insurance agents and brokers, solar and efficiency installers, estate agencies, training providers, B2B sales teams and outsourced call centres. All sizes.
where: national.
reality: sales calls from mobiles or geographic numbers are now blocked by operators. The firm must get 400 numbers through its operator and separate sales lines from customer-service lines (800/900 or geographic). It must also prove recent express consent, or any contract signed on the call is void.
evidence:
- All commercial calls must use 400 numbers, with blocking from October; 192M calls and 17M SMS blocked since March 2025 — [La Moncloa, 16 Apr 2026](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/serviciosdeprensa/notasprensa/transformacion-digital-y-funcion-publica/Paginas/2026/160426-prefijo-400-llamadas-comerciales.aspx)
- Start date 17 Oct 2026; 300M calls blocked by August — [ESdiario, 10 Aug 2026](https://www.esdiario.com/economia/260810/195137/gobierno-obligara-17-octubre-prefijo-400-llamadas-comerciales.html)
- LGTel serious infringement €50,001–€2,000,000; B2B coverage unclear — [Aircall, 2 Sep 2026](https://aircall.io/es/blog/prefijo-400-llamadas-comerciales/) (vendor; single source for the fine range)
- Ley 10/2025 art. 16.3–16.4 (separate code, operator blocking) and TRLGDCU art. 62.1 (contracts from calls breaching the rules presumed without consent and void; consent must be express and within 2 years) — [BOE, 27 Dec 2025](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2025/12/26/10)
scale: number of affected SMEs not quantified. The volume of blocked calls (300M) shows the scale of the traffic being targeted.
cost_impact: blocked outbound campaigns from day one; void contracts (lost revenue and refunds); fines up to €2M (vendor claim).
driver_status: Ley 10/2025 + Ministry of Digital Transformation resolution (in force 17 Apr 2026) + LGTel 11/2022 art. 66.1 + LOPDGDD art. 23 (advertising exclusion lists). **In force; blocking live since 17 Oct 2026.** Whether autónomos and B2B calls are covered is **unverified**.
solved_today: operators provide 400 ranges (assigned by the CNMC); cloud telephony vendors (Aircall); Lista Robinson checks — [Lista Robinson](https://www.listarobinson.es/). Prices not collected.
software_solvable: **yes.** A dialer compliance layer (400 numbering, consent ledger with a 2-year expiry, Robinson check, call-purpose tagging) fits as a SaaS add-on.
confidence: high on the rule and dates; medium on scope (B2B, autónomos)

title: New consumer-law duties for every B2C business (Ley 10/2025 amendments to the consumer law, TRLGDCU)
who: all B2C businesses of every size (retail, hospitality, personal services, gyms, academies, clinics, e-commerce, subscription startups).
where: national, plus regional consumer laws and inspection.
reality: complaints arriving by email, phone, counter or WhatsApp must get a reference key and written receipt and be answered within 15 days. Prices must show every fee. Fixed-term or auto-renewing contracts need 15 days' notice before the opt-out deadline. Websites must say whether reviews are verified. Few small firms log any of this.
evidence:
- TRLGDCU art. 21.2–21.3 (ID key, receipt, standard-cost phone line, answer within a maximum of 15 days); art. 20.1.c (full final price including management fees); art. 97.1.p (15 days' renewal notice); art. 20.4 (reviews); art. 62.1 (void phone contracts); in force the day after publication — [BOE, Ley 10/2025, 27 Dec 2025](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2025/12/26/10)
- Same points, with the renewal rule described for online subscriptions — [KPMG, Jan 2026](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/es/pdf/2026/01/legal-alert-regulacion-servicios-atencion-clientela-ley-10-2025.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf)
- Catalan consumer agency fines €10.5M in 2023 (+62%) — [Vozpópuli, 14 Mar 2024](https://www.vozpopuli.com/espana/cataluna/generalitat-cuadruplica-ano-multas-castellano-ya-recauda-30-veces-mas-que-en-2021.html)
scale: all B2C businesses. The count is not sourced here (see the macro researcher).
cost_impact: consumer-law sanctions (regional scales, not verified here); void contracts and refunds.
driver_status: Ley 10/2025, final provision 3 (amending RDLeg 1/2007). **In force since 28 Dec 2025.** Whether the 12-month adaptation period also covers these amendments is **unclear**.
solved_today: ad hoc email and Excel; helpdesk tools aimed at larger firms; lawyers updating terms and conditions. No SME-specific product or prices found.
software_solvable: **yes.** A complaints register with ID keys, receipts and a 15-day SLA, a renewal-notice scheduler, a price-display checker and a review-policy widget are all simple software.
confidence: high on the law; medium on how severe the pain is in practice

title: Customer-service quality regime for basic-service providers of any size and large firms (Ley 10/2025, deadline 28 Dec 2026)
who: small and medium internet and telecom providers, local water utilities, small electricity and gas retailers, bus and coach and ferry operators, postal and courier firms (regardless of size). Also large B2C firms (≥250 staff, or >€50M turnover, or >€43M balance sheet) and the SME contact centres they outsource to.
where: national. Co-official language duties apply in Catalonia, C. Valenciana, Baleares, País Vasco, Navarra and Galicia.
reality: a 30-person local internet provider or energy retailer must, by 28 Dec 2026, put a human on the phone for 95% of requests within 3 minutes, issue complaint keys, resolve complaints within 15 working days, measure all of this, and pay an ENAC-accredited auditor every year. Customers can also demand service in Catalan, Basque or Galician.
evidence:
- Scope, 3-minute rule, 15 working days, annual ENAC-accredited audit, co-official languages, 28 Dec 2026 deadline — [KPMG, Jan 2026](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/es/pdf/2026/01/legal-alert-regulacion-servicios-atencion-clientela-ley-10-2025.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf); [Sepín, 14 Jan 2026](https://blog.sepin.es/blog/2026/01/14/novedades-ley-10-2025-servicios-atencion-clientela/)
- Retailers below 5% market share exempt only from the 24/7 line and numbering rules (transitional provision 4) — [BOE, 27 Dec 2025](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2025/12/26/10)
- OCU says language costs will be passed on to consumers; FACUA notes offshore call centres lack co-official languages — [Forbes, 16 Oct 2025](https://forbes.es/?p=814900)
scale: number of small providers in scope not quantified (gap).
cost_impact: contact-centre staffing, annual audit fees (not quantified), consumer-law fines (up to €100,000 per infringement per a vendor, **unverified**) — [TÜV SÜD](https://www.tuvsud.com/es-es/servicios/sostenibilidad/soluciones-sostenibilidad-buen-gobierno/sostenibilidad-social/asesoramiento-cumplimiento-ley-servicio-atencion-cliente)
driver_status: Ley 10/2025 (arts. 2, 6–22, transitional provisions 1 and 4). **In force; adaptation deadline 28 Dec 2026 (upcoming).**
solved_today: big-company contact-centre suites; advisory and audit firms (TÜV SÜD, KPMG). No SME pricing found.
software_solvable: **yes (niche).** SLA monitoring, complaint-key issuing, multilingual routing and an audit-ready evidence pack for small providers.
confidence: high on the law; medium on the number of SMEs exposed

title: Online reviews: new authenticity duties and hostile or fake reviews
who: hospitality, retail, personal services, clinics, e-commerce. Autónomos to medium firms.
where: national.
reality: the business must say whether its reviews are verified and can now request removal of reviews from people who never bought. In practice, owners battle one-star attacks and fake reviews on platforms they do not control.
evidence:
- TRLGDCU art. 20.4 as amended: reviews must relate to purchase or use within 30 days; removal can be requested on proof of no purchase — [BOE, 27 Dec 2025](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2025/12/26/10)
- Described as an obligation to guarantee authenticity — [KPMG, Jan 2026](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/es/pdf/2026/01/legal-alert-regulacion-servicios-atencion-clientela-ley-10-2025.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf)
- **Fake-review extortion and defamation cases: not verified** (search budget exhausted).
scale: not quantified.
cost_impact: not quantified.
driver_status: Ley 10/2025, final provision 3 (art. 20.4 TRLGDCU). **In force since 28 Dec 2025.**
solved_today: platform reporting tools; reputation agencies. No prices verified.
software_solvable: **partly.** Collecting reviews tied to verified purchases and running a takedown-request workflow are software; platform cooperation is not.
confidence: medium on the rule; low on the size of the pain

title: Catalan-language obligations for signs, menus, labels, documents and service (Catalonia)
who: B2C businesses in Catalonia, especially restaurants and bars (about half of cases), shops, hairdressers and beauty salons, gyms, supermarkets, hotels and insurers. Autónomos to medium firms, plus national chains.
where: Catalonia (Barcelona, Girona, Tarragona, Lleida).
reality: a customer reports a Spanish-only sign, menu, price list or label to the Catalan consumer agency. The business receives a fine of a few hundred to a few thousand euros and has to redo its materials.
evidence:
- Complaints 206 (2021) → 456 (2022) → 1,873 (2023); 261 sanctions in 2023 — [3Cat, 16 Mar 2024](https://www.3cat.cat/3catinfo/es-multipliquen-per-quatre-les-denuncies-a-empreses-que-no-fan-servir-el-catala/noticia/3282394/)
- Fines collected €17,350 → €498,852 between 2021 and 2023 — [Vozpópuli, 14 Mar 2024](https://www.vozpopuli.com/espana/cataluna/generalitat-cuadruplica-ano-multas-castellano-ya-recauda-30-veces-mas-que-en-2021.html)
- Average fine €2,240, maximum €10,000; 7% of 5,406 complaints sanctioned (2012–2024); 1,250 cases in 2024; fixed information 29.9% and offers to buy 25.5% of sanctions — [NacióDigital, 23 Mar 2025](https://naciodigital.cat/societat/nomes-7-denuncies-vulnerar-drets-linguistics-consumidors-han-acabat-en-sancio.html)
- Legal basis: Codi de consum art. 128-1 — [BOE, Llei 22/2010](https://www.boe.es/eli/es-ct/l/2010/07/20/22)
scale: about 1,250–2,000 complaints a year; more than 600 against restaurants and bars in 2024 — [NacióDigital](https://naciodigital.cat/societat/nomes-7-denuncies-vulnerar-drets-linguistics-consumidors-han-acabat-en-sancio.html)
cost_impact: €600 (Macson store) to €7,500 (Carrefour, seen only in a search summary) per fine; reprinting signs and labels.
driver_status: Llei 22/2010 (Codi de consum de Catalunya) art. 128-1 and Llei 1/1998 de política lingüística (not re-verified). **In force; enforcement is complaint-driven and rising** (2025 data missing).
solved_today: manual translation, Catalan versions supplied by brands; no dedicated compliance tool or prices found.
software_solvable: **partly.** Most sanctions concern fixed written material (translation and checking of menus, signs, labels and templates). In-person service in Catalan cannot be automated.

title: Digital accessibility for e-commerce and covered services (EAA / Ley 11/2023)
who: e-commerce, banking and payments, passenger-transport ticketing, e-books, telecoms, and makers or sellers of covered products. Small and medium firms and startups. Micro-enterprises providing services are exempt.
where: national; enforcement by regional authorities.
reality: online shops with 10 or more staff must meet WCAG 2.1 AA from 28 Jun 2025 (existing services until 2030). Many buy an overlay widget whose legal effect is unclear, while no regional authority has yet reported enforcement.
evidence:
- Scope, micro exemption, 2030 transition, fines up to €30k / €90k / €1M, RD 143/2026 coordination unit, no enforcement reported — [RedInclusiva, 30 Jul 2026 (updated 30 Sep 2026)](https://redinclusiva.com/actualidad/ley-de-accesibilidad-de-productos-y-servicios-que-obliga-ya-a-webs-apps-y-comercios)
- Accede Me: more than 3,000 sites; legal-backing claims unverified; no public prices — [Accede Me](https://accedeme.com/)
scale: number of non-micro e-commerce firms not quantified.
cost_impact: Lawwwing WCAG module €28/month — [Lawwwing](https://lawwwing.com/precios/). Audit prices not public.
driver_status: Ley 11/2023 (transposing Directive 2019/882). **In force since 28 Jun 2025; transitional period to 2030; no enforcement reported.**
solved_today: overlay widgets, accessibility audits and remediation agencies.
software_solvable: **partly.** Automated scanning and reporting plus guided fixes help; full conformance needs development work.

title: AI Act literacy and transparency duties for SMEs using AI (chatbots, AI-generated content), plus Spain's pending AI law
who: any business deploying AI (website chatbots, AI-generated ad images and video, AI in hiring), startups building AI products. All sizes.
where: EU-wide and national (AESIA and sector authorities).
reality: since 2 Aug 2026, a customer-facing chatbot must say it is an AI, and realistic AI images or video of people or places must be disclosed. Staff using AI must receive some literacy support. Spain's sanction law is still in Congress, so penalties are uncertain.
evidence:
- Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force 27 Jul 2026; art. 4 softened; high-risk delayed to 2 Dec 2027 and 2 Aug 2028; art. 50(2) grace period to 2 Dec 2026 — [artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/ai-act-explorer/digital-omnibus/)
- Art. 50 applies from August 2026 — [Usercentrics (after 27 Jul 2026)](https://usercentrics.com/knowledge-hub/eu-ai-act-high-risk-delay-article-50-transparency-consent/); [Gibson Dunn, 27 May 2026](https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-ai-act-omnibus-agreement-postponed-high-risk-deadlines-and-other-key-changes/)
- Spanish bill: fines up to €35M or 7%; for SMEs the lower cap applies; in Congress since 12 Jun 2026 — [CMS, 16 Jun 2026](https://cms.law/es/esp/publication/claves-del-proyecto-de-ley-organica-de-inteligencia-artificial); [Economist & Jurist, 15 Jun 2026](https://www.economistjurist.es/zbloque-1/ley-organica-de-ia-espana-aterriza-el-ai-act-con-aesia-sanciones-y-sandboxes/)
scale: number of SMEs using AI not quantified here.
cost_impact: fines up to 7% of turnover in theory (lower cap for SMEs); in practice unknown until Spain's law passes.
driver_status: AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by 2026/1744) — **in force (art. 4, art. 50)**. Spanish PLOIA — **draft in Congress**.
solved_today: law-firm advisory; Lawwwing "AI Sentinel" add-on at €13/month — [Lawwwing](https://lawwwing.com/precios/). No other prices.
software_solvable: **partly.** AI inventory, literacy-training records, chatbot disclosure banners and AI-content labelling are software; risk classification needs judgement.
confidence: high on status; medium on SME pain

title: NIS2 and ENS security demands from clients without a Spanish NIS2 law
who: SaaS and IT startups, managed service providers, and small to medium suppliers to energy, health, transport, banking, digital infrastructure and the public sector.
where: national, with EU clients.
reality: large clients send security questionnaires and contract clauses (audit rights, 24h/72h incident reporting), and public tenders require ENS certification. Meanwhile Spain has no NIS2 law, so there is no national reference for what is "enough".
evidence:
- Draft law only (14 Jan 2025); CJEU referral on 8 Jul 2026; NIS1 framework still applies; fines €10M or 2% and €7M or 1.4% once transposed — [Ángel Ortega Castro, updated 22 Oct 2026](https://angelortegacastro.com/ley-coordinacion-gobernanza-ciberseguridad-nis2-estado-boe/)
- Small suppliers indirectly affected through art. 21 supply-chain clauses; ENS certification renewed every 2 years; only electricity measures transposed (RDL 7/2025) — [CEDESA, 16 Sep 2026](https://cedesa.es/blog/nis2-espana-proveedores-administracion-ens/)
scale: not quantified.
cost_impact: ENS certification costs not found (gap); lost tenders or clients.
driver_status: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 — **not transposed (draft bill; infringement case at the CJEU)**. ENS RD 311/2022 — **in force**.
solved_today: ENS certification bodies, cybersecurity consultancies, GRC (governance, risk and compliance) tools. No prices collected.
software_solvable: **partly.** A questionnaire answer bank, policy templates, evidence collection and ENS readiness are software; controls need implementation.

title: Trademark and trade-name conflicts (naming disputes, refusals)
who: startups, retail and hospitality brands, e-commerce. Autónomos to medium firms.
where: national (OEPM), plus EU trademarks.
reality: founders pick a name, launch, and later face an opposition, refusal or cease-and-desist from an earlier rights holder, forcing a rebrand.
evidence:
- 57,158 national trademark applications in 2025 (+11.5%) — [OEPM, 17 Feb 2026](https://oepm.es/es/detalle-noticia/La-OEPM-cierra-2025-con-record-de-solicitudes-de-titulos-de-Propiedad-Industrial/)
- 45,427 grants and 4,873 refusals; trade names: 13,345 grants, 1,642 refusals — [OEPM Estadísticas 2025 PDF (provisional)](https://www.oepm.es/export/sites/portal/comun/documentos_relacionados/PDF/Estadisticas-OEPM-2025.pdf)
- Single statistical source; no data on oppositions or disputes.
scale: about 6,500 refusals of marks and trade names in 2025 (from the figures above).
cost_impact: not quantified (rebranding and legal fees).
driver_status: Ley 17/2001 de Marcas (not re-verified). **Ongoing; filings rising.**
solved_today: IP agents and lawyers; registration services from compliance providers (PymeLegal, Lawwwing) without public prices.
software_solvable: **yes.** Pre-filing similarity search, cost guidance and trademark watch alerts.

title: ESG and sustainability data requests from large clients and banks (VSME), with legal pressure now reduced
who: small and medium suppliers to large corporates; firms borrowing from banks; public-tender bidders.
where: EU-wide and national.
reality: SMEs receive sustainability questionnaires (emissions, policies). Since the Omnibus I, companies with fewer than 1,000 employees cannot legally be asked for more than the voluntary SME standard (VSME) allows, but banks' and clients' own requests continue (not evidenced here).
evidence:
- CSRD limited to more than 1,000 employees and €450M turnover; under-1,000 firms protected beyond voluntary standards; transposition by 19 Mar 2027 — [EP Legislative Observatory final-act summary (Directive (EU) 2026/470, OJ 26 Feb 2026)](https://oeil.europarl.europa.eu/oeil/en/document-summary?id=1890047)
- Spain's carbon-footprint duty applies only to large reporting companies and the state sector; tender award criteria may use it — [BOE RD 214/2025](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2025/03/18/214)
scale: not quantified (no Spanish data on questionnaire volumes).
cost_impact: not quantified.
driver_status: Directive (EU) 2026/470 — **in force; transposition by 19 Mar 2027**. RD 214/2025 — **in force (large companies only)**.
solved_today: VSME templates, carbon calculators, consultants. No prices collected.
software_solvable: **partly.** A VSME report generator is feasible, but legal demand has fallen.
confidence: high on status; low on pain

title: Municipal noise sanctions and closures
who: bars and restaurants, gyms, workshops, event venues, shops with sound equipment. Autónomos to small firms.
where: city-specific ordinances under the national Ley 37/2003 (Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Sevilla, Málaga, Palma and others; no city data obtained).
reality: neighbour complaints lead to municipal inspections, fines and, in serious cases, licence suspension or closure.
evidence: very serious €12,001–€300,000 plus closure of 2–5 years; serious €601–€12,000 plus closure up to 2 years; minor up to €600; town halls sanction; provisional sealing or closure possible — [BOE, Ley 37/2003 arts. 28–31](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2003/11/17/37). Legal ranges only; **no enforcement data**.
scale: not quantified.
cost_impact: fines in the legal ranges above; closure risk.
driver_status: Ley 37/2003 plus municipal ordinances. **In force.**
solved_today: acoustic studies and sound limiters (no prices collected).
software_solvable: **partly / no.** Noise logging and complaint response are software; the core is physical soundproofing.

title: Official complaint forms and regional consumer inspection
who: all B2C premises and online sellers. Autónomos to medium firms.
where: regional rules (Catalonia evidenced; other regions not obtained).
reality: businesses must offer official complaint forms (hojas de reclamaciones; in Catalonia also online) and inform customers about dispute resolution. Each form typically starts a consumer-office case that requires a response.
evidence:
- Catalan Codi de consum art. 126-9: official forms on request and online; duty to inform about dispute-resolution mechanisms — [BOE, Llei 22/2010](https://www.boe.es/eli/es-ct/l/2010/07/20/22)
- Catalan consumer agency fines €6.4M (2022) → €10.5M (2023) — [Vozpópuli, 14 Mar 2024](https://www.vozpopuli.com/espana/cataluna/generalitat-cuadruplica-ano-multas-castellano-ya-recauda-30-veces-mas-que-en-2021.html)
- National 15-day complaint answer duty — [BOE Ley 10/2025](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2025/12/26/10)
scale: not quantified (no complaint-form or OMIC volumes).
cost_impact: not quantified.
driver_status: regional consumer laws plus TRLGDCU art. 21. **In force.**
solved_today: paper forms bought from regional authorities or business associations; manual handling. No prices collected.
software_solvable: **partly.** Digital complaint intake and case tracking that links the official form to the 15-day reply.

title: Proving and archiving the "causa de temporalidad" for every mid-term contract
who: every landlord letting furnished flats or rooms for 32 days to 12 months: small owners (1–5 units), property managers and coliving operators. Most exposed are company landlords, who face 7-year terms.
where: national since 8 Oct 2026 (RDL 29/2026); Catalonia since 1–2 Jan 2026 (Llei 11/2025), with filing at INCASÒL.
reality: before signing, the landlord must write the specific displacement cause into the contract (work posting, studies, treatment, works on the habitual home, remote work with a home abroad) and keep proof such as an enrolment letter, employer letter or foreign domicile proof. Without it, the lease is habitual from day one.
evidence:
- Art. 7.2 LAU: "real y acreditable, recayendo sobre el arrendador la carga de la prueba ... con efectos retroactivos". — [BOE, 7 Oct 2026](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823); [idealista, 30 Sep 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/09/30/916608-el-gobierno-obliga-a-justificar-cada-alquiler-de-temporada-y-limita-el-de)
- Catalonia: landlord must "acrediti documentalment la causa concreta de la temporalitat". — [idealista/ca, 15 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/ca/news/immobiliari/2026/06/15/901949-el-constitucional-admet-el-recurs-del-pp-contra-la-regulacio-del-lloguer-temporal-i-les)
- Catalonia: contract, deposit and supporting documents are filed with INCASÒL. — [idealista, 4 Feb 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/02/04/881584-todo-sobre-la-ley-que-regula-el-alquiler-de-temporada-en-cataluna-y-lo-que-esta-por)
- Document table by tenant profile; nomad cause "questionable if ... moving their life here". — [Lázaro Amable, 22 Oct 2026](https://lazaroamable.com/blog/alquiler-temporada-canarias-contrato-temporal)
scale: seasonal lets are 34% of rental listings nationally (Barcelona 57%, Málaga 37%, Madrid 35%, Valencia 35%, Sevilla 33%, Alicante 31%, Palma 25%). — [Pressdigital/idealista, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.pressdigital.es/articulo/economia/2026-10-20/6058369-oferta-alquiler-permanente-cae-10-espana-mientras-temporal-crece-7-segun-idealista); [Qué!, 23 Oct 2026](https://www.que.es/2026/10/23/oferta-alquiler-cae-temporada/). 1.15M people live in seasonal or room rentals. — [idealista/Europa Press, 7 Sep 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/finanzas/economia/2026/09/07/912998-consumo-estima-que-mas-de-un-millon-de-personas-vive-en-alquiler-de-temporada-o-de) (methodology undisclosed)
cost_impact: re-classification brings a 5-year minimum (7 for companies) plus extensions, refund of any deposit above one month, and rent caps. — [Captain Legal, 27 Aug 2026](https://www.captain.legal/es/blog/alquiler-temporada-causa-recalificacion/). In Catalonia, a fraudulent seasonal contract was "molt greu" (up to €900,000) under the earlier regime. — [3Cat, 2025](https://www.3cat.cat/3catinfo/multes-per-incomplir-el-topall-del-lloguer-quines-sancions-hi-ha-i-a-quins-contractes-afecten/noticia/3332834/)
driver_status: RDL 29/2026, BOE-A-2026-20823 (in force since 8 Oct 2026; Diputación Permanente vote expected ~12 Nov 2026). Llei 11/2025 Catalonia (in force; TC appeal admitted 15 Jun 2026, not suspended).
solved_today: law-firm templates and checklists, agencies and gestorías. Spotahome offers e-signed contracts. No tool was found that validates and archives cause evidence. Complaint: "un marco de inseguridad jurídica" (Catalan agents). — [idealista, 27 Jan 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/01/27/880092-regulacion-del-alquiler-de-temporada-en-catalunya-habra-un-trasvase-de-la-oferta-al)
software_solvable: yes. A guided contract builder with an evidence vault and audit trail fits well, though legal judgement risk remains.

title: Regulatory whiplash: three national decrees in 2026, dissolved Cortes, pending vote
who: all mid-term landlords, managers, platforms and coliving operators, and their tenants.
where: national, layered on top of Catalonia's separate regime.
reality: rules changed on 1 Oct (RDL 26/2026), reverted on 2 Oct and changed again on 8 Oct (RDL 29/2026). Contracts signed between 8 Oct and the convalidation vote may end up under a lapsed regime, and templates must be re-issued.
evidence:
- RDL 26 and RDL 27 derogated on 2 Oct 2026. — [Garrigues, 8 Oct 2026](https://www.garrigues.com/es_ES/noticia/regulacion-arrendamientos-vivienda-vivienda-temporal-real-decreto-ley-292026-limitaciones); [gentile.law, 6 Oct 2026](https://www.gentile.law/caen-los-reales-decretos-ley-26-2026-y-27-2026-que-queda-del-alquiler-tras-el-rechazo-del-congreso/)
- Cortes dissolved; elections on 29 Nov 2026. — [Demócrata, Oct 2026](https://www.democrata.es/boe/boe-disolucion-cortes-elecciones-29-noviembre/); [elEconomista, Oct 2026](https://www.eleconomista.es/actualidad/noticias/14018685/10/26/ni-dimite-ni-renuncia-pedro-sanchez-disuelve-las-cortes-generales-en-que-consiste.html)
- Vote expected around 12 Nov, forecast 35–34. Single source: [gestionatualojamiento, 20 Oct 2026](https://gestionatualojamiento.com/convalidacion-del-decreto-de-vivienda/)
- PL 122/000136 reportedly rejected on 26 Feb 2026. Single source: [Captain Legal](https://www.captain.legal/es/blog/alquiler-temporada-causa-recalificacion/)
- RDL 8/2026 (March 2026) referenced in the RDL 29/2026 transitional rules. — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823)
scale: the whole market (see HOU-01).
cost_impact: advisory time, re-papering, and the risk of mis-classified contracts. No € figure found.
driver_status: RDL 29/2026 pending convalidation (upcoming deadline). Elections 29 Nov; new Cortes 23 Dec 2026.
solved_today: law-firm alerts and ICAB courses ([ICAB course](https://icab.es/en/formacion/course/Jornada-El-Real-Decreto-ley-29-2026.-Arrendamientos-fiscalidad-grandes-tenedores-y-desahucios/)) and portal news. No rules engine was found.
software_solvable: partly. Stamping each contract with its applicable regime by date and region, and pushing template updates, is solvable; the political uncertainty is not.

title: Rent caps now reach seasonal and room lets in tensioned zones
who: landlords and managers in declared tensioned zones; Barcelona is the main case among the target cities.
where: Catalonia (Barcelona; also Girona, Tarragona and Lleida capitals); nationally in any tensioned zone via arts. 17.6–17.7. Not Madrid, Valencia, Málaga, Alicante or Palma, which are non-tensioned.
reality: to set the first rent, the landlord must find the last habitual rent of the past 5 years and/or the SERPAVI index (with gaps under 30 m² and over 150 m²). Ads must show the index and the previous rent. Prior seasonal rents don't count.
evidence:
- "tots els habitatges amb ús residencial han hagut de complir el límit de preus". — [idealista/ca, 15 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/ca/news/immobiliari/2026/06/15/901949-el-constitucional-admet-el-recurs-del-pp-contra-la-regulacio-del-lloguer-temporal-i-les)
- Index mechanics and gaps. — [idealista, 4 Feb 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/02/04/881584-todo-sobre-la-ley-que-regula-el-alquiler-de-temporada-en-cataluna-y-lo-que-esta-por)
- Ad-disclosure fines: €1,750 paid; others up to €10,000. — [Consum, 3 Feb 2026](https://consum.gencat.cat/ca/detalls/noticia/primers-sancionadors-contencio-preu-lloguers)
scale: Barcelona seasonal offer −37% y/y but still 57% of listings; permanent −22%. — [Pressdigital/idealista, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.pressdigital.es/articulo/economia/2026-10-20/6058369-oferta-alquiler-permanente-cae-10-espana-mientras-temporal-crece-7-segun-idealista). Barcelona listings −~30% in two weeks after entry into force. — [Spanish Property Insight, 3/16 Jan 2026](https://www.spanishpropertyinsight.com/2026/01/03/catalonia-has-effectively-outlawed-mid-term-rentals/)
cost_impact: fines of €3,000–90,000 (minor and serious); actual fines of €30,000 ×2 and €3,000 ×2. — [Consum, 3 Feb 2026](https://consum.gencat.cat/ca/detalls/noticia/primers-sancionadors-contencio-preu-lloguers). Very serious up to €900,000. — [3Cat](https://www.3cat.cat/3catinfo/multes-per-incomplir-el-topall-del-lloguer-quines-sancions-hi-ha-i-a-quins-contractes-afecten/noticia/3332834/)
driver_status: Llei 11/2025 (in force; TC appeal admitted, no suspension); RDL 29/2026 arts. 17.6–17.7 (in force, pending convalidation).
solved_today: the public SERPAVI index lookup, agencies and lawyers. No dedicated cap calculator for seasonal or room lets was found. Expert complaints: the index is unsuitable and the law has constitutional doubts. — [idealista, 4 Feb 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/02/04/881584-todo-sobre-la-ley-que-regula-el-alquiler-de-temporada-en-cataluna-y-lo-que-esta-por)
software_solvable: yes. A cap calculator (index plus rent history) with ad-disclosure generation and an audit file fits well.

title: Room and coliving pricing capped at "sum of rooms ≤ whole-flat rent"
who: coliving operators (Vandor, NAD, professional operators), room-letting landlords, and tenants paying €900–1,135 per room.
where: Catalonia (Llei 11/2025) and national (new art. 17.9 LAU); index limits also apply in tensioned zones.
reality: flats split into 6–10 rooms at about €1,000 each must now total no more than the flat's own rent. Mandatory extras face scrutiny, and in tensioned zones large holders cannot use charges to exceed caps (art. 17.7).
evidence:
- Art. 17.9 text. — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823)
- "la suma de les rendes ... no superi el preu del lloguer del pis". — [idealista/ca, 15 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/ca/news/immobiliari/2026/06/15/901949-el-constitucional-admet-el-recurs-del-pp-contra-la-regulacio-del-lloguer-temporal-i-les)
- €300 base plus extras exceeding €1,000; average €1,135. — [Metrópoli Abierta, 2 Mar 2026](https://www.metropoliabierta.cat/el-pols-de-la-ciutat/20260302/negoci-coliving-dispara-barcelona-lombra-frau-llei-dhabitatge/1003742737508_0.html)
- About €1,000 coliving against a €600 average room; coverage disputed. — [3Cat, 16 Feb 2026](https://www.3cat.cat/3catinfo/els-habitatges-de-coliving-es-doblen-en-dos-anys-estan-dins-o-fora-del-topall-de-preus/noticia/3394906/)
scale: about 20,000 coliving beds in Spain, about 5,000 in Barcelona. — [3Cat](https://www.3cat.cat/3catinfo/els-habitatges-de-coliving-es-doblen-en-dos-anys-estan-dins-o-fora-del-topall-de-preus/noticia/3394906/). JLL counts 19,089 flex beds. — [JLL, 12 Nov 2025](https://www.jll.com/es-es/insights/flex-living-en-espana)
cost_impact: Catalan fines (see HOU-03) and margin compression (no figure). Tenant complaints include a €600 "partner overnight" penalty and "És com una pensió".
driver_status: Llei 11/2025 (in force); RDL 29/2026 art. 17.9 (pending convalidation).
solved_today: operators restructure pricing into rent plus "services", backed by legal advice. No compliance tool was found.
software_solvable: partly. A compliance calculator and fee-structure audit can be built, but the underlying economic constraint cannot be engineered away.

title: Contract-lifecycle traps: 12-month cap, ">2 consecutive contracts" rule, one-month tenant exit
who: mid-term landlords and managers with repeat or extending tenants (corporate stays, academic-year lets).
where: national (arts. 9 bis and 11.2 LAU); Catalonia requires renewals to justify that the cause persists.
reality: the landlord must count total duration per tenant and dwelling. A third chained contract converts the first into a habitual lease. Tenants can leave after one month on 10 days' notice, so occupancy is unpredictable.
evidence: arts. 9 bis.1–2 and 11.2 (verbatim). — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823); [dig.es, Oct 2026](https://www.dig.es/alquiler-de-temporada-habitaciones-2026/). Renewal justification in Catalonia. — [idealista, 4 Feb 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/02/04/881584-todo-sobre-la-ley-que-regula-el-alquiler-de-temporada-en-cataluna-y-lo-que-esta-por)
scale: every temporary lease signed since 8 Oct 2026.
cost_impact: conversion to a 5/7-year lease; vacancy and turnover cost from early exits (no figure).
driver_status: RDL 29/2026 (pending convalidation).
solved_today: spreadsheets and generic property-management software. Homming has a free tier; it was not verified to track causes or chaining. — [Softwaredoit](https://www.softwaredoit.es/homming/homming.html)
software_solvable: yes. Duration and chaining counters, renewal alerts and vacancy forecasting are straightforward.

title: Caps on guarantees, tenant-paid insurance and fees shift costs to landlords and platforms
who: landlords and managers; marketplaces with tenant fees (HousingAnywhere, Spotahome); guarantee and insurance sellers; tenants.
where: national (arts. 20.2 and 36.5 LAU).
reality: the extra guarantee is capped at one month for temporary leases, and landlords cannot require tenant-bought rent-default insurance "u otras coberturas análogas". Management and formalisation fees cannot be passed on "ni directa ni indirectamente".
evidence:
- Verbatim text of arts. 20.2 and 36.5. — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823)
- HousingAnywhere tenant fee of 25–40% of the first month (minimum €175). — [HousingAnywhere, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://housinganywhere.com/pricing/landlords)
- The insurance ban was toggled with RDL 26/2026. — [Selectra](https://selectra.es/seguros/noticias/alquiler-seguro-impago-2026-casero-exigir)
scale: all temporary leases, and the tenant-fee revenue of platforms.
cost_impact: landlords now pay insurance themselves, €306–658 per year on €950/month rent. — [OCU, 28 Sep 2026](https://www.ocu.org/fincas-y-casas/gestion/seguros-y-prestamos/analisis/2026/07/comparativa-seguros-impago-rentas). Platforms' tenant-fee models may be at risk (interpretation; no ruling found).
driver_status: RDL 29/2026 (pending convalidation).
solved_today: landlord-paid insurance and Spotahome Plus rent guarantees (10% of contract value, per the UK/Ireland page). — [Spotahome plans](https://plans.spotahome.com)
software_solvable: partly. Fee and guarantee compliance checks and embedded landlord-paid guarantees can be built; insurance underwriting is not software.

title: Screening foreign remote workers and relocating employees with no Spanish payslips or credit file
who: landlords and managers, plus digital nomads, foreign remote workers, relocating employees and international students.
where: national; concentrated in Madrid, Barcelona, Málaga, Valencia, Palma and Canarias.
reality: insurers require annual rent ≤35–40% of net income, and foreigners are asked for avales of about 6 months' rent. Now that the extra guarantee is capped at one month, landlords lose their usual fallback and reject applicants instead.
evidence:
- Solvency ratio. — [OCU, 28 Sep 2026](https://www.ocu.org/fincas-y-casas/gestion/seguros-y-prestamos/analisis/2026/07/comparativa-seguros-impago-rentas)
- Aval of 6 months' rent; fees 0.5–2% per quarter. — [The Local, 9 Sep 2024](https://www.thelocal.es/20240909/aval-how-to-get-a-bank-guarantee-to-rent-a-property-in-spain)
- "incremento de las garantías exigidas" as indirect discrimination. — [Público](https://www.publico.es/economia/72-inmobiliarias-acepta-discriminar-migrantes-alquileres.html) (search-level)
- One-month extra-guarantee cap. — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823)
scale: 27,875 nomad-visa holders including dependants at end-2024. Single source: [Tekcevisa](https://tekcevisa.com/how-many-people-have-spains-digital-nomad-visa/). About 60% of Barcelona coliving tenants are foreign. — [Metrópoli Abierta](https://www.metropoliabierta.cat/el-pols-de-la-ciutat/20260302/negoci-coliving-dispara-barcelona-lombra-frau-llei-dhabitatge/1003742737508_0.html)
cost_impact: an aval blocks e.g. €6,000 and costs €30–120 per quarter, plus a notary. Rejected applicants mean longer vacancies (no figure).
driver_status: market practice; RDL 29/2026 limits (pending convalidation).
software_solvable: yes. Cross-border income and employment verification combined with a landlord-paid guarantee is a clear product gap.

title: Agency discrimination against foreign tenants
who: migrant and foreign tenants (including nomads and students); agencies and landlords.
where: tested in Madrid and Barcelona; likely national.
reality: agencies accept owners' "no foreigners" instructions and give foreign callers fewer alternatives, often in segregated districts.
evidence: 99% of 100 agencies accepted exclusion requests (72.5% in 2020), and foreigners got at most 2 alternatives against 4 for Spaniards. — [Ara, 25 Mar 2025](https://es.ara.cat/economia/inmobiliario/discriminacion-mercado-alquiler-alza-99-inmobiliarias-aceptan-clausulas-racistas_1_5327281.html); [La Marea, 26 Mar 2025](https://lamarea.com/2025/03/26/aumenta-el-racismo-y-la-segregacion-en-el-mercado-del-alquiler)
scale: sample-based (100 agencies; 600 renter calls); no national estimate.
cost_impact: one €90,001 fine (Barcelona, 2022). Single source, search-level: [Público](https://www.publico.es/economia/72-inmobiliarias-acepta-discriminar-migrantes-alquileres.html)
driver_status: anti-discrimination law (Constitution art. 14 per the sources); practice is persistent.
solved_today: nothing found beyond NGOs' testing.
software_solvable: partly. Standardised, criteria-based screening with audit logs reduces arbitrary rejection; it cannot remove intent.
confidence: medium (small sample; not specific to mid-term)

title: Fake listings and advance-payment scams aimed at newcomers
who: incoming tenants (nomads, students, relocating workers); landlords whose listings are cloned.
where: national. Cases in Asturias and Pamplona (Oct 2026), Benidorm, Tenerife (Nov 2025), Baleares and Palma (2025–26), Las Palmas (2021–22).
reality: scammers post fake ads and ask for a "fianza" or a Bizum to book a visit before any viewing, then disappear. Portals verify only email or phone.
evidence:
