- OCU's fake ad passed all 8 portals unnoticed. — [OCU, 16 Sep 2025](https://www.ocu.org/organizacion/prensa/notas-de-prensa/2025/portalesvivivenda160925)
- Asturias network: 80+ victims, >€80,000, 115 accounts. — [Moncloa.com, 17 Oct 2026](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/10/17/estafa-alquileres-asturias-detenidos-3450018/)
- Benidorm: >€20,300 in €80–300 payments. — [Valencia Plaza](https://valenciaplaza.com/cvalenciana/desmantelada-una-red-que-estafo-mas-de-20000-euros-en-benidorm-con-alquileres-ficticios)
- Tenerife: >€10,000. — [RTVC, 25 Nov 2025](https://rtvc.es/detienen-autora-multiples-estafas-alquileres-falsos-internet-25-noviembre-2025/)
- Baleares police warning. — [Última Hora, 28 Apr 2025](https://www.ultimahora.es/noticias/local/2025/04/28/2373315/policia-nacional-alerta-estafas-alquiler-pisos-baleares.html)
scale: no national aggregate found.
cost_impact: €80–1,100 per victim in the cases cited.
driver_status: market force; no specific regulation.
solved_today: Spotahome's "Verified" listings with in-person visits; HousingAnywhere's "fraud detection" and first-month escrow released 48 hours after move-in. — [HousingAnywhere](https://housinganywhere.com/pricing/landlords). OCU advises checking the nota simple and Catastro.
software_solvable: yes. Landlord identity plus ownership checks (nota simple, Catastro) and escrowed first payments are proven patterns.

title: Tenant identity verification without a usable digital ID for foreigners
who: landlords, managers and coliving operators; foreign tenants.
where: national; EU-wide timeline.
reality: passports are checked manually or by platforms. Spain's EUDI wallet ("Cartera Digital") has no launch date, and landlords will not be obliged to accept the wallet.
evidence: wallets due by 24 Dec 2026; private acceptance only by 24 Dec 2027 and only for regulated sectors and very large platforms; Spain has given no date. — [acens, 6 Oct 2026](https://blog.acens.com/actualidad/cartera-digital-europea/); [EADTrust, 3 Aug 2026](https://www.eadtrust.eu/blog/cartera-idue-estado-actual-en-espana/)
scale: n/a.
cost_impact: commodity KYC costs about $0.33 per applicant, with 500 free checks per month. — [Didit](https://didit.me/es/solutions/tenant-screening/)
driver_status: Reg. (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS 2.0). Availability deadline 24 Dec 2026 (upcoming); acceptance 24 Dec 2027.
solved_today: platform checks (Spotahome) and KYC vendors (Didit). Others such as Veriff, Onfido and Sumsub were not verified.
software_solvable: yes. Basic KYC is already cheap, so its value is as a component of HOU-01, HOU-07 and HOU-09, not as a standalone product.

title: Wasted registry costs and confusion after the Registro Único was annulled
who: owners of tourist and seasonal lets who registered in 2025–26; agencies and gestorías.
where: national; regional tourist registries remain (Canarias HVV, Baleares, Catalonia HUT).
reality: owners paid fees to obtain the NRUA from 1 Jul 2025 and an annual model was added. Then the Supreme Court annulled the registry, with effect from the BOE of 8 Jun 2026. Owners now face refund claims and uncertainty about what to show on listings, while platform-side Ventanilla duties continue.
evidence:
- The rulings. — [idealista, 21 May 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/05/21/898563-el-supremo-tumba-el-registro-unico-de-alquiler-de-corta-duracion-por-invadir); [Lázaro Amable, 22 Oct 2026](https://lazaroamable.com/blog/registro-alquiler-corta-duracion-canarias)
- 111,000 rejections. — [idealista, 22 May 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/05/22/898792-el-fin-del-registro-de-viviendas-de-corta-estancia-reabre-100-000-licencias)
- >€20M in fees; refund via responsabilidad patrimonial within 1 year. — [idealista, 5 Jun 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/06/05/900535-nulo-el-registro-unico-de-alquiler-turistico-pagaste-tasas-por-una-norma-ilegal-y)
- Notaries' complaint. — [idealista, 21 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/07/21/907140-notarios-denuncian-la-hipertrofia-administrativa-en-la-regulacion-de-alquiler-de)
scale: 111,000 rejected applications. Galicia alone had 17,969 applications, 1,264 of them seasonal. — [Galiciaé, 23 May 2026](https://www.galiciae.com/articulo/galicia/registro-unico-rechazo-mas-2200-alquileres-turisticos-temporales-galicia/20260523050000107767.html)
cost_impact: more than €20M in fees. FEVITUR, an interested party, claims about €33,000 average loss per owner and about €160M in total.
driver_status: RD 1312/2024 registry provisions annulled (TS, May–June 2026). The Ventanilla Única Digital and Reg. (EU) 2024/1028 remain in force.
solved_today: lawyers filing claims; gestorías.
software_solvable: partly. Bundling refund claims is one-off work; registration-number compliance for seasonal lets is now largely moot.

title: Deposits (fianzas) lodged region by region, with different deadlines, amounts and fines
who: all mid-term landlords; managers operating in several regions.
where: Catalonia (INCASÒL), Madrid, Andalucía (AVRA), C. Valenciana, Baleares (IBAVI), Canarias (Instituto Canario de Vivienda / Caja de Depósitos). No duty in Asturias, Cantabria, Murcia, Navarra or La Rioja.
reality: every short contract means a deposit filing and later a refund. Deadlines vary: 2 months in Catalonia, 30 working days in Madrid, 1 month in Canarias. Amounts are ambiguous: Catalonia uses a two-month base for seasonal contracts under one year, while the LAU housing rule implies one month.
evidence:
- Catalonia rules. — [INCASÒL, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://incasol.gencat.cat/ca/serveis-i-tramits/fiances-de-lloguers/informacio/diposit-de-fiances)
- Fines by region. — [El Español, 18 Mar 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/sociedad/20260318/entrado-vigor-penalizara-caseros-no-depositen-fianza-comunidad-autonoma/1003744163850_0.html)
- Canarias rules and the "no case law yet" point. — [Lázaro Amable, 22 Oct 2026](https://lazaroamable.com/blog/alquiler-temporada-canarias-contrato-temporal)
- Deposit filing used as evidence in A Coruña. — [idealista, 6 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/07/06/901838-la-clave-no-es-la-duracion-cuando-un-alquiler-de-temporada-pasa-a-ser-de-vivienda)
scale: every mid-term contract in 12 regions.
driver_status: regional deposit laws (in force); RDL 29/2026 (pending convalidation) changes the base classification.
solved_today: manual online filing (INCASÒL Model 2 with a digital certificate) and gestorías.
software_solvable: yes. A multi-region deposit workflow with deadline alerts fits, though e-government filing may need assisted or robotic submission.

title: Re-classification lawsuits turn "seasonal" contracts into 5–7-year leases
who: landlords (especially companies) and managers; tenants who stay on.
where: national; rulings in Albacete, A Coruña, Barcelona and Málaga (2022).
reality: when the agreed term ends, the landlord files for eviction for expiry. Courts examine objective indicators and keep the tenant in place.
evidence:
- SAP Albacete, 11 Jul 2025. — [OCU, 19 Jan 2026](https://www.ocu.org/fincas-y-casas/gestion/alquiler/analisis/2026/01/caso-fraude-alquiler-temporada)
- SAP A Coruña, 26 Feb 2026 (7 years). — [idealista, 6 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/07/06/901838-la-clave-no-es-la-duracion-cuando-un-alquiler-de-temporada-pasa-a-ser-de-vivienda)
- Art. 6.4 CC doctrine. — [Captain Legal, 27 Aug 2026](https://www.captain.legal/es/blog/alquiler-temporada-causa-recalificacion/)
- AP Málaga, 25 May 2022. — [Sepin](https://blog.sepin.es/alquiler-vivienda-residencial-arrendamiento-temporada) (search-level)
scale: no count of cases found.
cost_impact: eviction denied; 5–7-year tenancy; penalty clauses void.
driver_status: case law (ongoing), now written into law (art. 7.2, 9 bis; pending convalidation) and into Llei 11/2025 (in force).
solved_today: lawyers.
software_solvable: partly. Contracts can be risk-scored against the indicators courts use (identical successive contracts, empadronamiento, utilities in the tenant's name, pre-emption waiver, full-month rent); litigation itself cannot.

title: Overstaying or defaulting temporary tenants and slow evictions
who: landlords and managers.
where: national; LAU evictions are concentrated in Catalonia, Andalucía, C. Valenciana and Madrid.
reality: a tenant who does not leave at the end date, or stops paying, means a LAU eviction. Suspensions for vulnerable households are extended to 2030.
evidence: 18,317 LAU evictions in 2025 (−10.9%) and regional splits. — [Forbes/CGPJ, 20 Mar 2026](https://forbes.es/economia/893652/los-desahucios-caen-un-11-en-2025-hasta-los-25-540-segun-cgpj/). Vulnerable-household suspension regime to 31 Dec 2030. — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823)
scale: 18,317 LAU evictions in 2025 (all lease types; no seasonal split).
cost_impact: lost rent for the duration of proceedings (no figure). Insurance €306–658 per year. — [OCU](https://www.ocu.org/fincas-y-casas/gestion/seguros-y-prestamos/analisis/2026/07/comparativa-seguros-impago-rentas)
driver_status: LEC and RDL 29/2026 eviction changes (pending convalidation).
solved_today: rent-default insurance with legal defence (Arag, Allianz, Mapfre rated best by OCU); Spotahome Plus guaranteed rent.
software_solvable: partly. Documentation and early-warning tools help; enforcement does not.

title: Deposit-return disputes under the new mandatory end-of-lease record
who: high-turnover landlords and managers; tenants.
where: national (new art. 36.7 LAU).
reality: at move-out, both parties must sign a condition record. If they don't, or the record shows no damage, the flat is presumed returned in good condition, so the landlord loses deposit deductions.
evidence:
- Art. 36.7 (verbatim). — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823)
- Spotahome doesn't handle deposits. — [Spotahome](https://landlord.spotahome.com/l/how-it-works)
- Flatio bans deposits under 180 days. — [Flatio](https://www.flatio.com/i/renting-out-spain-a-coruna)
- HousingAnywhere has no damage insurance. — [HousingAnywhere](https://housinganywhere.com/pricing/landlords)
scale: every temporary lease; no dispute statistics found.
cost_impact: lost deductions, typically up to one month plus a one-month guarantee (no figure).
driver_status: RDL 29/2026 (pending convalidation).
solved_today: paper inventories; Spotahome damage protection (€500 Standard / 2 months Plus, per the UK/Ireland page).
software_solvable: yes. Photo-based check-in/out with e-signature and deposit reconciliation is a solved pattern in other markets.

title: Five-working-day repair deadline for temporary housing
who: landlords and managers, especially remote owners.
where: national (new art. 21 bis LAU).
reality: once a tenant reports a problem, the landlord must respond within 5 working days. Otherwise the tenant may repair it and deduct the cost from next month's rent.
evidence: art. 21 bis (verbatim); art. 21.5 gives 15 natural days to accept a tenant's quote. — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823). An expert criticised the repair-offset clause in the earlier bill. — [idealista, 4 Feb 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/02/04/881584-todo-sobre-la-ley-que-regula-el-alquiler-de-temporada-en-cataluna-y-lo-que-esta-por)
scale: all temporary leases.
cost_impact: rent offsets (no figure).
driver_status: RDL 29/2026 (pending convalidation).
solved_today: property-management incident modules (e.g. Homming "gestión de incidencias", per Softwaredoit) and WhatsApp.
software_solvable: yes. Ticketing with SLA timers and a contractor network fits well.

title: Tax treatment: VAT cliff at 30/31 nights, no IRPF reduction for temporary leases, IBI surcharges
who: owners and operators of furnished units; coliving operators offering hotel-type services; tourist-flat owners converting.
where: national (IVA, IRPF); IBI in tensioned municipalities; IGIC in Canarias.
reality: from 1 Dec 2026, a 30-night stay pays 10% VAT while a 32-night temporary lease stays exempt unless hotel services are provided. Temporary leases appear to get no IRPF rent reduction.
evidence:
- VAT rule and IBI surcharges. — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823); [idealista, 30 Sep 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/09/30/916608-el-gobierno-obliga-a-justificar-cada-alquiler-de-temporada-y-limita-el-de)
- VAT registration and Modelo 303 due by 30 Jan 2027. — [gestionatualojamiento, 20 Oct 2026](https://gestionatualojamiento.com/convalidacion-del-decreto-de-vivienda/)
- Canarias IGIC exclusion. — [Lázaro Amable](https://lazaroamable.com/blog/alquiler-temporada-canarias-contrato-temporal)
- IRPF art. 23.2 limited to art. 2.1 LAU. — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823) (interpretation)
scale: all furnished short and mid-term lets.
cost_impact: 10% VAT on stays of 30 nights or fewer; lost IRPF reduction (not quantified).
driver_status: RDL 29/2026 art. 7 (VAT from 1 Dec 2026, only if convalidated; otherwise it lapses); IBI surcharges optional for municipalities.
solved_today: gestorías.
software_solvable: partly. Tax classification per stay and invoicing logic can be automated; tax filing stays with gestorías.

title: Coliving's legal limbo: planning use, licences and enforcement
who: coliving operators and investors (Be Casa, Livensa Living, Cotown, Smart Rental, Node Living; Vandor, NAD); owners converting buildings.
where: Madrid (2023 "residencia compartida" class; Plan Reside conversions); Barcelona (permit enforcement, 30% rule, PGM change of 27 Mar 2026); Catalonia (room caps). Elsewhere there is no specific framework (weak source).
reality: operators split buildings with minor permits, the council opens files for major works, residents demand the 30% protected-housing share, and fines and evictions follow.
evidence:
- Madrid rules: 15 m² units, 25 m² + 5 m² per unit of common space, exclusive building. — [Andersen, 31 Aug 2023](https://es.andersen.com/como-afecta-al-coliving-las-nuevas-normas-urbanisticas-de-madrid/)
- Plan Reside coliving conversions. — [idealista, 15 Nov 2024](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2024/11/15/821299-madrid-capital-lanza-un-plan-para-impulsar-el-coliving-y-limitar-los-pisos)
- Vandor files. — [Ara, 12 Mar 2026](https://en.ara.cat/society/residents-affected-by-coliving-pressure-collboni-to-enforce-the-law-his-blogs_1_5676083.html)
- NAD fined >€20,000. — [Metrópoli Abierta, 2 Mar 2026](https://www.metropoliabierta.cat/el-pols-de-la-ciutat/20260302/negoci-coliving-dispara-barcelona-lombra-frau-llei-dhabitatge/1003742737508_0.html)
- €500 fines (advocacy source). — [Sindicat de Llogateres](https://sindicatdellogateres.org/collboni-no-fa-res-per-aplicar-el-30-multa-de-nomes-500-e-convertir-illegalment-els-pisos-de-sant-agusti-14-en-colivings-i-saltar-se-la-reserva-dhabitatge-protegit/)
- PGM change. — [Ara, 27 Mar 2026](https://en.ara.cat/society/barcelona-decrees-that-the-residential-use-of-apartments-prevails-over-temporary-use_1_5691565.html)
scale: 19,089 operating beds and 38,716 by 2028; Madrid 60% of stock. — [JLL, 12 Nov 2025](https://www.jll.com/es-es/insights/flex-living-en-espana)
cost_impact: fines from €500 to over €20,000; refurbishment of €70–85k per 80–90 m² flat (weak source: [merca2](https://www.merca2.es/2026/06/02/burbuja-coliving-madrid-convierte-en-un-hotel-fragmentado-por-habitaciones-2386620/)).
solved_today: planning consultants and lawyers.
software_solvable: partly / mostly no. Licensing and planning are legal work; at most a feasibility checklist tool.

title: Converting tourist flats to mid-term or coliving: the incentive exists but legal obstacles multiply
who: owners of Barcelona's 10,101 HUTs (expiring 24 Nov 2028); Madrid's 16,100 tourist flats (7% legal); Málaga owners under moratoria; property managers.
where: Barcelona, Madrid and Málaga; also Palma and Canarias.
reality: owners facing licence loss move to "temporada", but now need a real tenant cause. In Catalonia they also face caps, and in Barcelona the PGM change.
evidence:
- Barcelona's 2028 end date. — [Chekin](https://chekin.com/blog/regulacion-pisos-turisticos-barcelona/)
- "fuga hacia la modalidad de temporada"; 1,975 Barcelona seasonal listings in September 2026, +8.1% over 2 years. — [Tourinews, 13 Oct 2026](https://www.tourinews.es/resumen-de-prensa/notas-de-prensa-destinos-turismo/alquiler-temporada-se-dispara-en-barcelona-proximo-veto-vacacional-pero-tambien-tiene-dias-contados_4495117_102.html)
- Barcelona seasonal −37% y/y against Madrid +52% y/y. — [Pressdigital/idealista, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.pressdigital.es/articulo/economia/2026-10-20/6058369-oferta-alquiler-permanente-cae-10-espana-mientras-temporal-crece-7-segun-idealista)
- Madrid's 16,100 tourist flats, 7% legal. — [idealista, 15 Nov 2024](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2024/11/15/821299-madrid-capital-lanza-un-plan-para-impulsar-el-coliving-y-limitar-los-pisos)
- Málaga moratoria. — [Brainsre, 21 Jul 2026](https://brainsre.news/malaga-congela-licencias-turisticas-tres-anos/)
scale: as above.
cost_impact: lost tourist yield. No source gives the mid-term vs tourist yield gap.
solved_today: property managers rebranding to mid-term; Spotahome and Ukio named as growing in Barcelona.
software_solvable: partly. A conversion-feasibility and compliance dashboard is plausible, but the cause rule limits demand to genuinely temporary tenants.

title: Shrinking, volatile rental supply for incoming workers
who: relocating employees, nomads and students; employers and HR teams.
where: national. Permanent listings fell 22% in Barcelona and Alicante, 12% in Valencia, 11% in Málaga, 6% in Madrid and 2% in Palma, and rose 2% in Las Palmas.
reality: fewer long-term flats, and seasonal stock that disappears where it is capped. Incoming workers compete for scarce units or fall back on rooms and coliving.
evidence: Q3 2026 offer data. — [Pressdigital/idealista, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.pressdigital.es/articulo/economia/2026-10-20/6058369-oferta-alquiler-permanente-cae-10-espana-mientras-temporal-crece-7-segun-idealista); [El Diario de Madrid, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.eldiariodemadrid.es/articulo/vivienda/oferta-alquiler-permanente-cae-6-madrid-mientras-crece-peso-contratos-temporada/20261020103048144701.html). idealista argues "la intervención del mercado está generando escasez"; this is an interested party.
scale: national.
cost_impact: search time and higher prices (no figure).
driver_status: market force plus regulation.
solved_today: relocation agencies (expat track), Blueground corporate housing, coliving.
software_solvable: no. This is structural supply.

title: Marketplace and tool fees squeeze mid-term margins and tenant budgets
who: small landlords and property managers; tenants.
where: national; the platforms are pan-European.
reality: landlords pay a percentage of the whole contract value; tenants pay a large upfront fee on top of the first month and the deposit.
evidence:
- Spotahome 8/10/15% of total contract value (UK/Ireland page; Spanish rates not shown). — [Spotahome, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://plans.spotahome.com)
- HousingAnywhere tenant fee 25–40% of the first month (minimum €175) plus 2.5% on payment requests. — [HousingAnywhere, accessed 23 Oct 2026](https://housinganywhere.com/pricing/landlords)
- PriceLabs $19.99 per listing per month. — [PriceLabs](https://help.pricelabs.co/portal/en/kb/articles/how-much-does-pricelabs-costs)
- Professional management 18–22% of gross (weak source). — [merca2](https://www.merca2.es/2026/06/02/burbuja-coliving-madrid-convierte-en-un-hotel-fragmentado-por-habitaciones-2386620/)
scale: not quantified.
cost_impact: for example, €720 per 6-month €1,500/month contract at 8% (calculation), and €375–600 in tenant fees on the same flat.
driver_status: market; tenant fees possibly constrained by art. 20.2 LAU (interpretation; pending convalidation).
solved_today: direct portal ads (idealista and Fotocasa, limited free listings per OCU) and word of mouth.
software_solvable: yes, as a cheaper alternative (Type A), though marketplace demand has strong network effects.
confidence: medium (Spanish fee levels unverified; no complaints documented)

title: Pricing temporary leases under an IRAV ceiling across successive contracts
who: mid-term landlords and managers everywhere, including non-tensioned Madrid, Málaga and Valencia.
where: national (new art. 17.8 LAU).
reality: seasonal demand peaks (academic year, summer, corporate seasons) cannot be priced up between successive temporary contracts on the same flat by more than the IRAV annual percentage. Only the first rent is free outside tensioned zones.
evidence: art. 17.8 (verbatim). — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823); [idealista, 30 Sep 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/09/30/916608-el-gobierno-obliga-a-justificar-cada-alquiler-de-temporada-y-limita-el-de). The first IRAV was 2.2% for 2025. Single source: [The Corner](https://thecorner.eu/?p=118291)
scale: all temporary leases.
cost_impact: lost yield versus market repricing (no figure).
driver_status: RDL 29/2026 (pending convalidation). If it lapses, pricing is free again outside Catalonia.
solved_today: nightly-rate tools such as PriceLabs; no mid-term-specific features were documented.
software_solvable: partly. Compliance-aware initial pricing and IRAV tracking can be built; dynamic repricing of temporary leases is legally neutralised while the decree stands.
confidence: medium. The law is clear; reading it to cover different tenants on the same flat is literal.

title: Relocating employees and "try-out" movers don't fit the temporary-displacement cause
who: relocating employees on indefinite contracts, people testing a city before moving, nomads with no home abroad; the landlords who screen them.
where: national; Catalonia.
reality: someone moving their life to Spain needs a first base for months, but a temporary lease needs displacement from a habitual home elsewhere. Landlords either risk re-classification or refuse these tenants.
evidence:
- A Coruña: "trial" stay not a valid cause. — [idealista, 6 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/07/06/901838-la-clave-no-es-la-duracion-cuando-un-alquiler-de-temporada-pasa-a-ser-de-vivienda)
- Albacete: an indefinite job contract is inconsistent with a temporary lease. — [OCU, 19 Jan 2026](https://www.ocu.org/fincas-y-casas/gestion/alquiler/analisis/2026/01/caso-fraude-alquiler-temporada)
- Nomad cause weak if "moving their life here". — [Lázaro Amable, 22 Oct 2026](https://lazaroamable.com/blog/alquiler-temporada-canarias-contrato-temporal)
scale: part of the 422,000 people Consumo says would prefer habitual leases. — [idealista, 7 Sep 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/finanzas/economia/2026/09/07/912998-consumo-estima-que-mas-de-un-millon-de-personas-vive-en-alquiler-de-temporada-o-de)
cost_impact: exclusion or re-classification risk (no figure).
driver_status: RDL 29/2026 art. 2.3 / 7.2 (pending convalidation); Llei 11/2025 (in force); case law.
solved_today: corporate housing (Blueground), coliving and rooms; employers' relocation services.
software_solvable: partly. A tool can triage the tenant profile to the right contract type and evidence pack; the legal mismatch remains.

title: Utilities and service charges: all-inclusive pricing under legal scrutiny
who: mid-term landlords and coliving operators who bundle bills, cleaning and "community" fees.
where: national (arts. 17.6–17.7 and 20 LAU); Catalonia; Barcelona coliving cases.
reality: utilities in the tenant's name suggest a habitual lease, so landlords keep the contracts in their own name. But the charges must then be passed on transparently, and in tensioned zones no new charges may push rent above the cap.
evidence:
- Arts. 17.6, 17.7 and 20 (verbatim). — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-20823)
- Utilities in the tenant's name as an indicator of habitual use. — [idealista, 6 Jul 2026](https://www.idealista.com/news/inmobiliario/vivienda/2026/07/06/901838-la-clave-no-es-la-duracion-cuando-un-alquiler-de-temporada-pasa-a-ser-de-vivienda)
- Mandatory extras "freguen el frau de llei". — [Metrópoli Abierta, 2 Mar 2026](https://www.metropoliabierta.cat/el-pols-de-la-ciutat/20260302/negoci-coliving-dispara-barcelona-lombra-frau-llei-dhabitatge/1003742737508_0.html)
scale: all bundled-price mid-term and coliving units (not quantified).
cost_impact: cap breaches (Catalan fines up to €90,000 or €900,000); re-classification evidence.
driver_status: RDL 29/2026 (pending convalidation); Llei 11/2025 (in force).
solved_today: flat "gastos incluidos" pricing, legally risky in caps.
software_solvable: yes. Metered or allocated utility billing with cap-aware invoices fits well.

title: Steady attrition of neighbourhood shops (cierre del comercio de proximidad)
who: Independent retail run by autónomos and micro-businesses (<10 staff): bakeries, butchers, newsagents, jewellers, appliance shops, haberdashers, stationers, bookshops.
where: National. Best documented in the Comunidad de Madrid and the city of Barcelona.
reality: Owners face rising fixed costs (rent, energy, compliance) against flat neighbourhood demand. Many close at retirement or lease renewal rather than reinvest. The Madrid retail confederation (COCEM) complains that small shops carry big-store obligations: *"Se le pide lo mismo a una panadería de barrio que a una gran superficie"* ("a neighbourhood bakery is asked for the same as a hypermarket").
evidence:
- UPTA counted 13,586 fewer small retail businesses in 2025, about 1,132 per month. December 2025 alone lost 2,347, against 1,748 in December 2024. There were 716,637 retail affiliates in December 2025, and UPTA expects more than 12,000 closures in 2026 without action. — [Talent24h/OKDIARIO, 23 Jan 2026](https://talent24h.okdiario.com/2025-pone-en-jaque-al-pequeno-comercio-de-espana-con-mas-de-13-500-negocios-en-dicho-ano/). The same article also cites "586 small shops closed" in December with no explanation, which conflicts with the 2,347 figure.
- UPTA's president repeats "más de 13.500 pequeños negocios se han cerrado el año pasado" and blames "la especulación inmobiliaria" (property speculation). — [El Español, 17 Apr 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/sociedad/20260417/espana-pierde-comercios-cierran-negocios-subida-alquiler-genera-crisis-sector/1003744206489_0.html). This is the same originating source as above, not an independent one.
- INE data show the Comunidad de Madrid's "comercios de barrio" falling from 50,853 (2020) to 43,769 (2024), down 14% or 7,084 shops. The steepest year was 2023, with about 6,000 closures. COCEM sector data: butchers −24% over 5 years, appliance shops −14% over 2 years, jewellers −20%, press/newsagents −62%. — [Madrid Informa, 19 Jul 2025, updated 9 Mar 2026](https://madridinforma.es/?p=38863). The headline frames the 7,084 drop as "one year", but the data cover 2020–2024.
- In Barcelona, at least 10 emblematic shops closed in 2025, including Ferretería Lanza (1928), Papelería Lesseps (1909), Perfumería Regia (97 years), Bolsos Ballester (115 years) and Muebles Cáceres (80 years). — [Ara, 3 Jan 2026](https://es.ara.cat/sociedad/barcelona/barcelona-esfuma-comercios-emblematicos-han-cerrado-2025_130_5608130.html)
- El Español's claim of "at least 400" small-business closures in Jan–Apr 2026 is inconsistent with UPTA's monthly rate. Treat it as unreliable.
scale: About 13.6k net closures a year nationally (UPTA), out of 716,637 retail affiliates (Dec 2025).
cost_impact: Business closures. The causes UPTA cites are rising fixed costs, tax pressure, "competencia desigual con grandes plataformas" (unequal competition with big platforms) and missing public policy.
driver_status: Market forces: rent, costs, online competition, demographics. No single regulation drives it. Status: ongoing in 2026, per UPTA's forecast.
solved_today: No tool evidence found. Municipal and regional support schemes belong to the subsidies researcher.
software_solvable: Partly. The main drivers (rent, succession, demand) are structural. Software can only cut admin cost or lift footfall at the margin.
confidence: High on the trend; medium on exact counts, which come from UPTA and INE as reported by the press.

title: Commercial rent shocks at lease renewal
who: Shops, bars and personal-service micro-businesses (including tattoo studios) on short commercial leases.
where: City-specific. Madrid and Barcelona (Raval, Barri Gòtic, Sant Antoni, Gràcia).
reality: Businesses that are still profitable close or are sold on (traspaso) when the landlord doubles or quadruples the rent at renewal. The Raval traders' association: *"estamos perdiendo tejido empresarial, está quedando un monocultivo de gente de grandes franquicias"* ("we are losing our business fabric; what's left is a monoculture of big franchises").
evidence:
- Average commercial rent in Madrid and Barcelona is €19.2–21.3/m², or €1,536–1,704 a month for 80 m². A Raval restaurant's rent rose from €800 to €1,400, with a renewal quote of more than €2,400. A tattoo studio open 8 years saw rent go from €1,600 to €2,100, and the owner sold the business even though it *"era rentable"* ("it was profitable"). — [El Español, 17 Apr 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/sociedad/20260417/espana-pierde-comercios-cierran-negocios-subida-alquiler-genera-crisis-sector/1003744206489_0.html). The article's national €15/m² figure is inconsistently labelled.
- Bar Kasparo (Barcelona) closed after 30 years when the landlord wanted to quadruple the rent. Discos Revólver closed citing very high rent. La Casa de las Zapatillas had already been pushed out of its premises by property pressure in 2022. — [Ara, 3 Jan 2026](https://es.ara.cat/sociedad/barcelona/barcelona-esfuma-comercios-emblematicos-han-cerrado-2025_130_5608130.html)
- In Madrid, rising rents, unaffordable business transfers ("traspasos inasumibles") and premises left empty for years are cited as closure causes. — [Madrid Informa, Jul 2025](https://madridinforma.es/?p=38863)
scale: Not quantified nationally (gap).
cost_impact: +31% (tattoo studio), +75% (restaurant), up to 4× (Kasparo), in individual cases.
driver_status: Real-estate and tourism pressure. Commercial leases are freely negotiated under the Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos; this is general knowledge, not verified in this session. No pending regulation found.
solved_today: Renegotiation, moving or selling the business. No software evidence.
software_solvable: Mostly no. At most: rent benchmarks, renewal alerts and relocation search.
confidence: Medium. Case evidence comes from two outlets; the rent averages from one.

title: No successor: retiring owners cannot sell or hand over the shop
who: Long-established family shops (autónomos and micro).
where: Barcelona and Madrid documented; likely national.
reality: An owner reaches retirement (one aged 82) with no heir or buyer, and the shop's goodwill vanishes when it closes.
evidence: In Barcelona: Ferretería Lanza (owner retired at 82, no successor), Papelería Lesseps (no buyer found; customers had shifted to Amazon), Bolsos Ballester (no generational succession after 115 years) and Muebles Cáceres (retirement). — [Ara, 3 Jan 2026](https://es.ara.cat/sociedad/barcelona/barcelona-esfuma-comercios-emblematicos-han-cerrado-2025_130_5608130.html). In Madrid, lack of generational succession is cited as a closure driver. — [Madrid Informa, Jul 2025](https://madridinforma.es/?p=38863)
scale: Not quantified (gap).
cost_impact: Lost sale value and closure.
driver_status: Demographics and market. No regulation.
solved_today: No evidence found on transfer marketplaces or gestorías.
software_solvable: Partly. Matching buyers and sellers, and valuation, could help. The core problem is that many of these businesses are no longer attractive to buy.

title: Repeat shoplifting (multirreincidencia), staff aggression, and the evidence burden under the new penal reform
who: All physical retail; food retail is most affected and small shops suffer most.
where: National.
reality: The same people steal repeatedly. Staff report more verbal and physical aggression, and security guards are hard to hire. Since 10 April 2026, a petty thief can face the prison penalty of art. 234.1 CP once they have three prior final convictions. In practice a conviction record exists only if incidents are reported and prosecuted (inference).
evidence:
- The Barómetro del Hurto 2025 (Checkpoint Systems and AECOC) puts unknown loss at €2,817M, or 1.1% of turnover, up from 0.74% (about €1,800M). Breakdown: external theft 59%, internal theft 18%, administrative errors 15%, supplier fraud 9%. 51% of thefts are by repeat offenders (3 or more a year), 48% of whom are under 30. 74% of respondents say aggression towards staff has risen a lot, and 65% find security staff increasingly hard to hire. — [The Objective, 4 Nov 2025](https://theobjective.com/economia/2025-11-04/hurtos-perdida-2817-millones-comercios-espanoles/)
- AECOC (via Europa Press) gives more than €2,800M a year and the same 51% figure, and adds that small shops suffer on average 30% more thefts because they have fewer security resources. It welcomed the reform's removal of the €400 cumulative-value threshold. — [Última Hora, 5 Dec 2025](https://www.ultimahora.es/noticias/comunidades/2025/12/05/2525909/aecoc-celebra-reforma-multirreincidencia-causa-perdidas-comerciales-2800-millones.html). Conflict: Ara cites €2,917M for the same barometer **(snippet)**. — [Ara](https://es.ara.cat/economia/comercio/aceite-perfumes-ropa-interior-son-productos-robados-tiendas_1_5551266.html). Its headline names olive oil, perfume and underwear as the most-stolen goods.
- **Ley Orgánica 1/2026, de 8 de abril, en materia de multirreincidencia** was published in the BOE on 9 April 2026 and entered into force on 10 April 2026 ("al día siguiente de su publicación"). Its main changes:
- Art. 234 applies the art. 234.1 penalty when the offender has at least three final convictions for offences under the same title, at least one of them a delito leve.
- Art. 22.8 still excludes prior delitos leves from reincidencia, except where they form part of the multirreincidencia aggravation (hurto and estafa).
- A new art. 235.10.º aggravates theft of mobile phones.
- New LECrim art. 105.3 lets local authorities bring criminal actions for theft.
- LECrim art. 544 bis allows precautionary bans on going to specified places.
— [BOE consolidated text](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/lo/2026/04/08/1/con). A legal commentary says repeat thieves of goods under €400 can now get 6–18 months' prison instead of a fine **(snippet)**. — [LegalToday, 10 Apr 2026](https://www.legaltoday.com/opinion/articulos-de-opinion/la-reforma-penal-de-la-multirreincidencia-un-nuevo-modelo-de-respuesta-frente-a-la-delincuencia-reiterada-2026-04-10/). Conflict: the same snippet says the rule needs "at least three thefts for a joint amount over €400". That contradicts AECOC (the €400 cumulative threshold is removed) and the BOE text (three prior final convictions, no value threshold mentioned). Rely on the BOE text.
scale: All physical retail; €2.8bn a year.
cost_impact: 1.1% of turnover, and 30% more thefts in small shops.
driver_status: LO 1/2026, **in force since 10 April 2026**.
solved_today: Electronic article surveillance (EAS) tags, CCTV and security guards; 65% report trouble hiring guards. Checkpoint Systems, a tag vendor, co-authors the barometer. No prices found.
software_solvable: Partly. Incident logging, packaging CCTV clips, preparing police reports (denuncias) consistently, and district-level alerts (within GDPR limits) all help. Physical deterrence and policing do not.
confidence: High on loss figures and the law; medium on small-shop specifics.

title: Card-acceptance fees and a fragmented payments stack, with Bizum arriving at the till
who: All retail and personal services. Low-volume autónomos are most exposed.
where: National.
reality: Shops pay a percentage on every card payment plus terminal fees. Many nudge customers towards cash or Bizum. Bizum in-store payments started on 18 May 2026, unevenly, and their pricing has not been published.
evidence:
- Merchants pay 0.5–2% per card transaction depending on business type and volume. Bizum's in-store pricing "aún no se ha hecho público". Bizum has more than 27M users. — [Diario de León, 18 May 2026](https://www.diariodeleon.es/sociedad/260518/2085361/bizum-llega-comercio-fisico-desafia-duopolio-tarjetas-tradicionales.html)
- Card fees are 0.3–1.5% depending on contract. Bizum entered store and supermarket terminals from 18 May 2026 with a staggered rollout and more than 28M users. Its fees are described as "más liviana" (lighter) than cards, with no figure given. — [Moncloa.com, 29 Apr 2026](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/04/29/bizum-supermercados-tiendas-18-mayo-3374007/)
- SumUp Spain charges 1.49% per in-person card payment on pay-as-you-go, or 0% when the customer pays with a SumUp card. Pagos Plus costs €19/month, TPV Plus (POS) €49/month and Facturas Plus €10/month. — [SumUp pricing, accessed Oct 2026](https://www.sumup.com/es-es/precios/)
- Shopify POS charges 2.6% + 10¢ per in-person payment on Basic, and POS Pro costs $89/month per location. The page showed USD to our fetcher, so EUR prices were not seen. — [Shopify pricing, accessed Oct 2026](https://www.shopify.com/es-es/precios)
- BBVA has added Bizum to its Android terminals; a second terminal costs €3.5 + IVA **(snippet, single source)**. — [Finantres](https://finantresnoticias.com/negocios-y-autonomos/bizum-para-empresas-bbva-lo-lleva-al-tpv-fisico/)
scale: Every card-accepting business; no count found.
cost_impact: Illustration: at 1.49%, a shop taking €10,000 a month by card pays about €149 a month.
driver_status: Market pricing by acquirers. Bizum in-store **launched 18 May 2026** (market development, not regulation).
solved_today: Bank terminals, SumUp, Shopify POS, Bizum and cash.
software_solvable: Partly. Fee audits and steering customers to cheaper payment methods (Bizum, account-to-account) are possible. The fees themselves are set by acquirers.
confidence: Medium. Sources disagree on the range (0.3–1.5% vs 0.5–2%).

title: Ultra-low-cost cross-border platforms (Temu, Shein, AliExpress) undercutting local shops
who: Retailers of fashion, accessories, toys, homeware and gadgets (micro and small), and Spanish online SMEs in the same categories.
where: National.
reality: Local shops compete with parcels that entered duty-free until July 2026, often priced below local wholesale. Customers browse in-store and then buy online.
evidence:
- About 12 million parcels a day reach the EU from Temu, Shein and similar platforms. There were 4,600 million shipments in 2024, 91% from China. The European Commission counts about 5,900 million low-value items that reached consumers duty-free in 2025. — [OCU, 1 Jul 2026](https://www.ocu.org/consumo-familia/compras-online/noticias/tasa-aduana-paquetes-baratos)
- A fixed EU duty of €3 per product category now applies to parcels under €150 from outside the EU, from 1 July 2026 until about 1 July 2028. — [OCU, 1 Jul 2026](https://www.ocu.org/consumo-familia/compras-online/noticias/tasa-aduana-paquetes-baratos). RTVC calls it temporary until the 2028 customs reform **(snippet)**. — [RTVC, 2 Jul 2026](https://rtvc.es/entra-en-vigor-la-tasa-de-3-euros-para-compras-en-plataformas-como-shein-temu-y-aliexpress-2-julio-2026/). Euronews describes it as €3 per item, which conflicts on the calculation **(snippet)**. — [Euronews, 1 Jul 2026](https://es.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/07/01/se-acabo-comprar-sin-impuestos-en-shein-temu-y-aliexpress-la-ue-impone-un-nuevo-recargo). A separate handling fee "by 1 Nov 2026" appears in a single, unverified source **(snippet)**. — [Revista Mercado](https://revistamercado.do/technology/devices/el-fin-de-las-compras-baratas-en-shein-y-temu-la-medida-arancelaria-en-europa-que-frena-su-exito/)
- UPTA names "competencia desigual con grandes plataformas" as a closure cause. — [Talent24h, 23 Jan 2026](https://talent24h.okdiario.com/2025-pone-en-jaque-al-pequeno-comercio-de-espana-con-mas-de-13-500-negocios-en-dicho-ano/). Papelería Lesseps' customers moved to Amazon. — [Ara, 3 Jan 2026](https://es.ara.cat/sociedad/barcelona/barcelona-esfuma-comercios-emblematicos-han-cerrado-2025_130_5608130.html)
scale: National; billions of items a year EU-wide.
cost_impact: Impact on Spanish shops' sales not quantified (gap).
driver_status: EU €3 customs duty **in force since 1 Jul 2026** (temporary). Handling fee unverified.
solved_today: Not applicable.
software_solvable: No. This is a market and trade-policy force.
confidence: High on volumes and the duty; low on the Spanish impact.

title: Thin or decaying web presence after Kit Digital
who: Micro-businesses (<10) and autónomos in retail and services.
where: National.
reality: Most micro firms still have no website. Subsidised sites were often built fast with little SEO. After the subsidised period, owners either pay for maintenance or let the site lapse; the lapsing part is partly inference.
evidence:
- INE figures (published Apr 2025), as reported by Asest: 29.6% of companies with fewer than 10 employees had a website, against 33.2% in 2024. That leaves about 70%, or roughly 2.4M autónomos and micro firms, without one. The same article claims 37.0% a year after 33.2%, an internal contradiction. It also cites Kit Digital vouchers of up to €12,000 and a typical agency site at €600–1,500 plus monthly maintenance (unsourced). — [Asest (undated)](https://asest.es/story/pymes-y-autonomos-sin-web/)
- On Kit Digital providers: *"la calidad de los entregables suele ser la sacrificada en pro de entregar cuanto antes"* ("the quality of deliverables is usually sacrificed in order to deliver as fast as possible"). The article also says SEO management can be "prohibitivo" (prohibitively expensive) for small firms. — [Emprendedores, 27 Oct 2023](https://emprendedores.es/notas-de-prensa/el-kit-digital-no-es-la-solucion-a-la-digitalizacion-del-marketing-seo/)
- An individual's opinion: *"muchas de esas webs están completamente abandonadas, desactualizadas o simplemente… no generan resultados"* ("many of those sites are completely abandoned, outdated or simply bring no results") **(snippet; opinion)**. — [LinkedIn profile post](https://es.linkedin.com/in/davidmn)
scale: About 70% of micro firms have no website (Asest's reading of INE).
cost_impact: €600–1,500 to build plus maintenance (unsourced).
driver_status: Kit Digital, funded by NextGenerationEU. **The programme's 2026 status was not verified**: the acelerapyme.gob.es page returned 403.
solved_today: Agencies (agentes digitalizadores), website builders and Google Business Profile.
software_solvable: Yes. Low-cost managed sites, Google Business Profile and review management. It is a crowded market.
confidence: Low-medium. The INE figure is second-hand and the abandonment evidence is anecdotal.

title: Sunday and holiday trading rules, and fights over tourist zones (ZGAT)
who: Small shops competing with large chains.
where: Regional and municipal: Comunitat Valenciana (Benidorm, Alicante), Canarias (Arafo, Santa Úrsula), La Rioja, Castilla y León.
reality: Small retailers oppose declarations of zonas de gran afluencia turística (ZGAT) that let big stores open on Sundays. They also have to track annual lists of permitted Sundays, which differ by region and municipality.
evidence:
- Benidorm 2026: shops without free trading hours may open 11 Sundays and holidays. Shops under 300 m² have general freedom of hours, unless they belong to non-SME groups **(snippet)**. — [Benidorm, Horarios comerciales 2026 (PDF, Feb 2026)](https://contenidos.benidorm.org/sites/default/files/descargas/2026-02/HORARIOS%20COMERCIALES%202026.pdf)
- Alicante is a ZGAT with an extended period from 15 June to 5 January. The Observatorio del Comercio Valenciano proposes 11 Sundays **(snippet)**. — [Ayuntamiento de Alicante](https://www.alicante.es/es/node/46360)
- In Canarias, Arafo's consultation on a ZGAT declaration drew opposition from unions, neighbourhood associations and small local retail. In Santa Úrsula the PP accused the local government of abandoning small retail **(snippet)**. — [Diario de Avisos, Jun 2026](https://diariodeavisos.elespanol.com/2026/06/arafo-apertura-dominical-poligonos/)
- La Rioja allows 10 Sundays or holidays a year. — [La Rioja](https://www.larioja.org/comercio/es/apertura-festivos-domingos/festivos-habiles-2026)
scale: A national patchwork.
cost_impact: Not quantified.
driver_status: Regional trading-hours rules on top of the state framework; the state law was not verified in this session. 2026 calendars **in force**.
solved_today: Regional calendars and lobbying by associations.
software_solvable: No. This is political; software could offer at most a calendar lookup.
confidence: Medium on the rules; low as a quantified pain.

title: Compliance with the 30-day "precio anterior" rule on discounts (rebajas, Black Friday)
who: Every physical and online retailer that advertises price reductions.
where: National.
reality: Every advertised discount must be measured against the lowest price charged in the previous 30 days. Shops without price-history records risk fines (the risk is inference; no enforcement data found).
evidence: Ley 7/1996 art. 20.1 defines the "precio anterior" as *"el menor que hubiese sido aplicado sobre productos idénticos en los treinta días precedentes"* ("the lowest price applied to identical products in the preceding thirty days"). The paragraph was modified by RDL 24/2021, effective 28 May 2022. Fines: leve up to €6,000; grave €6,000–30,000; muy grave €30,000–900,000 (art. 68). — [BOE, consolidated Ley 7/1996](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1996-1072). Single official source; no data found on enforcement campaigns.
scale: All retailers.
cost_impact: Fines as above.
driver_status: Ley 7/1996 art. 20, **in force** (current wording since 28 May 2022).
solved_today: Not researched (POS and e-commerce price-history features).
software_solvable: Yes. Automatic logging of the 30-day lowest price and compliant labels or badges.
confidence: Medium. The rule is verified; how much it hurts is unverified.

title: WhatsApp selling and reminders become metered (Meta per-message pricing)
who: Shops and service businesses that send notifications, appointment reminders or promotions through the WhatsApp Business Platform (API) via a provider. Users of the free WhatsApp Business app are not affected.
where: National (Spain is a standalone market on Meta's rate card).
reality: Reminders, order updates and promotions are billed per delivered message. From 1 Oct 2026, utility messages sent inside an open 24-hour service window are charged too.
evidence: Per-message pricing since 1 Jul 2025. Spain's marketing rate rose on 1 Jul 2026. Since 1 Oct 2026, utility messages inside an open service window, and service messages beyond the free 1,000 a month, are chargeable. — [Meta for Developers, WhatsApp pricing, accessed Oct 2026](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/pricing/). Booksy includes 100 marketing SMS a month and prices bigger campaigns on request. — [Pabau, 8 Oct 2026](https://pabau.com/es/blog/booksy-precio/)

cost_impact: Spain's per-message rates sit in a rate-card file that was not captured.
driver_status: Meta pricing (market). Changes on 1 Jul 2025, 1 Jul 2026 and **1 Oct 2026 (in effect)**.

title: Returns: high volume, serial and late returners, and pressure to keep returns free
who: Online SMEs in fashion, footwear and electronics (micro to medium).
where: National.
reality: About a quarter of non-food orders come back. Consumers punish shops that charge for returns. A minority of serial and late returners consume a large share of margin.
evidence:
- ZigZag and Retail Economics estimate €13,300M of online returns by end-2025. 23.7% of non-food orders are returned (clothing 31%, footwear 27%, electronics 23%). Serial returners are 11% of shoppers but account for 23% of returns (about €2,600M), with a return rate near 48%. Late returners are 14% of shoppers and 24% of returns. The average return takes 9.1 days, and 32% come back after 10 days. — [Law&Trends, 28 Oct 2025](https://www.lawandtrends.com/noticias/consumidores/las-devoluciones-online-en-espana-superan-los-13-300-millones-en-2025-1.html). ZigZag sells returns software, so it has an interest in the topic.
- Per idealo, 35% of Spaniards might stop buying from shops that charge for returns **(snippet; date not seen)**. — [Forbes](https://forbes.es/ultima-hora/255575/tres-de-cada-diez-espanoles-podrian-dejar-de-comprar-en-tiendas-que-cobren-por-las-devoluciones-online/). Per Veepee and IESE, only 21% are willing to pay for returns, and never more than 10% of the price **(snippet; 2022)**. — [Modaes](https://www.modaes.com/entorno/las-devoluciones-siguen-frenando-el-online-solo-el-21-esta-dispuestos-a-pagarlas)
scale: All online fashion and electronics sellers.
cost_impact: €13.3bn of returned goods value. Handling cost per return not found.
driver_status: Consumer expectations of free returns, plus the statutory 14-day withdrawal right (general knowledge, not re-verified). **In force.**
solved_today: Returns portals and multi-carrier tools: ShippyPro Professional at €207.20/month for 4,000 labels; Outvio at an estimated ~€375/month (€4,500/year), a figure from its competitor ShippyPro. — [ShippyPro comparison, Apr 2026](https://www.shippypro.com/es/shippypro-vs-outvio). Sendcloud has a free plan and a "Lite" plan at €28/month billed annually **(snippet; page blocked)**. — [Hackceleration, Jun 2026](https://hackceleration.com/es/labs/sendcloud-precio)
software_solvable: Yes. Returns analytics, serial-returner detection, exchange-first flows and fit/sizing tools.
confidence: High on volume; medium on cost.

title: Parcels damaged in transit, and the packaging trade-off
who: Online retailers of all sizes.
where: National.
reality: About 5.5% of parcels arrive damaged. Retailers absorb the reshipments and returns while also being pushed to use less packaging (RET-15).
evidence:
A DS Smith study of about 100 executives at Spanish online retailers found:
- 15.2M items returned each year because of shipping damage, and 5.5% of parcels arriving damaged.
- 21% of shoppers received a damaged item in 2025, and 88% of retailers call it a problem.
- Total cost above €1,000M a year (average damaged item worth €68). Retailers spend on average €30,876 a year handling damaged returns, and large distributors more than €500,000.
- Causes: rough handling 57%, packaging deficiencies 27%, weather and temperature 16%. 58% of consumers would be less likely to reorder after a damaged delivery.
— [Alimarket, 16 Jan 2026](https://www.alimarket.es/envase/noticia/419911/el-ecommerce-en-espana-cierra-el-ano-con-15-2-m-de-articulos-devueltos-por-danos-durante-el-envio). This is a single source, sponsored by a packaging maker.
scale: As above.
driver_status: Carrier handling (market). PPWR empty-space limits mostly apply from 2030 (see RET-15).
solved_today: Carrier claims and packaging suppliers. No tool prices found.
software_solvable: Partly. Automating carrier claims, damage analytics by carrier and route, and choosing the right box.

title: Marketplace fee stacks (Amazon) and opaque margins
who: Online SMEs selling on Amazon.es.
where: National.
reality: Sellers stack a monthly fee, a referral fee, fulfilment and storage fees and surcharges, so the margin per product is hard to see. (Ad costs not found.)
evidence:
Amazon.es fees:
- Professional plan €39/month; Individual plan €0.99 per item.
- Referral fees are typically 8–15%. Fashion: 5% up to €15, 10% from €15 to €20, 15% above €20. Home: 8% up to €20, then 15%. Beauty: 8% up to €10, then 15%. Electronics: 7%. Minimum €0.30 per item.
- FBA storage costs €19.99–27.54 per m³ a month in Jan–Sep and €29.23–52.20 in Oct–Dec.
- A 1.5% fuel and logistics surcharge applies to FBA fees from 17 Apr 2026.
- When Amazon refunds the referral fee on a refund, it keeps the lower of €5 or 20% of that fee.
- Fee cuts on 15 Dec 2025 (clothing referral 8%→5% up to €15) and 5 Jan 2026 (home 15%→8% up to €20; low-price FBA rates extended to €20).
— [Amazon Sell Spain, accessed Oct 2026](https://sell.amazon.es/precios). Single official source. Miravia and other marketplaces not found.
scale: Not found (gap: number of Spanish SMEs selling on Amazon).
cost_impact: Commonly 15% referral plus fulfilment and storage, before advertising.
driver_status: Market. Fee changes Dec 2025–Apr 2026.
solved_today: Not researched (Seller Central reports, third-party profit tools).
software_solvable: Partly. Per-product profitability and fee audits; Amazon sets the fees.
confidence: Medium (fees verified; seller complaints not captured).

title: Selling and shipping to the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla
who: Online SMEs on the peninsula that sell to the islands, plus Canarian buyers and businesses.
where: Regional: Canarias, Ceuta, Melilla.
reality: Many shops simply refuse: *"No realizamos envíos a Canarias, Ceuta y Melilla"*. Buyers face courier "gestión aduanera" (customs handling) fees even below €150. Sellers have to deal with the islands' own taxes (IGIC, AIEM, and IPSI in Ceuta and Melilla) and with customs declarations (DUA).
evidence:
- Per Idealo, more than 60% of online shops do not ship to Canarias and only about 4% offer urgent delivery.
- IGIC's general rate is 7%; AIEM's general rate is 5%. The DUA has been waived for goods under €150 since 2017, and the Canarian tax agency extended the IGIC exemption under €150 in June 2021.
- Couriers still charge handling fees. Examples: €15 of fees on a €30 dress, and €30 of "other taxes" on shoes.
— [Xataka, 16 Jan 2022](https://www.xataka.com/servicios/comprar-online-canarias-se-ha-convertido-dolor-cabeza-para-usuarios-asi-odisea-para-adquirir-productos-islas) (older source).
- A petition started 17 Jul 2026 says couriers' "gestión aduanera" and "presentación al despacho" fees *"a veces duplican el valor del producto"* ("sometimes double the product's value"). It asks for a ban on such fees under €150 and on transport geoblocking. It had only 3 signatures, so it is weak evidence of salience but confirms the practice continues. — [Change.org, Jul 2026](https://www.change.org/p/envíos-justos-y-sin-bloqueos-para-canarias-ceuta-y-melilla)
scale: Over 60% of shops not shipping (2021–22 data). Number of affected buyers not cited.
cost_impact: €15–30 per parcel in documented cases; lost sales for sellers who don't ship.
driver_status: Canarias sits outside the EU VAT area (IGIC/AIEM under its special tax regime); Ceuta and Melilla use IPSI. **In force; no 2024–2026 change verified**, as Canarian tax agency updates could not be checked.
solved_today: Correos, customs agents and couriers' DUA services. No prices found.
software_solvable: Yes or partly. Landed cost at checkout (IGIC/AIEM), automated customs data, and choosing carriers for the islands.
confidence: Medium on the structure; low on current 2026 numbers.

title: Packaging EPR: registration, annual declarations, and the EU packaging regulation (PPWR) from 12 Aug 2026
who: Anyone who packs goods or first places packaged goods on the Spanish market, including online shops shipping their own products, importers and intra-EU buyers. Marketplaces and couriers are liable in some cases.
where: National, plus the EU layer.
reality: A seller needs a producer registration number (it must appear on invoices), proof of membership of a collective compliance scheme (SCRAP), packaging data by material filed every 31 March, and since 12 Aug 2026 the PPWR declarations of conformity and marking. Distributors must refuse products from unregistered producers.
evidence:
- From the consolidated text of RD 1055/2022 ([BOE](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2022-22690); no later amendments shown, accessed Oct 2026):
- Producers had to register in the envases section of the Registro de Productores de Producto within 3 months. A single, simplified registration applies to service packaging and to producers placing under 50,000 kg of commercial/industrial packaging. The registration number must appear on invoices and commercial documents (art. 15).
- Annual market data are due before 31 March, in simplified form for producers under 15 t a year, certain e-commerce platforms and some first distributors (art. 16).
- Producers established outside Spain must appoint a Spanish authorised representative; otherwise the first distributor is liable. In distance sales, couriers take on the financial and reporting duties for transport packaging, and e-commerce platforms do the same for third-party sellers' goods (art. 17).
- Distributors, in store or at a distance, may only sell products from producers that have a registration number (arts. 28–30).
- Producers not previously in a scheme had to set up schemes by 31 Dec 2024 (transitional provision DT3.1). New marking duties (art. 13) apply from 1 Jan 2025 (final provision DF5).
- Shops of 300 m² or more must inform customers on packaging (from 1 Jan 2023). Food stores of 400 m² or more must devote at least 20% of sales area to unpackaged goods (art. 7.4).
- The PPWR (EU 2025/40) applies from 12 Aug 2026 and repeals Directive 94/62/EC. It requires a Declaration of Conformity and marking that links the packaging to it and identifies the responsible operator. Empty-space limits, recycled content and recyclability rules mostly arrive from 2030. — [Interempresas (GENCI), 22 Jul 2026](https://www.interempresas.net/PrimeraPagina/652360-El-envase-profesional-ante-el-Reglamento-europeo.html)
- Cartón Circular, a scheme for industrial packaging, has published its 2026 tariff **(snippet)**. — [Industriambiente, Oct 2025](https://www.industriambiente.com/media/uploads/noticias/documentos/ENTREVISTA_A_CARTON_CIRCULAR-web.pdf)
scale: All packers and first placers on the market; number not found.
cost_impact: Scheme fees and fine amounts not captured (gap).
driver_status: RD 1055/2022 **in force since 29 Dec 2022** (deadlines of 31 Dec 2024 and 1 Jan 2025 have passed). PPWR (EU) 2025/40 **applies since 12 Aug 2026**, with later milestones from 2030.
solved_today: Collective schemes (GENCI and Cartón Circular for commercial and industrial packaging), consultants and gestorías. No prices found.
software_solvable: Yes. Capturing packaging bills of materials and weights by material, generating declarations and PPWR declarations of conformity, and checking suppliers' registration numbers.
confidence: High on the rules; low on how much it hurts and what it costs.

title: Plastic packaging tax paperwork (Impuesto especial sobre los envases de plástico no reutilizables)
who: Manufacturers, importers and intra-EU buyers of non-reusable plastic packaging. This includes online SMEs importing packaged goods with more than 5 kg a month of non-recycled plastic.
where: National.
reality: Above the 5 kg a month threshold, a seller must register, keep a stock ledger, file self-assessments (modelo 592) and hold certificates of recycled content.
evidence:
From Ley 7/2022 ([BOE consolidated text](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2022-5809)):
- The rate is €0.45 per kg of non-recycled plastic (art. 78).
- Imports or intra-EU acquisitions are exempt when their non-recycled plastic does not exceed 5 kg a month (art. 75.f).
- Taxpayers must register in the Registro territorial, and intra-EU buyers must keep a libro registro de existencias (stock ledger) (art. 82).
- Recycled content must be certified under UNE-EN 15343:2008 by an ENAC-accredited body (art. 77.3).
- Fines: €1,000 for failing to register; €75 per incorrect invoice or certificate (art. 83).
- The AEAT page (updated 20 Oct 2026) lists modelo 592 and modelo A22 (refunds) under Orden HFP/1314/2022, and Nota Informativa 19/2024 on the art. 75 pre-declaration. — [AEAT](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/impuestos-especiales-medioambientales/impuesto-especial-sobre-envases-plastico-reutilizables.html)
scale: Unknown.
cost_impact: The tax itself plus admin time; fines as above.
driver_status: Ley 7/2022, **in force**. The 2023 start date is general knowledge; the AEAT guidance is current as of Oct 2026.
solved_today: Gestorías, ERP systems and certification bodies.
software_solvable: Yes. Computing kilograms from purchase data, keeping the stock ledger and filing modelo 592. This overlaps with the tax researcher.
confidence: High on the rules; low on the pain's intensity.

title: Web accessibility obligations for online shops (EAA / Ley 11/2023)
who: Online shops with 10 or more employees or €2M or more turnover. Microenterprises providing services are exempt.
where: National, transposing EU law.
reality: The whole buying journey (site or app, product information, checkout and payments, search, customer service, invoices) must meet WCAG 2.1 AA and EN 301 549.
evidence: Applies from 28 Jun 2025. The only exemption is for microenterprises (fewer than 10 employees and under €2M turnover). Sanctions include fines, suspension of the service or taking the website down. — [Legalitas, 12 Jan 2026](https://www.legalitas.com/actualidad/european-accessibility-act). Sanctions follow each sector's regime, with Title III of RDL 1/2013 as a fallback **(snippet)**. — [Cuatrecasas](https://www.cuatrecasas.com/es/portugal/propiedad-intelectual/art/claves-proxima-entrada-vigor-ley-accesibilidad-espana). The microenterprise exemption covers services and generally not manufacturers of physical products **(snippet)**. — [captcha.eu](https://www.captcha.eu/what-is-ley-11-2023/)
scale: Small (10–49) and medium online sellers; count not found.
cost_impact: Audit and remediation costs; fine amounts not found.
driver_status: Ley 11/2023 / Directive 2019/882, **in force since 28 Jun 2025**.
solved_today: Accessibility audits and overlay tools; no prices found.
software_solvable: Partly. Automated scanning and monitoring help; full compliance needs design and development work.
confidence: Medium. The law is clear; no enforcement data found.

title: Product-safety information on online listings (GPSR)
who: Online and marketplace sellers of consumer products, including second-hand and refurbished goods.
where: EU-wide, and therefore national.
reality: Each listing must carry the manufacturer or EU responsible-person details and safety information. Marketplaces enforce this.
evidence: The GPSR (EU) 2023/988 applies from 13 Dec 2024 to products offered online to EU consumers, including used and refurbished ones. Marketplaces need a single point of contact and must act quickly on dangerous products. — [CCPC (Ireland), 13 Dec 2024](https://www.ccpc.ie/news-and-media/news/article/2024/12/13/new-eu-product-safety-laws-now-in-place). Spanish evidence is thin: a Spanish toy makers' association (AEFJ) petition on unsafe marketplace products **(snippet)**.
scale: Not found.
driver_status: GPSR, **in force since 13 Dec 2024**.
solved_today: Compliance-service providers (the search showed vendor blogs only).
software_solvable: Yes. Managing product compliance data and pushing it to listings.

title: Booking marketplaces: commissions, lock-ins and no-shows
who: Hair salons, barbers, beauty and nail centres (autónomos and micro), and boutique fitness studios.
where: National.
reality: Salons use Booksy and Treatwell for visibility and online booking, and pay a commission on marketplace-sourced first visits. Owners complain of being charged even when the client doesn't show, of support that doesn't answer, and of 12-month contracts.
evidence:
- Treatwell charges a 25% commission on first bookings by new marketplace clients, 0% on repeat bookings, and 2% + IVA when the client prepays online. The minimum contract is 12 months. Its Advanced plan bundles VeriFactu/TicketBAI e-invoicing. — [Treatwell pricing, accessed Oct 2026](https://www.treatwell.es/partners/precios/)
- Booksy costs €34.99 + IVA a month plus €8 per extra staff member, with no lock-in. Its "Boost" marketplace promotion takes 30% of a new client's first visit. Payment fees: 2% + €0.15 for mobile payments, 0.99% + €0.10 for Tap to Pay, and 1.5% for instant payouts. — [Booksy blog, 10 Aug 2026](https://biz.booksy.com/es-es/blog/cuanto-cuesta-un-software-de-reservas-para-salones)
- Boost is capped at €50 + IVA per client, and a 5-person team pays about €66.99 + IVA a month. Complaints aggregated from Capterra: poor support, unexpected commissions, weak Boost results, difficulty exporting client data. — [Pabau (competitor), 8 Oct 2026](https://pabau.com/es/blog/booksy-precio/). A second source confirms €34.99 a month and a 7-day trial **(snippet)**. — [La Voz de Ibiza](https://lavozdeibiza.com/?p=163018)
- A salon owner's review of Treatwell: *"comisiones abusivas que cobran, aunque el cliente no venga"* ("abusive commissions they charge even if the client doesn't come"), and partner support described as non-existent. Treatwell replied in March 2025 **(snippet)**. — [Capterra](https://capterra.com/p/181827/Treatwell/reviews/?page=2)
- No Spanish no-show statistics were found. Vendor claims (e.g., AgendaPro) cite unnamed studies.
scale: About 72,300 hairdressing and beauty establishments in 2021 **(snippet; DBK study, Dec 2022)**. — [DBK](https://dbk.es/en/estudios/16575/summary)
cost_impact: Illustration: 25% of a €40 first visit is €10 (Treatwell); 30% is €12 (Booksy Boost).
driver_status: Market.
solved_today: Booksy and Treatwell as above. Koibox from €40/month and Flowww (aesthetics) from €59/month **(Capterra snippets)**. Bewe targets sports centres and salons; no price found.
software_solvable: Yes. Direct booking with deposits or card-on-file, own-channel marketing and client-data portability. The market is crowded.
confidence: Medium. Pricing is solid; the size of the no-show problem is unknown.

title: 21% VAT on hairdressing and beauty services
who: Hairdressers, barbers and beauty centres, mostly autónomos and micro (in 2021, 60% of salons had a single worker).
where: National.
reality: Salons charge 21% VAT. They cannot pass it all on to price-sensitive clients, and they lose business to undeclared home-based work (an intrusismo claim common in the sector; not evidenced in the sources here).
evidence:
- Hairdressing moved from the reduced rate (8%) to 21% in Sept 2012. There were about 50,000 salons before the pandemic and about 35,000 in June 2021. Stanpa warned of 17,000 closures and costed the cut at about €140M. In June 2021 a cut already approved by parliament was vetoed. — [El Independiente, 5 Sep 2021](https://www.elindependiente.com/?p=1801776)
- Six amendments to the 2023 state budget restoring 10% were rejected. Valencian salons' billing was 25.28% below 2019 (national −20.2%) and costs rose 27.2%. The protesters called the repeated vetoes "expolio fiscal" (fiscal plunder). — [Valencia Plaza, 5 Dec 2022](https://valenciaplaza.com/valenciaplaza/peluquerias-valencianas-celebran-una-vigilia-de-luto-para-reclamar-una-reduccion-del-iva-al-10)
- The government blocked amendments using art. 134.6 of the Constitution, putting the cost at €194M. Congress passed two non-binding resolutions, which were ignored **(snippet; date not seen)**. — [Vozpópuli](https://www.vozpopuli.com/actualidad/iva-erc-bng-pp-presupuestos.html)
- Count conflict: DBK's 72,300 establishments (2021) against the sector's own ~35,000 salons (June 2021). The definitions are probably different (DBK includes beauty).
scale: Tens of thousands of establishments (see conflict above). DBK puts 2021 sales at €4,050M **(snippet)**.
cost_impact: An 11-point rate gap on price-sensitive services.
driver_status: Ley 37/1992 (IVA), general rate. **Proposals to cut it have been repeatedly rejected (2021, 2022). No 2025–2026 change was found.** The AEAT page (updated 13 Oct 2026) confirms reduced rates of 10% and 4% but its list of items could not be viewed, so the current rate for hairdressing is not verified at item level.
solved_today: Not applicable.
software_solvable: No (tax policy).

title: Independent gyms squeezed by consolidating low-cost chains
who: Independent gyms, boutique studios and CrossFit boxes (micro and small).
where: National. Madrid, Catalonia and Andalusia hold about 60% of gyms.
reality: Chains backed by private equity open and acquire clubs fast and set a price ceiling of €20–40 a month. Independents compete on niche and service while needing enough members (one estimate says 400–600 active members) to break even.
evidence:
- DBK: €1,500M market in 2024 (+14%), about €1,650M in 2025 (+10%), with +7–8% forecast for 2026. 4,600 gyms in Sept 2025 (+3.5%). The top 5 held 37% and the top 10 54% in 2024, with the rest a fragmented field of small independents. — [Emprendedores, 14 Jan 2026](https://emprendedores.es/franquicias/analisis-sectoriales/gimnasios-oportunidades-en-franquicia-2026/)
- VivaGym+Synergym: more than 450 clubs, over €270M revenue and about 1M members. VivaGym made seven acquisitions in 2025. Basic-Fit Spain grew from 90 to 139 centres in one year. The 15 largest chains lost more than €420M in 2020–2023. Members rose from 4.8M (2022) to 6.2M (end-2024). — [Xataka, 30 Apr 2026](https://www.xataka.com/magnet/gimnasio-se-ha-convertido-nuevo-supermercado-vivagym-compra-synergym-crea-primer-gigante-iberico-fitness)
- An average gym costs €30–50 a month; Basic-Fit and McFIT start from €20; sign-up fees run €30–100. — [eldiario.es, 16 Jan 2025](https://www.eldiario.es/consumoclaro/pagar-cuota-gimnasio-hacerte-equipo-casa-sale-rentable_1_11960124.html)
- More than 6.5M members in 2025, and acquiring a member costs 5–25× more than keeping one (both unsourced). — [Asest, 20 May 2026](https://asest.es/story/el-negocio-de-los-gimnasios/)
- Small and medium gyms need 400–600 active members to be profitable **(snippet)**. — [Fitgeneration](https://fitgeneration.es/merece-la-pena-montar-un-gimnasio/)
scale: 4,600 gyms, most of them independents.
cost_impact: Price ceiling set by the chains; churn cost not quantified (gap).
driver_status: Market consolidation; ongoing in 2026.
solved_today: AimHarder for boxes (no public price) **(Capterra snippet)**. Trainingym pricing not found.
software_solvable: Partly. Retention and CRM, class booking and dunning help; software cannot fix price competition.

title: Pet shops and animal businesses under Ley 7/2023 (bienestar animal)
who: Pet shops, breeders and animal-related professionals (residences, trainers). Whether groomers (peluquerías caninas) are covered is not addressed in the text read.
where: National basic law, applied by the regions.
reality: Shops can no longer sell dogs, cats or ferrets. They must keep sale contracts and records, register each sale within 3 working days, separate animals from the public with physical barriers, and stay off direct online sales, while several implementing regulations are still pending.
evidence:
From the consolidated text of Ley 7/2023 ([BOE](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2023-7936); no amendments to the law shown, accessed Oct 2026):
- In force 29 Sep 2023.
- Dogs, cats and ferrets may be sold only directly by registered breeders, not in pet shops (art. 27 l; art. 55.1). Shops had a 12-month transition (DT4), so the ban applied from about 29 Sep 2024 (computed).
- Each sale needs a written contract and written information for the buyer. Records must be kept at least 3 years, and the sale entered in the Registro de Animales de Compañía within 3 working days. Minimum age at sale is 2 months, or 4 months if sold from a different facility (art. 55).
- Shops must have physical barriers between the public and the animals, and staff must supervise any direct contact (art. 56).
- Direct online sale is prohibited, and ads must show the breeder's or núcleo zoológico's registration number (art. 57).
- Fines: leve €500–10,000; grave €10,001–50,000; muy grave €50,001–200,000 (art. 76).
- The government had 6 months to regulate the Central Registry. Registration of breeders, sellers and behaviour professionals becomes mandatory 12 months after that regulation (final provision DF5).
- The owners' training course and dog owners' liability insurance depend on implementing regulation (art. 30).
scale: Number of pet shops not found.
cost_impact: Lost puppy and kitten sales, fines, and record-keeping.
driver_status: Ley 7/2023, **in force**. The shop sales ban applies since about Sept 2024. **Whether the pending regulations (registry, course, insurance amount) have been approved by Oct 2026 was not verified.**
solved_today: No software found (gap).
software_solvable: Partly. Contract, record and registry workflows, and keeping ads compliant. The ban itself is not.
confidence: High on the rules; low on business impact.

title: Narrow, expiring startup certification gatekeeps all Ley de Startups benefits
where: national (ENISA). Highest counts: Madrid province 509 and Barcelona 466 (Feb 2026); Valencia 275 (Oct 2026). The certificate scores points in calls by the Madrid, Valencia and Málaga councils, among others.
reality: founders send ENISA their deeds, tax number, business plan and evidence of innovation, then must keep meeting every requirement. Once they cross the age or turnover line, or restructure, they lose the 15% tax rate, the 50% angel deduction, the €50k stock-option exemption and any residence routes tied to the status. Investors and public calls increasingly ask for the certificate.
evidence:
- As of 11 Oct 2026, 2,529 recognised, 2,046 still certified and 483 lost (about 19%) — [Economía 3, 15 Oct 2026](https://economia3.com/2026/10/15/762915-certificado-de-empresa-emergente-2-529-startups-lo-tienen-pero-no-garantiza-el-visado/); ENISA's page shows 2,527 — [ENISA](https://www.enisa.es/servicios/certificacion/) (accessed 23 Oct 2026).
- ENISA forecast 5,000–7,000 certifications in 2023 — [Innovaspain, 10 Mar 2023](https://www.innovaspain.com/ley-de-startups-emprendedores-enisa-carlos-mateo-jose-bayon-pons-ip-samaipata/). The first 1,000 only arrived in July 2024 — [El Diario de Madrid, 20 Feb 2026](https://www.eldiariodemadrid.es/articulo/emprendedores/enisa-2000-startups-certificadas-madrid-barcelona-ecosistema-emprendedor/20260220112754121816.html).
- 37% of applications were not certified by May 2024 — [Autónomos y Emprendedor, 16 May 2024](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/autonomos/37-startups-logra-certificacion-enisa-beneficiarse-ayudas-ventajas-fiscales/20240514155913036328.html).
- AES says the definition "se queda corta" (falls short) and opposes the 60% rule, the age limits and the €10M cap — [Computerworld, 23 Dec 2025](https://www.computerworld.es/article/4111037/carlos-mateo-la-inmensa-mayoria-de-startups-que-hay-en-espana-son-tecnologicas.html).
- "Los inversores cada vez lo piden más" (investors increasingly ask for it) — ENISA CEO, [El Español, 21 Oct 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/invertia/disruptores/ecosistema-startup/startups/20261021/carolina-rodriguez-enisa-certificado-startups-espana-valencia/1003744429744_0.html).
scale: about 2,046 currently certified, against more than 5,000 active startups nationally ([Computerworld](https://www.computerworld.es/article/4111037/carlos-mateo-la-inmensa-mayoria-de-startups-que-hay-en-espana-son-tecnologicas.html)) and 2,403 in Catalonia alone ([ACCIÓ](https://www.accio.gencat.cat/web/.content/bancconeixement/documents/pindoles/ACCIO-analisi-ecosistema-startup-catalunya-2026-pindola-en.pdf)). Inference: most startups are uncertified at any given time.
driver_status: Ley 28/2022 arts. 3–4 and Orden PCM/825/2023. **In force.** The BOE consolidated text shows no amendment since 22 Dec 2022 (checked 23 Oct 2026). AES is lobbying to widen the definition; no reform bill found.
software_solvable: Partly. An eligibility checker, continuous monitoring of the age, turnover and payroll thresholds, and automatic generation of the application pack are automatable. The thresholds themselves are policy.

title: Stock-option tax hits illiquid equity, and the €50k regime only covers certified startups
who: early employees and key hires (CTO packages of 0.3–3% equity) at certified startups from seed to Series B; founders designing employee share plans (ESOPs).
where: national (state income tax). The provincial (foral) regimes in Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa, Álava and Navarra were not checked.
evidence:
- €50k exemption only for startups (€12k for other companies); deferral until listing, sale or 10 years — [BOE](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2022-21739).
- Valuation rule — [GM Tax Consultancy, © 2026](https://gmtaxconsultancy.com/es/impuestos/tributacion-stock-options-ley-startups/) (single source).
- Exercise taxed at 19–47%; sale at 19–30% — [Iurit Corp, 25 Aug 2026](https://iuritcorp.com/stock-options-en-espana-y-fiscalidad-en-startups/).
- Pay bands for a CTO or Head of Engineering include "+ 0.5/3% equity" (5–10 years' experience) and "0.3/1.5%" (more than 10 years) — [Manfred, 12 Jan 2026](https://www.getmanfred.com/blog/guia-salarial-2026-salarios-en-tecnologia-espana-manfred).
- Few exits: 19 in H1 2026 (−32%), none with a disclosed value — [Bankinter H1 2026](https://www.fundacionbankinter.org/informe-observatorio/h1-2026-informe-de-inversion-en-startups/).
scale: employees of the roughly 2,046 certified startups can use the €50k regime; everyone else falls back to €12k with an equal-terms requirement. Catalan startups alone employ 30,537 people ([ACCIÓ](https://www.accio.gencat.cat/web/.content/bancconeixement/documents/pindoles/ACCIO-analisi-ecosistema-startup-catalunya-2026-pindola-en.pdf)).
cost_impact: tax at marginal rates up to 47% on paper gains. Inference: a tax event lands after 10 years whether or not there is liquidity, and plans need manual tracking over that decade.
driver_status: Ley 28/2022 final provision 3, amending arts. 14.2.m and 42.3.f LIRPF. **In force** since 1 Jan 2023; no 2025–26 change found.
solved_today: tax advisers and startup lawyers; global equity-management SaaS such as Ledgy or Carta (Spanish pricing and usage not verified); phantom-share plans (prevalence not verified in this session).
software_solvable: Partly. ESOP administration, vesting, valuation evidence, a 10-year tax-event clock and employee tax simulators are automatable. Corporate formalities remain: transfers of SL shares need a public deed, which I did not verify in this session.
confidence: Medium. The law is verified; documented complaints are scarce.

title: The step from seed to Series A, with capital concentrated in megarounds and foreign or mixed syndicates
who: VC-backed startups raising seed (€1–5M) or Series A (€5–10M), using Bankinter's definitions; typically 5–50 staff, B2B SaaS and deeptech.
where: national; hardest outside Madrid and Barcelona (see STA-17).
reality: founders who closed pre-seed or seed struggle to find a Series A lead. Rounds with only domestic investors are small. Large cheques come from mixed or foreign syndicates, so fundraising becomes an international process.
scale: about 200 first VC rounds a year. About 3,000 early-stage VC-backed startups, against 209 at breakout stage and 39 at late stage ([Dealroom 2025](https://www.spaincap.org/storage/documents/2025/06/the-spanish-tech-ecosystem.pdf)). 376 rounds in 2025 ([Bankinter](https://www.fundacionbankinter.org/noticias/startups-2025-observatorio/)).
