scale: National; Declarando claims more than 200,000 autónomos advised; TaxDown has about 9,900 reviews.
cost_impact: €300–€1,560/year in fees (from the published prices), plus penalty exposure when errors occur.
driver_status: Market force. Compliance complexity from TAX-01 to TAX-21. Ongoing.
solved_today: Switching providers; DIY with software; local traditional gestorías (prices not sourced).
software_solvable: Partly. AI-assisted review, case continuity and error-checking before filing improve quality; liability and representation stay human.
confidence: Medium. Review samples are small and self-selected.

title: Asesoría productivity gap (Excel, manual data entry, client re-education)
who: About 8,000+ advisers surveyed by Cegid; 71% of firms have three or fewer staff. They serve autónomos and micro firms.
where: National, with heavy local presence in all cities.
reality: Small firms key in invoices by hand, run on Excel, and at each regulatory change must review every client (bases in April 2026; VeriFactu and e-invoicing in 2026–2028), mostly without integration tools.
evidence:
- 63% use Excel for management; 6 in 10 invoice with Excel; 10% of clients ready. — [Merca2, 20 Jul 2025](https://www.merca2.es/2025/07/20/verifactu-asesorias-excel-2215495/)
- 72% re-educate clients; up to 60% time saved with compliant systems (vendor-reported). — [ElDerecho, 19 Nov 2025](https://elderecho.com/el-65-de-las-pymes-no-esta-preparada-para-la-entrada-en-vigor-de-verifactu)
- Invoice-processing automation claims of 85% time saved (promotional). — [AyE, 8 Oct 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/autonomos/asesorias-autonomos-pueden-ahorrar-cientos-horas-ano-programa-contabilizar-facturas/20261001095402056098.html)
- Asesorías' accounting software is exempt from VeriFactu, but invoicing for clients is not. — [AyE, 7 Sep 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/hacienda/hacienda-exime-asesorias-que-llevan-contabilidad-autonomos-adaptar-software-verifactu/20260905221011055741.html)
scale: Thousands of small firms (Cegid sample of 8,000 advisers).
cost_impact: Staff hours at peaks; capacity limits on client growth.
driver_status: Market force plus VeriFactu, e-invoicing and cotización changes. Ongoing.
solved_today: a3 (Wolters Kluwer), TeamSystem/DELSOL, Sage, plus add-ons such as Kabilio; Excel.
software_solvable: Yes. Multi-client compliance dashboards, document intake and OCR, bulk e-invoice and status operations.
confidence: Medium. The figures are vendor surveys.

title: The 10% VAT rate on renovations now depends on payment method (from 1 Dec 2026)
who: Construction and renovation autónomos and SMEs (reformas, obras); overlaps with the construction researcher.
where: National.
reality: To charge 10% instead of 21%, firms must check the dwelling age (at least two years), materials under 40% of the base, habitual-residence use (now including rented homes), and from 1 Dec 2026 that the client pays by card, transfer, nominative cheque or bank deposit. Cash payment means 21%. Advances and works in progress must be split by accrual date.
evidence:
- RDL 29/2026 (BOE 7 Oct 2026) includes VAT changes. — [AEAT, 7 Oct 2026](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/todas-noticias/2026/octubre/7/medidas-fiscales-tributarias-introducidas-real-292026.html)
- Details from REAF via the press (single press source). — [AyE, 16 Oct 2026](https://www.autonomosyemprendedor.es/articulo/autonomos/autonomos-pymes-reformas-podran-aplicar-iva-10-cobran-efectivo/20261016000200056348.html)
- Related housing RDL 26/2026 was not convalidated. — [AEAT, 30 Sep 2026](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/todas-noticias/2026/septiembre/30/medidas-fiscales-tributarias-introducidas-real-262026.html)
scale: Not quantified.
cost_impact: An 11-point VAT difference if conditions fail on the whole job (the press example uses €10,000 jobs).
driver_status: RDL 29/2026 (in force from publication; VAT rule from 1 Dec 2026). **Subject to Congress convalidation**, outcome unknown as of 23 Oct 2026.
solved_today: Gestoría advice; manual VAT-rate choice on invoices.
software_solvable: Partly. Rule-aware quoting and invoicing tools for trades (rate logic, payment-method capture, advance splitting).
confidence: Medium (single press source on details; official confirmation of the decree's existence).

title: Underserved tax regimes: Canarias (IGIC), foral territories, Ceuta/Melilla and módulos
who: Autónomos and SMEs outside the common-territory VAT and IRPF model, plus módulos users.
where:
- Canarias (Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Santa Cruz de Tenerife): IGIC administered by the ATC, which runs its own SII-IGIC.
- País Vasco (Bilbao, Vitoria-Gasteiz, Donostia): TicketBAI, plus LROE in Bizkaia.
- Navarra (Pamplona): regime unverified.
- Ceuta and Melilla: IPSI.
reality: National online asesorías and some software design for common-territory VAT and IRPF. Taxpayers in these regimes get fewer low-cost options and must find local gestorías or regional-specific software.
evidence:
- TaxDown Standard excludes "residents of foral communities, Canarias, Ceuta and Melilla" and módulos. — [TaxDown](https://taxdown.es/autonomos)
- The ATC runs a separate SII-IGIC. — [ATC](https://www3.gobiernodecanarias.org/tributos/atc/)
- Bizkaia LROE 140/240. — [Batuz](https://www.batuz.eus/es/inicio)
- Foral taxpayers excluded from VeriFactu. — [VeriBai](https://veribai.com/calendario-verifactu)
- Commercial content gets Navarra wrong. — [Webpsilon](https://www.webpsilon.com/blog/verifactu-que-es-cuando-entra-en-vigor-y-a-quien-afecta/)
scale: Not quantified here (regional business counts not retrieved).
cost_impact: Fewer competitive offers; likely higher advisory prices (inference, not evidenced).
driver_status: Constitutional tax regimes (foral) and the REF of Canarias. In force.
solved_today: Local gestorías; foral free apps (FakturaBAI, FakturAraba, Haz tu factura); vendors with TicketBAI certification (TS Facturas).
software_solvable: Yes. Localised filing and invoicing engines (IGIC, TicketBAI/LROE, IPSI).
confidence: Medium-low. The evidence is one provider's exclusions plus official regime facts.

title: Mandatory digital control document (DeCA): chaotic rollout, fines and liability shifting
who: Every public road-freight carrier, from the autónomo with one truck to medium fleets (50–249). Shippers (cargadores contractuales) and freight forwarders/operators are jointly liable.
where: National. It covers all domestic public road freight in Spain, cabotage included. International CMR transport is **not** covered, and final-mile parcel delivery is exempt.
reality: Since 5 Oct 2026 every domestic haulage service needs a native digital PDF with a QR code. The QR must link to a public HTTPS URL, and the document must be created before the truck leaves. Drivers are being fined at the roadside when inspectors' tablets or the shipper's repository fail. Some large shippers force carriers' drivers to log into private platforms en route and "validate" provisional DeCAs, which moves liability onto the driver.
evidence:
- Ley 9/2025, transitional provision 8: the control document "deberá ser necesariamente digital a los diez meses desde la entrada en vigor de esta ley" ("must necessarily be digital ten months after the law enters into force") ([BOE, Ley 9/2025 consolidated](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2025-24545); published BOE 4 Dec 2025, in force 5 Dec 2025 per the [Hacienda bulletin record](https://www.hacienda.gob.es/BoletinesHacienda/Boletines/2025/93921.pdf)). Ten months after 5 Dec 2025 gives **5 Oct 2026**.
- Technical rules come from the Resolución DGTCF of 5 June 2026 (BOE 12/06/2026, replacing the Resolución of 22 May 2023), Orden TRM/282/2026 and Orden FOM/2861/2012. They require:
- a native PDF of at most 5 MB with creation/modification metadata;
- a QR code pointing to a unique HTTPS URL (TLS ≥1.2) that downloads without credentials (a numeric code alone is no longer enough);
- a timestamp before the service starts and a copy to the driver before departure;
- retention for at least one year by **both** shipper and carrier.
Handwritten annotations are no longer valid. An e-signature is not required unless the document is also used as a contract or eCMR ([Gómez-Acebo & Pombo, 16 Jul 2026](https://ga-p.com/publicaciones/guia-para-no-perderte-con-el-nuevo-deca/)). A second source agrees: RD 1211/1990 art. 222, Orden FOM/2861/2012 art. 6, HTTPS/TLS 1.2, one-year repository ([Viafirma, 1 Sep 2026](https://www.viafirma.com/en/keys-mandatory-deca/)).
- The digital requirement was originally due on 1 Sep 2024 and was postponed to Oct 2026 ([Fieldeas, 22 Jan 2025, updated 4 Dec 2025](https://www.fieldeas.com/en/ecmr-mandatory/); vendor source, single source for the original date).
- **Readiness:** a Fenadismer/Continental survey of 750 transport professionals (Oct 2025) found 17% prepared, 35% insufficiently prepared and 23% not prepared at all. 25% expected the shipper to provide the document ([trans.info, 5 Feb 2026](https://trans.info/es/documentos-digitales-452450)).
- **Rollout incidents:**
- QR codes failed to scan at roadside checks.
- One major shipper required each external driver to register on its private DeCA platform, photograph the delivery note and correct data en route. It cancelled the carrier's services when the carrier objected.
- Shippers issued "provisional DeCAs" that only become final once the driver validates them. Fenadismer questions whether this is legal ([Fenadismer, 8 Oct 2026](https://www.fenadismer.es/primeras-incidencias-del-deca-tras-su-entrada-en-vigor/)).
- **Fines:** inspectors fined drivers "more than 400 euros" for "carecer del documento de control" (lacking the control document) even though the drivers showed the QR they had been given. Fenadismer says the haulier is "el eslabón más débil de la cadena" ("the weakest link in the chain") ([Fenadismer, 15 Oct 2026](https://www.fenadismer.es/deca-sanciones-injustas-a-transportistas-por-errores-de-sus-cargadores-o-de-las-inspecciones-en-carretera/)).
- **Ministry climb-down:** the DeCA and HeRU systems had incidents from 5 to 19 Oct 2026, and Guardia Civil tablets could not download documents. The DG de Transporte told the autonomous communities to archive reports caused by download failures in that window. Other DeCA infractions, such as missing data, are still prosecuted ([Fenadismer, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.fenadismer.es/deca-transportes-reconoce-fallos-tecnicos-y-no-tramitara-las-multas-impuestas/)).
- **Fine level:** not carrying a DeCA or omitting essential data is a serious infraction ("infracción grave", LOTT art. 141.17) with a fine of €401–600 under art. 143.1.d ([Veritas Gestión, updated 18 Oct 2026](https://veritasgestion.com/?p=7976); single source for the article numbers, consistent with Fenadismer's ">400 euros").
- **Scope details:**
- Shipper and carrier are jointly liable for the document existing. The shipper answers for shipment data and the carrier for vehicle data.
- Removals, cranes and small loads one person can handle are exempt. The sector reads a full pallet as in scope.
- **Final-mile parcel delivery from the hub to the end customer is exempt**, so only "primary" transport is covered ([Fenadismer training PDF, created 29 May 2026](https://www.fenadismer.es/wp-content/uploads/Pildora-formativa.-todo-sobre-el-Documento-Electronico-de-Control.pdf)).
scale:
- 152,871 road-freight companies at the start of 2026, 61,716 of them in heavy transport ([trans.info, 24 Aug 2026](https://trans.info/es/espana-pierde-miles-de-transportistas-498338)).
- Fenadismer represents more than 32,000 companies and 60,000 vehicles ([Fenadismer](https://www.fenadismer.es/)). CETM represents more than 31,000 companies, 129,000 industrial vehicles and 215,000 workers ([CETM](https://www.cetm.es/)).
- Shippers in every sector that buy domestic haulage are co-liable.
cost_impact: fines of €401–600 per infraction (more for falsification). Cancelled services when carriers refuse shipper platforms. Extra admin per trip (not quantified; gap).
driver_status: Ley 9/2025 transitional provision 8, Orden FOM/2861/2012, Resolución DGTCF 5 Jun 2026 and Orden TRM/282/2026. **In force since 5 Oct 2026.** Fines for the 5–19 Oct download failures are waived; nothing else is.
solved_today:
- Vendor DeCA tools range from "opciones viables desde los 5 euros al mes" (viable options from €5/month) to offers priced up to 1,000% higher for the most basic tool. Some tools do not meet the legal requirements ([Fenadismer, 10 Sep 2026](https://www.fenadismer.es/ojo-ofertas-abusivas-para-el-nuevo-documento-electronico-de-control/)).
- "No hace falta ningún programa homologado" (no homologated software is needed) ([Veritas Gestión](https://veritasgestion.com/?p=7976)).
- eCMR and e-signature vendors (Fieldeas, Viafirma, Edicom) do not publish prices.
- Shippers impose their own private platforms (see the complaints above).
- UNO has a "Guía DeCA" project page ([UNO](https://unologistica.org/proyectos-e-informes/guia-documento-electronico-de-control-administrativo-deca/); content and price not read).
software_solvable: **Yes.** The obligation is entirely digital: generation, QR hosting with guaranteed uptime, a one-year repository, audit trail, shipper–carrier data reconciliation and proof for inspections. The unsolved problem is now reliability and liability evidence, not basic issuance, and basic issuance is already priced as a commodity at about €5/month.

title: 2026 fuel-cost shock and the fight to enforce fuel-price indexation on invoices
who: Road hauliers of every size (autónomos to medium), plus the shippers and intermediaries who pay them.
where: National.
reality: Diesel costs jumped after the Iran war began. Carriers must now put a regulated fuel-revision line on every invoice, but many shippers resist it or quietly cut base rates first. Meanwhile carriers track per-litre and per-vehicle aid that changes month by month.
evidence:
- RDL 9/2026 says energy price rises have increased haulage costs "del orden del 30%" (around 30%). Road carries about 95% of goods transport ([BOE, RDL 9/2026, 15 Apr 2026](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-8283)).
- What RDL 9/2026 changes:
- The revision is mandatory and must be itemised on the invoice.
- It applies automatically at a fuel variation of 5% or more, and continuous contracts are revised every billing period.
- There is a new formula with a weekly diesel index (G) and a coefficient (C). For trucks of 20 t or more, C is 0.3 when pre-tax diesel is below €0.85/l, 0.4 between €0.85 and €1.40/l, and 0.5 at €1.40/l or above.
- New infractions apply to payers who block a separate fuel line. It is "grave" when the price is €3,000 or less (fines from €401–600 up to €801–1,000) and "muy grave" above €3,000 (from €1,001–2,000 up to €4,001–6,000). Repeat offences within 12 months can reach €18,000 (same source).
- Ley 15/2009 art. 38: the price "se incrementa o reduce de manera ineludible" (must rise or fall, no exceptions) with fuel. Revision is automatic at 5% or more, and any agreement to the contrary is void ([BOE, Ley 15/2009 consolidated, latest update 15/04/2026](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2009/11/11/15/con)).
- The Ministry's "Coeficiente G" rose 44.6% for heavy vehicles and 38.4% for light vehicles between early January and 1 Oct 2026. Fenadismer opened a confidential complaint channel. It wants inspectors to catch shippers that "artificially lowered" base prices before applying the formula ([Fenadismer, 13 Oct 2026](https://www.fenadismer.es/canal-de-denuncias-contra-los-cargadores-que-no-indexen-el-combustible-a-sus-transportistas/)).
- **Aid under RDL 7/2026:**
- €0.20/l for holders of the professional-diesel refund (supplies up to 30 Jun 2026).
- Up to €2,000M in ICO re-guarantees for the bank guarantees fuel-card holders must provide.
- Beneficiaries may not make crisis-related dismissals until 30 Jun 2026 ([BOE, RDL 7/2026](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-6544)).
- **Per-vehicle aid under RDL 9/2026:**
- €1,800 for heavy gas-powered trucks (and diesel trucks registered in the Canaries, Ceuta or Melilla).
- €665 for trucks under 7.5 t.
- €300 for light vans.
- €200 for taxis and VTC vehicles ([BOE, RDL 9/2026](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-8283)).
- **RDL 25/2026 extension:** professional-diesel aid of €0.05/l in October, €0.12/l in November and €0.19/l in December 2026. Paying with the professional-diesel card counts as the aid application ([Cooperativas Agro-alimentarias summary of RDL 25/2026, Oct 2026](https://www.agro-alimentarias.coop/docs_download/apoyar-al-campo-y-a-las-cooperativas-para-hacer-frente-al-impacto-de-la-crisis-energetica)).
- A French comparison: French hauliers called off protests after their government agreed fuel-indexation enforcement and an 18 c/l diesel cut. Fenadismer says many of those measures "ya se encuentran implementadas en España" (are already in place in Spain) ([Fenadismer, 19 Oct 2026](https://www.fenadismer.es/crisis-diesel-los-transportistas-franceses-desconvocan-movilizaciones-tras-acuerdo-con-gobierno/)).
scale: All of the roughly 152,871 road-freight companies ([trans.info, 24 Aug 2026](https://trans.info/es/espana-pierde-miles-de-transportistas-498338)).
cost_impact: Operating costs up about 30% (RDL 9/2026). The G index is up 44.6% in 2026 (Fenadismer). Shippers risk fines of up to €6,000, or €18,000 for repeat offences.
driver_status: A market shock from the Iran war. RDL 7/2026 has been in force since 21 Mar 2026, RDL 9/2026 since 16 Apr 2026 and RDL 25/2026 since 1 Oct 2026, with measures running to 31 Dec 2026. All are **in force**. Some aid depends on EU state-aid compatibility (Cooperativas summary). **Not verified:** whether Congress validated each RDL. In July 2025 Parliament repealed an earlier decree-law, RDL 7/2025 ([Wikipedia, 2025 Iberian blackout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Iberian_Peninsula_blackout)).
solved_today:
- CETM's site lists a "Calculadora de Costes e Indexación" (cost and indexation calculator; price and access terms not shown) ([CETM](https://www.cetm.es/)).
- Fenadismer runs its complaint channel.
- The Ministry's historical ACOTRAM cost simulator is described in past Observatorio de Costes editions ([Observatorio de costes, abril 2016](https://sarreplec.caib.es/pluginfile.php/21164/mod_resource/content/0/OTM02/OTM02_Web_2016/ObservatorioCostes_abril2016.pdf)).
- Otherwise, invoices in a TMS or ERP or by hand (no price data).
software_solvable: **Yes.** A tool can pull the weekly G index, apply the right coefficient per vehicle class, itemise the fuel line on every invoice, keep an evidence file for inspection complaints, and track eligibility and claims for monthly aid.

title: Driver shortage, an ageing workforce and slow, expensive licensing
who: Haulage companies of every size. The autónomos who make up much of the sector are themselves ageing.
where: National. Regional shortage lists name heavy-lorry drivers in Galicia, the Basque Country, Aragón, Castilla-La Mancha and Catalonia ([EURES, 24 Feb 2025](https://eures.europa.eu/living-and-working/labour-market-information/labour-market-information-spain_en)). Base pay is highest in Gipuzkoa and Barcelona and lowest in Ourense (CETM via [El Español, 8 Aug 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/sociedad/20260808/espana-necesita-conductores-camiones-faltan-camioneros-pagan-sueldos-euros-ano/1003744347084_0.html)).
reality: Trucks stand idle without drivers. Firms recruit in Peru, Morocco and Colombia and then wait on licence exchanges and the CAP (Certificado de Aptitud Profesional, the professional-driver certificate). Young people avoid the job because of time away from home, waits at docks and insecure rest stops.
evidence:
- CETM puts the deficit at 30,000 drivers and says it "could double by 2028". Average driver age is 55. Employers and unions filed a joint request for early retirement in Dec 2025, which is still pending ([Europa Press via Bolsamanía, 4 Feb 2026](https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias_amp/empresas/economia--los-transportistas-piden-medidas-reales-ante-la-grave-falta-de-camioneros-y-critican-trabas-administrativas--21606838.html)).
- Major employers' associations estimate up to 116,000 drivers will be needed by 2028. Only 3% of drivers are under 25. SEPE has added the job to its Catálogo de Ocupaciones de Difícil Cobertura (official list of hard-to-fill occupations). Gross pay is €20,000–24,000/yr in general haulage, about €37,900 for international drivers in Spain, and €45,000–50,000 in Germany, Belgium or Italy ([El Español, 8 Aug 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/sociedad/20260808/espana-necesita-conductores-camiones-faltan-camioneros-pagan-sueldos-euros-ano/1003744347084_0.html)).
- In a parliamentary answer the Government said more than 20,000 drivers are needed. Exchanges of foreign C/D licences rose from 13,903 (2024) to 15,589 (2025), +12%: Peru 4,317, Morocco 2,248, Colombia 1,206. The DGT process has been fully online since May 2025 ([EFE via Menorca.info, 3 May 2026](https://www.menorca.info/actualidad/nacional/2026/05/03/2621635/escasez-camioneros-acelera-canje-carnes-extranjeros-15500-pasado-ano.html)).
- UNO Logística puts the deficit at 20,000 ([Europa Press via Bolsamanía](https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/empresas/economia--uno-reclama-soluciones-urgentes-ante-la-falta-de-20000-conductores-de-transporte-por-carretera-en-espana--21479501.html); seen only as a search snippet, not opened).
- Road-freight companies fell by 3,608 in 2025 (−2.31%) to 152,871. Heavy-transport companies fell by 2,754 (−4.27%) to 61,716 (trans.info citing SNAP, [24 Aug 2026](https://trans.info/es/espana-pierde-miles-de-transportistas-498338)).
- Getting the licences costs €3,000–4,000 and takes close to a year. The Plan Reconduce offers aid of up to €3,000. More than 50% of drivers are over 55 ([trans.info, 31 Mar 2026](https://trans.info/es/espana-sin-camioneros-465872)).
scale: The whole road-haulage sector (about 152,871 companies). Estimates of the gap range from 20,000 (Government, UNO) to 30,000 (CETM). There is no official figure.
cost_impact: Lost capacity. €3,000–4,000 and about a year to train each new driver. Firms leaving the market (−3,608 in 2025).
driver_status: A demographic and working-conditions problem. The CAP is required under RD 284/2021 (a 140-hour course, per El Español). The early-retirement request is **pending**.
solved_today: Foreign recruitment plus licence exchange, the Plan Reconduce (up to €3,000), and vocational training proposals from CETM. Recruiters' fees are not verified.
software_solvable: **Partly.** Software can run foreign-driver pipelines (licence exchange, CAP, residence paperwork) and retention tools such as home-time planning and dock-wait reduction. The root causes, demographics and pay, are not software problems.
confidence: High on the existence and direction of the shortage. Medium on the exact size of the gap, since the figures are association estimates.

title: Late payment by shippers and intermediaries
who: Carriers, especially autónomos and micro firms subcontracted through intermediaries.
where: National.
reality: Carriers finance their clients for about two months. More than a third of payers still break the 60-day legal maximum, despite a transport-specific sanction regime.
evidence:
- In August 2026 the average payment period was **52 days**, the best in Fenadismer's series, and 38% of shippers and intermediaries paid after 60 days. Of those late payers, 76% paid at 60–90 days and 6% after 120 days. The figures were 59 days and 48% in December 2025, and 83 days in 2021. Bank transfers make up 69% of payments and confirming 25%. The proposed EU 30-day payment regulation is "blocked" in the Council ([trans.info, 22 Sep 2026](https://trans.info/es/los-transportistas-espanoles-esperan-52-dias-para-cobrar-la-reforma-europea-se-atasca-504049)).
- Baseline: in February 2022, 63% of payments exceeded 60 days and the average was 78 days. Of the late payers, 34% paid after more than 90 days and 21% after more than 120 days. The sanction regime approved in October 2021 allows fines of up to €6,000, or €30,000 for repeat or abusive cases ([EFE via Vivir Ediciones, 29 Mar 2022](https://vivirediciones.es/?p=102403)).
- Ley 15/2009 art. 41: the payer is in default after 30 days, by reference to Ley 3/2004 ([BOE, Ley 15/2009](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2009/11/11/15/con)).
scale: All hauliers. Fenadismer's observatory covers the whole sector.
cost_impact: Working capital tied up for about 52 days on average. Confirming and factoring costs (not quantified; overlaps with the finance researcher).
driver_status: Ley 3/2004 and Ley 15/2009, plus a transport-specific sanction regime in force since Oct 2021 (the name of the amending law was not verified). The EU Late Payment Regulation proposal is **stalled**.
solved_today:
- Wtransnet's freight exchange includes a payment guarantee with Coface covering at least 90% of the invoice, plus payment mediation. Prices are quote-only ([Wtransnet](https://www.wtransnet.com/es/), [pricing page](https://www.wtransnet.com/es-es/bolsa-de-cargas/precios/)).
- CETM runs "Icired", a published registry of payment defaults ([CETM](https://www.cetm.es/)).
- Confirming and factoring.
software_solvable: **Partly.** Software can score shippers' payment behaviour, generate statutory interest and compensation claims automatically, and assemble inspection complaints. Enforcement itself stays legal and administrative.

title: Tachograph now required on 2.5–3.5 t vans in international transport and cabotage
who: Van operators (autónomos, micro and small firms) doing paid international transport or cabotage.
where: National, on cross-border work.
reality: Since 1 July 2026 these vans need a smart tachograph (G2V2) fitted by an authorised workshop. The operator also needs a company card, driver cards, data downloads, file retention and EU driving-time rules, which is truck-level admin for very small firms.
evidence:
- The device costs "en torno a 1.000 euros netos" (around €1,000 net) plus installation. Spain's sanction is €2,001. Driver cards must be downloaded at least every 28 days and the vehicle unit every 90 days, with files kept for 1–2 years. Drivers fall under the 9-hour daily and 56-hour weekly limits, posting rules and the return-to-base obligation. The exemptions are the craftsman exemption (art. 3(aa), within 100 km) and own-account transport (art. 3(ha)) ([trans.info FAQ, 23 Jun 2026](https://trans.info/es/tacografo-en-furgonetas-desde-el-1-de-julio-de-2026-a-quien-afecta-exenciones-y-sanciones-faq-484861)).
- An IRU survey found 88% of affected vans still without the device in May 2026. 27.7% of operators expected to be ready and 46.5% admitted they would not be. Workshop shortages, cost and compatibility were cited ([trans.info, 11 May 2026](https://trans.info/es/cuenta-atras-para-las-furgonetas-el-88-aun-sin-tacografo-para-2026-473744)).
- After the deadline, about a third of fleets had not finished adapting and 15.6% had not started. Cost was the biggest obstacle for 62.5% (Kienzle clients, n=116, which the article says is not representative) ([trans.info, 12 Aug 2026](https://trans.info/es/el-plazo-del-tacografo-ya-ha-vencido-muchas-furgonetas-siguen-sin-adaptarse-495758)).
- Only authorised workshops can install and activate the G2V2. From 7 Jul 2026, new heavy-vehicle types also need event data recorders ([trans.info, 29 Jun 2026](https://trans.info/es/revolucion-de-julio-en-el-transporte-europeo-tacografos-en-furgonetas-cajas-negras-en-camiones-y-nuevos-peajes-486204)).
scale: The number of Spanish vans affected is unknown (gap).
cost_impact: About €1,000 per van plus installation. A €2,001 sanction. Recurring download and retention admin.
driver_status: Reg. (CE) 561/2006 and the tachograph rules as amended by the EU Mobility Package. **In force since 1 Jul 2026**, with no general grace period.
solved_today: Authorised workshops plus tachograph download and analysis services or telematics (for example Geotab). No price data was verified.
software_solvable: **Partly.** Remote download, infringement analytics and posting declarations can be software. The hardware cannot.
confidence: Medium-high. The sources are trade press and the surveys are not representative.

title: Waiting times at loading docks, and detention compensation that goes unclaimed
who: Carriers (all sizes) and shippers' warehouses.
where: National.
reality: Trucks wait more than an hour at distribution centres. The law entitles carriers to hourly compensation, but claiming it needs proof of arrival times and risks the client relationship.
evidence:
- Over 40% of shippers and 70% of carriers report waits of more than one hour. 70% of carriers say the main consequence is missing agreed deadlines. 46% of shippers use dock-management technology. 86% of carriers say fewer than half of their clients provide rest areas (CEL and CargoON study, [CadenadeSuministro, 21 Nov 2023](https://cadenadesuministro.es/noticias/cargadores-y-transportistas-siguen-sufriendo-esperas-en-los-muelles-de-carga-y-descarga_478995_102.html); this predates 2024 and is a single study).
- Ley 15/2009 art. 22: after the first hour of waiting the carrier may claim 2×IPREM/day for each hour or fraction, up to 10 hours a day. Day two pays 25% more and day three onwards 50% more ([BOE, Ley 15/2009](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2009/11/11/15/con)).
- Waiting at docks is cited as a reason drivers leave the job ([trans.info, 31 Mar 2026](https://trans.info/es/espana-sin-camioneros-465872)).
scale: Sector-wide (70% of carriers in the 2023 study).
cost_impact: Lost truck hours. How much statutory compensation goes unclaimed is unknown (gap).
driver_status: Ley 15/2009 art. 22, **in force**.
solved_today: Dock booking and slot tools (used by 46% of shippers in 2023). Vendor prices not verified.
software_solvable: **Yes.** Geofenced arrival and departure timestamps can generate paralización claims automatically, and slot booking cuts waits.
confidence: Medium. The data is dated, but the legal hook is solid.

title: Cargo theft and insecure rest stops
who: Long-haul carriers and their drivers.
where: The source singles out the AP-7. That motorway runs along the Mediterranean corridor through Catalonia, Valencia, Murcia and Andalusia (the regional list is my geographic inference).
reality: Drivers check for theft after sleeping in the cab. A lack of secure parking discourages new drivers.
evidence:
- There are "about 20,000 robberies a year in goods transport, especially on the AP-7" ([trans.info, 31 Mar 2026](https://trans.info/es/espana-sin-camioneros-465872); **single source**, and the underlying data source is not named).
- Limited access to secure parking and rest areas is cited as a barrier to recruitment ([trans.info, 24 Aug 2026](https://trans.info/es/espana-pierde-miles-de-transportistas-498338)). CETM asks for "áreas de descanso seguras" (secure rest areas) ([Bolsamanía, 4 Feb 2026](https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias_amp/empresas/economia--los-transportistas-piden-medidas-reales-ante-la-grave-falta-de-camioneros-y-critican-trabas-administrativas--21606838.html)).
scale: About 20,000 incidents a year (single source).
cost_impact: Not quantified (gap).
driver_status: A market and infrastructure problem; no regulation identified.
solved_today: Telematics alarms and paid secure parking (not verified).
software_solvable: **Partly.** Software can book secure parking and raise theft alerts. Physical infrastructure is the real fix.

title: Last mile and urban delivery: a patchwork of city rules, seasonal peaks and new EU customs paperwork
who: Couriers, parcel companies and their subcontracted van autónomos. Also e-commerce logistics operators (micro to medium).
where: City-specific. In UNO's directory, Madrid, Barcelona, Sevilla and Málaga have a "Ordenanza Definitiva" (final mobility ordinance), while Valencia, Zaragoza and Bilbao are "Pendiente Borrador ZBE" (low-emission-zone draft still pending) ([UNO, Ordenanzas de movilidad directory, accessed Oct 2026](https://unologistica.org/proyectos-e-informes/ordenanzas-de-movilidad/)).
reality: Each city has its own ordinance and low-emission-zone rules, and many are still in draft. Peak seasons stretch capacity. Cross-border e-commerce parcels now carry a per-item EU customs duty and new data requirements.
evidence:
- Ley 7/2021 required municipalities of more than 50,000 inhabitants to adopt mobility plans "antes de 2023" (before 2023). Most have not defined a final low-emission zone or ordinance (UNO directory, above).
- More than 127 million shipments are expected over Black Friday and Christmas 2026, +2.4% on 2025 ([UNO press release, 15 Oct 2026](https://unologistica.org/sala-de-prensa/nota-de-prensa/la-logistica-gestionara-durante-el-black-friday-y-la-navidad-un-24-mas-de-envios-que-en-2025/)).
- Final-mile parcel delivery is exempt from the DeCA ([Fenadismer training PDF, May 2026](https://www.fenadismer.es/wp-content/uploads/Pildora-formativa.-todo-sobre-el-Documento-Electronico-de-Control.pdf)).
- From 1 Jul 2026 the EU charges a flat €3 customs duty on non-EU e-commerce consignments of up to €150, **per item line rather than per parcel**. Product identifiers (PIDs) were voluntary from 1 Jul and become mandatory from 1 Nov 2026 ([trans.info, 29 Jun 2026](https://trans.info/es/revolucion-de-julio-en-el-transporte-europeo-tacografos-en-furgonetas-cajas-negras-en-camiones-y-nuevos-peajes-486204); single trade-press source).
- Ley 9/2025 amends LOTT art. 42 so vehicles limited to 40 km/h (for example small delivery vehicles) are exempt from transport authorisation. It also promotes bicycles for the "último tramo del reparto de mercancías" (last leg of goods delivery) ([BOE, Ley 9/2025](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2025-24545)).
scale: UNO has more than 350 members ([UNO](https://www.unologistica.org/)). 127 million or more peak-season shipments.
cost_impact: Not quantified. Loading-zone fines and time limits were not verified (gap).
driver_status: Municipal ordinances: final in Madrid, Barcelona, Sevilla and Málaga; still in draft in Valencia, Zaragoza and Bilbao. EU €3 duty **in force** since 1 Jul 2026; PID requirement from 1 Nov 2026. (Low-emission zones themselves are another researcher's topic.)
solved_today: Not verified. The examples I would expect (route-planning SaaS, municipal loading-zone apps) could not be checked because the pages would not load.
software_solvable: **Partly.** Software can provide a rules database per city, plan routes and handle customs product data for cross-border parcels. Kerb space and city infrastructure are not software.

title: Sustainable-mobility-law duties for larger logistics employers (mobility plans, EDIM data)
who: Logistics and warehouse operators with more than 200 workers or 100 per shift, so medium firms and up. Most SMEs are **exempt**.
where: National.
reality: Large warehouses must draw up sustainable work-mobility plans and may have to supply data to the State mobility data platform (EDIM, Espacio de Datos Integrado de Movilidad).
evidence:
- Ley 9/2025 makes "las empresas con más de 200 personas trabajadoras o 100 por turno" (companies with more than 200 workers or 100 per shift) responsible (art. 104 b). Missing the plan deadline is a minor infraction (art. 106.2 a). Transport operators must supply data to EDIM, and supplying false data is a serious infraction. Fines are €101–2,000 for minor and €2,001–6,000 for serious infractions (art. 107) ([BOE, Ley 9/2025](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2025-24545)).
- RDL 7/2026 cut the deadline for mobility plans from 24 to 12 months ([BOE, RDL 7/2026](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-6544); taken from a summary, the article text was not read).
scale: Only large employers. The count is unknown.
driver_status: Ley 9/2025, **in force** since 5 Dec 2025. The plan deadline is in art. 26, which was not read.
solved_today: Not verified (presumably mobility consultancies).
software_solvable: **Yes.** Software can run employee mobility surveys, generate plans and report data to EDIM. The market is narrow because SMEs are exempt.
confidence: Medium. This overlaps with the bureaucracy and HR researchers.

title: Energy volatility and supply reliability (the 2025 blackout and the 2026 gas/oil shock)
who: Manufacturing SMEs (small and medium), the food industry (cold chain) and cooperatives' processing plants.
where: National. The blackout covered the whole peninsula.
reality: Plants lost a day's production on 28 Apr 2025. In 2026 gas and fuel prices spiked again. Firms are now juggling temporary tax cuts, a window to change contracted volumes, and aid whose levels depend on CPI triggers.
scale: Nationwide. No SME-level survey was found.
cost_impact: €1.6bn from the blackout (CEOE). The size of the 2026 gas spike on SME bills is not quantified.
driver_status: A market shock. RDL 7/2026 and RDL 25/2026 are **in force**, with measures to 30 Jun and 31 Dec 2026. RDL 7/2025 was **repealed**.
solved_today: Energy brokers and consultants, PPAs and self-consumption (none of the prices verified).
software_solvable: **Partly.** Monitoring, re-optimising contracts while the flexibility window is open, and tracking eligibility for tax relief and aid can be software. Prices and grid reliability cannot.
confidence: High on the facts. Medium on what it means for SMEs.

title: Shortage of skilled technical trades (welders, mechanics, machine operators, technicians)
who: Small and medium manufacturers, metalworking and the food industry.
where:
National, with regional variation ([EURES, updated 24 Feb 2025, data to Dec 2024](https://eures.europa.eu/living-and-working/labour-market-information/labour-market-information-spain_en)):
- Galicia: welders, vehicle mechanics.
- Basque Country: electricians, industrial engineers.
- Navarra: electrical engineers and technicians, crane operators.
- Castilla-La Mancha: industrial electricians, welders.
- Catalonia: vehicle mechanics.
- Murcia: machine-tool operators, welders, electricians, forklift operators.
reality: Firms cannot fill trade roles even though overall vacancy rates are low, so the shortage is specific to certain occupations.
evidence:
- The national 2024 shortage list includes "stationary plant and machine operators". In industry the shortages are welders, mechanics, machine-tool operators and industrial technicians (EURES, above).
- Spain's job vacancy rate was **0.9% in 2023, against an EU27 average of 2.8%** (EURES, above). This contradicts any general labour-shortage story.
scale: Not quantified for manufacturing SMEs (gap).
cost_impact: Not quantified.
driver_status: A market and demographic problem; no regulatory driver.
solved_today: Not verified (FP dual vocational training, temp agencies).
software_solvable: **Partly.** Training, knowledge capture and maintenance work instructions can be software. The shortage itself cannot.
confidence: Medium. This rests on a single official aggregator and overlaps with the HR researcher.

title: Packaging EPR (RD 1055/2022) plus the EU PPWR from 12 Aug 2026
who: Manufacturers and food and drink SMEs (micro to medium) that place packaged goods on the market, including commercial and industrial (B2B) packaging.
where: National, plus the EU single market.
reality: Firms must register as packaging producers, declare tonnes placed on the market every year, join and pay a collective system (or set up their own), mark packaging, and now redesign labels and recyclability documentation for the EU regulation.
evidence:
- RD 1055/2022:
- Producers of commercial and industrial packaging who had no previous obligation had to set up extended-producer-responsibility systems "antes del 31 de diciembre de 2024" (before 31 Dec 2024), with applications before 31 Dec 2023.
- Marking obligations (art. 13) apply "desde el 1 de enero de 2025" (from 1 Jan 2025).
- Producers must register in the packaging section of the Registro de Productores de Productos.
- Annual data is due before 31 March. Firms placing under 15 t a year may report in simplified form. When a producer places under 50,000 kg of commercial and industrial packaging, its manufacturer, importer or acquirer registers on its behalf.
- Collective-system fees must appear separately on invoices.
- Separate collection of industrial packaging must reach 75% in 2027, 85% in 2030 and 95% in 2035 ([BOE, RD 1055/2022 consolidated](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2022/12/27/1055/con)).
- The PPWR (Regulation (EU) 2025/40) has been in force since 11 Feb 2025 and **applies from 12 Aug 2026**. Packaging must be recyclable by 2030. PFAS are limited in food-contact packaging, and reuse and deposit-return targets apply. A December 2025 Environmental Omnibus proposal would suspend the authorised-representative obligation for direct cross-border sellers; it is still under examination ([European Commission, packaging page](https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/waste-and-recycling/packaging-waste_en)).
scale: Food and drink alone counts more than 27,300 companies, 483,300 jobs and €52,565M of exports ([FIAB](https://fiab.es/); reference year not shown).
cost_impact: Collective-system fees and admin (amounts not verified). RD 1055/2022 refers sanctions to Ley 7/2022 (amounts not read).
driver_status: RD 1055/2022 is **in force** (commercial and industrial EPR from end-2024, marking from 2025). The PPWR is **in force and applicable since 12 Aug 2026**. The Omnibus amendment is a **proposal**. (The plastic-packaging tax overlaps with the tax researcher.)
solved_today: Collective-system membership, consultants and spreadsheets (prices not verified).
software_solvable: **Yes.** Software can keep a packaging bill-of-materials inventory, compute tonnage by material, prepare the annual declaration and the fee lines on invoices, and check PPWR labelling and recyclability.

title: Food-chain law: written contracts, cost-of-production pricing, pre-delivery RCA registration and payment terms
who: Buyers of primary products: food-industry SMEs (small and medium), wholesalers in origin and destination markets, retailers, and cooperatives buying from non-members. Farmers (autónomos and micro) are the counterparty.
where: National. AICA's 399 on-site inspections in 2025 were spread as follows: fruit and vegetables 224, meat 53, dairy 28, wine 22, olive 15.
reality: For every purchase from a farmer the buyer needs a signed written contract with minimum terms, including a price above the producer's costs. Each contract and each change must be uploaded to the RCA **before delivery**. Missing that step is now the most common sanctioned infraction.
evidence:
- AICA 2025 headline figures ([AICA, Memoria Anual 2025, published 24 Sep 2026](https://www.aica.gob.es/content/dam/aica/docs/publicaciones/memorias/Memoria_Anual_de_Actividades_2025.pdf)):
- 399 on-site inspections, 2,978 commercial relationships checked and 28 complaints investigated.
- **991 infractions sanctioned**; 109 companies sanctioned (99 in 2024).
- Since 2014: 4,947 infractions and **€27,923,451 in fines** (€17,311,313 actually paid).
- Infractions by type in 2025 (same report):
- **506 failures to register in the RCA (51%), all in the "industria" link.**
- 186 payment-term breaches (124 wholesalers, 38 industry, 24 retail).
- 98 contracts missing minimum terms, 67 of them missing the price.
- 74 with no written contract.
- 53 price changes not agreed by both parties.
- 50 cases of obstructing inspectors.
- Other 2025 figures (same report):
- 66 warnings, including 31 in fruit and vegetables for not registering contracts and 30 in pork for missing minimum terms.
- 82 sanctions published.
- The RCA went live in Dec 2022 and is sized for 30 million documents a year and 300,000–400,000 users. Its help desk has handled 3,266 queries and incidents (700 in 2025). An API exists for high-volume buyers.
- Ley 12/2013:
- contracts in writing before delivery (art. 8.1);
- the price "deberá ser, en todo caso, superior al total de costes asumidos por el productor" (must always exceed the producer's total costs) (art. 9.1.c);
- every operator pays the previous one "un precio igual o superior al coste de producción" (a price equal to or above the cost of production) (art. 12 ter);
- RCA registration before delivery (art. 11 bis), with non-registration a minor infraction (art. 23.1.k).
- Fines: minor €250–3,000, serious €3,001–100,000, very serious €100,001–1,000,000, capped at 5% or 10% of turnover ([BOE, Ley 12/2013 consolidated](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2013/08/02/12/con)).
- The RCA is regulated by RD 1028/2022. The buyer registers, or the integrator in integration contracts. Contracts between a cooperative and its members are exempt, but a cooperative buying from non-members must register. Uploads are by web form with a digital certificate (up to 5 documents and 5 MB per upload) or by API ([AICA, RCA FAQ](https://www.aica.gob.es/servicios-en-linea/Registro%20de%20Contratos%20Alimentarios/preguntas-frecuentes-rca)).
- On 30 Sep 2026 AICA opened a public consultation on a new Real Decreto for its inspection regime ([AICA homepage](https://www.aica.gob.es/)).
scale: More than 27,300 food and drink companies ([FIAB](https://fiab.es/)) and 3,669 agri-food cooperatives ([Cooperativas Agro-alimentarias](https://www.agro-alimentarias.coop/datos-cooperativismo)), plus wholesalers.
cost_impact: Fines from €250 up to €1M per infraction; €27.9M in fines since 2014. Fines for serious and very serious infractions are published, which names the company.
driver_status: Ley 12/2013 as amended by Ley 16/2021 (in force), and RD 1028/2022 (RCA operating since Dec 2022). A new AICA inspection decree is a **draft** (consultation 30 Sep 2026).
solved_today: Manual RCA uploads, the RCA API for large buyers, and gestorías or consultants (prices not verified).
software_solvable: **Yes.** Software can generate contracts with a cost-of-production clause, register them in bulk through the RCA API before the weighbridge or delivery event, manage amendments and monitor payment terms.

title: Water scarcity and uncertainty over the Tajo-Segura transfer

where: Región de Murcia (the source of the figures). The transfer also serves Alicante and Almería, but that is my inference and was not verified.

title: Animal-disease trade bans (lumpy skin disease, Morocco) and emerging diseases
who: Cattle farmers and exporters (micro and small), live-animal traders.
where: The outbreak was in Catalonia and Aragón. The export impact is national.
reality: After lumpy skin disease (dermatosis nodular contagiosa) appeared in north-eastern Spain at the end of 2025, Morocco closed its border to Spanish live cattle and has kept it shut for more than ten months.
evidence:
- Morocco took sanitary precautions after the outbreak at the end of 2025, detected only in Catalonia and Aragón. Exports of beef cattle over 300 kg fell from 61,715 head (2024, 52% of live exports) to 51,986 (2025, 64%) to **0 in 2026**. UPA wants Morocco to accept regionalisation, and the Ministry meets its Moroccan counterpart at the end of November 2026 ([UPA, 16 Oct 2026](https://upa.es/upa-traslada-a-agricultura-el-clamor-del-vacuno-de-carne-debemos-recuperar-ya-las-exportaciones-a-marruecos/)).
- Unió de Pagesos demands action protocols for the spread of the Shamonda virus and other emerging animal diseases ([Unió de Pagesos, 23 Oct 2026](https://uniopagesos.cat/comunicat-de-premsa/reclamem-protocols-dactuacio-davant-lexpansio-del-virus-de-shamonda-i-daltres-malalties-animals-emergents/)).

scale: About 52,000 head a year of lost export volume.
cost_impact: The value is not quantified.
driver_status: Animal-health trade barriers. The ban is ongoing (Oct 2026).
solved_today: Diplomatic regionalisation negotiations.
software_solvable: **Partly.** Traceability and evidence of regional disease-free status can be software. Bans are political decisions.

title: Food-waste law (Ley 1/2025): prevention plans and donation agreements
who: Food manufacturers, wholesalers and cooperatives' processing businesses with 10 or more staff or more than €2M turnover (small and medium). Microenterprises and small farms are **exempt**.
where: National. The autonomous communities define infractions in detail.
reality: Covered firms must keep a prevention plan, follow a priority order for surplus food (donation first, then animal feed, then recycling), sign donation agreements and cooperate with waste measurement.
evidence:
- Agents must "disponer de un plan de aplicación para la prevención de las pérdidas y desperdicio alimentario" (have a plan for preventing food loss and waste) and promote donation agreements unless they are unfeasible and justified. Any contractual ban on donation is void.
- Microenterprises (fewer than 10 employees and €2M or less) are exempt, as are establishments of up to 1,300 m², and small farms are excluded.
- Fines: minor up to €2,000 (for example not donating edible food where obliged); serious €2,001–60,000 (for example **having no prevention plan**); very serious €60,001–500,000. The art. 6 obligations apply **one year after BOE publication** ([BOE, Ley 1/2025 consolidated](https://www.boe.es/eli/es/l/2025/04/01/1/con)).
- The BOE extract shows publication on 02/04/2025 and an inconsistent "entrada en vigor 02/01/2025", so verify the dates.
- FIAB has a "Prevención del desperdicio alimentario" section ([FIAB](https://fiab.es/)).
scale: The share of FIAB's 27,300 companies with 10 or more employees is not known (gap).
cost_impact: Fines of up to €60,000 for having no plan.
driver_status: Ley 1/2025, **in force**. The art. 6 duties apply from about April 2026 (my inference from "one year after publication").
solved_today: Consultants and food-bank agreements (not verified).
software_solvable: **Yes.** Software can generate the plan, measure waste, manage donation logistics and certificates, and handle reporting.
confidence: High on the obligations. The burden is not quantified.

title: Fake-review extortion and review bombing of local businesses
who: restaurants and bars most visibly; also local service businesses. Autónomo / micro <10.
where: national. Documented in Catalonia (Barcelona, Girona, Empordà, Delta de l'Ebre). Court awards are reported (unverified) in Madrid and Barcelona.
reality: A bar sees about 20 suspicious profiles post one-star reviews in under an hour, alleging cockroaches, rotten food and an insulting waiter, and its 4.8 rating "se desploma en tiempo real" ("collapses in real time"). Extortionists offer to stop or remove the reviews for money: "O me pagas tanto o te escribiré comentarios negativos en Tripadvisor" ("Either you pay me this much or I'll write negative comments on Tripadvisor").
evidence:
- Xavier Bosch, opinion column: the threat quoted above; "Es una práctica casi mafiosa" ("It's an almost mafia-like practice"); all the restaurants he spoke with had received offers. — [Ara, 3 Dec 2024](https://es.ara.cat/opinion/extorsion-restaurantes_129_5218159.html)
- About 20 profiles in under an hour hit an unnamed bar. A "pack de odio" (hate pack) against a competitor costs "apenas 200 euros". Fines for fake reviews reach 100,000 €. Courts in Madrid and Barcelona reportedly award up to 20,000 € in compensation, but no cases are named, so this is unverified. — [Merca2, 28 Apr 2026](https://www.merca2.es/2026/04/28/resenas-bar-google-2373862/)
- Spanish law firm Álvarez Villamediana says Google's reporting system "rara vez funciona" ("rarely works"), because it comes down to the owner's word against the reviewer's. The extortion cases in this article are from the US and elsewhere, not Spain. — [Xataka Móvil, 14 Sep 2025](https://www.xatakamovil.com/movil-y-sociedad/pagas-te-frio-a-resenas-negativas-google-maps-asi-estafa-que-esta-destrozando-reputacion-pequenos-negocios/amp)
- "Cada vez son más los negocios que denuncian una práctica alarmante" ("More and more businesses report an alarming practice"). No figures. — [Puro Marketing, 14 May 2025](https://www.puromarketing.com/141/215522/ciberextorsion-falsas-resenas-amenaza-creciente-para-reputacion-imagen-negocios-empresas)
- Chef Alberto Chicote's restaurant was offered five-star reviews and told it could get negative ones if it did not pay. — [Genbeta, 14 Aug 2023](https://www.genbeta.com/actualidad/estan-vendiendo-resenas-falsas-cinco-estrellas-a-bares-restaurantes-no-baratas-asi-negocio-para-dar-reputacion-a-local)
scale: no Spanish count found. Global proxy: in 2024 Google removed more than 240M policy-violating reviews and more than 12M fake business profiles, and restricted more than 900,000 accounts. — [Ara, 9 May 2025](https://es.ara.cat/comer/lee-resenas-restaurante-alerta-hay-falsas_1_5373668.html)
cost_impact:
- Lost rating and visibility. Merca2 says Google's algorithm may demote the business before it verifies the complaints.
- Up to 20,000 € in court compensation (unverified).
- In non-Spanish cases, extortion payments of 75–150 USD. — [Puro Marketing, 14 Jul 2022](https://www.puromarketing.com/141/36684/ultimo-timo-online-pesadilla-marketing-pagas-hunden-reputacion-online-restaurante); [Xataka Móvil, 14 Sep 2025](https://www.xatakamovil.com/movil-y-sociedad/pagas-te-frio-a-resenas-negativas-google-maps-asi-estafa-que-esta-destrozando-reputacion-pequenos-negocios/amp)
driver_status: local demand runs through Google Maps and Tripadvisor rankings. Merca2 and Puro Marketing say fake reviews have been illegal in Spain since May 2022, under the EU "Omnibus" rules. Status (Oct 2026): still being reported (Merca2, Apr 2026). I found no Spain-specific enforcement data.
solved_today:
- Free: Google's reporting tool and its "Herramienta de Gestión de Reseñas" for owners (criticised as "rara vez funciona").
- Police: the Policía Nacional Unidad de Delitos Telemáticos or the Guardia Civil.
- Lawyers: unfair-competition law, and the right to honour (which also protects companies).
- Workarounds: preserving certified screenshots; removing the phone number from the listing to stop WhatsApp approaches (Xataka).
- Reputation agencies exist (for example OnbrandinG, cited by Puro Marketing), but I captured no prices.
software_solvable: partly. Monitoring and alerting on review spikes, certified evidence capture and escalation workflows can be automated. Removal still depends on Google's decision.
confidence: medium. There are several press sources, but few direct Spanish owner quotes and no scale data.

reality: Owners are pitched paid reviews and some swap or buy them. Legitimate owners push for reviews in person (QR codes, a free sip of wine, a prize-wheel spin). On whether people pay for reviews: "Nadie te reconocerá que ha pagado" ("Nobody will admit they've paid").
evidence:
- An offer of 200 €/month for 20 Tripadvisor reviews. — [Ara, 3 Dec 2024](https://es.ara.cat/opinion/extorsion-restaurantes_129_5218159.html)
- Review-selling firms: 5 Google reviews for 95 USD, 10 for 185 USD (Reviews Company); 50 reviews for 635.25 USD (Social Blade). Owners also use QR codes, wine and prize wheels to collect reviews. — [Ara, Rosa Rodon, 9 May 2025](https://es.ara.cat/comer/lee-resenas-restaurante-alerta-hay-falsas_1_5373668.html)
- Fake five-star reviews at 2.5 € each, sold as "el más barato del mercado" ("the cheapest on the market"). — [Genbeta, 14 Aug 2023](https://www.genbeta.com/actualidad/estan-vendiendo-resenas-falsas-cinco-estrellas-a-bares-restaurantes-no-baratas-asi-negocio-para-dar-reputacion-a-local)
- A TripAdvisor review-swap thread: "si alguien está interesado puedo pagarle 1.5 euros" ("if anyone's interested I can pay them 1.5 euros"). Forum post, unverified. — [Forocoches, opened 10 Oct 2026](https://forocoches.com/foro/showthread.php?t=10832787)
- On the supply side, a local-SEO consultant pitches clinics, workshops, renovation firms, installers and lawyers ("Te ayudo a conseguir más clientes desde Google"), with no prices given. — [Forocoches, 12 Oct 2026](https://forocoches.com/foro/showthread.php?t=10834580)
scale: not quantified for Spain.
cost_impact:
- 1.5–2.5 € per fake review; 200 €/month packages.
- Restaurateurs in Ara warn that Google can suspend accounts caught buying reviews.
- Fines of up to 100,000 € (Merca2, 28 Apr 2026).
driver_status: ranking depends on review volume. Ara (May 2025) reports that Google's warning alerts for removed suspicious five-star reviews launched in the US, UK and India, with global rollout planned from May 2025. Spain status: not verified.
solved_today: manual QR or table cards; illegal paid reviews; legitimate review-request tools (I captured no Spanish prices).
software_solvable: yes, for legitimate, policy-compliant post-visit review requests (WhatsApp, SMS, email). Incentivised or fake reviews remain illegal and violate platform rules.

title: Phishing, vishing and CEO/BEC fraud aimed at small businesses
who: all sectors. Autónomo / micro <10 / small 10–49.
where: national. Regional breakdowns are available for Canarias and Las Palmas.
reality: Owners get spoofed calls, SMS and emails impersonating banks, public bodies or suppliers. In BEC ("business email compromise") and CEO fraud, a fake executive or supplier orders an urgent transfer or a change of bank account. A historic AEAT-impersonation example used the subject line "Denuncia de facturas no declaradas" ("Report of undeclared invoices").
evidence:
- INCIBE, 2025: 122,223 incidents (+25.6%); 142,767 queries to 017 (+44% on 2024). In Canarias, companies made 7% of 017 queries. Top themes: vishing 14.5%, fraudulent purchases 10.8%, smishing 9.2%, identity impersonation 6.7%. The fetch flagged an internal inconsistency in the regional percentages. — [INCIBE, 24 Sep 2026](https://www.incibe.es/incibe/sala-de-prensa/gran-canaria-impulsa-la-prevencion-en-ciberseguridad-entre-las-empresas-ante)
- More than 470,000 fraud and cybercrime offences in 2024 (Interior Ministry). CEO/BEC fraud averages more than 15,000 € per incident, attributed to INCIBE. SMEs are preferred targets because they have fewer verification protocols. Secondary source: a finance blog aggregating official data. — [El blog del Euríbor, 21 Jul 2026](https://www.euribor.com.es/2026/07/21/los-10-tipos-de-estafa-mas-denunciados-en-espana-en-2025/?amp=1)
- The Guardia Civil (EDITE Navarra) investigated AEAT-impersonating emails demanding payment of "undeclared invoices". Old example. — [Escudo Digital, 29 Mar 2020](https://www.escudodigital.com/interior/estafas-suplantan-a-la-agencia-tributaria-para-reclamar-facturas-falsas-a-empresas.html)
scale: 122,223 incidents in 2025, across all victim types and not only firms (INCIBE).
cost_impact: more than 15,000 € per BEC incident (secondary, single source). Recovery after the transfer is "very low" (same source).
driver_status: fraud is growing fast. INCIBE's counts are up 25.6% in 2025, and 017 queries up 44%. Status (Oct 2026): rising.
solved_today: the free INCIBE 017 helpline; bank fraud alerts; antivirus and security suites (no SME prices captured); Kit Digital's subsidised "ciberseguridad" category (prices not captured).
software_solvable: partly. Payment-change verification workflows, email authentication checks and micro-training can be productised. Social engineering cannot be fully eliminated.
confidence: high for the trend (official data); medium for SME-specific losses (secondary source).

title: Data breaches at SaaS vendors (e.g., booking software) put notification duties on their SME customers
who: hotels mainly (hospitality, covered in depth by another researcher), but the issue reaches any SME that relies on third-party SaaS processors. Micro to medium.
where: national.
reality: One incident at a single booking-software provider in March 2026 caused breaches at several hotels at once. Unauthorised third parties accessed guest and booking data that could be used for fraud attempts. Each hotel must notify the AEPD and, where the risk is high, its guests. The AEPD stresses that notifying the Agency "es tan importante como informar a las personas afectadas" ("is as important as informing the people affected").
evidence: 3,027 notifications in H1 2026 against 1,271 (+138%); 4,556 in Jan–Aug against 1,728 (+163%); more than 71 million communications to data subjects. Single source (official). — [AEPD, 20 Oct 2026](https://www.aepd.es/prensa-y-comunicacion/notas-de-prensa/la-aepd-recibe-mas-de-3.000-notificaciones-de-brechas-de)
scale: 4,556 breach notifications in Jan–Aug 2026. No SME share given.
cost_impact: not quantified. GDPR exposure, and follow-on fraud against guests.
driver_status: more attacks on SaaS supply chains. Status (Oct 2026): H1 2026 alone exceeded all of 2025.
solved_today: data-protection consultancies and DPO services (no prices captured); breach-response handled ad hoc (my inference).
software_solvable: partly. Breach-notification workflows and vendor-risk registers can be productised, but the root cause lies with the vendors.
confidence: high for the trend; low for how owners themselves describe the pain (no owner quotes).

title: Telecom contracts: business lines fall outside consumer protection
who: autónomos, micro <10 and small companies (S.L., S.A.).
where: national.
reality: When an autónomo or an S.L. disputes a bill or a permanencia (minimum-term) penalty, consumer arbitration often isn't available. For companies, "la única vía posible será la vía judicial" ("the only possible route will be the courts").
evidence:
- The consumer administration handles only final consumers. An autónomo can use consumer arbitration only if the phone is not part of their professional activity (the contract type is a clue, not proof). The telecom ministry route is open to natural persons, including autónomos, but excludes companies, associations and comunidades de bienes. Otherwise, the courts. — [Infoautónomos, updated 26 Feb 2025](https://www.infoautonomos.com/blog/internet/como-reclamar-un-servicio-de-telefonia-o-internet-siendo-autonomo)
- Since 1 Apr 2012, lines held by an S.L. or S.A. can only go to court. The Secretaría's decisions are non-binding: "no tiene este carácter ejecutivo" ("does not have that enforceable character"). Old article, but consistent with Infoautónomos 2025. — [Legálitas, 23 Apr 2014](https://www.legalitas.com/actualidad/solucion-de-conflictos-entre-operadores-de-telefonia-y-sus-clientes)
- The rule that a permanencia penalty must be proportional to the unserved period (art. 62.5 TRLGDCU) is consumer law. The article does not cover business lines. — [Economist & Jurist, 15 Jan 2022](https://www.economistjurist.es/articulos-juridicos-destacados/como-reclamar-la-penalizacion-por-incumplir-la-permanencia-de-companias-telefonicas)
- In a Comunidad de Madrid arbitration file, the operator invoked art. 3 RDL 1/2007 to challenge the claimant's consumer status. Seen in a search snippet only. — [Comunidad de Madrid arbitration document](https://www.comunidad.madrid/info/docs/2023-10/03423.5.2020.pdf)
scale: I found no data on business telecom disputes.
cost_impact: not quantified. Penalties and disputed bills must be fought in court for small sums.
driver_status: the legal definition of a consumer (art. 3 TRLGDCU). Status: unchanged as of the Feb 2025 Infoautónomos update. I found no newer reform.
solved_today:
- In-house complaint, then the free ministry route (non-binding), then court.
- Legal subscriptions (Legálitas promo plans 16.92–45.50 €/month, but at least one plan excludes business matters; see VOX-20).
software_solvable: partly. Contract and permanencia tracking, renewal alerts and complaint-letter generation are software. The missing legal remedy is regulatory.
confidence: medium. The legal structure is solid; owner voice is thin in the sources I could reach.

title: Energy mis-selling by phone and exit penalties
who: autónomos / micro <10 (shops, bars, offices). The complainant's business status is not always stated.
where: national. Example from Murcia.
reality: A caller posing as the incumbent supplier (Endesa) promises "un importante descuento" ("a significant discount") and instead switches the customer to another retailer at a higher kWh price. The customer exercised the right of withdrawal and was charged a penalty: "Me engañan y no se trata de Endesa, se trata de la comercializadora IRIS ENERGÍA" ("They deceive me, and it isn't Endesa, it's the retailer IRIS ENERGÍA").
evidence:
- The OCU Reclama complaint above, with a 40 € penalty. — [OCU Reclama, 1 Aug 2023](https://www.ocu.org/reclamar/lista-reclamaciones-publicas/penalizaci-C3-B3n-tras-ser-enga-C3-B1ado/CPTES01844975-35)
- CNMC data for 2017: 793,080 SMEs on the free market against 13,945 on the regulated tariff; 964,067 complaints (3.4 per 100 supply points). Some retailers raised contract prices 20–30%, even in the first bill. Door-to-door selling was banned from Oct 2018 (RDL 15/2018). — [Público, 15 Mar 2019](https://www.publico.es/economia/asi-te-engana-compania-luz.html)
- I found no 2024–2026 business-specific dataset.
scale: about 793k SMEs on the free market (2017 data, old).
cost_impact: penalties (40 € in the example) and price rises (20–30% in 2017–18).
driver_status: a liberalised market sold through commission-based channels. The Forocoches thread recruiting commission recommenders for "seguros / luz / telefonía" (Oct 2026) shows the channel is alive. Current CNMC enforcement status: not verified.
solved_today: OCU complaints, consumer authorities (where the customer qualifies as a consumer), brokers.
software_solvable: partly. Bill auditing and contract or renewal tracking, yes. The selling practice itself is a market and enforcement issue.

title: Banking and card-acceptance costs, and funds held by payment fintechs
who: autónomos and micro <10 retailers and service providers.
where: national. One review implies the Basque Country, since it mentions TicketBAI.
reality: Bank maintenance fees keep creeping up, and fintech card acquirers sometimes hold funds or block transfers without explanation: "Me an retenido 60 euros sin ninguna explicación" ("They've withheld 60 euros with no explanation"). Another merchant was sold a terminal that failed TicketBAI: "me han vendido un aparato que no sirve para lo que su comercial me prometió" ("they sold me a device that doesn't do what their salesperson promised").
evidence:
- Average current-account maintenance fee of 160 €/year in 2025, up 6% on 148.82 €. Santander, CaixaBank, Sabadell, Deutsche Bank and Cajamar charge up to 240 €. Cajamar doubled its fee from 120 € to 240 €. Consumer accounts, not business accounts. — [Diario de León / Asufin, 27 May 2025](https://www.diariodeleon.es/economia/250527/2049229/bancos-disparan-comision-mantener-cuenta-corriente-160-euros.html)
- SumUp pricing (observed 23 Oct 2026): pay-as-you-go 1.49% for in-person card payments; "Pagos Plus" 19 €/month (189 €/year) at 0.75%; free business account with next-day payouts. — [SumUp ES pricing](https://www.sumup.com/es-es/precios/)
- SumUp Trustpilot reviews from Spanish reviewers, Oct 2026: funds retained (1 Oct), transfers blocked (2 Oct), "no atienden por teléfono" ("they don't answer the phone", 19 Oct), TicketBAI failure (12 Oct). — [Trustpilot SumUp, 1–2★ filter](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/sumup.com?stars=1&stars=2)
scale: SumUp has 60,139 Trustpilot reviews (global). I found no counts of Spanish merchants.
cost_impact: 160–240 €/year in account fees; 1.49% per transaction on pay-as-you-go.
driver_status: bank fee increases (+6% in two years); fintech risk controls. Status: ongoing.
solved_today: switching to free accounts (Asufin names Bankinter as offering a free non-online current account; SumUp's free business account); negotiating TPV (card-terminal) rates.
software_solvable: partly. Fee auditing and comparison are possible; the core is a banking product.

title: SaaS price creep and essential features gated behind higher tiers
who: autónomos, micro <10 and small 10–49 using invoicing, accounting or HR SaaS.
where: national.
reality: Owners report yearly price rises and having to move up a tier for basics: more invoices, sending invoices from their own email domain so they don't land in spam, phone support. "el precio solo sube y sube cada año" ("the price just keeps going up every year"). Invoices sent from Holded "las envía directamente a SPAM o no llegan al cliente" ("go straight to spam or never reach the client"), and the fix requires "un plan superior del doble" ("a plan twice the price").
evidence:
- Holded reviews: 1 Jul 2026 (price rises), 30 Sep 2026 (spam and forced upgrade), 25 Mar 2026 (invoice caps). — [Trustpilot Holded](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/holded.com?stars=1&stars=2)
- Holded Plus is capped at 250 invoices a year, including corrective invoices, and monthly billing costs about twice annual. — [Softabase, Jul 2026](https://softabase.com/es/guides/best-verifactu-invoicing-software)
- Factorial: "nos dijeron un precio y después nos añadieron paquetes para tener los servicios" ("they told us one price and then added packages to get the services", 3 Dec 2025), and a renewal tariff rise (24 Apr 2026). — [Trustpilot Factorial](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/factorialhr.es?stars=1&stars=2)
- Factorial's modular pricing means the starting figure "rarely resembles" the final one. — [Rework, 11 Sep 2026](https://resources.rework.com/es/tools/hr-people/best-factorial-alternatives)
- Declarando: "nunca me informaron de que además cobrarían 60 € + IVA por cada alta de trabajador" ("they never told me they'd also charge €60 + IVA for each employee registration", 3 Aug 2026). — [Trustpilot Declarando](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/declarando.es?stars=1&stars=2)
scale: Holded claims more than 80,000 companies (promotional, El Independiente, 26 Jun 2026). Similar complaints appear on at least three vendors' pages.
cost_impact: a plan "twice the price"; monthly billing at about 2× annual (Holded); 60 € + IVA per employee registration (Declarando).
driver_status: consolidation under private-equity-backed or strategic groups (ownership facts above; motive is my inference). Verifactu is a natural upsell moment (inference). Status: ongoing.
solved_today: switching to cheaper or free tools (Billin 6.60–20; Contasimple 0–15.95; FacturaDirecta 0–40; FacturaScripts 0; the free AEAT app).
software_solvable: yes. Flat, transparent pricing without invoice caps is a product decision.
confidence: medium. Reviews are unverified but consistent across vendors; I found no documented list-price history.

title: Hard cancellation, silent auto-renewals and charges after cancelling
who: autónomos, micro <10, small 10–49.
where: national.
reality: Owners cancel and keep being billed, can only "request" cancellation, or are told about a multi-year lock-in. "Cualquier SaaS permite cancelar con un click. No Factorial, quienes solo permiten solicitar la cancelación" ("Any SaaS lets you cancel with one click. Not Factorial, which only lets you request cancellation").
evidence:
- Factorial: "Cancelé mi suscripción anual dos veces, la última la noche anterior a la fecha de renovación" ("I cancelled my annual subscription twice, the last time the night before the renewal date", 6 Feb 2026); cancellation obstructed after a price rise (24 Apr 2026). — [Trustpilot Factorial](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/factorialhr.es?stars=1&stars=2)
- Billin: "Me siguen haciendo cargos meses después de dar de baja mi suscripción" ("They keep charging me months after I cancelled", 12 Oct 2023); "Quizás deberían enviar un mensaje recordando que se va a proceder a la renovacion" ("Maybe they should send a reminder that the renewal is coming", 8 Oct 2024). — [Trustpilot Billin](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/billin.net?stars=1&stars=2)
- Quipu: "se acogen a un contrato de permanencia de dos años para impedir la cancelación" ("they invoke a two-year minimum-term contract to block cancellation", 5 May 2026). Quipu's FAQ says you can cancel "en cualquier momento" ("at any time"). — [Trustpilot Quipu](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/getquipu.com?stars=1&stars=2); [Quipu pricing](https://getquipu.com/es/plan-de-precios)
- Holded: "Holded no facilita la baja de la suscripción" ("Holded doesn't make cancelling easy", 11 Sep 2026). — [Trustpilot Holded](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/holded.com?stars=1&stars=2)
- Legálitas: "Un auténtico calvario para darte de baja, cuotas que se siguen cobrando sin tener el servicio" ("A real ordeal to cancel; fees keep being charged without the service", 21 Oct 2026). — [Trustpilot Legálitas](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/www.legalitas.com)
- Declarando: "Cobran por todo, e incluso para cerrar" ("They charge for everything, even for closing", 15 Sep 2026). — [Trustpilot Declarando](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/declarando.es?stars=1&stars=2)
scale: the pattern recurs across at least six vendors. 1★ shares: Holded 8%, Quipu 11%, Factorial 14%, Legálitas 9% (observed 23 Oct 2026).
cost_impact: unexpected annual renewals (for example Quipu Premium at 588 €/yr) and hours spent chasing refunds.
driver_status: annual prepay with auto-renewal; B2B buyers lack consumer-style cancellation protections (inference linked to VOX-05). Status: ongoing.
solved_today: chargebacks and disputed SEPA direct debits (a SumUp review mentions a disputed SEPA authorisation, 26 Sep 2026), public reviews, lawyers.
software_solvable: yes. One-click cancellation and renewal reminders are a differentiator, and an SME-side subscription and renewal tracker is a product in itself.
confidence: medium-high (many independent, unverified reviews across vendors).

title: Data held hostage at exit
who: autónomos and micro <10 on invoicing or autónomo platforms.
where: national.
reality: On cancelling, users lose access to the invoice history they need for tax purposes, or are asked to pay to see it. "me han bloqueado el acceso a la plataforma de forma inmediata" ("they blocked my access to the platform immediately"), and then a maintenance fee was requested to view past invoices.
evidence:
- Quipu (6 May 2026), quoted above. — [Trustpilot Quipu](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/getquipu.com?stars=1&stars=2)
- Declarando: "Cuando he decidido darme de baja no me entregan las copias de mis facturas que tenía en su plataforma" ("When I decided to cancel, they wouldn't give me copies of the invoices I had on their platform", 10 Aug 2026). — [Trustpilot Declarando](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/declarando.es?stars=1&stars=2)
- Holded: the only way the user found to stop payments was deleting the account, losing the data (11 Sep 2026); "tengo que migrarlo a otra plataforma" ("I have to migrate it to another platform", 20 May 2026). — [Trustpilot Holded](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/holded.com?stars=1&stars=2)
- Counter-example: Cuéntica advertises "Sin permanencia" and data export "en cualquier momento". — [Cuéntica](https://cuentica.com/precios/)
scale: not quantified.
cost_impact: migration hours; fees to reach archives; a possible compliance risk if records are lost (inference).
driver_status: invoice records must be kept (the retention rules are the tax researcher's scope, not verified here). Verifactu records may deepen lock-in (inference).
solved_today: manual exports before cancelling, or staying subscribed.
software_solvable: yes. A free or cheap read-only archive tier and portability or migration tools.

title: Support gap: phone only on premium tiers, slow chat, chatbots
who: autónomos, micro <10, small 10–49.
where: national.
reality: When an invoice is rejected or payroll can't run, owners can't reach a human by phone. "El soporte telefónico está disponible únicamente para cuentas Premium" ("Phone support is only available for Premium accounts"); "no hay un telefono de atención para una urgencia" ("there's no phone line for an emergency").
evidence:
- Holded, phone on Premium only (21 Jul 2026). — [Trustpilot Holded](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/holded.com?stars=1&stars=2)
- Factorial (1 Sep 2026). — [Trustpilot Factorial](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/factorialhr.es?stars=1&stars=2)
- SumUp: "no atienden por teléfono, los agentes del Chat, son incompetentes" ("they don't answer the phone, the chat agents are incompetent", 19 Oct 2026). — [Trustpilot SumUp](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/sumup.com?stars=1&stars=2)
- Quipu: "llevo literalmente 2 meses esperando a que alguien me responda" ("I've literally been waiting 2 months for someone to answer", 12 Sep 2025). — [Trustpilot Quipu](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/getquipu.com?stars=1&stars=2)
- Declarando: "chatbot horrible" (11 Sep 2026). — [Trustpilot Declarando](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/declarando.es?stars=1&stars=2)
- Vendor pages, observed 23 Oct 2026: Quipu Starter has email-only support, with chat and phone from Solution at 30 €/month ([Quipu](https://getquipu.com/es/)). Declarando's response times vary by plan: <1 h Premium, <2 h Pro, <24 h Básico; Verifactu Plus gets an AI chat ([Declarando](https://declarando.es/precios)). Cuéntica offers phone Mon–Fri 8:00–15:00 ([Cuéntica](https://cuentica.com/precios/)). None of the fetched vendor pages mentions WhatsApp support.
scale: at least five vendors.
cost_impact: lost hours, missed filings, payroll delays.
driver_status: support cost-cutting through AI chat and tiering (inference). Status: ongoing.
solved_today: the gestor acts as the human support layer (inference); upgrading to a premium tier.
software_solvable: partly. This is a service-design choice: AI triage with human, Spanish-speaking phone or WhatsApp escalation.

title: Verifactu forces new software onto businesses, amid deadline confusion and rejected invoices
who: all businesses that issue invoices with software, in common-regime Spain. Autónomo / micro / small / medium.
where: national. Foral territories (Basque Country, Navarra) run their own systems such as TicketBAI; not verified here, see the tax researcher.
reality: Owners must move to compliant software while guides give different dates, and early users report AEAT rejections: "Error 4124 de Verifactu" (Holded user); "durante prácticamente todo el mes de enero esta funcionalidad no ha estado operativa" ("for practically all of January this function wasn't working", Quipu user, about bulk Verifactu sending).
evidence:
- Deadlines: 1 Jan 2027 for corporate-tax payers; 1 Jul 2027 for autónomos and others, under RDL 15/2025 (BOE 3 Dec 2025). Using non-compliant software carries a fine of 50,000 € per year (art. 201 bis LGT); software makers face up to 150,000 €. "La AEAT no certifica, homologa ni aprueba ningún programa de facturación" ("The AEAT does not certify, approve or endorse any invoicing program"). — [Softabase, checked 3–5 Jul 2026](https://softabase.com/es/guides/best-verifactu-invoicing-software)
- El Independiente gives the same dates. — [26 Jun 2026](https://www.elindependiente.com/eli/2026/06/26/programas-de-facturacion-con-verifactu-cuales-cumplen-y-cuales-elegir/)
- Conflicting dates in circulation: GuiaDeSoftware (updated 8 Sep 2026) still says "desde el 1 de julio de 2025 para empresas y desde el 1 de enero de 2026 para autónomos" — outdated. — [GuiaDeSoftware](https://www.guiadesoftware.com/blog/software-contabilidad-pymes-espana)
- Holded markets a "certificación Verifactu" (El Independiente), which Softabase says does not exist.
- User reports: Holded (7 Mar 2026, [Trustpilot](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/holded.com?stars=1&stars=2)); Quipu (31 Jan 2026, [Trustpilot](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/getquipu.com?stars=1&stars=2)).
scale: not captured here (tax researcher's scope).
