cost_impact: fines of up to 50,000 €/year; software at 0–99.50 €/month.
driver_status: the anti-fraud law and RD 1007/2023. Postponed to 2027 by RDL 15/2025; Softabase says not to expect a third postponement. Status (Oct 2026): a switching window before 2027.
solved_today:
- Free: the AEAT app (no simplified invoices, no export); free tiers of Billin, Contasimple (12 documents/yr), FacturaDirecta and FacturaScripts.
- Cheap: Billin 6.60, Holded Plus 7.50, Declarando "Verifactu Plus" 9.90, a3factura 9.95.
software_solvable: yes by definition, but the market is crowded at near-zero prices.
confidence: high for the regulatory facts; medium for the pain voice.

title: Errors in automated tax filings by low-cost platforms
who: autónomos on DIY platforms.
where: national.
reality: Owners rely on the platform to calculate quarterly and annual tax forms (models 303, 130, 390) and later find errors: "voy a recibir una penalización de Hacienda" ("I'm going to get a penalty from the tax agency").
evidence:
- Declarando (19 Oct 2026), quoted above. — [Trustpilot Declarando](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/declarando.es?stars=1&stars=2)
- Quipu: "yo he tenido durante dos años problemas con el modelo 390, que tiene errores" ("for two years I've had problems with the 390 form, which has errors", 5 Feb 2026); "hace los cálculos de forma incorrecta" ("it does the calculations wrong", 14 Jul 2025). — [Trustpilot Quipu](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/getquipu.com?stars=1&stars=2)
- At Declarando, an adviser reviews the books only on Premium ("Un asesor fiscal revisa tu contabilidad antes de presentar tus impuestos", "a tax adviser reviews your books before filing"), at 99.90 €/month +IVA. — [Declarando](https://declarando.es/precios)
scale: not quantified.
cost_impact: tax surcharges and penalties (amounts not captured).
driver_status: the shift from gestorías to DIY platforms.
solved_today: "tutelada" (adviser-reviewed) plans (Cuéntica 59, Declarando Premium 99.90, Quipu adviser from 80) or a traditional gestor (60–150 €/month, see VOX-19).
software_solvable: partly. Automated cross-checks and validations help; liability needs professional review.

title: HR and time-tracking software: per-employee minimums, add-on modules, module failures
who: micro <10 and small 10–49 employers, all sectors.
where: national.
reality: Small employers face per-employee pricing with minimums and paid add-on modules, and an outage can block payroll: "El modulo compensación lleva meses que no funciona y no se pueden pagar las nominas" ("The compensation module hasn't worked for months and payroll can't be paid").
evidence:
- Sesame HR: 4.75–9.00 € per employee per month excl. IVA, and "el mínimo de contratación son 15 empleados" ("the minimum contract is 15 employees"). — [Sesame, observed 23 Oct 2026](https://www.sesamehr.es/precios/)
- Factorial Core from 8 USD per user, modules by quote; Kenjo 6–10 € per employee. — [Rework, 11 Sep 2026](https://resources.rework.com/es/tools/hr-people/best-factorial-alternatives)
- A Capterra review says Factorial's price "puede resultar elevado para pequeñas empresas con un reducido número de empleados" ("can be high for small companies with few employees"). Search snippet only; the page returned 403. — [Capterra](https://capterra.com/p/168685/Factorial-HR-Software/reviews/?page=5)
- Holded's HR add-on costs 1.50 € per employee. — [Infoautónomos, 25 May 2026](https://www.infoautonomos.com/blog/mejor-programa-facturacion-pymes/)
- Factorial payroll failure (21 May 2026). — [Trustpilot Factorial](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/factorialhr.es?stars=1&stars=2)
scale: not captured. The time-tracking obligation and its status belong to the labour researcher.
cost_impact: my calculation from Sesame's FAQ and card price: a 3-person firm would still pay for 15 employees × 4.75 € = 71.25 €/month +IVA on Essential.
driver_status: the legal duty to record working hours (registro de jornada; labour researcher). Its status as of Oct 2026 is not verified here.
solved_today: Holded's HR add-on, Sesame, Factorial, Kenjo; paper or spreadsheets (inference).
software_solvable: yes. A micro-employer time-tracking product with no minimum seat count.

title: Low-quality, overpriced Kit Digital deliverables, harassment by sellers, pressure to sign
who: autónomos and micro <10 (segment III and below), some small 10–49.
where: national.
reality: Beneficiaries were cold-called repeatedly ("A mí no paran de acosarme 3 o 4 empresas de estas para hacerme una web", "3 or 4 of these companies won't stop harassing me to build me a website"). They then received templated sites billed at the full bono, sometimes after a two-year wait, and were pushed to sign the completion certificate. "Pero es que una web por 2000€ es una puta mierda" ("a €2,000 website is total crap"); "solo ha completado el 60% de lo presupuestado" ("they've only completed 60% of what was budgeted").
evidence:
- The pitch: "es todo gratis tu tranquilo solo tienes que firmar" ("it's all free, don't worry, you just have to sign"). One owner waited two years for a site ("2 años para que me hagan una web") and says Red.es told him he would have to pay 1,400 € himself if he did not sign the final justification. — [Forocoches, 14 May 2025](https://forocoches.com/foro/showthread.php?t=10343559)
- The agent pressured the couple to sign by warning "podrían exigirnos la devolución del Kit Digital" ("they could make us repay the Kit Digital"). Aid of 2,000 €; the beneficiary paid the 420 € VAT upfront. — [Forocoches, 26 Mar 2025](https://forocoches.com/foro/showthread.php?t=10295300)
- "Lo peor es que como mínimo se quedan los 2000 pavos del kit digital por ese trabajo nefasto" ("the worst part is they pocket at least the €2,000 of Kit Digital for that awful work", 29 Dec 2024). One agency reportedly had a single web designer handling 50–60 projects a month (31 Dec 2024). — [Forocoches, "Lo del kit digital es espeluznante", p. 2](https://forocoches.com/foro//showthread.php?p=495521024)
- "Pero es que una web por 2000€..." (9 Feb 2025); "La pedí.... y no veo resultados sinceramente" ("I applied... and honestly I see no results", 12 Feb 2025). — [Forocoches, "Sanguijuelas del Kit Digital", p. 3](https://forocoches.com/foro//showthread.php?p=489625325)
- Harassment by sellers (30 Jan 2024), and an agent's view: "veo muchas empresas haciendo mierda con tal de lucrarse lo máximo posible" ("I see many companies doing crap work to profit as much as possible"). — [Forocoches](https://forocoches.com/foro/showthread.php?t=9844561)
- Counterpoint: some users report good experiences with known firms and strict audits (Forocoches, 14 May 2025, same thread).
scale: more than 860,000 grants. — [España Digital](https://espanadigital.gob.es/lineas-de-actuacion/programa-kit-digital)
cost_impact: bono of 2,000 € per the forum (España Digital now lists 3,000 € for segment III); 420 € of VAT paid upfront; 1,400 € out-of-pocket risk; owner hours and a poor-quality website.
driver_status: NextGenerationEU-funded programme paid on the beneficiary's sign-off. Applications closed Oct 2025; justifications, payments and audits are still running (Oct 2026).
solved_today: freelancers rebuilding sites (one Forocoches user offered a rebuild for 20 € plus hosting); complaints to Red.es and Acelera Pyme; asking the gestor.
software_solvable: partly. Website-quality audits, rebuild or migration to cheap hosting, and contract checks are software or service. The subsidy design is policy.
confidence: medium-high (abundant, consistent forum voice; the press source is older).

title: After the subsidy: monthly fees, early-exit charges and an inflated "Kit price"
who: autónomos, micro <10, small 10–49 beneficiaries.
where: national.
reality: Once the subsidised 12 months end, beneficiaries keep paying monthly for services they barely use, sometimes with early-termination fees. Some established SaaS vendors charged more for the same service when the bono paid. "se queda con unos gastos mensuales absurdos de los servicios contratados" ("[the beneficiary] is left with absurd monthly costs for the services contracted"); "Venden el mismo servicio a un precio inflado" ("They sell the same service at an inflated price").
evidence:
- "contratos con terceros que le cobran dinero por darse de baja antes de 1 año" ("contracts with third parties that charge money to cancel before one year"), 12 Feb 2025. — [Forocoches, "Sanguijuelas del Kit Digital"](https://forocoches.com/foro//showthread.php?p=489625325)
- Billin: "Venden el mismo servicio a un precio inflado" (15 Apr 2025). After a switch from a free plan, a user was billed for several months once the Kit Digital subsidy was denied: "me lo facturan todo más el mes siguiente" ("they bill me for all of it on top of the next month", 23 Mar 2026). — [Trustpilot Billin](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/billin.net?stars=1&stars=2)
- Arsys: "Kit de página web Desde 1.250€/primer año (100% subvencionable) después desde 21,98€/mes". Search snippet; the page returned 404 on 23 Oct 2026. — [arsys.es/kit-digital](https://www.arsys.es/kit-digital)
- A forum poster puts a .com domain at about 10 €/yr and hosting at about 8 €/month, and says of the upkeep fee: "Esos 66 euros al mes son para TODO" ("those 66 euros a month are for EVERYTHING"), 10 Sep 2024. — [Forocoches, "Lo del kit digital es espeluznante", p. 2](https://forocoches.com/foro//showthread.php?p=495521024)
- An asesoría (tax adviser) used the kit to "costear 20 meses de servicios fiscales del autonomo" ("cover 20 months of the autónomo's tax services"), 31 Jan 2024. — [Forocoches](https://forocoches.com/foro/showthread.php?t=9844561)
scale: more than 860,000 grants. Renewal and cancellation rates: not found.
cost_impact: about 22–66 €/month after year one (Arsys from 21.98; forum figure 66), against about 8 €/month for hosting plus about 10 €/yr for a domain.
driver_status: the bonos covered 12 months of SaaS. With applications closed in Oct 2025, most subscriptions are past their subsidised year by Oct 2026 (inference).
solved_today: cancelling and moving to cheap hosting or site builders, keeping on paying, or hiring a lawyer for exit charges (forum).
software_solvable: yes. A subscription audit plus one-click migration of Kit-built sites and SaaS to low-cost plans.
confidence: medium (forum and vendor evidence; no aggregate data).

title: Kit Digital applications filed with autónomos' digital signatures without consent
who: autónomos (the case began with a physiotherapist) and micro <10.
where: Málaga (where the complaint started), Las Palmas de Gran Canaria (the investigating court), national reach.
reality: Autónomos found they were listed as beneficiaries of aid they never requested, filed with their digital signature, and that silence could leave them liable for repayment. "los autónomos aparecieron como beneficiarios de ayudas que jamás solicitaron" ("the autónomos appeared as beneficiaries of aid they never applied for").
evidence:
- A Supreme Court order of 1 Jun 2026 moves the investigation to Las Palmas (Juzgado de Plaza nº 2). TikTok promotions claimed "Puedes acceder al Kit Digital aunque tengas deudas con Hacienda" ("You can get Kit Digital even if you owe the tax agency"). The scheme relied on collusion between agents and "representantes voluntarios" (voluntary representatives). — [Vozpópuli, 14 Jun 2026](https://www.vozpopuli.com/espana/canarias/el-supremo-zanja-la-disputa-y-las-palmas-asumira-la-investigacion-del-fraude-masivo-del-kit-digital.html)
- "miles de autónomos" ("thousands of autónomos") "podrían figurar como beneficiarios" ("could appear as beneficiaries"). Victims are advised to check their application on Acelera Pyme with a certificate or Cl@ve. — [Merca2, 14 Jun 2026](https://www.merca2.es/2026/06/14/fraude-kit-digital-supremo-las-palmas-2397192/)
- Both outlets report the same court order on the same day, so they are not fully independent.
scale: "miles" (thousands), an unquantified claim.
cost_impact: possible repayment of the bono (segment caps of 3,000–12,000 € for micro and small firms) and legal fees.
driver_status: a weak identity check in the representative model, plus aggressive social-media recruitment. The investigation is open in Las Palmas (Jun 2026).
solved_today: checking the Acelera Pyme or sede electrónica records; lawyers; filing a complaint.
software_solvable: partly. Monitoring of public-registry and sede notifications and of use of one's digital certificate could be productised. Prevention depends on administrative controls.

title: Agentes digitalizadores unpaid for months
who: agentes digitalizadores, typically micro <10 and small 10–49 web agencies and IT providers, plus autónomos.
where: national. Albacete example (2023).
reality: Agencies that delivered Kit Digital work wait months for payment and lay off staff. "me deben 220.000€ por trabajos ya hechos y entregados" ("they owe me €220,000 for work already done and delivered").
evidence:
- The official terms are 70% within 60 days and 30% at 12 months; in practice the first 70% takes 5–7 months. One poster laid off most of a 5-person team. Another says his clients were owed "700 u 800k". — [Forocoches, 18 Feb – 28 Mar 2026](https://forocoches.com/foro/showthread.php?t=10610006)
- In 2023, Javier (Albacete) was owed more than 300,000 € and Ana (Oferplay) 200,000 €. More than 50 agents had organised in a Telegram group. Outsourcing the justification paperwork costs 300–400 € per file. "Este podría haber sido un proyecto muy guapo, pero la gente se está ahogando" ("This could have been a great project, but people are drowning"). — [The Objective, 8 May 2023](https://theobjective.com/economia/2023-05-08/autonomos-kit-digital/)
- About 25% of the budget had been paid by Feb 2026 (Tribunal de Cuentas). — [Vozpópuli](https://www.vozpopuli.com/espana/canarias/el-supremo-zanja-la-disputa-y-las-palmas-asumira-la-investigacion-del-fraude-masivo-del-kit-digital.html)
scale: about 9,300 registered agents (Genbeta, 2022); 25% payment execution (Feb 2026).
cost_impact: receivables of 200,000–300,000 € per agent cited; layoffs.
driver_status: Red.es justification bureaucracy, flagged by the Tribunal de Cuentas. The programme is closed to new applications but payments are ongoing (Oct 2026).
solved_today: working-capital credit (not captured), complaints, patience.
software_solvable: no, mostly. It is an administrative payment process. Justification-document automation could help a little.
confidence: medium-high (two independent sources three years apart, plus official execution data).

title: The cost of a gestoría for autónomos, and partial substitution by online platforms
who: autónomos and micro <10.
where: national.
reality: Autónomos pay a monthly gestoría fee or switch to online platforms that bundle software and tax filings for less, with uneven quality (see VOX-13). Some gestorías used Kit Digital to fund their own fees ("costear 20 meses de servicios fiscales del autonomo", "cover 20 months of the autónomo's tax services").
evidence:
- Estimated gestor cost of 60–150 €/month for autónomos and 200–400 €/month for a 10-employee SME. These are one guide's estimates. — [GuiaDeSoftware, 8 Sep 2026](https://www.guiadesoftware.com/blog/software-contabilidad-pymes-espana)
- Platform alternatives, observed 23 Oct 2026: Declarando 49.90 / 69.90 / 99.90 €/month +IVA with filings, or 29.90–49.90 € if "tu gestor presenta" (your gestor files) ([Declarando](https://declarando.es/precios)); Cuéntica Fiscalidad Tutelada 59 € and Contabilidad Tutelada 129 € +IVA ([Cuéntica](https://cuentica.com/precios/)); Quipu adviser "desde 80 €" ([Quipu](https://getquipu.com/es/plan-de-precios)); Billeo from 65 € +IVA for up to 15 invoices (search snippet, [Billeo](https://www.billeo.es/software)).
- The Kit Digital use by a gestoría is from the forum. — [Forocoches, 31 Jan 2024](https://forocoches.com/foro/showthread.php?t=9844561)
scale: Declarando has 4,023 Trustpilot reviews; Quipu claims "+20.000 negocios". The total number of autónomos using gestorías was not captured.
cost_impact: 720–1,800 €/year for a gestor (60–150 €/month, estimated).
driver_status: complex quarterly obligations; Verifactu by 2027. Status: ongoing.
solved_today: traditional gestorías; online gestorías and platforms (Declarando, Cuéntica, Quipu with adviser, Billeo).
software_solvable: partly. Software cuts the cost; advice and liability still need professionals.
confidence: medium (vendor prices are solid; the gestoría fee range is one guide's estimate).

title: Legal-advice subscriptions: coverage disputes and cancellation friction
who: autónomos and micro <10 (and households).
where: national.
reality: Owners pay a monthly legal subscription for peace of mind, then report a coverage refusal tied to a waiting period, and trouble cancelling. "Cuando lo contratas todo bien, pero cuando te hace falta te dicen que no llevas un año" ("When you sign up everything's fine, but when you need it they tell you haven't been a customer for a year").
evidence:
- The quote above and "Un auténtico calvario para darte de baja" ("a real ordeal to cancel"), both 21 Oct 2026. The company replied that the service is annual and renewable without lock-in. TrustScore 4.5 from 13,656 reviews, 9% 1★. — [Trustpilot Legálitas](https://es.trustpilot.com/review/www.legalitas.com)
- At least one promo plan covers "asesoramiento jurídico sobre asuntos de la vida familiar (no empresarial ni profesional)" ("legal advice on family-life matters, not business or professional"), so business coverage needs a specific plan. — [legalitas.com promo pages (snippet)](https://www.legalitas.com/promo/um/vol)
- Demand for cheap legal help: a Forocoches thread, "Abogado ofrece servicios jurídicos profesionales a precios forococheros", has 1,068 replies (still active Oct 2026). — [Forocoches f=23 listing](https://forocoches.com/foro/forumdisplay.php?f=23)
scale: 13,656 Trustpilot reviews (a proxy for a large customer base).
cost_impact: about 203–546 €/yr.
driver_status: cheap access to lawyers; the annual auto-renewal model.
solved_today: Legálitas and similar subscriptions; ad hoc lawyers.
software_solvable: partly. AI legal triage with lawyer escalation is possible, but this is a regulated profession.
confidence: medium-low (few negative reviews visible; prices from promo pages).

title: The gestor decides the software; otherwise, double data entry
who: autónomos, micro <10, small 10–49.
where: national.
reality: The owner's software choice is limited by what the gestor uses (for example a3). Otherwise the owner exports and the gestor re-imports or re-keys. On a3: "La opción obligada si tu asesor externo lo usa" ("the obligatory option if your external adviser uses it").
evidence:
- GuiaDeSoftware (8 Sep 2026), as above. Single analytic source. — [GuiaDeSoftware](https://www.guiadesoftware.com/blog/software-contabilidad-pymes-espana)
- Vendor gestor features: Cuéntica, Declarando, Quipu, Anfix (sources above).
- A gestoría used Kit Digital to fund its client's fees. — [Forocoches, 31 Jan 2024](https://forocoches.com/foro/showthread.php?t=9844561)
scale: no figure found for the share of autónomos who use a gestor or for how often the gestor chooses the software.
cost_impact: duplicated data entry and export/import hours (not quantified).
driver_status: gestorías standardise on professional suites (a3 by Wolters Kluwer, among others). Status: ongoing.
solved_today: CSV and Excel exports, gestor access to client software, or the gestor-mandated tool.
software_solvable: yes. Connectors and export formats for the main gestoría suites, and gestor-side multi-client dashboards.
confidence: medium-low (qualitative; one analytic source plus vendor product design).

title: A patchwork of about 150 local rule-sets for multi-city fleets
who: fleet operators, couriers and delivery partners operating in several cities (from autónomos with one van to national carriers); e-commerce sellers using them.
where: national. Examples: Madrid, Barcelona/AMB, Bilbao, Zaragoza, Sevilla, Palma, Granada, Valladolid, Córdoba, A Coruña.
reality: each city defines its own perimeter, hours, restricted labels, residency or domicile tests, quotas and exemptions. Some are label-based and some are whitelist (access-control) based. A van compliant in Zaragoza (B allowed 8–20h) is not necessarily compliant in Madrid Distrito Centro (B light vans banned since 2024) or Bilbao (B restricted 7–20h since Jun 2025).
evidence:
- 151 municipalities and 33M people; 56 "fully active" ZBEs and 89 in approval. — [Motor16, 16 Feb 2026](https://www.motor16.com/las-ultimas-noticias/zbe-ciudades-multas-coches/)
- 149 municipalities; the association built a national ZBE info site for hauliers. — [Fenadismer, 7 Jul 2024](https://www.fenadismer.es/los-transportistas-ya-pueden-consultar-todas-las-zonas-de-bajas-emisiones-en-una-sola-web/)
- Rule diversity across cities: see the section 2 table (madrid.es, ecomovilidad, BOIB).
scale: about 150 obliged municipalities and 45 NAP resources ([NAP](https://nap.dgt.es/es/dataset/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones)); 2.74M vans and 2.46M trucks nationally ([DGT Anuario 2024](https://www.dgt.es/export/sites/web-DGT/.galleries/downloads/dgt-en-cifras/publicaciones/Anuario_Estadistico_General/Anuario-Estadistico-General-2024.pdf)).
cost_impact: €200 per infringement (€260 in Barcelona episodes); time spent reading ordinances (no hours data found).
driver_status: Ley 7/2021 art. 14 and RD 1052/2022 (in force) plus individual municipal ordinances; status ranges from in force with fines to not yet adopted (section 2).
solved_today:
- Association websites (Astac/RACC, price unknown), consumer apps (ZBE España, free tag), aggregator blogs (ecomovilidad, Iberfurgo, RACE).
- HERE and TomTom LEZ layers, which are Euro-class based with unverified Spanish coverage and no prices found.
- Documented issue: Green-Zones still says "one of 7 zones in Spain" ([green-zones.eu](https://www.green-zones.eu/en/)).
software_solvable: **Yes.** A normalised, versioned rules database and API is the direct fix.

title: Legal whiplash: annulments, suspensions and reinstatements change rules overnight
who: all fleets, couriers and autónomos; municipalities.
where: Madrid, Málaga, Valladolid, Barcelona (suspension), Bilbao (appeal pending), and other TSJ cases.
reality: a zone that fined last week may stop (Málaga, 14 Oct 2026), be suspended for an emergency (Barcelona, 22 Jan–16 Mar 2026), be annulled but keep fining (Valladolid), or be replaced by a new ordinance while old fines are litigated (Madrid). Fleets cannot tell from official feeds which state applies today.
evidence:
- Málaga TSJA 896/2026 of 6 May 2026; fines stopped 14 Oct 2026. — [ecomovilidad Málaga, 22 Oct 2026](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/malaga/malaga/); [Motorpasión, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.motorpasion.com/industria/oficial-zbe-malaga-no-multara-a-coches-etiqueta-b-justicia-tumba-ayuntamiento-devolvera-dinero)
- Madrid: Supreme Court inadmission 15 Apr 2026; new ordinance in force 7 Apr 2026; TSJM enforcement proceedings July 2026. — [Infobae, 21 Apr 2026](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/04/21/el-tribunal-supremo-confirma-la-anulacion-parcial-de-la-zona-de-bajas-emisiones-en-madrid-al-rechazar-el-recurso-del-ayuntamiento/); [El Diario de Madrid, 15 Jul 2026](https://www.eldiariodemadrid.es/articulo/tribunales/tsjm-pieza-separada-ejecucion-sentencia-zonas-bajas-emisiones-madrid/20260715165846137443.html)
- Barcelona suspension and resumption. — [zbe.barcelona](https://www.zbe.barcelona/)
- Valladolid annulled 16 Mar 2026 but not final. — [ecomovilidad](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/valladolid/valladolid/)
scale: Madrid alone about 3.4M sanction files ([El Diario de Madrid](https://www.eldiariodemadrid.es/articulo/tribunales/tsjm-pieza-separada-ejecucion-sentencia-zonas-bajas-emisiones-madrid/20260715165846137443.html)); Málaga 46,562 fines ([Motorpasión](https://www.motorpasion.com/industria/oficial-zbe-malaga-no-multara-a-coches-etiqueta-b-justicia-tumba-ayuntamiento-devolvera-dinero)).
cost_impact: €663M in disputed Madrid fines (AEA estimate); Málaga €1.38M refunds with up to four years' delay.
driver_status: Madrid OMS as amended by Ordenanza 2/2026 (in force; old-fine execution pending); Málaga ordinance ZBE chapter (annulled, not final); Valladolid 2024 ordinance (annulled, not final, still fining); Barcelona 2023 ordinance (in force, upheld 24 Nov 2025).
solved_today: press monitoring, lawyers and associations (AEA, OCU). No software alerting product found.
software_solvable: **Partly.** Legal-change monitoring and alerts can be productised, but interpreting rulings needs human legal review.

title: The national NAP feed is incomplete, stale and semantically thin
who: fleet-software vendors, navigation and routing providers, fleet operators; municipalities as publishers.
where: national (DGT NAP).
reality: anyone building routing on official data finds missing cities (Zaragoza, Vigo, Córdoba), "active" records for zones not enforcing (Valencia, Málaga), start dates that do not match when fines began (Palma), and rule details in free text or links to PDFs.
evidence:
- My parsing on 23 Oct 2026: Valencia.xml "active" from 2026-06-01; Málaga.xml description is only a PDF link; Palma.xml published 2025-01-07; Valladolid phases in free text. — [NAP files](https://nap.dgt.es/datex2/v3/dgt/zbe/ControledZonePublication/)
- The DGT 3.0 model has only labels, free-text conditions and a timetable. — [DGT ED MOV 2023/01](https://www.dgt.es/export/sites/web-DGT/.galleries/downloads/muevete-con-seguridad/normas-de-trafico/MOV-gestion-trafico/ED1_2023-ZBE-en-DGT30.pdf)
- Second source on reality: no ZBE in Valencia. — [ecomovilidad Valencia](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/valencia/valencia/)
scale: 45 resources and 46 files; at least 3 of the 10 fining or regime cities in section 2 are missing.
cost_impact: wrong routing or compliance decisions leading to €200 fines; unquantified.
driver_status: RD 1052/2022 art. 10.2 requires notification within one month (in force); DGT ED MOV 2023/01 (in force since Feb 2023).
solved_today: vendors' own curation (HERE, TomTom) and manual research. No complaints on record, but the inconsistencies are documented above.
software_solvable: **Yes.** Curation, validation against ordinances and press, and enrichment of semantics.

title: Domicile and residency rules penalise out-of-town fleets and are legally fragile
who: fleets and autónomos whose vehicles are registered or taxed outside the city (including vehicles owned by renting or leasing companies), regional delivery partners and commuters' work vans.
where: Madrid (cars on the city tax roll since 2022), Granada (tax domicile), Málaga (annulled non-domicile rule), Palma (resident authorisations), Valencia draft (out-of-province first).
reality: the same unlabelled vehicle is legal for a local and fined for a visitor. For vans the impact varies: Madrid now lets unlabelled non-cars circulate regardless of domicile outside the special zones, while Granada restricts any unlabelled vehicle without local tax domicile.
evidence:
- Madrid unlabelled cars must have been on the tax roll continuously since 1 Jan 2022; non-cars are exempt from that test. — [madrid.es FAQ](https://www.madrid.es/portales/munimadrid/es/Inicio/Movilidad-y-transportes/Zonas-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Preguntas-frecuentes-sobre-Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones-ZBE-/?vgnextfmt=default&vgnextoid=9dec1d96b08ed710VgnVCM1000001d4a900aRCRD&vgnextchannel=d2d2edf0f70ab710VgnVCM2000001f4a900aRCRD)
- Granada requires both no label and no local tax domicile. — [Xataka, 2 Oct 2025](https://www.xataka.com/movilidad/granada-multa-hoy-su-nueva-zona-bajas-emisiones-quienes-pueden-acceder-multas-excepciones)
- Málaga's non-domicile regime was annulled (reasoning disputed). — [Motorpasión, 22 Oct 2026](https://www.motorpasion.com/industria/oficial-zbe-malaga-no-multara-a-coches-etiqueta-b-justicia-tumba-ayuntamiento-devolvera-dinero)
scale: Málaga's 46,562 fines were all under a non-domicile rule. National scale unknown.
cost_impact: €200 per entry; refunds in Málaga.
driver_status: municipal ordinances (Madrid in force; Granada in force; Málaga annulled, not final).
solved_today: case-by-case registration; no tool models domicile rules (NAP encodes none).
software_solvable: **Partly.** The rules can be encoded per vehicle and holder. Vehicle domicile data comes from the fleet's own records.

title: An ageing commercial fleet of about 1.08M vans and 1.02M trucks aged 20+ years
who: autónomos with old vans (trades, markets, small couriers), small hauliers.
where: national, most acute in Madrid, Barcelona/AMB, Bilbao, Palma and Granada.
reality: owners of pre-2006 diesel vans (no label) cannot enter label-restricted ZBEs during restricted hours. They choose between buying a newer van, using permits or quotas, sub-contracting, or exiting the zone.
evidence:
- 1,084,677 of 2,741,010 vans and 1,021,451 of 2,462,425 trucks are aged 20+. — [DGT Anuario 2024, tables 72 and 80](https://www.dgt.es/export/sites/web-DGT/.galleries/downloads/dgt-en-cifras/publicaciones/Anuario_Estadistico_General/Anuario-Estadistico-General-2024.pdf)
- More than half of vans and trucks are unlabelled (unnamed DGT analysis). — [Ecoticias, 24 Jan 2024](https://www.ecoticias.com/co2/etiquetas-ambientales-dgt)
scale: about 1.1–1.3M unlabelled vans is an inference (section 3).
cost_impact: MOVES III aid up to €7k/€9k per N1 (status after 2024 unclear) ([IDAE](https://www.idae.es/ayudas-y-financiacion/para-movilidad-y-vehiculos/programa-moves-iii)); no sourced van prices.
driver_status: label system per the Reglamento General de Vehículos (unchanged at least to 2027, snippet-level: [motor.es](https://www.motor.es/noticias/confirmado-etiquetas-dgt-quedan-como-estan-2025111050.html)); ZBE ordinances (various).
solved_today: dealers and renting, MOVES aid (uncertain in 2026), city exemptions for older autónomos (Madrid 59+, Barcelona near-retirement until 31 Mar 2028).
software_solvable: **Partly.** Renewal planning, total-cost tools and aid finders help, but the core problem is capital expenditure.

title: Madrid Distrito Centro has label × MMA time windows plus per-vehicle registration
who: delivery fleets, trades and suppliers serving central Madrid (including rental, replacement and leased vans).
where: Madrid (ZBEDEP Distrito Centro).
reality: a C-label van may only enter 7–15h, and a B-label light van not at all since 2024. Light-vehicle holders must have IAE registration and pre-register each plate in the permits system (Mi Carpeta or appointment). Rented, leased and replacement vehicles need extra documents. Night deliveries need a declaración responsable renewed yearly with proof of deliveries.
evidence: [madrid.es DC professionals page](https://www.madrid.es/portales/munimadrid/es/Inicio/Movilidad-y-transportes/Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones-de-Especial-Proteccion-ZBEDEP-Distrito-Centro-Empresas-y-profesionales-que-presten-servicios-y-entreguen-o-recojan-suministros/?vgnextfmt=default&vgnextoid=f4f085282f8eb710VgnVCM2000001f4a900aRCRD&vgnextchannel=220e31d3b28fe410VgnVCM1000000b205a0aRCRD) (single official source; primary).
scale: unknown number of registered professional vehicles (gap).
cost_impact: €200 per entry outside the window; admin hours per vehicle (not quantified).
driver_status: Madrid OMS as amended by Ordenanza 2/2026 and Decreto 178 (acoustic loading protocol); in force with fines.
solved_today: manual registration in Mi Carpeta, gestorías (administrative agents) for ownership-change documents, dispatchers' spreadsheets (inference). No prices.
software_solvable: **Yes.** Permit-ledger and dispatch-window constraints.

title: Heterogeneous permit quotas and invitations to ration and notify
who: local shops and e-commerce sellers receiving deliveries, trades, autónomos with unlabelled or B vans.
where: Bilbao (6 invitations per month), Barcelona (24 daily passes per year), Zaragoza (8 accesses per month), Sevilla (10 per month, snippet-level), Granada (forms), Córdoba (exemption list).
reality: businesses must track quotas per plate and per month, notify plates within deadlines (Bilbao up to 2 days after access), and re-register vehicles. Errors produce €200 fines.
evidence: [ecomovilidad Bilbao](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/vizcaya/bilbao/); [ecomovilidad Barcelona](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/barcelona/barcelona/); [ecomovilidad Zaragoza](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/zaragoza/zaragoza/); [ecomovilidad Sevilla](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/sevilla/sevilla/). Single secondary source per city.
scale: unknown.
cost_impact: €200 per missed notification or over-quota entry.
driver_status: municipal ordinances (in force with fines in all four cities).
solved_today: municipal portals and apps per city; manual.
software_solvable: **Yes.** A permit wallet with quota tracking, though many cities lack APIs.

title: Foreign-registered vehicles and cross-border partners
who: EU hauliers and couriers, foreign-plated rental or relocation vans, seasonal workers and tourism-sector vans.
where: Palma, Barcelona/AMB, Bilbao, Madrid, Zaragoza.
reality: foreign vehicles have no DGT label, so cities require Euro-class-based registration. Palma requires registration 5 days ahead with a ferry or flight ticket for a 30-day permit. AMB authorisations last up to 2 years. Bilbao has its own register. Zaragoza instead exempts foreign plates not in the DGT register.
evidence:
- Palma: fines on foreign plates were the first category of complaints after fines began on 1 Jul 2025. — [BOIB 37, 24 Mar 2026](https://www.caib.es/eboibfront/pdf/ca/2026/37/1215590)
- AMB registry. — [ecomovilidad BCN](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/barcelona/barcelona/)
- Bilbao register. — [bilbao.eus](https://www.bilbao.eus/cs/Satellite?c=Page&cid=1279235266667&language=es&pageid=1279235266667&pagename=Bilbaonet%2FPage%2FBIO_contenidoFinal)
- Madrid: same rules apply. — [madrid.es FAQ](https://www.madrid.es/portales/munimadrid/es/Inicio/Movilidad-y-transportes/Zonas-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Preguntas-frecuentes-sobre-Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones-ZBE-/?vgnextfmt=default&vgnextoid=9dec1d96b08ed710VgnVCM1000001d4a900aRCRD&vgnextchannel=d2d2edf0f70ab710VgnVCM2000001f4a900aRCRD)
- Zaragoza exemption. — [ecomovilidad Zaragoza](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/zaragoza/zaragoza/)
scale: unknown.
cost_impact: €200 per fine plus cross-border collection; registration admin.
driver_status: municipal ordinances; the Palma resolution of 20 Mar 2026 (BOIB 37) is in force.
solved_today: city web forms; Green-Zones (stale for Spain); TCS and ADAC travel guides (snippet-level).
software_solvable: **Yes.** Euro-class-to-label mapping plus multi-city registration filing.

title: Rented, leased and replacement vans: fines hit the registered holder and documents are needed per vehicle
who: renting and leasing companies, van-rental firms, the SMEs and delivery partners who drive their vehicles.
where: Barcelona and Madrid documented; likely national.
reality: camera fines go to the registered holder (the lessor), who re-invoices the customer. Madrid's permits system requires renting or leasing contracts and lessor certificates, and repair orders for replacement vehicles, before the vehicle may enter Distrito Centro.
evidence: "Rental companies pass the fine to the customer who was driving" ([Iberfurgo, 26 Jun 2026](https://www.iberfurgo.com/zbe-barcelona/)); Madrid document requirements ([madrid.es DC](https://www.madrid.es/portales/munimadrid/es/Inicio/Movilidad-y-transportes/Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones-de-Especial-Proteccion-ZBEDEP-Distrito-Centro-Empresas-y-profesionales-que-presten-servicios-y-entreguen-o-recojan-suministros/?vgnextfmt=default&vgnextoid=f4f085282f8eb710VgnVCM2000001f4a900aRCRD&vgnextchannel=220e31d3b28fe410VgnVCM1000000b205a0aRCRD)).
scale: unknown.
cost_impact: €200 per fine plus admin re-invoicing fees (not quantified).
driver_status: municipal ordinances; the traffic law's owner-liability rule (art. 76 z3 classifies ZBE breaches as serious infringements).
solved_today: manual fine-transfer workflows at lessors (inference).
software_solvable: **Yes.** Fine-to-driver matching and pre-trip compliance checks for rental fleets.

title: Fine exposure at scale
who: all vehicle holders; for business, fleets with repeated daily entries.
where: Madrid, Málaga, Barcelona, Granada, Bilbao, Palma, Zaragoza, Sevilla.
reality: each non-compliant entry is a €200 serious infringement. For a van making daily central deliveries, the exposure accumulates quickly. Fines arrive by post or electronic address days later.
evidence: Madrid more than 3.3M fines and €650M (Sept 2021–Nov 2025, AEA) ([Xataka, 27 Apr 2026](https://www.xataka.com/movilidad/madrid-cobro-650-millones-euros-multas-zbe-supremo-le-da-razon-a-conductores-dinero-no-vuelve)); more than 3.4M and €663M to 31 Dec 2025 ([El Diario de Madrid, 15 Jul 2026](https://www.eldiariodemadrid.es/articulo/tribunales/tsjm-pieza-separada-ejecucion-sentencia-zonas-bajas-emisiones-madrid/20260715165846137443.html)); Málaga 46,562 ([Motorpasión](https://www.motorpasion.com/industria/oficial-zbe-malaga-no-multara-a-coches-etiqueta-b-justicia-tumba-ayuntamiento-devolvera-dinero)).
scale: millions of fines (Madrid); business share unknown.
cost_impact: €200 per fine (€100 early payment); €260 in Barcelona episodes.
driver_status: Ley sobre Tráfico art. 76 z3 plus municipal ordinances (in force).
solved_today: paying, appealing via lawyers or associations, fine-management services (not researched).
software_solvable: **Partly.** Prevention through pre-trip checks and fine centralisation. Appeals still need legal input.

title: Refund and appeal limbo after court rulings
who: SMEs and autónomos who paid or appealed ZBE fines.
where: Madrid, Málaga, Valladolid.
reality:
- Madrid refuses automatic refunds while lower courts annul individual fines.
- Málaga will refund only after the ruling is final, possibly over 4 years.
- Valladolid fines continue under a ruling that is not final.
- Businesses do not know whether to pay early at the 50% discount or appeal.
evidence: Madrid: "no procede devolver las multas" ([El Diario de Madrid, 15 Jul 2026](https://www.eldiariodemadrid.es/articulo/tribunales/tsjm-pieza-separada-ejecucion-sentencia-zonas-bajas-emisiones-madrid/20260715165846137443.html)); OCU says non-final appealed cases have better odds ([Xataka](https://www.xataka.com/movilidad/madrid-cobro-650-millones-euros-multas-zbe-supremo-le-da-razon-a-conductores-dinero-no-vuelve)); Málaga ([Motorpasión](https://www.motorpasion.com/industria/oficial-zbe-malaga-no-multara-a-coches-etiqueta-b-justicia-tumba-ayuntamiento-devolvera-dinero)).
scale: Madrid about 3.4M files; Málaga 13,694 paid and 32,868 suspended.
cost_impact: €663M (Madrid, AEA estimate); €1.38M (Málaga).
driver_status: TSJM execution proceedings (pending); TSJA 896/2026 (not final, expected about 25 Nov 2026).
solved_today: associations (AEA), lawyers, consumer organisation OCU.
software_solvable: **Partly.** Tracking fines and appeal deadlines; claims processing is legal work.

title: Dynamic pollution-episode restrictions
who: fleets and autónomos with B or unlabelled vans.
where: Madrid (unlabelled non-cars banned on episode days), Barcelona (B banned in episodes since 1 Jan 2026; €260), Alicante (rings II and III by decree), Castellón and Sevilla episode-only models.
reality: a vehicle legal yesterday is illegal today because the regional or city government declares an episode, and fleets need same-day alerts. NacióDigital notes no Catalan episode has been declared since 2015.
evidence: [madrid.es FAQ](https://www.madrid.es/portales/munimadrid/es/Inicio/Movilidad-y-transportes/Zonas-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Preguntas-frecuentes-sobre-Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones-ZBE-/?vgnextfmt=default&vgnextoid=9dec1d96b08ed710VgnVCM1000001d4a900aRCRD&vgnextchannel=d2d2edf0f70ab710VgnVCM2000001f4a900aRCRD); [Iberfurgo, 26 Jun 2026](https://www.iberfurgo.com/zbe-barcelona/); [NacióDigital, 28 Apr 2026](https://naciodigital.cat/impacte/ciutats/les-zbe-de-larea-de-barcelona-senduriran-el-2028.html); [ecomovilidad Alicante](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/alicante/alicante/); [El Español, 7 Mar 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/valencia/20260307/vox-rechaza-valencia-zona-bajas-emisiones-aprobo-castellon-pone-riesgo-millones/1003744158258_0.html) (Castellón)
scale: B vehicles are 12% of Barcelona's fleet (NacióDigital).
cost_impact: €260 per entry in Barcelona episodes; €200 elsewhere.
driver_status: Catalan Decree 132/2024 (cited by ecomovilidad; the episode-declaration instrument itself was not verified); Madrid OMS DT 7ª (the transitional provision; in force).
solved_today: official websites and press; no fleet-integrated alerting found. The NAP has no episode field.
software_solvable: **Yes.** Alerts and dispatch blocking, but only if episode declarations are machine-readable or scraped.

title: The conditional "NO2 kill-switch" in Madrid's transitional regime
who: holders of unlabelled vans and trucks (including non-Madrid fleets) operating in Madrid outside the special zones.
where: Madrid.
reality: unlabelled vans may circulate only while NO2 limits are met at every station. A single breach lets the Junta de Gobierno end the regime, with fines 6 months after BOCM publication. Fleets cannot plan renewal on a fixed date.
evidence: [madrid.es FAQ](https://www.madrid.es/portales/munimadrid/es/Inicio/Movilidad-y-transportes/Zonas-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Preguntas-frecuentes-sobre-Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones-ZBE-/?vgnextfmt=default&vgnextoid=9dec1d96b08ed710VgnVCM1000001d4a900aRCRD&vgnextchannel=d2d2edf0f70ab710VgnVCM2000001f4a900aRCRD); [ecomovilidad Madrid](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/comunidad-de-madrid/madrid/)
scale: unknown number of unlabelled vans operating in Madrid.
cost_impact: potential forced renewal on 6 months' notice; MOVES aid uncertain.
driver_status: Ordenanza 2/2026, disposición transitoria séptima; in force since 7 Apr 2026; regime active as of Oct 2026 (no termination found).
solved_today: nothing specific; associations monitor.
software_solvable: **Partly.** Air-quality and legal monitoring with renewal-planning alerts; the underlying cost is capital expenditure.

title: Scheduled B-label phase-outs (2027–2030)
who: fleets with diesel vans from 2006–2013 or petrol vans from 2001–2005 (B), and heavy vehicles from 2006 onward.
where:
- Catalonia: municipalities over 50,000 before 1 Jan 2028.
- Palma: B out from 1 Jan 2027.
- Bilbao: B exemptions end by 31 Dec 2029; only Cero, ECO and C from 2030.
- Valladolid: B from end-2027 (ordinance annulled, not final).
- Vigo: B from 2029.
reality: vans compliant today become non-compliant on known future dates. Fleet owners must plan renewals city by city.
evidence: [NacióDigital, 28 Apr 2026](https://naciodigital.cat/impacte/ciutats/les-zbe-de-larea-de-barcelona-senduriran-el-2028.html); [ecomovilidad BCN (Decree 132/2024)](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/barcelona/barcelona/); [BOIB 37, 24 Mar 2026](https://www.caib.es/eboibfront/pdf/ca/2026/37/1215590); [ecomovilidad Bilbao](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/vizcaya/bilbao/); [Atlántico, 10 Sep 2026](https://www.atlantico.net/vigo/entran-vigor-zonas-bajas-emisiones_1_20260910-4408680.html)
scale: Barcelona B = 12% of vehicles; Vigo 57,934 B vehicles. Van-specific B count unknown.
cost_impact: renewal capex; resale-value loss for B vans (unquantified).
driver_status: Catalan Decree 132/2024 (in force; the ordinance amendment had not started as of Oct 2026); Palma ordinance (BOIB 167/2024, in force); Bilbao ordinance (in force); Vigo ordinance (in force, phased).
solved_today: dealer and renting advice; no planning tool found.
software_solvable: **Partly.** Fleet compliance forecasting per city and date.

title: When the destination is inside the zone, avoidance routing does not help
who: last-mile couriers and delivery partners, e-commerce sellers' carriers, trades visiting customers.
where: every enforcing city; especially Madrid Distrito Centro, Barcelona, Bilbao and Granada.
reality: route optimisers and LEZ "avoid" flags (HERE, TomTom) route around zones, but a stop inside the zone cannot be avoided. Compliance depends on which vehicle is dispatched, at what hour, with which permit, or on an exempt car park or hand-off.
evidence:
- HERE avoidance is parameter-based (Euro class, fuel, weight, departure) and avoids a zone if any one parameter matches. — [HERE docs](https://docs.here.com/routing/docs/truck-restrictions-env-zones)
- Madrid windows are label- and MMA-specific. — [madrid.es DC](https://www.madrid.es/portales/munimadrid/es/Inicio/Movilidad-y-transportes/Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones-de-Especial-Proteccion-ZBEDEP-Distrito-Centro-Empresas-y-profesionales-que-presten-servicios-y-entreguen-o-recojan-suministros/?vgnextfmt=default&vgnextoid=f4f085282f8eb710VgnVCM2000001f4a900aRCRD&vgnextchannel=220e31d3b28fe410VgnVCM1000000b205a0aRCRD)
- Granada car-park exemption. — [Xataka, 2 Oct 2025](https://www.xataka.com/movilidad/granada-multa-hoy-su-nueva-zona-bajas-emisiones-quienes-pueden-acceder-multas-excepciones)
scale: all in-zone deliveries; no volume data.
cost_impact: €200 per wrong dispatch; idle compliant vehicles (unquantified).
driver_status: all municipal ordinances (in force where fining).
solved_today: dispatcher knowledge; route optimisers without ZBE semantics (inference). No Spanish ZBE-aware dispatch product found.
software_solvable: **Yes.** Constraint-aware vehicle assignment (vehicle state, permit state and time windows) via an API.
confidence: medium. The mechanism is well evidenced; demand is inferred.

title: Loading and unloading (DUM) windows and night-delivery permits
who: suppliers to shops, markets and HORECA (hotels, restaurants, cafés); parcel carriers; e-commerce sellers' delivery partners.
where: Madrid (night 23–7h and food 5–7h by declaración responsable valid 1 year); A Coruña (6–11h, 5–12h for Cero and ECO); Córdoba (home delivery and supplier exemptions); Granada (loading exemption form, snippet-level); Málaga (N1 4-year transition, now moot); Zaragoza (DUM authorisation claim, unverified).
reality: loading rules sit outside or alongside label rules, need yearly re-filing with proof of deliveries (Madrid), and differ by city.
evidence: [madrid.es DC](https://www.madrid.es/portales/munimadrid/es/Inicio/Movilidad-y-transportes/Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones-de-Especial-Proteccion-ZBEDEP-Distrito-Centro-Empresas-y-profesionales-que-presten-servicios-y-entreguen-o-recojan-suministros/?vgnextfmt=default&vgnextoid=f4f085282f8eb710VgnVCM2000001f4a900aRCRD&vgnextchannel=220e31d3b28fe410VgnVCM1000000b205a0aRCRD); [ecomovilidad A Coruña](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/la-coruna/la-coruna/); [ecomovilidad Córdoba](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/cordoba/cordoba/); [ecomovilidad Málaga](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/malaga/malaga/)
scale: unknown.
cost_impact: €200 per breach; filing hours (unquantified).
driver_status: Madrid OMS and Decreto 178 (in force); A Coruña OMS (BOP 185/2025, in force); Córdoba ordinance (BOP 33/2023, in force).
solved_today: manual filings; loading-zone apps not verified.
software_solvable: **Partly.** A filing and evidence pack is feasible; loading-zone occupancy is a physical constraint.

title: Exemption paperwork for older and low-income autónomos
who: self-employed tradespeople and drivers with old vans, near retirement or on low incomes.
where:
- Madrid: 59+ with ≥50% of the fleet unlabelled, renewed yearly.
- Barcelona: within 5 years of retirement, until 31 Mar 2028; households under 2× IPREM.
- Granada: workers under €16,800 income.
- Valladolid: under 1.3× IPREM.
reality: exemptions exist but require sworn statements, fleet lists, insurance, ITV and income proofs, renewed per calendar year and per city.
evidence: [madrid.es FAQ](https://www.madrid.es/portales/munimadrid/es/Inicio/Movilidad-y-transportes/Zonas-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Preguntas-frecuentes-sobre-Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones-ZBE-/?vgnextfmt=default&vgnextoid=9dec1d96b08ed710VgnVCM1000001d4a900aRCRD&vgnextchannel=d2d2edf0f70ab710VgnVCM2000001f4a900aRCRD); [ecomovilidad BCN](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/barcelona/barcelona/); [Xataka Granada](https://www.xataka.com/movilidad/granada-multa-hoy-su-nueva-zona-bajas-emisiones-quienes-pueden-acceder-multas-excepciones); [ecomovilidad Valladolid](https://ecomovilidad.es/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones/valladolid/valladolid/)
scale: unknown number of beneficiaries.
cost_impact: €200 fines if lapsed; filing time.
driver_status: municipal ordinances (in force).
solved_today: gestorías (administrative agents) and municipal offices (prices not found).
software_solvable: **Partly.** Eligibility checks, reminders and document packs. The users are low-digital, price-sensitive autónomos (inference).

title: Mismatch between DGT labels and Euro classes in routing data
who: fleet-software vendors, international carriers, foreign vehicles.
where: national.
reality: Spanish rules use DGT labels (derived from fuel, Euro class and registration date). Commercial engines take Euro class and fuel (HERE, cargoffer MCP). Foreign vehicles have no label and are mapped by Euro class (Palma's equivalence lists). Mis-mapping yields wrong compliance answers.
evidence: [HERE docs](https://docs.here.com/routing/docs/truck-restrictions-env-zones); [Glama cargoffer](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/cargoffer/zbe-mcp-server/tools/zbe.checkRoute); [BOIB 37, 24 Mar 2026](https://www.caib.es/eboibfront/pdf/ca/2026/37/1215590); [bilbao.eus](https://www.bilbao.eus/cs/Satellite?c=Page&cid=1279235266667&language=es&pageid=1279235266667&pagename=Bilbaonet%2FPage%2FBIO_contenidoFinal)
scale: unknown.
cost_impact: €200 per wrong decision.
driver_status: Reglamento General de Vehículos label annex (in force); municipal equivalence tables.
solved_today: vendor approximations.
software_solvable: **Yes.** A label-resolution service by plate or vehicle data. Whether the DGT allows programmatic label lookups was not verified in-session.

title: No consolidated national dataset of ZBE dates, perimeters and status
who: fleet-software vendors, insurers and renting firms, researchers, policymakers.
where: national.
reality: no official table answers "which ZBEs fine, since when, for which vehicles". A public request has gone unanswered for almost a year.
evidence: data request of 16 Nov 2025, status "Asignado", no response as of 19 Oct 2026 ([datos.gob.es](https://datos.gob.es/es/solicitud-de-datos/zonas-de-bajas-emisiones)); conflicting press counts ([Motor16](https://www.motor16.com/las-ultimas-noticias/zbe-ciudades-multas-coches/) vs [Fenadismer](https://www.fenadismer.es/los-transportistas-ya-pueden-consultar-todas-las-zonas-de-bajas-emisiones-en-una-sola-web/)).
scale: about 150 municipalities.
cost_impact: research and vendor curation costs (unquantified).
driver_status: RD 1052/2022 art. 10.2 (in force, partly complied with).
solved_today: aggregator sites (ecomovilidad, RACE, Iberfurgo) and NAP files.
software_solvable: **Yes.** A data product and API.

title: Commercial LEZ vendors have unverified Spanish coverage and opaque pricing
who: SME fleets and software integrators evaluating HERE, TomTom, urbanaccessregulations.eu and Green-Zones.
where: national.
reality: vendors advertise global LEZ coverage (HERE 19 countries; TomTom 376 cities) but do not list Spanish ZBEs. Prices are not public, and some sources are visibly stale (Green-Zones).
evidence: [HERE one-pager](https://assets.here.com/x7rx8ayph7ee/1hLhgrGc50DT8Wtaos2JO7/f914305bc96941845d38c198e276d4e1/HERE-Environmental-Zone-product-one-pager-2021.pdf); [TomTom release notes](https://docs.tomtom.com/routing-api/documentation/tomtom-maps/product-information/release-notes); [green-zones.eu](https://www.green-zones.eu/en/); [Polis Network](https://polisnetwork.eu/?p=16859)
scale: n/a.
cost_impact: unknown prices (gap).
driver_status: n/a (market).
solved_today: enterprise contracts with map vendors (large fleets) and manual lookups (SMEs) (inference).
software_solvable: **Yes** (an opportunity), but incumbents could add Spanish semantics.

title: Municipal capacity gap: obliged towns are not enforcing or communicating
who: municipalities over 50,000 (mid-sized cities especially); indirectly, fleets facing uncertainty.
where: Catalonia (17 of 23 not effectively fining; only 4 of 23 with communication plans); Comunitat Valenciana (0 of 15 by Mar 2025, snippet-level); Aragón (delays, snippet-level); Murcia and Las Palmas (no ZBE).
reality: towns approve ordinances but lack cameras, sanction workflows, registries and communication. Audit bodies flag deficiencies, e.g., in El Prat, Rubí, Sant Boi and Lleida.
evidence: [Metrópoli Abierta, 10 Sep 2026](https://www.metropoliabierta.cat/gran-barcelona/20260910/nomes-sis-municipis-larea-barcelona-apliquen-multes-forma-eficac-zona-baixes-emissions/1003742793528_0.html); [À Punt](https://www.apuntmedia.es/noticies/politica/15-municipis-valencians-50-000-habitants-va-implantar-zona-baixes-emissions-2023_1_1832698.html) (snippet-level); [Segre](https://www.segre.com/ca/lleida/260911/la-sindicatura-de-comptes-conclou-que-la-zbe-de-lleida-es-va-implantar-amb-carncies_1327971.html) (snippet-level)
scale: about 100 of 150 obliged municipalities may not effectively fine (inference, section 1).
cost_impact: risk to aid and EU funds (Valencia €14M, €4M and €115M).
driver_status: Ley 7/2021 art. 14; RD 1052/2022; transport-aid decree-laws (in force).
solved_today: public tenders for camera and back-office systems, e.g., Valencia's tender for the ZBE management and control system, Dec 2025 (snippet-level). — [TED notice 866909-2025](https://ted.europa.eu/es/notice/866909-2025/pdf)
software_solvable: **Partly.** Municipal SaaS for registries, whitelists and communication is feasible, but sales go through public procurement.

title: Funding conditionality drives rushed or "paper" ZBEs
who: municipalities; indirectly fleets, through unstable rules.
where: national (transport-aid decree-laws); Valencia, Málaga and Alicante as examples.
reality: cities race to qualify for transport subsidies and EU funds. Some adopt minimal or sanction-free zones (Alicante, the Vox-backed model in Valencia, episode-only proposals in Sevilla), which creates rule churn for fleets.
evidence: 2025 condition (snippet-level) ([Astrave](https://astrave.com/noticias/subvenciones-transporte-zbe/)); 2026 relaxation ([Valencia Plaza, 24 Dec 2025](https://valenciaplaza.com/valenciaplaza/valencia/el-ministerio-de-transportes-alivia-a-catala-le-permite-acceder-a-las-ayudas-pese-a-no-contar-aun-con-una-zbe)); Valencia €14M plus €4M ([El Español, 7 Mar 2026](https://www.elespanol.com/valencia/20260307/vox-rechaza-valencia-zona-bajas-emisiones-aprobo-castellon-pone-riesgo-millones/1003744158258_0.html)); Málaga EU-funds risk ([Motorpasión](https://www.motorpasion.com/industria/oficial-zbe-malaga-no-multara-a-coches-etiqueta-b-justicia-tumba-ayuntamiento-devolvera-dinero)).
scale: 141 entities applied for €355M of aid in 2025 (snippet-level).
cost_impact: €355M national programme (2025); €115M at risk in Valencia (opposition estimate).
driver_status: RDL 1/2025 (2025; snippet-level) and the Dec 2025 decree-law extending aid through 2026 (in force).
solved_today: political negotiation.
software_solvable: **No.** A policy and political problem.

title: Information phases and switch-on dates create surprise-fine risk
who: fleets and autónomos currently receiving warnings only.
where: Vigo (fines from 10 Sep 2027), Madrid (resident warnings to 31 Dec 2026), Alicante (open-ended), Badalona (moratorium to 1 Jan 2027), Palma (phase 2 from 1 Jan 2027).
reality: warnings arrive without cost, so behaviour does not change until the switch-on date, when fines start at full rate.
evidence: [Atlántico, 10 Sep 2026](https://www.atlantico.net/vigo/entran-vigor-zonas-bajas-emisiones_1_20260910-4408680.html); [madrid.es FAQ](https://www.madrid.es/portales/munimadrid/es/Inicio/Movilidad-y-transportes/Zonas-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones/Preguntas-frecuentes-sobre-Madrid-Zona-de-Bajas-Emisiones-ZBE-/?vgnextfmt=default&vgnextoid=9dec1d96b08ed710VgnVCM1000001d4a900aRCRD&vgnextchannel=d2d2edf0f70ab710VgnVCM2000001f4a900aRCRD); [Metrópoli Abierta](https://www.metropoliabierta.cat/gran-barcelona/20260910/nomes-sis-municipis-larea-barcelona-apliquen-multes-forma-eficac-zona-baixes-emissions/1003742793528_0.html); [BOIB 37](https://www.caib.es/eboibfront/pdf/ca/2026/37/1215590)
scale: Vigo about 62,100 unlabelled vehicles at the first switch-on.
cost_impact: €200 per fine after switch-on.
driver_status: municipal ordinances in grace periods (as listed).
solved_today: nothing specific.
software_solvable: **Yes.** Calendar-driven alerts tied to fleet composition.
